description: Make Printyx print shop management SaaS enterprise-grade, professional, and production-ready. Platform: React 18 + TypeScript + Express + PostgreSQL (Drizzle ORM) + Supabase. Architecture: multi-tenant 4-tier hierarchy (Platform > Company > Regional > Location), 8-level RBAC, 213 pages, 127 route files, 91 services, 51 schema files. Quality checks: npm run check (typecheck), npm run test (unit tests), npm run lint (eslint), npm run build (vite build).

userStories.title: Set up Drizzle migration system replacing db:push
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need proper database migrations instead of db:push so schema changes are versioned, auditable, and safely deployable to production without data loss.
acceptanceCriteria: Configure drizzle-kit to generate migration SQL files in a drizzle/migrations/ directory
drizzle-kit migrate applies pending migrations in order
Add npm scripts: db:generate, db:migrate, db:migrate:status
Create an initial baseline migration from the current schema in shared/schema.ts
Add a migration lockfile pattern to prevent concurrent migrations in production
Update the Database section in CLAUDE.md with new migration workflow replacing db:push references
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Currently using db:push which is not safe for production. Drizzle supports generate+migrate workflow. Main schema: shared/schema.ts (293KB) with 43 additional files in shared/*-schema.ts. Forecasting DB config: drizzle.forecasting.config.ts. See drizzle.config.ts for current setup.

userStories.title: Fix a cluster of type-safety bugs in server/shared core files
userStories.description: As a maintainer, several core server + shared-schema files contain real type-safety bugs that tsc flags (and that mask runtime defects). Fix the highest-value cluster: the structured logger silently DROPPED the error/meta argument when called message-first (errors never reached the logs in prod); an async method was typed boolean instead of Promise<boolean>; two Zod schemas were malformed (marginAnalysisReport was a raw object so z.infer produced an error type; insertCalculatorSessionSchema refined a non-existent email column); a self-referencing FK was untyped; and Set iteration needed downlevelIteration.
acceptanceCriteria: Logger calls of the form log.error("msg", errOrMeta) converted to pino object-first form so the error/meta is actually logged (fixes silent log-data-drop) and types pass — apiErrorHandler, error-sanitizer, company-id-generator, websocket-service (7 sites)
websocket-service.isRealTimeReport typed Promise<boolean> (was async ...: boolean — a real bug)
marginAnalysisReport wrapped in z.object so z.infer<MarginAnalysisReport> resolves (was an error type)
Bogus email refinement removed from insertCalculatorSessionSchema (email is on calculatorLeads, not calculatorSessions)
platform-crm self-referencing reportsToId FK typed via AnyPgColumn
user-lifecycle transferDetails index signature widened to number | undefined to match optional members
schema.ts totalPaid decimal default corrected to string (.default("0")) matching every other decimal default in the file
downlevelIteration enabled + illustrative *.example.ts excluded from typecheck scope
All targeted tsc errors in these specific files resolved (verified: 0 remaining) with no new errors introduced in them
NOTE: this does NOT make npm run check globally green — see QUALITY-002 (6176 pre-existing errors repo-wide)
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-06-25 (QUALITY-001). Scope corrected mid-flight: an earlier `npm run check | tail` had hidden the true error count — the full tsc run shows 6176 pre-existing errors repo-wide (5013 server/shared + 1163 client), so this codebase has never typechecked clean and global-green is a large separate effort (tracked as QUALITY-002). This story fixes the highest-value correctness cluster I found and VERIFIES those specific errors are gone (grep of the fresh tsc log shows 0 remaining in websocket-service.ts, utils/apiErrorHandler.ts, error-sanitizer.ts, company-id-generator.ts, platform-crm-schema.ts, print-cost-calculator-schema.ts, product-pricing-schema.ts, user-lifecycle-schema.ts, schema.ts:2685). Most valuable fixes: (1) the structured logger silently dropped the 2nd arg on message-first calls, so caught errors never reached logs in prod — now logged via {err}; (2) marginAnalysisReport z.infer was broken; (3) isRealTimeReport async-return-type bug. Changes are non-additive (relaxing tsconfig + type-correcting code). Build (vite/esbuild) was never gated on tsc so this changes no shipped behavior except the corrected/improved logging.

BATCH 13 (2026-06-26): server-wide req.session.user typing — the single highest-leverage root cause remaining. ENV NOTE: this container shipped with an EMPTY node_modules (no typescript/@types/node/vite), so npx tsc resolved a stray GLOBAL TS 6.0.2 and reported a bogus ~2 errors (deprecation-only) off a stale incremental cache. Ran `npm ci` to restore the pinned local TS 5.6.3 (the CI toolchain): TRUE count was 3577 baseline -> 3507 after upstream merges. ALWAYS verify node_modules is populated before trusting a tsc count. ROOT CAUSE: 500 TS2339 across 19 files all = "Property 'user' does not exist on type 'Session & Partial<SessionData>'". Two access patterns: direct (req.session.user.tenantId, 5 files: apollo/email-marketing/field-service/lease/signature) and destructured (const user = req.session?.user; 11 files: advanced-billing/automated-billing/customer-success/geofence-alerts/gps-tracking/lead-scoring/manufacturer-order/mfa/mileage/route-optimization/workflow-automation). LATENT RUNTIME BUG FOUND: nothing populates req.session.user — session login (auth-routes.ts) sets FLAT req.session.userId/req.session.tenantId, and these 19 routers mount with NO auth middleware, so every `if (!req.session.user?.tenantId)` guard always 401s at runtime. FIX (type-only, zero runtime risk — chosen over a login-flow change that's security-sensitive and unverifiable with the broken build): new server/types/express-session.d.ts declaring `interface SessionData { user?: {...} }`. Made id+tenantId REQUIRED string (auth-critical, always set together when a user exists) so `if (!user)` guards narrow them to string for downstream storage calls — keeping them optional left 209 string|undefined TS2345/TS2322. role/roleLevel/role_level/email/firstName/fullName/twoFactorEnabled/twoFactorSecret optional (every field the route layer reads; types confirmed from usage e.g. role.toLowerCase(), roleLevel||...||1). Removing the any-poisoning (req.session.user TS2339 -> any propagated through {...data, tenantId:any}) re-typed 6 pre-existing field-service errors any->string (same locations, NOT new) and surfaced ONE new: mfa-routes.ts(813) user.email string|undefined into sendEmailOtp(email:string) — fixed faithfully with a `if (!user.email) return 400` guard (can't email-OTP without an email; also narrows). VERIFIED: ratchet 3507 -> 3017 (-490); `comm` on file+line+col+code shows ZERO genuinely-new error locations. Baseline tightened 3577 -> 3017. Documented latent always-401 bug for a follow-up story (populate req.session.user at login OR migrate the 19 routes to getUserId/getTenantId helpers). prettier clean; server/ eslint-ignored. Build still pre-existing-broken (@sentry/react absent). passes STAYS false (tsc not yet green; cumulative 6176 -> 3017, -51%).

THREE THINGS THE SCANNER GOT WRONG FIRST, each caught by testing rather than review, and each worth knowing if it is touched again:

(1) The chain detector was /\.where\([\s\S]{0,400}?\)\s*\.where\(/ and reported 500 sites. A lazy quantifier does not respect statement boundaries, so nearly every hit was two CORRECT single-where queries that happened to sit within 400 characters of each other. Replaced with balanced-paren scanning that walks only the calls actually chained onto the first where().

(2) The baseline was keyed by file:line. storage.ts is 9,000 lines, so any edit above a known site renumbered it and the gate reported old findings as new - observed directly while mutation-testing, where restoring ONE historical bug produced five findings, four of them line shifts. Found by mutation-testing against the REAL routes-product-models shape rather than a synthetic one - the synthetic version happened to be multi-line and passed. Anchor dropped; requiring the same identifier on both sides of the `=` is what keeps it from over-matching.

[2026-08-29 BATCH: routes-admin-workflows deleted, 371 -> 362 (-9). The nine errors were one defect wearing three hats, and the most useful thing here is WHY THE FIX WAS DELETION RATHER THAN REPAIR.

THE TABLE WAS WRONG. Every query in the file filtered `activity_reports` on type, severity and resolved. None is a column on it - activity_reports is a SALES ACTIVITY ROLLUP (report_date, period, total_calls, total_emails, total_meetings, connected_calls). The author knew: the comment at the first one reads 'simulated - would query tenant_onboarding table'. Drizzle gives `activityReports.type` as undefined, so eq(undefined, ...) threw and every one of those handlers 500'd. The two audit inserts had the same shape from the other side - type/severity/description/metadata/resolved are all dropped as unknown keys, leaving a row that violates NOT NULL on tenant_id, report_date and period.

SIX OF SEVEN ROUTES HAD NO CALLER anywhere in client/src. The seventh, POST /api/admin/execute-action, is called by AdminCommandCenter.tsx and returned a canned success for every branch: 'Tenant provisioning workflow initiated', 'Application cache cleared successfully', 'Database backup initiated', and a security scan reporting 0 critical / 2 medium / 5 low findings it never looked for. /workflows/:id/status reported status 'completed', progress 100 for ANY workflow id. The action ids it switched on ('cache-clear', 'backup-generation') did not even match the ids the page sends ('clear-cache', 'generate-backup'), so every real click fell through to its default 'executed successfully'.

THE PART WORTH REMEMBERING: repairing the insert would have made this WORSE. The audit insert threw before any of the switch ran, so the endpoint 500'd and the page showed 'Failed to execute action'. Fixing the column names would have converted an honest error into a green 'The action has been completed successfully' toast on Suspend Tenant, Reset Passwords and Generate Backup. A typecheck batch that only makes types line up would have shipped exactly that. Check what a handler DOES before making it compile.

DONE: router deleted (400 lines) with the reasoning left in routes-registry.ts where the mount was; AdminCommandCenter's executeAction mutation removed along with the Proceed button, so the dialog now says the workflow is not implemented instead of contradicting its own 'under development' note two lines later. The page /security-dashboard IS routed and calls three of its four endpoints. It looked like a live broken dashboard. It is not: /api/security is in crmProxies, the proxy registers at routes-registry:297 and this router mounted at :848, so it was SHADOWED and never ran. supabase/functions/security/ has served all four endpoints since EDGE-005d, and its own header says 'the Express implementation queried non-existent columns (createdAt, resourceType, details)' - the bug was found and fixed on the edge side, and the Express file was left behind.   (b) DYNAMIC IMPORT: `const r = await import('./routes-x'); app.use('/api/x', r.default)`. The spec lookup found nothing. This hid routes-customer-numbers and routes-company-ids.
Both are now detected - a selfMountedFindings pass over every server file, and dynamic `await import` specs folded into the same importedFrom map the static ones use. Verified against the real files before deleting them: restoring routes-security-dashboard made the count go 61 -> 65 with /api/security as a new prefix, and the dynamic-import pass surfaced /api/company-ids, a prefix nobody had looked at.

DELETED, all three fully covered by their edge functions, which say so in their own headers: routes-security-dashboard.ts (218 lines, 4 routes), routes-customer-numbers.ts (358 lines, 8 routes - the edge fn covers all eight, the frontend calls four), routes-company-ids.ts (150 lines, 4 routes - the edge fn also fixes the named-route-before-:id precedence the Express copy got wrong).

PROGRESS 2026-08-29 - 340 -> 334, and the useful part was reading the error DISTRIBUTION rather than fixing errors.

There is no big cluster left; the largest single file is 10. So I used the distribution as a diagnostic instead, which is what CLAUDE.md says a TS2339 cluster on a table type is worth. Two findings came out of it.

server/routes/calendar-routes.ts is DELETED - 288 lines, nine handlers, every one a mock that said so ("Mock response for now", "Mock event creation", "Mock event deletion"), and no client tree called /api/calendar. The only reference anywhere was a test NAME inside client/src/pages/_archived/TestingDashboard.tsx.backup. Its six errors were `Property 'tenantId' does not exist on type 'User | undefined'`, which would have been a five-minute "fix" that left a mock router compiling cleanly - the exact QUALITY-002 trap this story already records for routes-admin-workflows.

THE REAL CALENDAR SURFACE IS A DIFFERENT PREFIX, and it is broken in production for a reason unrelated to types. CalendarProvider wraps the routed /demo-scheduling page and calls /api/integrations/calendar/{connect,events}, which NEITHER backend serves - no Express handler, no branch in the integrations edge function, not proxied. It degrades honestly on paper ("Calendar sync is not configured", "Event Saved Locally"), and in production those branches never ran: a relative fetch('/api/...') never passes through getApiUrl, so it hit the static-bundle origin, which answers an unknown path with index.html at 200. `response.ok` was TRUE and `response.json()` then threw on the HTML, so the destructive "Event Creation Failed" branch ran instead of the graceful one. Through apiRequest the request reaches the functions host, 404s, throws, and the honest branch runs. Three entries off the PROD-013 raw-fetch baseline (81 -> 78).

server/routes-contract-alerts.ts LOOKED like the better target and is not, which is worth recording so the next pass does not re-derive it: four TS2339s naming phantom columns (contracts.contractType, service_contracts.includedPages, service_contracts.billingCycle), which by the CLAUDE.md rule means a feature that cannot work. It serves /api/alerts/*, and nothing in any client tree calls that prefix. So it is unconnected work, not a live defect, and making it compile would be churn. Left alone deliberately.

A MISTAKE WORTH THE SPACE: deleting calendar-routes.ts broke server/tests/api-endpoints.test.ts, which imported it - beforeAll threw and all 33 of its tests SKIPPED rather than failed, which is the exact failure mode that file's own header documents from PROD-002. I did not notice because I have been reading the "Tests N passed" line out of a pipe and never the exit code. `npm run test > /tmp/t.txt; echo $?` is the check. The Calendar Routes describe block is removed along with the router - tests that pin a mock's shape go with the mock, since keeping them would mean keeping the mock to satisfy them.

PROGRESS 2026-08-29 (part 3) - ran every check script BY EXIT CODE for the first time, and it found three things I had not.

THE HABIT WAS THE BUG. I have been running guards individually and reading their output, which misses two failure modes: a guard that is not in my head at all, and a guard whose message looks like a summary but whose exit code is 1. Both happened. The sweep is `for c in $(node -e "...scripts starting with check:..."); do npm run -s $c >/dev/null || echo $c; done` - it takes a few minutes and needs no interpretation.

Also worth knowing: `npm run -s <name>` for a script that does not exist exits 1 with a suggestion, which reads exactly like a guard failure. My first sweep reported check:nav-targets failing; the script is called check:nav. Confirm a name before believing a red line.

WHAT IT FOUND. (1) check:query-states was failing on two components I added this session - TwoFactorCard and AIInsightsView - each calling useQuery and never reading isError. That guard exists because a component which renders identically on success, loading and failure turns an outage into an empty account, and on the 2FA card specifically it would have told someone with MFA enabled that they had none and invited them to enrol again. Both handled now. (2) check:error-shape had drifted, 117 -> 118 in server/routes/gps-tracking-routes.ts, from commit 0427f17 on 2026-08-27 - before this session. That commit's own point was that /api/gps has no caller, which is presumably why nobody looked at the ratchet. The one site is a 501 that returned a bare `error` key; it uses sendError now, and the baseline is back at its real number rather than grown to accommodate it.

(3) Two scripts fail for reasons that are not defects and should stay understood rather than fixed: check:schema needs a live database and crashes without one, and check:stage-resolution exits 2 on purpose when DATABASE_URL is unset, so that "did not run" is never read as "passed".

CORRECTION 2026-09-02 (WF-L-08). The INSTALLED->ACTIVE and ACTIVE->RETIRED entries above are wrong: "activate monitoring" and "deactivate monitoring" were never implemented. userStories.notes: Existing InlineEdit component (client/src/components/ui/inline-edit.tsx) supports text, number, email, textarea, select, currency, dates. Integrate this into the table renderer. userStories.title: Build configurable record page layout engine with activity timeline

Reference: CRM_Layout.md 'Deal record page layout' section: 'Header: name, stage/pipeline, quick actions. Left: editable property groups. Center: timeline with filters and compose inputs. userStories.title: Build board options and in-context configuration UIs

'Edit Columns' panel: toggle visibility of pipeline stages as columns, reorder columns, configure column total display (sum/count/weighted/average/none), column color customization

userStories.notes: This story provides the configuration UIs for CRM-004 (card configs). HubSpot has two levels: global admin setup (Objects > Deals > Pipelines in settings) and in-context configuration (Edit board, Card setup) for power users. This story focuses on the in-context configuration. The global admin setup is handled by the existing PipelineConfiguration.tsx page. userStories.title: Apply unified CRM index pattern to contacts, companies, and all object types
userStories.description: As a platform user, I need contacts, companies, and other CRM object types to use the same unified index/board/record page patterns as deals, so the entire CRM feels consistent and professional like HubSpot where every object type shares the same UX.
acceptanceCriteria: CrmIndexShell from CRM-002 accepts objectType as a generic parameter and renders appropriate columns/fields per type

Leads page (/leads) uses CrmIndexShell with objectType='leads' including board view with lead stages
Each object type defines its own: available properties for card config, default saved views, quick filter fields, default table columns

userStories.notes: HubSpot's core UX principle: 'Contacts, companies, deals, tickets, and custom objects all share the same basic index + board + record patterns.' This story generalizes the deals-specific work from CRM-002 through CRM-009 into a generic object view system. The object registry pattern lets each type define its behavior. Existing pages to refactor: Contacts.tsx, CustomersPage.tsx, CompanyContacts.tsx, ProspectsPage.tsx. Reference: CRM_Layout.md 'Custom objects and extensible UI' section.

userStories.title: Complete frontend route permission guards for all 261 pages

acceptanceCriteria: Audit all 261 routes in client/src/App.tsx against client/src/lib/navigation-permissions.ts
Add permission entries for every page missing from navigationPermissions map
Group missing pages by module: dashboards, equipment, billing, reports, admin, settings, integrations
Create a ProtectedRoute wrapper component that checks navigationPermissions before rendering
Wrap all lazy-loaded routes in App.tsx with ProtectedRoute
Unauthenticated users redirected to /login; authenticated users without permission see a 403 page with 'Request Access' link
Create a simple /unauthorized page component explaining the user lacks permission
Verify platform admin (level 8) can access all pages
Verify location-level user (level 1) is blocked from admin pages
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Currently only ~80 of 261 pages have permission rules in navigation-permissions.ts. Pages like /gpt5-dashboard, /social-media-generator, /autopilot-*, many admin pages lack guards. Users can bypass sidebar role filtering by navigating directly to URLs. The sidebar hides items but doesn't prevent access. Key files: client/src/App.tsx (261 routes), client/src/lib/navigation-permissions.ts (~80 entries), client/src/components/layout/RoleAwareCollapsibleSidebar.tsx.

userStories.title: Standardize auth middleware imports across all 156 route files
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a single consistent auth middleware pattern across all route files so security behavior is uniform and auditable.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit all server/routes-*.ts and server/routes/*.ts files for auth middleware usage
Replace all inline requireAuth definitions with centralized imports
Standardize on: import { requireSupabaseAuth as requireAuth } from './middleware/supabase-auth' for JWT auth
Ensure every route file uses getUserId(req) and getTenantId(req) from utils/auth-helpers instead of direct req.user access
Remove any duplicate middleware definitions found in individual route files
Create a lint rule or code comment convention documenting the standard pattern
Verify no route files define their own auth middleware inline
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Found ~8-10 different auth middleware patterns across route files. Some define requireAuth inline, some import from replitAuth, some from supabase-auth. This inconsistency makes security auditing difficult. CLAUDE.md documents the correct patterns but they aren't consistently followed.

userStories.title: Add granular RBAC permission checks to all CRUD and sensitive endpoints
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I need every API endpoint that modifies data to enforce granular RBAC permissions (not just authentication) so users can only perform actions their role allows.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit all POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE endpoints across route files for requirePermission usage
Add requirePermission middleware to all data-modifying endpoints that currently only use requireAuth
DELETE endpoints require appropriate .delete permission (e.g., sales.lead.delete_own, admin.record.delete_all)
Bulk operation endpoints (/api/*/bulk-update, /api/*/bulk-delete) require elevated permissions (scope: _all or _team)
Settings/configuration endpoints require admin-level permissions
Export endpoints require appropriate .export permission
Document the complete permission matrix: endpoint → required permissions in a permissions-matrix.ts file
Add tests verifying permission denial returns 403 with descriptive message
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Many endpoints currently only check requireAuth (is the user logged in?) but not requirePermission (does the user have the right role/permission?). Bulk operations and DELETE routes are the highest risk. The enhanced-rbac-middleware.ts has full support for granular permissions but adoption is incomplete.

userStories.title: Eliminate legacy string-role checks and unify on enhanced RBAC system
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the codebase to use a single RBAC system instead of mixing legacy string role checks ('admin', 'root_admin') with the enhanced RBAC permission system.
acceptanceCriteria: Find all instances of legacy role string comparisons (role === 'admin', role === 'root_admin', role === 'manager', etc.) in server/ directory
Replace each with equivalent enhanced RBAC permission checks using requirePermission or hasPermission
Map legacy roles to their enhanced RBAC equivalents and document the mapping
Remove or deprecate the legacy role-to-permission mapping functions that bridge old and new systems
Update the roles seeder (npm run seed:rbac) to ensure all enhanced roles have complete permission sets
Verify platform admin bypass still works correctly through enhanced RBAC (level 8 auto-grants)
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Tests pass: npm run test
userStories.notes: Two role systems exist: 'roles' table (frontend via PostgREST) and 'enhanced_roles' (backend RBAC). Legacy string checks create duplicate logic paths that are hard to audit. The enhanced RBAC system is complete and should be the single source of truth.

userStories.title: Add role-based UI element visibility throughout frontend

Apply PermissionGate to at least: LeadsManagement, QuotesManagement, Invoices, Customers, Orders, and all Admin pages

userStories.notes: Currently the sidebar hides navigation items by role, but within pages all action buttons render regardless of permission. userStories.title: Add global search with Cmd/Ctrl+K shortcut and universal results

userStories.title: Add breadcrumb navigation to all detail and nested pages

userStories.title: Add consistent empty states, loading skeletons, and error states to all list pages

userStories.title: Unify snake_case to camelCase data transformation with centralized entity mappers

Create a generic mapResponse<T>(response, mapper) utility that handles both single and array responses
Integrate mappers into apiRequest or create entity-specific query hooks that auto-transform
Refactor at least 8 major pages (Leads, Customers, Quotes, Invoices, Orders, Contacts, Contracts, Equipment) to use centralized mappers
Remove duplicate inline transformation code from refactored pages
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Every page currently does manual field mapping like: invoiceNumber: item.invoiceNumber || item.invoice_number || ''. This creates 50+ lines of duplicate transformation per page, is error-prone, and makes it hard to add new fields. A centralized mapper eliminates this entirely.

userStories.title: Implement optimistic mutations for inline edits and status changes
userStories.description: As a user editing records, I need the UI to update immediately when I make changes rather than waiting for the server round-trip so the app feels fast and responsive.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a useOptimisticMutation hook that wraps TanStack Query's useMutation with optimistic cache updates

On success: merge the server response into the cache (server is source of truth for computed fields)
On error: roll back the optimistic update, show error toast, restore previous state
Apply to inline cell edits in table views (status changes, field updates)
Apply to drag-and-drop stage changes on pipeline boards
Apply to toggle operations (active/inactive, pin/unpin, archive/unarchive)
Show a subtle 'Saving...' indicator near the edited field during the API call
Batch rapid edits: if user edits multiple fields within 500ms, debounce into a single PATCH request
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Currently pages use queryClient.invalidateQueries() which does a full refetch after every mutation. This causes visible loading flicker and feels slow, especially on mobile. useOptimisticMutations hook already exists in the codebase but isn't widely adopted. This story expands adoption.

userStories.title: Add contextual help tooltips and onboarding hints for key workflows

userStories.title: Enhance Invoices page with aging analysis, payment reminders, and AR dashboard

userStories.title: Enhance Orders page with fulfillment tracking, status timeline, and delivery management
userStories.description: As an operations manager, I need to track order fulfillment stages, see status change history, and manage delivery scheduling so orders move smoothly from confirmed to delivered.
acceptanceCriteria: Add visual fulfillment pipeline at top of orders page: Confirmed → In Production → Quality Check → Ready to Ship → Shipped → Delivered with counts per stage

userStories.description: As a sales manager, I need records to be automatically scoped to what each user is authorized to see at the API level — reps see only their own leads and quotes, managers see their team's, directors see their region's — so data isolation is enforced on the server, not just the UI.

Build passes: npm run build

hierarchical-query-builder.ts exists at server/middleware/hierarchical-query-builder.ts but is not applied consistently across all list endpoints. Currently most endpoints only filter by tenantId which means any authenticated user in the tenant sees all records. This is correct for admins but wrong for reps. The enhanced-rbac-middleware.ts provides EnhancedUserContext with roleLevel, teamId, regionId, territoryScope — use these for scoping. This is a data security story, not just UI.
REOPENED 2026-09-02 (WF-R-01). passes:true was asserting the opposite of the tree.

The deliverable, server/middleware/scope-middleware.ts, HAS NO IMPORTERS. Nothing
in server/, client/ or supabase/ references it, and it sits in
docs/server-orphans-baseline.json as an unreachable server file. So no request is
scoped by it and a rep sees exactly what a manager sees on every endpoint it was
meant to cover.

server/middleware/hierarchical-query-builder.ts is in the same position by
transitivity: its only importers are themselves orphans (AUDIT-034's rule -
reachability is transitive, and a one-level grep gets this wrong in both
directions).

This is not a small gap in a working feature; it is a feature with no caller, the
commonest defect shape in this repository (AUDIT-024). Closing it needs the WF-R
chain: the decision is recorded in docs/rbac-decision.md and the scoping work is
WF-R-04 through WF-R-07, which cannot start until WF-R-02 seeds the surviving role
table and WF-R-03 puts the claims in the token.

userStories.title: Add role-specific dashboard views that surface relevant KPIs and actions per role

acceptanceCriteria: Modify the main Dashboard page (client/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx or equivalent) to detect the user's roleLevel from usePermissions() and render the appropriate view
roleLevel 1-2 (Individual Contributor / Team Lead): Show 'My Pipeline' widgets — My Open Leads count, My Active Quotes with total value, My Upcoming Tasks (next 7 days), My Recent Activity feed
roleLevel 3-4 (Supervisor / Manager): Show team widgets — Team Pipeline Summary by stage, Team Quota Attainment %, Top Performing Reps (ranked by deals closed this month), Team Activity Feed
roleLevel 5-6 (Regional / Company Director): Show regional widgets — Regional Revenue vs Target, Pipeline by Stage (all teams in region), Deals at Risk (no activity > 14 days), Conversion Rate trend
roleLevel 7-8 (Executive / Platform Admin): Show company-wide KPIs — Total Revenue MTD/YTD, MRR, NRR, Customer Count, ARR Forecast, Churn Rate
Each dashboard tier must use the existing KpiSummaryBar component with role-appropriate metrics
Quick action buttons on each tier: Rep → 'New Lead', 'New Quote'; Manager → 'Review Pipeline', 'Team Assignments'; Director → 'Reports', 'Forecast'; Admin → 'Admin Hub', 'System Settings'
Dashboard does not redirect or change URL — same route / but renders different components based on role
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes:
Currently the Dashboard at / renders a single view for all roles. KpiSummaryBar component exists at client/src/components/dashboard/KpiSummaryBar.tsx and accepts configurable metrics. This is a high-impact UX improvement — reps currently see company-wide charts that aren't actionable for them. usePermissions() returns level and role tier. The API scoping from RBAC-003 means the data returned is already role-scoped, so the dashboard widgets can use the same endpoints and get role-appropriate data.
REOPENED 2026-09-02 (WF-R-01). The dashboards exist; the role resolution behind
them does not, so "role-specific" is not what a user gets.

client/src/components/dashboards/RoleBasedDashboard.tsx resolves the role with:

    if (isPlatformUser) return 'PLATFORM_ADMIN';
    if (roleCode) return roleCode.toUpperCase();
    ... level inference, department inference ...

and client/src/hooks/usePermissions.ts:70 defines

    const roleCode: string = role?.code || role?.name || 'USER';

which is NEVER EMPTY. So `if (roleCode)` always returns, and every fallback beneath
it - the level tiers (L7 EXECUTIVE, L6 COMPANY_ADMIN, L5 REGIONAL_MANAGER, L4
LOCATION_MANAGER) and the sales/service department inference - is unreachable dead
code. It was written to handle exactly the case it can never see.

The consequence for a real user: a role row carrying no `code` and no `name`
resolves to the literal 'USER', which is not one of the twelve seeded codes in
DEFAULT_ROLE_LAYOUTS, so getDefaultLayout falls to 'DEFAULT'. Every such user gets
the generic dashboard while the careful inference that would have given them a
sales or service layout never runs.

Filed with WF-R-10 as the fix. The sharper form of the finding, worth carrying: an
always-truthy default in a hook is enough to make a whole fallback chain in its
consumer unreachable, and neither file looks wrong on its own.

userStories.title: Security headers hardening with Helmet.js and strict CSP

acceptanceCriteria: Install and configure helmet in server/index.ts as early middleware with strict settings

Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' with nonce-based inline scripts; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' (for Tailwind); img-src 'self' data: https:; connect-src 'self' wss: https://api.printyx.net https://functions.printyx.net; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on all responses
X-Frame-Options: DENY (prevent clickjacking)
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=(self)
Remove X-Powered-By header (Express fingerprint removal)
Create server/tests/unit/security-headers.test.ts verifying all headers present on API and page responses
CSP violation reporting endpoint at /api/csp-report that logs violations with createModuleLogger
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: COMPLETE. Helmet v7.2.0 configured in server/index.ts with full CSP (nonce-based scripts), HSTS, X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Powered-By removed, Permissions-Policy, Referrer-Policy. CSP violation reporting at /api/csp-report. Tests in server/tests/unit/security-headers.test.ts.

userStories.title: CORS hardening and origin validation

userStories.title: Internal penetration testing harness using OWASP methodology

userStories.title: Session security hardening - token rotation, device binding, and replay prevention

Add /api/auth/sessions endpoint for users to view and revoke their active sessions (device, location, last active)
Store session metadata in security_sessions table: device fingerprint, IP address, created_at, last_active_at, is_suspicious flag

userStories.notes: COMPLETE. server/middleware/session-hardening.ts with device fingerprinting, refresh token rotation with replay detection, token family revocation, session invalidation on role changes. Tests in server/tests/unit/session-hardening.test.ts.

userStories.title: Request fingerprinting and bot detection middleware

Create server/config/bot-signatures.ts with updatable list of known tool signatures and detection patterns

userStories.description: As a security engineer, I need the SQL injection vulnerability in routes-custom-reports.ts fixed because filter.value from request body is passed directly to sql.raw() inside an INTERVAL clause, allowing an attacker to break out of the interval and inject arbitrary SQL.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace sql.raw(filter.value) on line 782 with a validated and parameterized numeric value
Validate that filter.value is a positive integer before use in the INTERVAL clause
Use Drizzle parameterized query: sql`interval '1 day' * ${validatedDays}` or equivalent safe pattern
Reject non-numeric filter.value with appropriate error response
Custom reports last_n_days filter works identically for valid numeric inputs
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: FIXED: Replaced sql.raw(filter.value) with parseInt() validation and parameterized interval multiplication: sql`${column} >= CURRENT_DATE - (${days} * interval '1 day')`. Validates days is a positive integer between 0 and 3650. Returns null (no filter) for invalid values.

userStories.notes: Express source: routes-subscriptions.ts. Stripe webhooks may need their own route — use Supabase webhook function pattern. | PROGRESS 2026-07-17 — AC BULLET 3 (schema-audit) DONE; THE STORY'S OWN SCOPE STATEMENT CORRECTED IN THREE WAYS. No port started: the porting AC bullets are not completable in this environment (bullet 4 wants /checkout/session/:id and /portal round-tripped through STRIPE, and bullet 6 wants SubscriptionDashboard/BillingPlanUpgrade/TrialConversion smoke-tested — both need live credentials and a running app). The audit is the bounded, code-only slice, so it was done properly rather than half-porting 13 endpoints. | SCHEMA AUDIT: CLEAN — and this is the first audit in this run of work that came back clean, which is itself worth recording. routes-subscriptions.ts has ZERO tsc errors, and both implementations query only REAL tables: the edge fn reads tenant_subscriptions / subscription_plans / subscription_features / billing_history / subscription_events / usage_metrics; Express reads subscriptionPlans / subscriptionFeatures / subscriptionNotifications. No phantom columns on either side. Contrast every other schema audit in this session (batches 13-24), each of which found never-worked code. | BUT THE AC'S OWN TABLE NAMES ARE PHANTOM. It says "Schema-audit subscriptions, subscription_invoices, subscription_features tables". Only subscription_features exists. There is NO `subscriptions` table — the real one is `tenant_subscriptions` — and NO `subscription_invoices` — invoice history lives in `billing_history`. The CODE is right and the ACCEPTANCE CRITERION is wrong; anyone taking the AC literally would go looking for two tables that never existed. All 14 real tables are in shared/schema-subscriptions.ts. | THE ENDPOINT GAP IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The description says "Edge function only has /plans, /usage, /invoices, /features, /change-plan" and lists 13 missing endpoints. Measured:   - The edge fn ALSO already serves /cancel and /resume. So /cancel is in the AC's port list but is ALREADY PORTED.   - Express serves 25 endpoints, not the 13 the AC enumerates.   - Measured against what the FRONTEND actually calls (the EDGE-002a rule — parity is defined by client/src, not by the     Express surface), the real gap is 13 paths, but NOT the 13 the AC names: checkout, checkout/addon,     checkout/session/:id, convert-trial, create, current, notifications, notifications/:id/dismiss,     notifications/:id/read, portal, preview-upgrade, setup-intent, stripe/config, upgrade.   - /setup-intent and /notifications/:id/read are MISSING FROM THE AC entirely but ARE called by the frontend.   - Conversely the edge fn serves /change-plan, /features, /invoices and /resume, which the frontend NEVER calls —     four endpoints already ported that nothing consumes. Worth deciding whether they are for a future UI or dead. | NOT DONE, and each needs something this environment lacks: the Stripe port itself (needs the stripe client wired via esm.sh AND live keys to verify the checkout/portal round-trip in AC bullet 4), the notification port, the crmProxies entry (AC bullet 5 — do NOT add it until the port is complete: per the proxy's own header comment, adding a prefix makes DEV forward the WHOLE prefix to the edge function, and fall-through happens only on a network error, never on a 404 — so proxying now would 404 every un-ported endpoint in dev, i.e. break the entire Stripe flow locally), and the smoke tests. | ONE THING FOR WHOEVER PORTS IT: routes-subscriptions.ts also serves POST /webhooks/stripe. Do NOT fold that into the subscriptions edge function — CLAUDE.md is explicit that "Stripe's live webhook URL is /api/webhooks/stripe, NOT under /api/billing", i.e. the webhook is a separate top-level route Stripe posts to directly, and it must keep its own path and its own signature verification. The AC's own note ("Stripe webhooks may need their own route — use Supabase webhook function pattern") is right; this confirms it against the documented live URL. | 2026-08-27 CROSS-REFERENCE: this story's closing note ("routes-subscriptions.ts also serves POST /webhooks/stripe -- do NOT fold that into the subscriptions edge function") led to a defect worth knowing before anyone ports this. That handler is at /api/subscriptions/webhooks/stripe, but scripts/setup-stripe-products.ts:362 and CLAUDE.md both name /api/webhooks/stripe as the URL to configure in the Stripe dashboard -- a DIFFERENT route, the generic receiver in server/integrations/webhook-routes.ts, whose Stripe branch was a stub that verified the signature and discarded the event. Subscription state therefore never moved from a real Stripe event. Fixed under INTEG-WEBHOOK-001 by having the generic receiver record the delivery and dispatch it to StripeService.handleWebhookEventEnhanced. The advice here still stands -- the webhook keeps its own top-level path and its own signature verification -- but the working path is /api/webhooks/stripe, not the one this file registers.

userStories.notes:
Express source: routes-root-admin.ts. /execute-query is a security-sensitive feature; consider whether to port at all. [PARTIAL 2026-08-20. THE GAP IS WIDER THAN THIS STORY STATES: the frontend also calls /trial-funnel and /high-value-signups, so it is EIGHT endpoints, not six. Verified by grepping /api/root-admin across client/src.

THREE OF THE EIGHT ARE NOT PORTABLE AT ALL, and that is a finding rather than a shortfall. /system-resources, /database-tables and /execute-query do not read tenant tables - they introspect POSTGRES ITSELF: pg_database_size(), pg_stat_activity, information_schema.tables, pg_tables JOIN pg_class (with pg_stat_get_tuples_returned / pg_stat_get_last_vacuum_time), and in the last case an operator-supplied statement. PostgREST exposes ONE SCHEMA OF TABLES and reaches none of that. They now return 501 REQUIRES_DIRECT_SQL naming the reason rather than 404ing.

/execute-query DESERVES ITS OWN PARAGRAPH BECAUSE PORTING IT WOULD BE A SECURITY REGRESSION. Express runs the statement inside SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY, so POSTGRES rejects any write with SQLSTATE 25006 - and the code comment there is explicit that this transaction, not the static validateReadOnlyQuery lexer in front of it, is the real boundary. The PostgREST client cannot express a transaction at all. Reproducing this on the edge would mean creating a database FUNCTION that executes arbitrary operator SQL, which is a materially worse attack surface than the current arrangement. RPC is available in edge functions (27 uses, e.g. pipeline_template_clone) so it is technically possible - which is exactly why it is worth writing down that it should not be done. This story's own AC allows removing the feature instead of porting it. Leave it on Express; the real improvement the Express comment already names is a dedicated low-privilege role / read replica, which is an ops change.

/pending-tasks WAS BROKEN ON EXPRESS TOO - fourth sighting of the activity_reports defect. It filters activityReports on .type, .resolved and .severity. activity_reports is the SALES rollup (total_calls / total_emails / meetings_scheduled / proposal_win_rate); it has none of those three columns. This is the SAME defect COP-M01 round 17 found in this function's /security-alerts, which was rebuilt on audit_logs. Rebuilt /pending-tasks the same way, from sources that exist: platform_signups in pending/new/trial status, and audit_logs rows with category=security severity=critical. WORTH GENERALISING: activity_reports is a magnet for this - anything filtering it by type/severity/resolved is wrong, because those belong to audit_logs.

/signups is a straight port over platform_signups, returning { data, pagination } with camelCase rows (the page reads companyName / firstName / qualificationScore / lastActivityAt). ONE GUARD ADDED BEYOND EXPRESS: sortBy arrives from the query string and Express passes it straight into an order-by, so an unknown name is a 42703 - a user-triggerable 500. It is now whitelisted against six real columns and falls back to created_at.

DELIBERATELY LEFT FOR THE NEXT ROUND: /signups-analytics, /trial-funnel, /high-value-signups. Each is a multi-aggregate endpoint whose exact shape the page types (SignupsAnalytics / TrialFunnel / HighValueSignups interfaces in RootAdminSignupsCRM.tsx), and by now this story-family has established that a 200 with the wrong shape is worse than the 404 they return today. They get their own pass. NOTE they will need the aggregation moved into the handler - PostgREST expresses no SUM/AVG/GROUP BY/count(DISTINCT), which has held for every dashboard endpoint ported in EDGE-002g.]
[PORTABLE HALF COMPLETE 2026-08-20. Every /api/root-admin path the frontend calls now resolves: overview, tenants, security-alerts, users, audit-logs (pre-existing), signups, pending-tasks, signups-analytics, trial-funnel, high-value-signups (ported), and system-resources / database-tables / execute-query returning 501 REQUIRES_DIRECT_SQL.

FOUND A REAL BUG IN EXPRESS AND DID NOT COPY IT. /signups-analytics computes avgQualificationScore as `db.select({ avg: platformSignups.qualificationScore })` then reads `[0]?.avg`. That is not an average - it selects the column for every row and takes the FIRST ONE. The field is named avgQualificationScore and the card above it in RootAdminSignupsCRM.tsx reads "Avg Qualification Score", so replicating it would mean knowingly serving a wrong number under a correct label. Computed properly here, over rows that actually carry a score. This is the third deliberate divergence from Express in this story-family, and they share a shape: auto-lead-routing /config said "saved successfully" while storing nothing; chart-of-accounts' delete guard read a phantom column so it never fired; this one labels a first-row sample as a mean. PORT THE BEHAVIOUR, NOT THE BUG - but say so in the commit and here, so the divergence is a decision on the record rather than a silent difference between two backends.

Second guard added beyond Express: trial-funnel's drop-off divides by the PREVIOUS stage's count. Express does not check it, so a stage with zero events yields NaN (0/0) or Infinity in the chart. Now yields 0.

AGGREGATION RULE HOLDS AGAIN, sixth time in this family: signups-analytics needed GROUP BY (byStatus, bySource) and AVG moved into the handler, because PostgREST expresses none of SUM/AVG/GROUP BY/count(DISTINCT). Assume it for any Express dashboard endpoint - they all reach for sql`` templates.

trial-funnel note: conversion_funnel_events has NO tenant_id (it is keyed by signup_id), and Express does not filter by tenant either - root-admin is platform-scoped by design. That is correct here, but it is the kind of thing worth checking rather than assuming, given how many findings in COP-M01 were missing tenant filters.

REMAINING FOR THIS STORY: the crmProxies entry + smoke test. NOTE THIS ONE IS DIFFERENT FROM THE OTHER PREFIXES: /api/root-admin can NEVER be fully proxied, because three of its endpoints must stay on Express. A proxy entry would send system-resources, database-tables and execute-query to the edge function's 501 and break the DatabaseManagement page in dev, which works today. So either leave this prefix unproxied, or add a server.ts route override that forwards ONLY the portable endpoints - and that decision needs stating in EDGE-008/EDGE-014 rather than being made silently here.]

Port /regenerate-robots and /regenerate-llms (file generation)
Add '/api/seo': 'seo' to crmProxies
Smoke-test SEODashboard and RootAdminSEO
userStories.notes: Express source: routes-seo-core.ts. SEO features are platform-admin-tier; lower-priority than customer-facing pages. | PROGRESS 2026-07-17 — SCOPE AUDIT ONLY (no code changed), and it found something that INVERTS the story's premise. | THE SEO EDGE FUNCTION IS BROKEN IN PRODUCTION — ALL OF IT. The story says "Edge function has /settings, /pages, /pages/:id, /analytics, /sitemap/generate, /redirects", i.e. treats those as the already-done half. It has the HANDLERS, but none of them can ever fire in prod. supabase/functions/seo/index.ts:33-37 does `const pathParts = url.pathname.split('/').filter(Boolean)` and then `const resource = pathParts[1]`, with an explicit comment asserting "pathParts[0] = 'seo', pathParts[1] = resource" — it expects the /seo PREFIX TO BE INTACT. It is not: supabase/functions/server.ts:150 sets stripSegments = 1 and line 232 rewrites the path to `'/' + pathParts.slice(stripSegments).join('/')` BEFORE invoking the handler. So a prod request to functions.printyx.net/seo/settings reaches this handler as `/settings` -> pathParts = ['settings'] -> pathParts[1] === undefined -> resource === undefined -> EVERY route guard (`resource === 'settings'`, `resource === 'pages'`, ...) is false -> the function 404s on all six of its endpoints. Confirmed it has NOT been migrated to normalizePath (grep: 0 occurrences), which is precisely the defect CLAUDE.md already documents for its sibling: "The integrations fn still indexes pathParts[1] (NOT migrated to normalizePath in EDGE-002m) so its OTHER routes are off-by-one under server.ts strip". Same bug, different function, and unlike the integrations note this one affects EVERY route rather than some. | WHY NOBODY HAS NOTICED: '/api/seo' is NOT in crmProxies, so DEV serves SEO from Express and never touches the edge function. The breakage is prod-only and invisible locally — the same dev/prod asymmetry CLAUDE.md warns about ("a query param supported only by Express silently breaks in production"), in its most total form. THIS ALSO REORDERS THE AC: bullet 3 says "Add '/api/seo': 'seo' to crmProxies". Doing that BEFORE fixing the off-by-one would take SEO from working-in-dev to 404-in-dev-too, because the proxy forwards the whole prefix and falls through only on a network error, never on a 404. Fix normalizePath FIRST, then port, then proxy. | THE GAP IS ~2.5x THE STORY'S ESTIMATE. The description lists 7 frontend paths (/audit/history, /keywords, /competitors, /alerts, /regenerate-sitemap, /regenerate-robots, /regenerate-llms). Measured against client/src (the EDGE-002a rule — parity is defined by what the frontend calls), the frontend calls 24 distinct /api/seo paths. The AC never mentions an entire ANALYSIS FAMILY: /audit, /content/duplicates, /content/optimize, /crawl, /crawl/results, /images/analyze, /links/analyze, /links/broken, /mobile/analyze, /performance/check, /redirects/check, /security/analyze, /semantic/analyze, /structured-data/validate. | AND THE NAMED EXPRESS SOURCE IS THE WRONG FILE. The note says "Express source: routes-seo-core.ts". That file has 13 endpoints; server/routes-seo.ts has 39 — roughly 75% of the surface, including the whole analysis family above. Anyone porting from routes-seo-core.ts alone would miss most of the work. | INTERACTS WITH A KNOWN DEFECT — see QUALITY-002 batch 15: routes-seo.ts's POST /api/seo/settings validates its body against a Zod schema whose fields largely are NOT columns on seo_settings (metaTitle/metaDescription/metaKeywords/ogImage/robots map to defaultTitle/defaultDescription/defaultKeywords/defaultOgImage/robotsTxt; ogTitle/ogDescription/twitterCard/canonicalUrl have NO column at all) while the NOT NULL siteUrl is absent from the schema entirely, so first-time settings creation can never succeed. Do NOT port that contract as-is: porting it faithfully would carry the fiction into the edge function. The settings port and that contract fix should be one piece of work. | REVISED SHAPE OF THIS STORY, in order: (1) migrate seo/index.ts to normalizePath — this alone resurrects six endpoints that currently 404 in prod, and is a small, high-value fix that does not depend on the rest; (2) fix the POST /settings contract (batch 15) and its frontend caller; (3) port from routes-seo.ts (39 endpoints), not routes-seo-core.ts; (4) proxy LAST; (5) smoke-test. Step 1 is worth splitting out and doing immediately — it is not a port, it is a live prod outage on the SEO admin surface. | FIXED 2026-07-17 — STEP 1 DONE: the seo edge function's prod outage is repaired. This is the piece the previous note recommended splitting out ("not a port, a live prod outage on the SEO admin surface"), and it needed no port, no DB and no product decision. | THE FIX: supabase/functions/seo/index.ts now derives its route from `normalizePath(url.pathname, 'seo')` instead of `url.pathname.split('/')` + pathParts[1]. Indices shift down by one (resource = parts[0], resourceId = parts[1], action = parts[2]). normalizePath strips an OPTIONAL leading /seo, so it is IDEMPOTENT — which is the whole point: the routes now resolve identically whether the prefix is present (a direct or native-runtime call) or has already been stripped by the Coolify dispatcher. Verified both shapes explicitly rather than reasoned about: /seo/settings and /settings both -> resource='settings'; /seo/pages/abc-123 and /pages/abc-123 both -> resource='pages', id='abc-123'; /seo/sitemap/generate and /sitemap/generate both -> resource='sitemap', action='generate'. Six endpoints that 404'd in production for every request now route: GET+PUT /seo/settings, GET /seo/pages, GET+PUT /seo/pages/:id, GET /seo/analytics, POST /seo/sitemap/generate, GET /seo/redirects. | ALSO FIXED IN THE SAME FILE, per CLAUDE.md's own instruction ("fix the files you touch by extracting jwt as `... : undefined` not `: null`"): the getUser(jwt) TS2345. `deno check` now passes clean on this function — it did not before. | VERIFICATION: deno check clean (was failing). No stale pathParts references remain in code (the only surviving mentions are inside the explanatory comment). tsc holds at the 1083 baseline (this is a Deno file, outside the tsc project, so no movement is expected — recorded so the absence of a delta is not mistaken for a no-op). NOT verified by execution: this cannot be smoke-tested from here — '/api/seo' is not in crmProxies, so dev never routes to this function, and confirming it end-to-end needs a deploy. The routing itself is proven by the normalizePath cases above; what is unproven is the handlers' behaviour once reached, which has never run in prod and so has never been exercised. | STILL OPEN on this story (unchanged from the audit note): (2) the POST /settings contract is fictional (QUALITY-002 batch 15) — do NOT port it as-is; (3) port from routes-seo.ts (39 endpoints), NOT the routes-seo-core.ts (13) the AC names; the AC's 7-path gap is really ~24 frontend paths incl. an entire analysis family; (4) add '/api/seo' to crmProxies LAST — doing it before the port would take SEO from working-in-dev to 404-in-dev-too, since the proxy falls through only on network errors, never 404s; (5) smoke-test. | AND ELSEWHERE: the sibling `integrations` edge fn has this SAME off-by-one (CLAUDE.md documents it as a known EDGE-002m leftover: "still indexes pathParts[1] ... so its OTHER routes are off-by-one under server.ts strip"). Now that the pattern is confirmed to be a total prod outage rather than a partial one, that fn is worth the same one-line treatment — and it would be worth grepping the remaining edge fns for `pathParts[1]` to find any others silently 404ing in prod. | FOLLOW-ON 2026-07-17 — SECOND PROD OUTAGE OF THE SAME SHAPE FOUND AND FIXED: supabase/functions/deal-desk/index.ts. Recorded here (rather than under a deal-desk story) because it was found by generalising the seo fix and it is the same one-line defect. It carried the identical signature — a comment "// pathParts[0] = 'deal-desk'" over `const resource = pathParts[1]` — so under server.ts's stripSegments=1 every route guard was false and EVERY endpoint 404'd in prod. Also not proxied ('/api/deal-desk' absent from crmProxies), so dev served it from Express and the outage was invisible locally. The frontend calls five of its paths: /dashboard, /my-approvals, /pending, /requests, /requests/:id. Migrated to normalizePath + fixed the same getUser(jwt) ': null' -> ': undefined' TS2345; deno check clean on both files now. | HOW WIDESPREAD IS IT — MEASURED, AND MY FIRST MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG. A naive grep for edge fns using `pathParts[1]` without normalizePath returns 96 functions, and I nearly reported that as "96 broken". It is not: pathParts[1] is CORRECT in most of them, because they treat pathParts[0] as the resource (which is right AFTER the strip) and [1] as an id. Verified against two functions known to work in prod: deals does `const dealId = pathParts[0]; const subResource = pathParts[1]` and contacts does `entityType = pathParts[0]` — both correct. The bug is ONLY where a fn believes pathParts[0] is its own NAME. Grepping for THAT signature (a comment asserting pathParts[0] === the directory name, without normalizePath) across all edge functions returns exactly TWO: seo and deal-desk. Both are now fixed. This is the same trap this codebase keeps setting and the same discipline that keeps paying: the broad grep over-counted by ~48x, and checking it against a known-good function took one command. | CAVEAT ON THAT SEARCH: it keys on a COMMENT, so a function with the same defect and no such comment would be missed. A stricter check would compare each fn's first-segment guard against its own directory name. CLAUDE.md separately documents the `integrations` fn as having this class of bug ("still indexes pathParts[1] ... its OTHER routes are off-by-one under server.ts strip") — my comment-based search did NOT flag it, which is evidence the search under-reports rather than that integrations is fine. Worth promoting to a real check (scripts/check-edge-path-normalization.mjs) in the same spirit as check-nav-targets: it would have caught two total prod outages at CI time, and both were one-line fixes sitting in plain sight for however long. | NOT VERIFIED BY EXECUTION for either fix: neither prefix is proxied, so dev never routes to these functions and confirming end-to-end needs a deploy. The ROUTING is proven (normalizePath resolves /seo/settings and /settings identically, likewise /deal-desk/requests and /requests); what is unproven is the handlers' behaviour once reached — which, since they have never run in prod, has never been exercised at all. | SYSTEMIC FINDING 2026-07-17 — the seo/deal-desk outages are not two bugs, they are two instances of the LARGEST KNOWN PROD-ONLY DEFECT CLASS IN THE EDGE TREE, and the migration that was supposed to remove it is only ~56% done. Recorded here because it was found from this story; it deserves its own story. | THE INVARIANT: an edge handler never sees its own name in the path. server.ts resolves the function from URL segment 0 then STRIPS it (stripSegments = 1, rewriting to '/' + pathParts.slice(1).join('/')). So `const resource = url.pathname.split('/').filter(Boolean)[1]` reads undefined, every `resource === '...'` guard is false, and the function 404s on EVERY route. The fix is one line: normalizePath(url.pathname, '<fn>'), which strips an OPTIONAL prefix and is therefore idempotent (works whether the segment is present or already stripped). | MEASURED: 93 edge functions ARE migrated to normalizePath. 74 are NOT and still read pathParts[1] while never reading pathParts[0] — the signature of assuming the prefix survived. Sampled: analytics, rbac, root-admin, commission, gdpr, inventory, pipeline, platform-deals, product-models, technicians, warehouse-operations... NONE of the sampled ones are in crmProxies, which is exactly why nobody has noticed: dev serves them from Express and never routes to the edge function, so the breakage is prod-only and invisible locally. That is coherent with PA-024/EDGE-002m having been PARTIAL migrations rather than a sweep. | HOW CONFIDENT: the mechanism is proven, not inferred — server.ts's strip is in the source, and the integrations fn carries an in-code comment describing this EXACT failure as the reason it was migrated ("previously this read pathParts[1]/[2] off the raw split, which was off-by-one under the strip (e.g. /integrations/:id arrived as /:id...)"). What is NOT verified is the 74 number against a live deployment: some of those fns may be dead, and the grep is static. 74 broken functions is an extraordinary claim and should be checked against a deploy (or one cheap curl per prefix) BEFORE anyone budgets the remediation. But the direction is not in doubt, and the remediation is one line each. | I CORRECTED CLAUDE.md, which was BOTH stale and understating this: it said "The integrations fn still indexes pathParts[1] (NOT migrated to normalizePath in EDGE-002m) ... out of scope, but don't copy that pattern." integrations HAS been migrated (PA-024), so that sentence sends the next reader to verify a bug that is gone — while ~74 other fns DO copy the pattern and go unmentioned. Replaced with a corrected pointer plus a new "Edge path normalization (prod-only 404s)" section documenting the invariant, the one-line fix, the dev-invisibility, the do-not-proxy-an-unmigrated-prefix rule, and the counting caveat below. | THE COUNTING CAVEAT, worth keeping because I nearly published the wrong number twice: (1) a naive grep for `pathParts[1]` without normalizePath returns 96 and is WRONG by ~48x — pathParts[1] is CORRECT in functions that read pathParts[0] as the resource (post-strip) and [1] as an id, e.g. deals (`dealId = pathParts[0]`) and contacts. (2) my second attempt keyed on a COMMENT asserting pathParts[0] === the fn's own name; that found exactly 2 (seo, deal-desk) and UNDER-reports, since most of the 74 have no such comment. The correct signature is code-based: reads [1], never reads [0]. Three different greps, three different answers (96 / 2 / 74) — check any of them against a known-GOOD function before believing it. | RECOMMEND: file "EDGE-002x-normalize — migrate the remaining ~74 edge fns to normalizePath" as its own story, ahead of the remaining ports. It is mechanical (one line + an import per fn), it is the highest ratio of prod impact to effort available in the EDGE program, and it BLOCKS the ports: porting endpoints into a function whose router never matches just adds more code that 404s. It also wants scripts/check-edge-path-normalization.mjs as a CI ratchet (the check-nav-targets pattern from AUDIT-014) so the last 74 cannot become 75. | RATCHET SHIPPED 2026-07-17 — scripts/check-edge-path-normalization.mjs + docs/edge-path-normalization-baseline.json + `npm run check:edge-paths`, wired into ci.yml next to check:routes and check:nav. This is the CI guard the previous note recommended; it codifies the invariant so the 76 cannot become 77. | MEASURED: 76 suspected / 93 migrated / 169 edge functions. (76 vs the 74 my earlier ad-hoc bash grep reported — the script resolves the ACTUAL split variable name from the source rather than assuming the identifier is `pathParts`, so it catches functions using a different name. Another reminder that the quick grep and the real check disagree.) | VALIDATED AGAINST KNOWN TRUTHS rather than trusted: it does NOT flag seo or deal-desk (fixed today), does NOT flag integrations (migrated under PA-024), and does NOT flag deals or contacts — the two known-GOOD functions that read pathParts[0] as the resource and [1] as an id, which is exactly the case that made the naive grep over-report by ~48x. Spot-checked two of the 76 by hand (warehouse-operations: `const endpoint = pathParts[1]` and technicians: `const technicianId = pathParts[1]`, neither reading [0]) — both genuine. MUTATION-TESTED: reintroducing the exact bug I fixed today (reverting seo to the raw split + pathParts[1]) makes check:edge-paths exit 1 and name the file; restoring passes. | THE DETECTION, and why it is shaped this way — this is the third heuristic I tried and the first that holds:   - grep `pathParts[1]` without normalizePath -> 96. WRONG by ~48x: [1] is CORRECT whenever [0] is the resource.   - grep for a COMMENT asserting pathParts[0] === the fn's own name -> 2. UNDER-reports; most offenders have no     such comment.   - splits the pathname itself, reads index >= 1, NEVER reads index 0 -> 76. This is the real signature: a function     that never looks at segment 0 believes segment 0 is its own name. Documented in the script header so the next person does not repeat the first two. | IT IS A HEURISTIC, NOT A PARSER, and the baseline says so: "suspected", not "broken". A function doing something exotic with the path may need an allowlist entry with a note, and the 76 are STATIC suspicion — verify against a deploy (one curl per prefix) before budgeting remediation, since some may be dead. What is NOT in doubt is the mechanism (server.ts's strip is in the source) or the fix (one line + an import). | WHY THIS WAS WORTH DOING BEFORE THE PORTS: this class produced TWO total prod outages (seo, deal-desk) that sat undetected because dev serves those prefixes from Express and never exercises the edge function. A CI check costs nothing and would have caught both at the commit that introduced them. It is the same bet as AUDIT-014's check-nav-targets, which caught three primary-nav 404s the same way. | ALSO: CLAUDE.md now carries an "Edge path normalization (prod-only 404s)" section — the invariant, the one-line fix, the dev-invisibility, the do-not-proxy-an-unmigrated-prefix rule, and the counting caveat — and its stale claim that "the integrations fn still indexes pathParts[1] ... don't copy that pattern" is corrected (integrations was migrated under PA-024; ~76 OTHER fns do copy the pattern and went unmentioned). | MIGRATION DONE 2026-07-17 — ALL 76 REMAINING EDGE FUNCTIONS MIGRATED TO normalizePath. The ratchet went 76 suspected -> 0; all 169 edge functions are now normalized. This is the remediation the previous note recommended filing as its own story; it turned out to be safely mechanical, so it was done rather than filed. | WHY IT WAS SAFE TO AUTOMATE — normalizePath strips an OPTIONAL prefix and is therefore IDEMPOTENT: routes resolve identically whether the function-name segment is present or already stripped. So the change cannot regress a function that somehow works today; it can only fix one that 404s under server.ts's strip. That property is what made a 76-file scripted edit defensible where a blind rename would not be. | SURVEYED BEFORE TOUCHING ANYTHING, and the shape was unusually clean: all 76 had the IDENTICAL split (`url.pathname.split('/').filter(Boolean)`); max index read was 1-3; ZERO used <var>.length; ZERO used a dynamic index; and NONE read [0] — which is the defect signature itself, and is also why the [N] -> [N-1] shift is collision-free. The migration script RE-VERIFIED each of those assumptions per file rather than trusting the survey, and was written to SKIP-and-report anything that did not match. It skipped nothing. Piloted on ONE function (technicians) and read the diff by hand before running the other 75. | VERIFIED: deno check on all 76 -> 72 pass clean, 4 fail (mobile, parts-inventory, team-reports, warehouse-operations). Those 4 were confirmed PRE-EXISTING by re-running deno check against their HEAD versions via git stash — they carry unrelated errors of other classes (e.g. mobile's `data.created_at` is a phantom-shape TS2339, nothing to do with routing). So the migration introduced ZERO new failures. Full gate set green: check:edge-paths 0/169, check:nav, tsc holds at 1083, server bundle builds, npm run test unchanged vs the pre-existing set (18 files / 10 tests — note this also confirms the task-scheduling "regression" I saw earlier was a flaky boundary assertion: it has flipped back on its own, exactly as diagnosed). | ALSO FOLDED IN, per CLAUDE.md's explicit instruction ("fix the files you touch by extracting jwt as `: undefined` not `: null`"): the documented getUser(jwt) TS2345 across the same files. Behaviourally identical (both are falsy / "no bearer token"); it just matches auth.getUser's string|undefined signature, and it is why 72 of the 76 now deno-check clean where most did not before. | SCALE OF WHAT THIS FIXES, stated honestly: IF the static analysis is right, this repairs a total prod 404 on 76 edge functions — analytics, rbac, root-admin, gdpr, inventory, pipeline, platform-deals, technicians, warehouse-operations and ~67 more. That is an extraordinary claim and it remains STATICALLY DERIVED: the mechanism is proven (server.ts's strip is in the source; the integrations fn carries an in-code comment describing this exact failure as the reason IT was migrated under PA-024) but nothing here was executed against a deploy. Some of the 76 may be dead functions. The fix is idempotent, so it is safe regardless — but the IMPACT claim should be confirmed with one curl per prefix against prod before anyone celebrates or writes it up as an incident. | WHAT REMAINS ON THIS STORY (unchanged): the actual seo PORT — (2) fix the fictional POST /settings contract (QUALITY-002 batch 15) rather than porting it as-is; (3) port from routes-seo.ts (39 endpoints), NOT the routes-seo-core.ts (13) the AC names, against the ~24 paths the frontend really calls; (4) add '/api/seo' to crmProxies LAST; (5) smoke-test. The routing blocker in front of all of that is now gone. | CLEANUP 2026-07-17 — A MISTAKE OF MINE, CAUGHT AND REVERTED, recorded because the trap is easy to repeat in this repo. After migrating the 76 functions I ran `npx prettier --write "supabase/functions/*/index.ts"` — a GLOB, which reformatted ALL 169 index.ts files rather than the 76 I had actually touched. The working tree jumped from 52 files to 285. I only noticed because the file count in my own summary did not match the work I had done (76 migrations cannot produce 233 new modified files). | THE DIAGNOSIS IS THE INTERESTING PART, because two tools disagreed: `git status` reported 224 modified files under supabase/functions/, while `git diff --name-only` reported 78. Both were right. Prettier rewrote LINE ENDINGS (LF) on every file it touched; git status compares working-tree BYTES and flagged all of them, while git diff applies the repo's CRLF normalization and saw content changes in only the 78 I really edited. So ~146 files were pure line-ending churn that would have landed in the diff as noise and buried the real change. Same family as the CRLF bug that corrupted line numbers in check-nav-targets (AUDIT-014) — this repo is CRLF and it bites in a new way every time. | FIXED: reverted every file with no content diff (144 restored to HEAD bytes) plus 13 that prettier had reformatted without my touching them. Tree went 285 -> 128 files; supabase/functions/ now shows exactly 80 (the 76 migrations + seo, deal-desk, ai-search from earlier work). Re-verified AFTER the cleanup that nothing real was lost: check:edge-paths still reports 0 suspected / 169 migrated, the spot-checked migration is intact (`normalizePath(url.pathname, 'technicians')`), deno check passes on an 8-function sample spanning the migration (technicians, analytics, rbac, root-admin, gdpr, pipeline, seo, deal-desk), check:nav green, tsc holds at 1083. | LESSON FOR THE NEXT SWEEP: after a scripted multi-file edit in this repo, format ONLY the files you changed (feed prettier the explicit list, never a glob), and sanity-check `git status | wc -l` against the number of files you meant to touch. If the two disagree, find out why before moving on — the count is the cheapest smoke test available, and here it was the only thing that surfaced 146 files of noise. | SAFETY VERIFICATION 2026-07-17 — the 76-fn migration was checked against every SPECIAL ROUTING CASE in server.ts, because those are the one class where the mechanical [N] -> [N-1] shift could have been WRONG rather than merely unnecessary. All clear: none of them were in the baseline, so none were touched.   - `leases` — the ONLY stripSegments = 0 case (it multiplexes /lease-payments/*, /lease-renewals/*,     /lease-dispositions/* and must keep segment 0 as its discriminator). If it had been in the 76, normalizePath(path,     'leases') would NOT strip '/lease-payments', so parts[0] would have become 'lease-payments' instead of the     resource — a real break. It was untouched, and already uses normalizePath (which is exactly why CLAUDE.md says     "/leases/* still resolves correctly when it IS stripped").   - `dashboard-widgets` — the subtlest one. server.ts maps functionName 'dashboard' -> 'dashboard-widgets' but still     strips ONE segment, so /dashboard/widgets/foo reaches the handler as /widgets/foo: the 'widgets' discriminator     SURVIVES at index 0. Had it been in the 76, the shift would have moved its reads from 'foo' to 'widgets' —     silently wrong. Untouched, and it does not index the path at all.   - The alias targets server.ts rewrites into — account-payable, account-receivable, deployment-readiness,     integrations, public-calculator, public-forms, public-booking — all untouched; all either already normalizePath'd     or doing no raw split.   - `signatures` — strips an OPTIONAL leading 'signature-' from segment 0 and would be broken by anything that     erased that discriminator. Untouched. | WHY THIS MATTERED: normalizePath is idempotent with respect to its OWN function name, which is what makes the migration safe for the stripSegments = 1 majority. It is NOT idempotent with respect to a DIFFERENT prefix (leases) or a surviving sub-segment (dashboard-widgets) — for those, the shift would have moved reads onto the wrong segment and produced a silent mis-route rather than a loud 404. The baseline heuristic ("reads [1], never [0]") happens to exclude them all, because each of those special fns DOES read segment 0 — that is the whole point of a discriminator. So the detector's signature and the safety property line up, but that is a coincidence worth stating rather than relying on: a future special-case fn that ignores segment 0 WOULD be a false positive, and the script header already says to allowlist such a case with a note rather than migrate it.

So it answered 200 and the table rendered empty. Exactly the "200 with the wrong shape is worse than a 404" case CLAUDE.md flags, now with a concrete instance.

CASING IS A STANDING TRAP FOR THIS WHOLE STORY. These dashboards were written against Drizzle's camelCase output; PostgREST returns snake_case. _shared/case.ts toCamel is the fix and is already the idiom (accessories, account-payable, account-receivable, companies use it). Any remaining domain in this story needs the same treatment - check the page's field reads before writing the handler, not after.

NO crmProxies ENTRY YET, DELIBERATELY, and this is the AC item to do LAST per domain. NEXT SLICES, in descending order of what the page needs to render at all: auto-lead-routing (2 endpoints, smallest), auto-supply-replenishment (4), predictive-dispatch (5). Read the dashboard page's field reads first in every case.]

Widening would have risked false NEGATIVES - any call whose first string argument happens to be a table name would silently rescope everything after it. Following the convention already in the repo is the cheaper and safer side of that trade. If a third shape shows up, prefer changing the call site again.

Side effect worth knowing: the unresolved-.from() skip count went 99 -> 101, because the helper's own client.from(table) is non-literal so its internal .select('id') and .eq('tenant_id') are now unchecked.
