NAMED-VARIABLE BLIND SPOT HANDLED EXPLICITLY. The renewal_proposals insert spreads a built row (`...proposalRow`), which is precisely what check:phantom-cols cannot see - the blind spot documented at the top of the checker and hit five times in the COP-M01 rounds. So I verified the 31 emitted columns against the real table PROGRAMMATICALLY (parse the row builder's return literal, diff against getTableConfig) rather than reading them. All 31 exist, plus tenant_id and contract_renewal_tracking_id which the handler adds. WORTH REUSING: when a payload is a named variable, a 10-line script diffing its keys against getTableConfig is better evidence than a careful read, and it takes about a minute.

Also pinned the analysis write-back timestamps to the single `now` captured at the top of the run rather than calling new Date() per row, so one invocation stamps consistently.

EDGE-002g REMAINING: (1) predictive-dispatch analysis - a SCHEMA story (service_calls_enhanced / equipment_metrics / technician_resources_enhanced exist in no schema or migration), recommended for the third time to be SPLIT OUT rather than left blocking this story; (2) the four crmProxies entries + the AC's smoke test, needing a deployed environment. If (1) is split out, (2) is the only thing left, and it is a single change someone with deploy access can make in minutes.]
PROGRESS 2026-08-29 - AUTO-LEAD-ROUTING: the domain is worse than "missing endpoints", and the order of the remaining ACs matters.

WHAT THE PAGE ACTUALLY GETS. AutoLeadRoutingDashboard.tsx (routed at /auto-lead-routing) calls /dashboard, /config GET+PUT and POST /route/:leadId. All four are now served by supabase/functions/auto-lead-routing/ - the EDGE-002g port for this domain landed. /dashboard and /config are sound: /config persists to tenants.metadata.autoLeadRouting, which is strictly better than Express, whose PUT logs the body, answers "Configuration updated" and stores nothing.

THE ROUTING HALF CANNOT WORK IN PRODUCTION. Every rules query in that function reads lead_routing_rules, and that relation is named by NOTHING else in this repository: no pgTable in shared/, no CREATE TABLE in drizzle/, no server code, no seeder, no script. One file in the whole tree mentions it, and it is the function itself. Unless it exists as untracked db:push drift, POST /route/:leadId gets 42P01, and PostgREST reports that by leaving .data null rather than throwing.

WHAT THAT LOOKED LIKE TO A USER. GET /rules answered the error with TWO HARDCODED SAMPLE RULES - "Enterprise Leads" and "SMB Leads", with conditions and priorities - at status 200. So the routing UI listed rules that did not exist, could not be edited, and matched nothing. POST /route answered `{ routed: false, error: "No matching routing rule found" }`, also 200, which reads as "this tenant has not configured routing yet" rather than "the table has never existed". FIXED: both now return 503 ROUTING_RULES_UNAVAILABLE naming the relation, via the new _shared/postgrest-errors.ts predicate.

TWO MORE THINGS FIXED WHILE IN THERE. The rule chosen by POST /route was `for (const rule of rules) { matchedRule = rule; break; }` - a loop that always takes the first row, with the comment "In production, implement proper condition matching". rule.conditions was never evaluated. It is now an explicit index with the response carrying conditionsEvaluated: false, so no caller can read a routed lead as having qualified. The isMissingTableError predicate had been copied into billing/handlers/_context.ts and customer-portal/handlers/_context.ts; both now re-export one definition, covered by server/tests/unit/postgrest-errors.test.ts.

DO NOT ADD /api/auto-lead-routing TO crmProxies YET, even though this story's fifth AC says to. It is not in there today, so dev serves the domain from server/routes-auto-lead-routing.ts, and that Express path is the ONLY working routing implementation: it drives auto-lead-routing-service.ts, which scores the lead and scores every rep against it (585 loc, real tables). Proxying now would replace a working dev feature with the 503 above. Correct order: give production a routing engine first - either create lead_routing_rules with a migration and implement condition matching, or port the scoring service to the edge function - THEN proxy, so dev and prod agree. Endpoints Express has and the edge function does not (/route-batch, /preview/:leadId) have no caller in any client tree, so they cost nothing in that move.

GUARD ADDED. scripts/check-phantom-tables.mjs already hard-gated "undeclared table queried by a function that swallows 42P01/PGRST205". Neither of the two real instances tripped it, because neither tested the error code - they wrote `if (error) {` and returned invented rows. A second hard rule at zero now catches an error branch that returns an array-of-objects literal. Mutation-tested against both: reverting either fix fails the check.

userStories.notes:
Bundled because each is a small surface gap (1-3 endpoints). Could be split per domain if a sub-team picks them up. [AUDIT DONE + FIRST DOMAIN 2026-08-20. AC1 asks for a per-domain audit of frontend caller URLs vs edge endpoints, so I scripted one over all sixteen. RESULT (called sub-paths vs served, first segment only):
  commission                MISSING analytics, calculate, disputes
  gdpr                      MISSING deduplication, dpa
  manufacturer-integrations MISSING audit-logs, stats
  oid-mappings              MISSING export, import, test  (manufacturers is a FALSE POSITIVE - served)
  performance               MISSING alerts, health, metrics  (fn has NO endpoint comparisons at all - look before trusting)
  products                  MISSING all

  remote-monitoring         MISSING acknowledge-alert, equipment-status, fleet-overview, sensor-data

TWO FALSE POSITIVES IN SIXTEEN, both from the same cause: the audit greps for `endpoint === 'x'` style comparisons, and functions that route on a differently named variable (oid-mappings uses mappingId) or handle a path BEFORE the dispatch (supplies /import) look unserved. TREAT THE LIST AS A STARTING POINT, NOT A VERDICT - grep the actual function before porting anything.

REMOTE-MONITORING DONE. /acknowledge-alert is backed and now served (acknowledged_at + acknowledged_by; device_alerts records acknowledgement as a TIMESTAMP not a boolean - same correction the /alerts filters needed in COP-M01 round 17). The page also sends acknowledgmentNote, which has no column, so it is reported.

THE OTHER THREE ARE A SCHEMA GAP, NOT A PORTING GAP - same class as EDGE-002g-remainder, and the second page in this codebase found to be typed entirely against a mock. RemoteMonitoring.tsx declares location.floor, location.coordinates, currentMetrics.pagesPerMinute/temperature/humidity/jamCount/lastJobCompleted, a whole performance block (utilizationRate, efficiency, averageJobSize, peakUsageHour) and a maintenance block (nextScheduled, lastCompleted, maintenanceScore, predictiveAlerts[].estimatedLife); SensorData wants temperature and powerConsumption TIME SERIES plus next7/30/90-day failure probabilities. monitored_devices and device_metrics carry NONE of it - real columns are toner_levels, paper_levels, error_codes, response_time, uptime, total_impressions, last_seen, consecutive_failures.

TWO REASONS A PARTIAL SHAPE IS WORSE THAN A 404 HERE, the first of which is new and worth generalising:
  (1) THE CONSUMER'S OWN TRANSFORM CAN CRASH. RemoteMonitoring.tsx passes a `select` to useQuery that does equipment.currentMetrics.lastJobCompleted and equipment.maintenance.predictiveAlerts.map() with NO guards. A response missing those nested objects throws a TypeError and takes the page down. A 404/501 does not: equipmentStatus defaults to [] and fleetOverview/sensorData are guarded at every use. SO: BEFORE SERVING A PARTIAL SHAPE, READ THE CONSUMER'S select/transform, NOT JUST ITS RENDER. A page can be more fragile to bad data than to no data.
  (2) Zeros would be actively misleading - the fuserLife trap from EDGE-002g slice 4. uptime 0, maintenanceScore 0, tonerLevels.black 0 all read as critical conditions.
The 501 (MONITORING_SHAPE_NEEDS_SCHEMA) enumerates the unbacked fields so the next person has the list without re-deriving it.

NEXT: the remaining ten domains with real gaps. Suggest checking each for the mock-shape pattern FIRST - two of sixteen pages so far have turned out to be typed against schemas that do not exist, and that changes the work from a port into a schema story.]
[DOMAIN 2 DONE 2026-08-20: commission. All three gaps closed, and each turned out to be a DIFFERENT kind of gap - worth recording because it means "missing endpoint" is not one problem with one fix.

/analytics - A HARDCODED MOCK ON EXPRESS. routes-commission.ts returns a literal object: "John Smith", totalCommissionPaid 245780, two fixed monthly_trends entries, one fake plan. It never touches the database. This is a THIRD failure mode alongside the two already catalogued (phantom columns on a real table; a page typed against a schema that does not exist): AN ENDPOINT THAT LOOKS IMPLEMENTED AND RETURNS FICTION. Porting it would have put fabricated numbers behind the same URL on a second backend. Computed instead from commission_calculations (total_sales, quota_achievement, gross_commission, total_bonuses, total_adjustments, net_commission, period_name, plan_id, employee_id), commission_disputes, commission_plans and users. All of the mock's shape is derivable except two fields, now in `unbacked`: performance_metrics.tierDistribution (no tier is recorded on commission_plans OR commission_calculations - commission_plan_tiers exists but is per-plan config, not per-calculation) and top_performers[].role (users.role is a SYSTEM role, not a sales role). averageCommissionRate has no column either but IS derivable: gross_commission / total_sales.

/disputes - BROKEN THREE WAYS ON EXPRESS, all in one raw-SQL handler in routes-operations-extended.ts. (1) `u.name` - users has first_name/last_name, the same phantom CLAUDE.md already documents. (2) `WHERE cd.tenantId = $1` and `ORDER BY cd.createdAt` - UNQUOTED CAMELCASE IN RAW SQL, which Postgres FOLDS TO LOWERCASE, so it looks for tenantid and createdat; the columns are tenant_id and created_at. This is a new sub-species worth watching for: the Drizzle-side phantom-column work never sees raw SQL, and camelCase there is silently wrong in a way that looks right. (3) the POST writes dispute_amount / claimed_amount; the columns are disputed_amount / expected_amount. Rewritten against the real columns, joining users and commission_calculations for the employeeName and calculationPeriod the page renders.

/calculate - NO IMPLEMENTATION ANYWHERE. Not on the edge fn, not on Express: it 404s on BOTH backends today, so it is a feature request, not a porting gap. Returns 501 COMMISSION_ENGINE_NOT_BUILT naming the schema that already exists for it: commission_plans + commission_plan_tiers (tiered rates), commission_product_rates (per-product overrides), employee_commission_assignments (who is on which plan), commission_sales_transactions (what to pay on), writing commission_calculations. Someone with the business requirements can build it; guessing the tier maths would have been inventing a payroll rule.

RUNNING TALLY OF WHY AN ENDPOINT IS "MISSING", now four kinds: (a) genuinely never ported, (b) ported but pointed at phantom columns, (c) page typed against a schema that does not exist (remote-monitoring, predictive-dispatch), (d) Express handler returns a hardcoded mock (this one). Check which kind BEFORE writing code - the right output differs completely, and only (a) is a port.

REMAINING DOMAINS with real gaps: gdpr (deduplication, dpa), manufacturer-integrations (audit-logs, stats), oid-mappings (export, import, test), performance (alerts, health, metrics - and that fn has NO endpoint routing at all, so read it first), products (all), purchase-orders (generate-from-suggestions, stats, suggestions), quickbooks (connect, entities), rbac (organizational-units, seed, status), warehouse-operations (stats).]
[DOMAINS 3-4 DONE 2026-08-20: warehouse-operations, manufacturer-integrations. Both were KIND (a) - genuinely never ported, Express handlers real and correct - so these were straight ports. Recording that because after commission and remote-monitoring it would be easy to assume every gap hides a defect. It does not; roughly half are just unported.

TRIAGE STEP THAT MADE THIS FAST, worth reusing on the remaining domains: for each missing endpoint, first ask whether Express has a handler AT ALL (grep "api/<domain>/<endpoint>" over server/), then whether that handler touches the database (/await db|\.select\(|\.from\(|db\.\$client|storage\./). Two greps sort every gap into the four kinds before any code is read. Results for the whole remaining set: gdpr/deduplication, gdpr/dpa and products/all have NO Express handler (kind d - feature, not port); quickbooks/connect has a handler that never touches the DB (kind c - likely mock, verify before porting); manufacturer-integrations, warehouse-operations, rbac/organizational-units and performance/metrics are all DB-backed (kind a).

warehouse-operations/stats: Express pulls EVERY operation row and counts in JS. PostgREST counts server-side, so the port uses ten head-only counts and transfers no rows. Same numbers, less traffic - worth doing rather than mirroring the JS filtering.

manufacturer-integrations/audit-logs: Express does two leftJoins and returns { log, integration, device } per row. PostgREST expresses that as an EMBED (integration:manufacturer_integrations(*), device:device_registrations(*)) on integration_id/device_id - one round trip instead of three. The response shape is preserved by lifting the log's own columns back under `log` after destructuring the embeds out.

FALSE ALARM WORTH RECORDING SO NOBODY RE-RAISES IT: manufacturer-integrations/index.ts reads `const endpoint = parts[1]`, which is the signature CLAUDE.md flags for prod-404s. It is NOT a bug here - the function reads parts[0] as a MANUFACTURER and parts[1] as the sub-resource, which is exactly the legitimate case that note carves out ("CORRECT in functions that read pathParts[0] as the resource and [1] as an id, e.g. deals and contacts"). The new top-level endpoints therefore match on parts[0], not parts[1]. Check which segment the function treats as the resource before believing the grep.

REMAINING (7 domains): gdpr (deduplication, dpa - no Express handler), oid-mappings (export, import, test), performance (alerts, health, metrics - the fn has NO endpoint routing at all, read it first), products (all - no Express handler), purchase-orders (generate-from-suggestions, stats, suggestions), quickbooks (connect, entities - connect never touches the DB), rbac (organizational-units, seed, status).]
[DOMAINS 5-6 DONE 2026-08-20: rbac, purchase-orders.

/rbac/organizational-units - SECOND SIGHTING OF THE RAW-SQL CASING BUG, and it is worth treating as a pattern now rather than a coincidence. Express does `SELECT * FROM organizational_units` (raw SQL, so snake_case rows) and then builds the tree with `nodes.filter(node => node.parentUnitId === parentId)`. parentUnitId is undefined on every row because the column is parent_unit_id, so nothing ever matches a parent and `hierarchy` COMES BACK EMPTY on every call - silently, with a 200. The commission/disputes bug last round was the mirror image: camelCase inside the SQL string. THE GENERAL SHAPE IS: raw SQL returns snake_case, the JS around it was written as if Drizzle had mapped it, and nothing errors. Grep for `.rows` / `SELECT *` followed by camelCase property access. Fixed here by filtering on parent_unit_id; ordering by lft, which is the nested-set left bound and therefore already the tree order.

/rbac/status is the page gate - RoleManagement.tsx shows a setup prompt when initialized is false and the manager when true - so it needed to be right before anything else in that page mattered. Two head-only counts.

/purchase-orders/stats/summary: Express fetches every PO and runs six .filter() passes plus two .reduce()s in JS. Counts are server-side here; only status+total_amount come back for the two money totals, since SUM has no PostgREST equivalent. Third domain in a row where the Express version pulls whole tables to count them - it is a consistent enough habit that it is worth checking for on every remaining port.

/rbac/seed DEFERRED ON PURPOSE (501 RBAC_SEED_NOT_PORTED). ~160 lines creating the default organizational unit plus a per-dealerType role set with hierarchy_level and department on each role. Mechanical, but it DEFINES WHAT PERMISSIONS A TENANT'S ROLES CARRY - a transcription slip hands someone the wrong access, which is the one category of error worth spending a whole round avoiding. It is also one-time initialisation that still runs through Express in dev, so deferring costs nothing today. When someone does it, diff the ported role list against the Express literal rather than reading it twice.

REMAINING (5 domains): gdpr (deduplication, dpa - NO Express handler, so feature not port), oid-mappings (export, import, test), performance (alerts, health, metrics - fn has NO endpoint routing at all, read it before assuming), products (all - NO Express handler), quickbooks (connect never touches the DB, entities unknown).]
[DOMAIN 7 DONE 2026-08-20: performance. THE WIDEST BLAST RADIUS IN THIS STORY SO FAR - this function feeds SystemAlertBell, which sits in the app chrome on EVERY page.

THIRD AUDIT FALSE POSITIVE, same cause as the first two: the function routes with `switch (endpoint)`, not `endpoint === '...'`, so my regex saw zero served endpoints. Three false positives in sixteen domains, ALL from assuming one routing idiom. If that audit is ever turned into a committed script, match on the segment being compared rather than the comparison syntax - or better, list what the function CANNOT serve by driving it, not by grepping it.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY DID WAS WORSE THAN MISSING THE ENDPOINTS. /metrics returned a hardcoded object (responseTime 185, throughput 1250, errorRate 0.5, uptime 99.95, memoryUsage 62, cpuUsage 45, diskUsage 38, activeUsers 24) with a comment saying a real version would read monitoring tables. /alerts returned ONE literal alert: {type:'info', message:'System running normally', resolved:false}. Two consequences, and the second is the bad one: (1) SystemAlertBell renders alerts.length as its badge, so every page carried a permanent red "1"; (2) because that single literal was ALL that was ever returned, NO GENUINE ALERT COULD EVER REACH THE BELL. A mock that returns "everything is fine" is not a placeholder, it is a suppressed alarm.

BOTH TABLES ALREADY EXISTED AND MATCHED. system_alerts has type, category, message, severity, resolved, expires_at, created_at - i.e. exactly the fields SystemAlertBell (severity/type/message) and PageAlerts (category/severity) filter on. performance_metrics has metric_type, value, unit, endpoint, timestamp. So this was never a schema gap like remote-monitoring; someone stubbed it and the stub outlived the tables. WORTH CHECKING ELSEWHERE: a "// In a real implementation, you'd fetch this from ..." comment is a strong signal the table now exists - grep the edge tree for that phrasing.

/alerts now returns open, unexpired alerts newest first, exposing created_at as the `timestamp` both components read. /metrics returns the latest value per metric_type; a type with NO rows lands in `unreported` rather than getting a plausible number - important here because a fabricated uptime is exactly what this endpoint was already doing wrong. /health was genuinely unserved (not in the switch, fell through to 404) while PerformanceMonitoring.tsx called it; derived now from the same two tables - critical open alerts -> critical, any open alert -> degraded, else healthy.

ONE UNBACKED FIELD REPORTED, NOT FAKED: PageAlerts filters on a.page when given a pageKey, and system_alerts has no page column (source is the nearest, but means the emitting system). That filter therefore matches nothing; noted rather than mapped onto source, which would silently change which alerts a page shows.

REMAINING (4 domains): gdpr (deduplication, dpa - NO Express handler), oid-mappings (export, import, test), products (all - NO Express handler), quickbooks (connect never touches the DB, entities unknown).]
[DOMAINS 8-9 DONE 2026-08-20: products, oid-mappings. A FIFTH KIND OF GAP appeared here, distinct from the four already catalogued.

/products/all - kind (d), no handler on EITHER backend. THE SHAPE IS THE WHOLE STORY: PricingManagement.tsx does `(response || []).map(...)` and reads product.productName, so it needs a FLAT camelCase ARRAY. The sibling /products/with-pricing, in the SAME edge function, returns { data, total } with snake_case rows. Two endpoints on one function with opposite envelopes and opposite casing - copying the neighbour would have produced a page that renders nothing. Read the caller, never the sibling. productName resolves differently per source table too: product_models/software_products use product_name, product_accessories uses accessory_name, enabled_products uses custom_name.

/oid-mappings/export and /import are straightforward. /import is /bulk plus an overwriteExisting flag; the replace is an explicit DELETE-then-insert rather than an upsert because this table has NO UNIQUE KEY to conflict on (round 15 removed a bogus onConflict:'oid' for the same reason), and it is scoped to is_custom so shipped presets survive - consistent with the update/delete guards added in round 15.

/oid-mappings/test IS THE FIFTH KIND: NOT A DATA PROBLEM, A CAPABILITY PROBLEM. The page posts { ipAddress, oids, snmpCommunity, snmpVersion } and expects each OID polled. That is an SNMP request over UDP PORT 161 to a device INSIDE THE CUSTOMER'S NETWORK. Edge functions have outbound HTTP(S) only, and that host is not internet-routable regardless. No amount of schema or porting fixes this - the on-prem agent (printyx-client) is the only component that can poll it. Returns 501 SNMP_REQUIRES_LOCAL_AGENT.
Worth noting WHY faking it would be especially bad here: the page reports "N/M OIDs successful (X%)" and a technician acts on that number when commissioning a device. A fabricated success rate is a field-service decision made on fiction.

RUNNING TALLY, NOW FIVE KINDS OF "MISSING ENDPOINT": (a) genuinely never ported; (b) ported but pointed at phantom columns; (c) page typed against a schema that does not exist (remote-monitoring, predictive-dispatch); (d) handler exists and returns a hardcoded mock (commission/analytics on Express, performance/metrics+alerts on the EDGE side); (e) the runtime cannot do it at all (SNMP here; raw SQL / Postgres catalogs in root-admin). Only (a) is a port. Identify the kind before writing code - the right output differs completely, and three of the five are "do not implement this here".

REMAINING (2 domains): gdpr (/deduplication/stats, /dpa/stats - NO Express handler, so check whether the tables exist before assuming it is buildable), quickbooks (/connect - handler exists but never touches the DB, so likely a mock or an OAuth redirect; /entities - unknown).]
[DOMAINS 10-11 DONE 2026-08-20: gdpr, quickbooks. STORY STATUS: 15 of 16 domains have every endpoint their pages call; purchase-orders has 1 of 3 (stats done, suggestions and generate-from-suggestions still genuinely unserved).

/gdpr/dpa/stats and /gdpr/deduplication/stats: kind (d) - no handler on EITHER backend, so features rather than ports - but both computable from tables that were already there. data_processing_agreements + dpa_compliance_checks cover totalDpas / byStatus / expiringIn / pendingCompliance; duplicate_matches covers totalMatches / pendingMatches / mergedRecords. ONE MODELLING NOTE: mergedRecords counts rows where merged_record_id IS NOT NULL rather than a status value, because that column is what actually records a merge having happened - a status of "merged" would be a second source of truth for the same fact.

/quickbooks/connect IS A SECURITY-CONTROL CASE, and it is the second one in this story family after root-admin/execute-query. It generates a CSRF `state`, stores it in req.session as qb_oauth_state, and /api/quickbooks/callback verifies Intuit's returned state against THAT SESSION VALUE (routes-quickbooks-integration.ts:67). Serving the initiator from an edge function does not break loudly - the callback still runs, still compares, and compares against nothing. IT QUIETLY STOPS PROTECTING ANYTHING. qb_refresh_token lives in the same session, so the whole token lifecycle is host-bound. Porting requires moving OAuth state and tokens into a table, which is a redesign of the credential flow and should be decided on purpose, not absorbed into a migration story. Returns 501 OAUTH_STATE_IS_SESSION_BOUND.
GENERAL RULE THIS AND execute-query BOTH POINT AT: before porting an endpoint, ask what SECURITY PROPERTY the current host provides. Session-bound CSRF state and a READ ONLY transaction are both invisible in the handler's own code and both silently lost on the other runtime.

/quickbooks/entities is a static capability list (configuration, not data), kept in step with server/quickbooks-mapping.ts.

THE AUDIT SCRIPT'S FINAL SCORE, worth recording before anyone reuses it: re-running it after all this work still reports FIVE domains as having missing endpoints, and ALL FIVE ARE FALSE POSITIVES - oid-mappings routes on mappingId, performance on switch(endpoint), manufacturer-integrations on a `manufacturer` segment, supplies handles /import before the dispatch, purchase-orders matches poId === 'stats'. That is 5 false positives out of 16 domains, ~31%, all from one cause: matching the COMPARISON SYNTAX rather than the compared VALUE. If this is ever committed as a check, either match on the string literals a function contains regardless of how it compares them, or drive the function and observe. As it stands it is a lead generator that must be confirmed by reading the function - which is how every domain in this story was actually handled.

REMAINING FOR EDGE-002h: purchase-orders /suggestions/low-stock and /generate-from-suggestions (Express source is server/routes-products-crud.ts:1174 and :1239), then the crmProxies entries + smoke test, which need a deployed environment. NOTE the same caveat root-admin has: any prefix where some endpoints legitimately stay on Express (quickbooks/connect here) cannot take a blanket proxy entry.]
[DOMAIN 12 DONE 2026-08-20: purchase-orders. ALL SIXTEEN DOMAINS NOW SERVE EVERY ENDPOINT THEIR PAGES CALL. What remains for this story is the crmProxies entries + the AC's smoke test, which need a deployed environment.

/suggestions/low-stock was ANOTHER un-portable source. Express selects inventoryItems.currentStock and inventoryItems.supplier; there is exactly ONE inventory_items definition in shared/ and it has NEITHER field, so those are tsc errors (part of the 1003 baseline), and the handler's raw WHERE names current_stock and supplier for the same reason, which is a 42703. The endpoint has been failing wherever it was reachable. Real columns: quantity_on_hand, primary_vendor.
ALSO WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN COPYING: Express aliases quantityOnOrder -> currentStock and reorderQuantity -> reorderPoint, i.e. two fields standing in for values the table records SEPARATELY (quantity_on_order, reorder_quantity both exist). The consequence is that Express's recommendedQty is the item's REORDER POINT, not its reorder quantity - it would order enough to reach the trigger level, not enough to restock. Fixed here; that is a behavioural difference worth knowing about if anyone compares outputs.

POSTGREST CONSTRAINT WORTH RECORDING: it CANNOT COMPARE TWO COLUMNS. `current_stock <= reorder_point` has no filter equivalent, so the query narrows on what it can express (reorder_point IS NOT NULL, > 0, primary_vendor IS NOT NULL) and the comparison happens in the handler. Same class as the SUM/AVG/GROUP BY/count(DISTINCT) limitation but a different axis - worth checking for whenever an Express WHERE mentions two column names. (daily-briefing's inventory shortage check hit this too and already does it in JS with a comment.)

/generate-from-suggestions: one draft PO per vendor group plus line items. Groups with no resolved vendorId are SKIPPED rather than written, as Express does - inventory_items records the vendor by NAME only, so a group whose name matches no vendors row has nothing to point a PO at. Difference from Express: the response NAMES what was skipped (skipped[] + skippedReason) instead of just returning a smaller created count, so a user who expected four POs and got two can see why.

EDGE-002h SUMMARY, all twelve domains that had real gaps: remote-monitoring (1 served, 3 refused - mock-shaped page), commission (2 rebuilt, 1 refused - Express returned a hardcoded mock), warehouse-operations (1), manufacturer-integrations (2), rbac (2 served, 1 deferred - seed defines permissions), purchase-orders (3), performance (3 - Express-side mock that was suppressing real alerts), products (1 - opposite envelope to its sibling), oid-mappings (2 served, 1 refused - SNMP needs the local agent), gdpr (2 - features, not ports), quickbooks (1 served, 1 refused - session-bound OAuth state). Four domains (equipment, parts-orders, platform-deals, social-media) had no gap at all.
OF THE ~24 ENDPOINTS TOUCHED, ROUGHLY HALF WERE NOT PORTS: 7 refused or deferred on principle, and at least 6 were rewrites of Express handlers that could not run. If this story-family gets extended to more domains, budget for that ratio rather than assuming a port per endpoint.]

userStories.notes:
Lower priority than the audit-log/audit-logs split because these child functions weren't broken — they just create deployment overhead and code duplication. Deferred from EDGE-006. | PROGRESS 2026-07-17 — AC BULLET 1 (the load-bearing check) DONE, AND THE STORY IS MOSTLY ALREADY IMPLEMENTED. No code changed; this is the analysis that makes the rest executable, and it changes the shape of the job substantially. | THE LOAD-BEARING CHECK PASSES, WITH A CAVEAT THE AC MISSES. Nothing pins the child function names: the Coolify dispatcher (supabase/functions/server.ts) builds its registry DYNAMICALLY via `Deno.readDir('/app/functions')`, and supabase/config.toml contains no entry for any of them (the only other hits repo-wide are generated audit-reports/*.json artifacts, not manifests). BUT the AC's framing — "verify the manifest doesn't pin the child names, deletion would break URL routing if it enumerates them" — is necessary and NOT sufficient, because of exactly HOW that dynamic registration works: the dispatcher keys on the FIRST URL SEGMENT and looks up a directory of that name, so THE DIRECTORY NAME *IS* THE MANIFEST. /lead-assignment-rules/* resolves only because a dir called lead-assignment-rules exists. Deleting the dirs breaks those URLs whether or not any manifest lists them. There is no manifest to check — the filesystem is the manifest. | THE CONSOLIDATION IS ALREADY WRITTEN IN BOTH PARENTS — AC bullet 2 is largely done and the story does not know it:   - tasks/ already has handlers/bulk.ts, handlers/comments.ts and handlers/stats.ts, and index.ts:84-90 dispatches     them (`if (first === 'stats') ... else if (first === 'bulk') ... else if (parts[1] === 'comments')`). The four     child dirs (tasks-bulk 119 lines, tasks-enhanced 134, tasks-stats 100, task-comments 171) are superseded     duplicates, not code awaiting a port.   - lead-assignment/index.ts:49-53 goes further and already carries an explicit PREFIX TABLE for its children:     { prefix: '/lead-assignment-rules', handler: 'rules' }, { prefix: '/lead-assignment-history', handler: 'history' },     { prefix: '/user-assignments', handler: 'history' }, { prefix: '/lead-assignment-queue', handler: 'queue' },     with matching `case 'rules'/'history'/'queue'` branches. That is precisely the multiplexing pattern CLAUDE.md     documents for the `leases` fn (/lease-payments/*, /lease-renewals/* -> leases with stripSegments = 0). | ...AND THAT PREFIX TABLE IS CURRENTLY DEAD CODE. server.ts has NO alias for any child prefix (grepped: zero hits for lead-assignment*/tasks-*/task-comments/user-assignments). So today /lead-assignment-rules/* routes by directory name to the CHILD fn, and the parent's prefix table can never fire — it was written in ANTICIPATION of this consolidation and has been sitting unreachable ever since. Whoever finishes this must add the server.ts aliases with stripSegments = 0 (the leases precedent, and for the same documented reason: the discriminator IS segment 0, so stripping it would leave the parent unable to tell /lead-assignment-rules from /lead-assignment-queue). NOTE the tasks family needs different handling from lead-assignment: the tasks parent dispatches bulk/stats/comments as SUB-paths (first === 'stats'), not as prefixes, so /tasks-bulk/* would need a path REWRITE to /tasks/bulk/*, not just a stripSegments=0 alias. | THE FINDING THAT MAY COLLAPSE THE WHOLE STORY: NOTHING CALLS THE CHILD PREFIXES. Grepped client/, server/ and mobile/ for every child prefix — the frontend calls ONLY /api/tasks (57 sites, sub-paths: /, /:id, /ai-schedule, /stats — all of which the tasks PARENT already serves and which are already proxied via crmProxies '/api/tasks': 'tasks'). It calls /api/lead-assignment-* and /api/tasks-bulk|enhanced|stats and /api/task-comments ZERO times. The only repo-wide references are Express route DEFINITIONS in server/routes-lead-assignment.ts (which serves /api/lead-assignment-rules etc. and is NOT proxied). So the child edge functions may have no caller at all, in which case the honest job is not "port then delete" but "confirm the surface is dead, then delete the child dirs AND the unreachable parent prefix table AND decide what to do with the Express routes" — a smaller and different story than the one written. VERIFY BEFORE DELETING: my grep covered client/server/mobile in this repo only; if any external consumer (a partner integration, a saved Postman collection, an ops script) calls functions.printyx.net/lead-assignment-rules/* directly, deleting the dir 404s it silently. That is the one thing I could not establish from inside the repo. | NOT DONE: bullets 2 (the residual port + the server.ts aliases), 3 (proxy — note NONE of the child prefixes are currently proxied, only '/api/tasks'), 4 (deletion), 5 (smoke test), 6 (check/build). Bullet 5's smoke test needs a deployed function; bullets 2-4 are safe to do in one focused diff once the "is the surface dead?" question above is answered.
PROGRESS 2026-08-29 - THE CONSOLIDATION LANDED AND WAS NEVER PLUGGED IN, and the frontend half changes what the story is for.

PR 1 SHIPPED, PR 2 NEVER DID, AND PR 1's PRECONDITION WAS NEVER MET. supabase/functions/lead-assignment/ is a complete dispatcher - 652 loc across index.ts, _engine.ts, _territory.ts and _context.ts, plus all seven handlers (territories, rules, capacity, history, queue, assign, routing). Its PREFIX_MAP carries the nine child prefixes. docs/lead-assignment-parity.md says "frontend paths stay unchanged; Cloudflare/Supabase router fans out to the canonical edge function based on prefix". That fan-out does not exist. Checked all four invocation paths: no client tree names /api/lead-assignment, there is no crmProxies entry, supabase/functions/server.ts has no override mapping any of the nine segments onto it, and no drizzle/cron/*.sql posts to it. Nothing can reach the canonical function. The nine children it was written to replace are still the directories that serve, which is why AC bullet 4 was never safe to run.

THE MECHANICS OF THE MISSING WIRE, for whoever does it. server.ts strips segment 0 before invoking a handler, but this dispatcher matches on the prefix it would strip - stripKnownPrefix reads '/sales-territories' out of the pathname. So a plain server.ts alias breaks it; each of the nine segments needs stripSegments = 0, the pattern already used for lease-payments, kpis, reporting and ai-employees.

BEFORE WIRING ANYTHING, NOTE WHO CALLS THESE. Of the ten directories, NINE have no caller in any client tree: assign-lead, lead-assignment, lead-assignment-history, lead-assignment-queue, lead-assignment-rules, rep-capacity, sales-territories, territories, user-assignments - all nine are in docs/unreferenced-edge-fns-baseline.json. Only auto-lead-routing is called, by AutoLeadRoutingDashboard.tsx, and it is NOT one of the children being folded in. The two pages that sound like this domain go elsewhere: PlatformTerritories.tsx and PlatformAssignmentRules.tsx call /api/platform-crm/*, and SalesRepAssignments.tsx calls /api/sales-rep-assignments, its own edge function. /api/territories does have a crmProxies entry, but nothing calls that path either.

SO THE STORY'S QUESTION HAS CHANGED. This is not "fold children into a parent to save deployment slots". It is: a 652-line consolidation with no door, in front of nine back ends with no callers, for a UI surface that does not exist. Wiring the fan-out would make working code reachable and change nothing a user can see. The cheaper answer is probably to delete the canonical function and the nine children together and keep auto-lead-routing, but that is a product call - territories, rep capacity and an assignment queue are real features someone specified - so it belongs to whoever owns the roadmap, not to this pass. The tasks-{bulk,enhanced,stats}/task-comments half of this story is unaffected by any of this and is still a straight superseded-duplicate deletion.

DONE 2026-08-29 - TASKS HALF COMPLETE. tasks-bulk, tasks-enhanced, tasks-stats and task-comments are deleted. All four ACs that apply to them are satisfied and the checks are recorded here rather than asserted:

  1. Nothing pins the names. Confirmed again per the 2026-07-17 analysis - server.ts reads the directory listing, and no config.toml entry exists. The directory IS the manifest, so deleting the dirs removes those URLs, which is safe only because of check 2.
  2. Nothing calls them. All four invocation paths are empty for each: no client tree names /api/tasks-bulk, /api/tasks-enhanced, /api/tasks-stats or /api/task-comments (seven trees checked, source files only), none is a crmProxies target, none is a server.ts alias, and no drizzle/cron/*.sql posts to one.
  3. The parent covers the endpoint set. tasks/index.ts dispatches stats, bulk, :id/comments, :id/time, :id/time-entries and :id/timer/*; the frontend's actual calls are /api/tasks, /:id, /:id/time, /:id/time-entries[/:id], /:id/timer/start|stop, /ai-schedule and /stats. acceptanceCriteria: audit_log table: workspace_id, actor_user_id, action (string), target_type, target_id, before (jsonb), after (jsonb), ip, user_agent, created_at
Middleware logs every POST/PATCH/DELETE on the API
Admin UI: audit log viewer with filters (actor, action, date range)
Logs retained 1 year minimum; configurable
Append-only — no UPDATE or DELETE permission on audit_log via RLS
userStories.notes: Consider periodic export to immutable storage (S3 with object lock) for tamper-evidence.
userStories.reopen_reason: REOPENED: the deliverable cannot be invoked. It ships as the edge function blog-platform-api, and nothing reaches it - no client tree names the path, no crmProxies alias targets it, server.ts maps no segment onto it, and no drizzle/cron/*.sql posts to it. userStories.title: Background job queue with retries and observability
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a reliable job system so AI calls, syndication, and analytics ingest can run async with backoff.
acceptanceCriteria: pg-boss (preferred — uses Postgres) or BullMQ adapter
Job types defined as TypeScript discriminated unions; handlers in apps/worker
Default policy: exponential backoff (1m, 5m, 30m, 2h), max 5 attempts
Job dashboard in admin UI: pending, active, failed, completed counts; retry / cancel buttons
Failed jobs surface in audit_log with full error stack
Idempotency keys on every job to prevent duplicate work
userStories.notes: pg-boss avoids a Redis dependency for small deployments. Implemented as a lightweight Postgres-native queue (no pg-boss/BullMQ since the deploy has no always-on Node worker — everything is Deno edge functions). Built: blog_jobs table (status/priority/scheduled_at/attempts/max_attempts/last_error/result/idempotency_key/locked_until/locked_by), POST /blog-jobs (enqueue with idempotency dedup), GET /blog-jobs/stats (queued/active/failed/completed/cancelled counts), GET /blog-jobs?status&type, POST /blog-jobs/:id/retry, POST /blog-jobs/:id/cancel, POST /blog-jobs/run-due (cron entry point — claims due jobs with two-step UPDATE ... WHERE status='queued' AND id IN(...) approximating SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, runs in-process, applies 1m/5m/30m/2h exponential backoff, marks final fail after max_attempts). Built-in handlers: noop (smoke test) + retention_cleanup (invokes US-BLOG-009 cleanup logic). Dashboard at /platform-admin/blog/settings/jobs with status cards (5s polling), filterable jobs table, retry/cancel actions, expandable row showing payload/result/stack. Every state transition writes a blog_audit_log row (enqueue, complete, fail_retry, fail_permanent, retry, cancel). External cron wiring (k8s CronJob → POST /blog-jobs/run-due) is operations-side, not in this story.

userStories.title: SERP analyzer for any keyword
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want to see what currently ranks so I can match or exceed the bar.
acceptanceCriteria: SERP fetcher (DataForSEO or scraping adapter) returns top 20 organic results + SERP features (PAA, featured snippet, knowledge panel, video, image pack, local pack)
For each result: URL, title, meta description, domain, estimated DA, word count (fetched + parsed), heading structure (H2/H3)
Aggregated metrics: median word count, common headings, common entities, dominant content type (listicle/guide/comparison/etc.)
Stored in serp_snapshots table with fetched_at timestamp; re-fetch on demand or weekly
Admin UI: SERP analyzer view with sortable table + aggregate summary card
userStories.notes: Word count parsing must handle paywalls and JS-rendered content gracefully — fall back to meta description length when blocked. Implemented: KeywordAdapter contract extended with optional fetchSerp(creds, keyword, opts) returning {organic, features, cost}. DataForSEO impl wraps POST /v3/serp/google/organic/live/advanced and maps items to organic (rank/url/title/description/domain), featured_snippet, paa (with expanded answers), knowledge_panel, has_video_pack/image_pack/local_pack. blog_serp_snapshots table caches per (tenant, keyword, location_code, language_code, fetched_at). blog-serp edge function: POST /blog-serp/fetch (fetches, does best-effort per-URL parse with 3s timeout + 6 concurrency, falls back to snippet word-count when blocked), GET /blog-serp (list summaries), GET /blog-serp/:id (full), DELETE /blog-serp/:id. Aggregates computed at insert time: median/mean word count, common H2s (top 5, normalized + folded, requires count>=2), dominant_content_type heuristic (listicle/how_to/comparison/guide/review based on title patterns; nulls when no clear winner). Admin UI at /platform-admin/blog/serp with keyword + location + language input, recent snapshots sidebar, aggregate summary card, feature chips, sortable organic table (rank/word_count/domain), PAA section. New blog sub-nav entry 'SERP' (g e shortcut). userStories.title: People Also Ask + autocomplete miner
userStories.description: As a strategist, I want every related question surfaced so my content covers the actual user journey.
acceptanceCriteria: Recursive PAA crawler: fetch PAA for seed keyword, then for each PAA result, fetch its PAA (depth 2 default, configurable up to 4)

userStories.notes: Respect rate limits — back off aggressively on 429s. Implemented: extended blog_keywords with source_type, parent_keyword_id (self-FK), parent_question, mining_depth columns (backfill SQL idempotent). blog-paa-miner edge function: POST /mine (BFS over PAA up to depth 4, persists each Q with parent link; concurrent autocomplete fan-out across A-Z + 0-9 prefixes — 36 calls/seed when enabled; both passes share a normalized-keyword dedup set so the same string never round-trips twice), GET /tree?keyword= (walks descendants via parent_keyword_id, splits into PAA chain + flat autocomplete list, capped at 2000 nodes), DELETE /clear?keyword= (removes descendants only, preserves seed). New blog sub-nav 'PAA' (g q shortcut). Dedup is exact normalized-string match (lowercase + alphanumeric); near-duplicate clustering by Levenshtein/Jaro deferred — current dedup is enough for v1 since DataForSEO normalizes most rephrasings.

userStories.title: Auto-brief generator from keyword + SERP
userStories.description: As a writer, I want a thorough brief auto-generated so I can focus on writing instead of research compilation.
acceptanceCriteria: Input: target keyword (or cluster + pillar role) + workspace context

Brief sections: target keyword, secondary keywords, search intent, target audience persona, target word count (median of SERP +20%), target reading level, suggested H2/H3 outline (synthesized from top SERP), entities/NLP terms to include (extracted from top SERP via NER), FAQs (from PAA + community questions), schema markup plan, internal link opportunities, source list (top SERP + cited research), originality angle (what this post will say that nobody else does), CTA placement plan
Brief is editable Markdown; saved to briefs table with status = draft|approved|in-writing|done
Approve workflow: writer claims brief → status = in-writing; editor approval gate before status = approved
One-click 'Start writing' creates a post draft prefilled with brief outline as H2 placeholders
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-05-17. New edge fn supabase/functions/blog-briefs/index.ts: GET list (status/search filters, paged), GET :id, POST /generate, PATCH :id, POST :id/start-writing, DELETE (soft) — blog.post.edit gate, tenant-scoped, audit-logged. /generate pulls the latest blog_serp_snapshots row for the keyword (same pattern as the US-BLOG-014 classifier), sets target_word_count = median competitor word count * 1.2, feeds top-10 SERP titles/snippets + common H2s into a Claude JSON prompt that REQUIRES a specific contrarian originality_angle (per the notes), and persists the full structured brief + rendered markdown into blog_briefs.outline jsonb (markdown + sections) plus typed columns (target_audience, search_intent, recommended_word_count, key_takeaways, serp_snapshot) — no migration (blog_briefs already exists). userStories.description: As a platform admin, I want the auto-refresh agent to detect SERP decay and re-edit posts WITHOUT human review (per scope decision 5D), with every change captured in the audit log and revertable, so content stays competitive without operator overhead.

No human-approval step in the default path; admin can opt back into manual review per-tenant via a flag on a new blog_agent_settings row (auto_refresh_requires_review boolean, default false)

Hard guardrails: agent will NOT auto-publish if (a) the predicted change exceeds N% of the post body (configurable, default 40%), (b) the SEO score would drop, or (c) brand-voice or style-guide violations are introduced — these cases land in a review queue surfaced on the Refresh page
Every auto-refresh run respects the global agent kill switch (US-BLOG-086) — if paused, run is skipped and a blog_audit_log entry records the skip
Cost-per-run captured in the AI cost dashboard (US-BLOG-079)
Integration test: simulate SERP decay → assert revision created → assert CMS adapter called → assert audit log entry exists
Typecheck passes: npm run check

userStories.title: client_activity_logs schema drift breaks every agent-ingest activity write
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need client_activity_logs to have one declaration matching the live table, so the monitoring agent's ingest path can record activity instead of erroring on columns that no longer exist.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide which shape is canonical: shared/client-monitor-schema.ts (uuid tenant_id, uuid client_id with an FK to monitoring_clients, activity/status/details/error_code) or shared/printyx-client-schema.ts (serial id, INTEGER tenant_id, TEXT client_id, event_type/event_data/severity). Every writer in this repo passes a uuid tenantId and a uuid clientId, which only the first shape accepts

Remove the duplicate declaration so @shared/schema resolves to one table. Today the explicit named re-export at shared/schema.ts:83 wins over the `export * from './client-monitor-schema'` at :8534, so the type is the printyx one while the code is written against the monitor one

Land a migration reconciling the live table with the chosen shape (0001_complete_zombie dropped activity, status, details, devices_in_submission, metrics_count and error_code, narrowed tenant_id uuid->integer and client_id uuid->text, and dropped the monitoring_clients FK)

Fix the 11 call sites so they compile: server/routes-client-metrics.ts:116,160,191,327,518 and server/routes-client-monitoring.ts:995,1024,1084,1145,1212 (one more at :658 was deleted with EDGE-016). All 11 are TS2769 inside the tsc baseline

Re-point supabase/functions/monitoring-clients GET /:id/activity at the chosen shape - it currently reads event_type/severity/event_data and filters on client_id alone to avoid the uuid-vs-integer tenant_id comparison
Test covering one write and one read on the ingest path
userStories.notes: Found 2026-08-20 while porting the /activity handler for EDGE-016. This is a live failure, not dead code: /api/client-metrics/* is the agent ingest and is deliberately NOT proxied to an edge function, so it is the Express handlers that run. Every one of them writes activity/status/details/errorCode into client_activity_logs, and migration 0001_complete_zombie (journaled, therefore applied) dropped all four columns - a 42703 per write. Two of the inserts sit in a catch block that logs the failure of the first, so a metrics submission cannot even record why it failed. Separately, tenant_id is now integer while every caller passes a uuid, so the filter comparison in a read errors too. The tell was 11 TS2769 errors all on one table, sitting inside the 1002-error baseline where nobody would look. printyx-client-schema.ts uses integer('tenant_id') on all seven of its tables, which is a foreign convention - this app is uuid tenants everywhere else - so the likely history is that a vendored schema was merged and db:generate happily wrote a migration reshaping the app's own table to match it. That makes the monitor shape the probable canonical answer and 0001's treatment of this table the mistake, but reverting it needs a data check on the live table first (rows written before 0001 are in the old shape, rows after are absent because the writes fail). This is one of the 15 tables check:dup-tables skips as ambiguous. | RESOLVED 2026-08-27, with one of this story's own premises corrected by measuring it. AC1 DECIDED: shared/client-monitor-schema.ts is canonical. Evidence, not preference - every writer in the repo passes a uuid tenantId and uuid clientId and writes activity/status/details/errorCode; integer('tenant_id') is a foreign convention in an application that keys tenants by uuid everywhere else; and the LIVE TABLE already carries a uuid id and tenant_id. THE PREMISE THAT WAS WRONG: this story said 0001 'narrowed tenant_id uuid->integer'. It never did. Those statements were 'SET DATA TYPE serial' (serial is not a type) and a tenant_id-to-integer cast with no USING - both invalid SQL that Postgres rejected every time, removed under PA-032. So the uuid-vs-integer read failure described here has never existed; what 0001 actually achieved was dropping the six columns, converting client_id to text, and dropping the monitoring_clients FK. Measured on a database built from the migrations, not inferred. AC2: the duplicate declaration is gone from printyx-client-schema.ts, along with its relation entry and its two exported types, and schema.ts no longer names clientActivityLogs in the explicit re-export that was beating the wildcard. check:dup-tables tightened 4 -> 3. AC3: two migrations, because drizzle-kit prompts interactively when it sees three dropped and six added columns and tries to guess renames - 0060 restores the six columns, converts client_id back to uuid and re-adds the FK; 0061 drops event_type/event_data/severity. Three hand-edits to the generated SQL, each for a reason: text does not cast to uuid without USING; a bare ADD COLUMN NOT NULL fails on a table with rows, so activity and status are added with a transitional 'unknown' default that is then dropped; and the FK is added plainly rather than guarded, because skipping it silently would leave exactly the drift this story exists to close (the migration carries the DELETE to run if an environment has orphans). AC4: all 11 TS2769s are gone and NOT ONE CALL SITE WAS TOUCHED - they were only ever wrong because the type resolved to the other declaration. tsc 506 -> 496. AC5: the detail handler had already been fixed since this story was written, but check:phantom-cols found a SECOND activity handler at monitoring-clients/index.ts:810 that still read event_type/event_data/severity and filtered on client_id ALONE. Now reads the canonical columns and scopes by tenant_id as well; the comment justifying the missing tenant filter cited the integer-tenant_id claim that was never true. AC6: server/tests/unit/client-activity-logs-shape.test.ts, 7 tests over the write and the read as SQL rather than as types, so it still catches the table drifting out from under the writers after tsc is satisfied. VERIFIED END TO END on a database rebuilt from the migrations: db:migrate exits 0, the table matches the canonical declaration exactly (uuid id/tenant_id/client_id, FK present, six columns back, event_* gone), a real ingest insert with all nine fields succeeds, the exact SELECT the edge function now issues returns it, and the FK correctly REJECTED an orphan while I was setting the fixture up. db:generate reports no drift. 156 test files / 3442 tests pass. NOT APPLIED to any live environment - 0060 and 0061 are committed and pending, like 0057/0058/0059.

userStories.title: Fix the four route-ownership regressions failing check:routes on main (3 PROD 404s + 1 ambiguous domain)
userStories.description: As a user of web forms, email drip sequences, custom fields and the AI employee dashboard, I need those pages to work in production and not just in dev — four domains regressed past the EDGE-018 ratchet and npm run check:routes has been failing on main.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a web-forms edge function with parity for the endpoints client/src/hooks/useWebForms.ts calls (list/create/read/update/delete + /:id/submissions)
Add an email-sequences edge function with parity for client/src/hooks/useEmailSequences.ts (:campaignId/enroll, :campaignId/enrollments, enrollments/:id, enrollments/:id/unenroll)

Add an ai-employees edge function with parity for AIEmployeeDashboard.tsx (GET /, GET /analytics/overview) — the analytics aggregation needs a Postgres RPC, since it uses generate_series + COUNT FILTER which PostgREST cannot express
