Every new edge function uses normalizePath and returns camelCase rows matching what the frontend types
npm run check:routes exits 0 and the baseline is re-tightened without absorbing unrelated upstream drift
userStories.notes:
Opened 2026-07-29 while working the prd backlog: npm run check:routes was FAILING on an untouched checkout of main (verified by stashing all local work and re-running — byte-identical output), so this is upstream debt that slipped past the EDGE-018 ratchet, not something a story introduced. Four findings: /api/custom-fields ambiguous (Express + edge, no proxy entry) and /api/ai-employees, /api/email-sequences, /api/web-forms missing-edge — i.e. the frontend calls them, Express answers in dev, and PROD 404s because the frontend hits functions.printyx.net directly. | PROGRESS 2026-07-29 — 3 of 4 DONE, check:routes down from 4 findings to 1. (1) CUSTOM-FIELDS: found a SECOND, worse bug than the ambiguity the ratchet reported. The edge fn returned raw PostgREST snake_case while the Express handler it mirrors returns Drizzle rows, which are ALREADY camelCase — and SIX consumers type camelCase (useCustomFields' CustomFieldDefinition, and through it CustomFieldsSettings, CrmDataTable, crm-columns, CustomFieldInput/Section, WebFormBuilder). So in PROD the settings table rendered blank Type/Active cells and the sortOrder-based sort degraded to NaN. Added an explicit toCamel mapper on all four response paths, THEN the proxy entry. Note routes-custom-fields.ts is NOT deleted: its validateCustomFieldValues is imported by routes-business-records.ts and routes-deals.ts — only the HTTP handlers are superseded. | (2) WEB-FORMS: new edge fn, full parity including /:id/submissions with a bounded ?limit=. slug / public_token / tenant_id / submission_count are deliberately not client-patchable. (3) EMAIL-SEQUENCES: new edge fn. Two things worth knowing — the routing gotcha is that 'enrollments' is a LITERAL first segment on two endpoints but a campaignId on the other two, so the literal branch must match first or /enrollments/:id is read as campaignId='enrollments'; and the enroll path replicates enrollRecipient()'s decision logic from server/services/email-sequence-scheduler.ts (campaign must exist, suppression honoured, delay from step 0) — KEEP THE TWO IN SYNC. Sending stays in the Node cron; this fn owns enrollment STATE only. | TWO BUGS CAUGHT IN MY OWN FIRST DRAFT and fixed before commit, both worth remembering: (a) the suppression check interpolated campaignId (a URL segment) into a PostgREST .or() filter STRING, where a comma or paren in the value would silently change the predicate's meaning — replaced with one batched .in() query decided in JS, which also removed an N+1 (it had been one query per recipient); (b) that rewrite then paired recipients by emails.indexOf(email), which mis-assigns businessRecordId/contactId when the same address appears twice in one payload — now an indexed loop. | A TOOL FALSE NEGATIVE WORTH RECORDING: npm run audit:routes classifies web-forms and email-sequences as 'edge-only', i.e. it does NOT see their Express side. It is wrong — routes-web-forms.ts and routes-email-sequences.ts declare full /api/... paths INSIDE a Router that routes-registry.ts mounts with a bare app.use(router) (lines 635-636), a shape the audit's Express detection misses. They really are both-served, which is why both got crmProxies entries: without one the new edge fns would run ONLY in prod, which is the exact 'invisible in dev' trap that let these rot in the first place. Anyone re-running the audit should not trust that column for app.use-mounted routers. | REMAINING — /api/ai-employees, deliberately not rushed. GET / is trivial, but GET /analytics/overview cannot be ported as-is: getAnalyticsOverview() in server/services/ai-employee-service.ts is five raw-SQL queries using COUNT(*) FILTER, GROUP BY, a LEFT JOIN, and a generate_series 7-day series that keeps empty days at 0 so the chart does not misalign. PostgREST expresses none of that. The right fix is a Postgres function + migration called via admin.rpc(), so ONE implementation of the SQL serves both backends; reimplementing it as JS-side aggregation would duplicate non-trivial logic and drift. That needs a migration added through db:generate (never a hand-dropped .sql — SUPA-005 journal integrity), so it gets its own pass. Note the dashboard already tolerates both casings via toAiEmployee(), but reads analytics as camelCase directly, so the RPC must return camelCase keys. | VERIFICATION so far: tsc holds at 1067; ESLint holds at 11916; check:edge-paths green and now reports 171 migrated (up from 169 — both new fns use normalizePath, so neither is born with the prod-only 404 bug); check:proxy-overrides green; unit suite byte-identical to the clean tree. HONEST LIMITATION: the new fns could NOT be typechecked with deno (not installed in this container) or by tsc (tsconfig includes only client/shared/server), so they were syntax/type-checked with tsc --noResolve and verified against the real schema columns and the live _shared helper signatures by hand — treat prod behaviour as UNEXERCISED until someone curls each endpoint. The check:routes baseline was deliberately NOT re-tightened: doing so now would absorb the still-open ai-employees finding. | PROGRESS 2026-07-29 (part 2) — THE 4TH AND LAST FINDING IS CLOSED: npm run check:routes now EXITS 0. It had been failing on main before any of this work. | AI-EMPLOYEES, the one the previous pass parked. Both of the dashboard's queries (GET / and GET /analytics/overview) were 404ing in prod. Built the edge fn plus the Postgres function the analytics needs. KEY DECISION — the aggregation went into drizzle/functions/ai-employee-analytics.sql, NOT a drizzle migration and NOT a JS reimplementation. There is an established pattern for exactly this (drizzle/functions/, alongside dashboard-widget-data.sql and billing-aggregates.sql, applied by hand with \i and idempotent via CREATE OR REPLACE); its README explains why hand-written SQL cannot live in drizzle/migrations — drizzle-kit generate produces no schema delta for a function, and the migrator may choke on the orphaned file. That also keeps SUPA-005 journal integrity intact, since nothing was hand-dropped into drizzle/migrations. The function reproduces getAnalyticsOverview()'s five queries clause for clause so applying it moves no number the dashboard already shows. | THREE THINGS THE SQL PORT GOT WRONG ON THE FIRST DRAFT, all caught before commit and all worth remembering. (a) TENANT ID TYPE: the sibling functions declare p_tenant_id text because their tables store tenant_id as varchar, but ai_employees.tenant_id and ai_employee_tasks.tenant_id are uuid (drizzle/rls/ai-employee-tables.sql). Inside a function body the parameter has a KNOWN type, so `tenant_id = p_tenant_id` is an invalid uuid = text comparison — it would have failed at call time, not at CREATE time. Declared uuid instead, which also keeps the index usable and lets PostgREST reject a malformed id with a 400. This is why the file's parameter type deliberately differs from its siblings. (b) AGGREGATE ORDERING: a CTE's ORDER BY does not bind a later jsonb_agg over it. For performanceTrends the order IS the contract — tasksCompleted/qualityScores/responseTime are three arrays read POSITIONALLY as one 7-day series, so an unordered agg would silently scramble the chart rather than fail. Every jsonb_agg now carries its own ORDER BY. (c) The recent-tasks CTE had to carry assigned_at as a column purely so the aggregate could order by it. | NO PROXY ENTRY FOR /api/ai-employees, deliberately, and this is the interesting call. web-forms and email-sequences got crmProxies entries because their edge fns have FULL parity with the Express routers. ai-employees does not: the edge fn covers the two READ endpoints the dashboard calls, while the Express router also owns create / tasks / workflows-execute, which run agents through ClaudeAIService and are not ported. CLAUDE.md warns precisely about this shape — the proxy forwards the WHOLE prefix and falls through only on a NETWORK error, never a 404 — so an entry would have taken those write endpoints from working-in-dev to 404-in-dev. Prod is unaffected either way, since it never reached Express; that is why the read endpoints were 404ing there in the first place. Porting agent execution is separate work, not a routing fix. | The list endpoint returns raw snake_case ON PURPOSE, unlike the other fns in this story. It mirrors the Express handler, which returns SELECT * untouched, and AIEmployeeDashboard.tsx already normalises either casing through toAiEmployee(). Converting here would be a gratuitous divergence from the endpoint being mirrored. The ANALYTICS response is camelCase, because the page reads analytics.totalEmployees / .performanceTrends.* directly with no normaliser — a snake_case analytics response would render the dashboard as zeroes rather than erroring, so that shape is part of the contract and is documented in the SQL file header. | BASELINE TIGHTENED, and reviewed rather than trusted: missingEdge 45 -> 44, bothDivergent unchanged at 59. The single removal is `lead-intelligence`, which resolved because the dead LeadIntelligenceDashboard.tsx that called it was deleted in the QUALITY-002 batch-27 dead-code sweep earlier the same day. No unrelated upstream drift was absorbed — that was the specific risk flagged when the previous pass deliberately did NOT tighten it. | VERIFICATION: check:routes EXITS 0 (was 4 findings on main); check:edge-paths green at 172 migrated, up from 169 at the start of this story — all three new fns use normalizePath, so none is born with the prod-only 404 bug; check:proxy-overrides green; check:migrations green (40 files / 40 journal entries, untouched); check:rootsql green; tsc holds at 1067; ESLint holds at 11916; unit suite byte-identical to the clean tree (26 files / 10 tests failing before and after — they need a live DB this container lacks). | REMAINING — passes stays FALSE on two operational steps that cannot be done from this container, NOT on missing code. (1) drizzle/functions/ai-employee-analytics.sql must be APPLIED to each target database (\i drizzle/functions/ai-employee-analytics.sql). Until it is, /analytics/overview returns the zeroed shape as a 200 — the fn detects the missing function (42883 / PGRST202) and degrades instead of 500ing, matching the fallback convention documented in drizzle/functions/README.md — so the dashboard renders zeroes rather than breaking. The README notes this has no in-JS fallback, because the aggregation is the reason the function exists. (2) NOTHING HERE HAS BEEN EXERCISED AGAINST A DEPLOY. deno is not installed in this container and edge fns sit outside tsconfig (include is client/shared/server only), so the three new fns were syntax/type-checked with tsc --noResolve and verified by hand against the real schema columns and the live _shared helper signatures. That is static evidence, not runtime evidence: treat prod behaviour as unconfirmed until someone curls each endpoint once — GET /web-forms, GET /email-sequences/:campaignId/enrollments, GET /ai-employees, GET /ai-employees/analytics/overview, GET /custom-fields.

VERIFIED DONE (2026-07-30 production-gap deep dive): npm run check:routes is green. The ai-employees, web-forms and email-sequences edge functions exist under supabase/functions/, and custom-fields ambiguity is resolved.

userStories.title: Split missing-edge route findings by reachability — 10 of the 44 "prod blockers" are orphaned callers
userStories.description: As a maintainer planning the edge-function porting work, I need the route-ownership ratchet to distinguish a route a real user 404s on from one whose only caller is dead code, so the prod-blocker count means what it says and porting effort goes where users are actually affected.
acceptanceCriteria: computeParity() scans client files individually instead of one concatenated blob, so calls can be attributed to their source file
Reachability from App.tsx/main.tsx classifies each frontend call as LIVE or DEAD, exposed as byClassLive()/byClassDead()
check:routes gates only on LIVE missing-edge domains; dead-caller ones are reported without failing CI
The baseline format is unchanged so no re-baselining is required
audit:routes reports the LIVE/DEAD split in both the markdown matrix and the console summary
The gate is mutation-tested in both directions (live caller fails, orphaned caller passes but reports)
userStories.notes: Opened and DONE 2026-07-29, straight after EDGE-019. Working EDGE-019 exposed that the route-ownership ratchet reports 44 grandfathered `missing-edge` domains, and its own legend calls that class a PROD BLOCKER — i.e. it was claiming 44 domains 404 in production right now. That number was never split by whether a user can actually reach the calling code, which is the same mistake AUDIT-014 had already fixed once for nav targets ('That LIVE/DEAD split is the key output — most of the noise is on dead pages'). | THE FINDING: 34 of the 44 are REAL live prod 404s. 10 are noise — their only callers are orphaned files, so the fetch can never run. The 10: approvals (pages/my-approvals.tsx), assignment-groups (pages/assignment-groups.tsx), email-parser (pages/settings/email-parser-settings.tsx), equipment-disposal (components/equipment/EquipmentDisposalDialog.tsx), record-layout-config (components/crm/RecordPageLayout.tsx), salesforce (components/integrations/SalesforceIntegration.tsx), and financial-forecasting + platform + sales-performance + system-monitoring, which ALL come from ONE file: client/src/lib/role-dashboard-config.ts, a role-based dashboard config with ZERO importers anywhere in the tree. That single orphan was inflating the prod-blocker count by four domains on its own. | WHY THAT MATTERS BEYOND THE COUNT: the 44 list is what the EDGE-002x porting stories work from. Roughly a quarter of it is not porting work at all — it is dead-code deletion, and porting an edge function for a page nobody can reach would be pure waste. The live 34 are also now ranked by caller count, so the worst are visible: task-workflows (4 live callers: WorkflowBuilderPage/WorkflowDetailPage/WorkflowStepPage), then contract-pnl, pipeline-forecast, sales-forecasts, service and workflow-automation at 2 each. | WHAT WAS BUILT, following the check-nav-targets.mjs precedent rather than writing a throwaway script: reachability moved INTO scripts/lib/route-parity.mjs (the shared classifier both the audit and the CI guard import, so there stays exactly one source of truth). Step 3 previously concatenated every client file into ONE blob before regexing for /api/ segments, which structurally discarded per-file attribution and is why the split could not exist. It now scans per file, walks the import graph from App.tsx/main.tsx, and exposes frontendLive per row plus byClassLive()/byClassDead() helpers and a callerFiles map. | GATING RULE CHANGED, deliberately and narrowly: check:routes now fails only on a new missing-edge domain that a LIVE file calls. A new one reachable only from orphans is REPORTED under its own heading and does not fail CI — exactly the rule check-nav-targets.mjs already applies ('deleting an orphan is not this check's job'). The baseline format is UNCHANGED and still stores the full missing-edge list, which is a superset of the live one, so it keeps working as a plain membership test and no re-baselining was needed. both-divergent gating is untouched. | MUTATION-TESTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because a guard whose failure path is never exercised is not a guard: (a) appending a call to a brand-new /api/zzz-mutation-probe in a LIVE page (pages/DealDetail.tsx) makes check:routes exit 1 and name the domain — so real regressions are still caught; (b) the SAME call appended to an ORPHANED page (pages/assignment-groups.tsx) exits 0 but prints it under the not-gated heading, and the summary's dead count moves 10 -> 11. Both files restored afterwards; verified no probe text remains in the tree. | ALSO CORRECTED, found while reading the classifier: the file header claimed '60 both-divergent + 56 missing-edge' when the real figures are 59 and 44. Fixed rather than left, since that header is what anyone reads before trusting the tool. NOT fixed here, and worth its own story — the classifier's Express detection only matches app.METHOD('/api/x') and app.use('/api/x'), so it MISSES routers that declare full '/api/...' paths internally and are mounted with a bare app.use(router). That is the false negative EDGE-019 hit on web-forms and email-sequences, and it means the both-divergent count is an UNDER-count of unknown size. | FOLLOW-UP THIS ENABLES (not done here, deliberately — deleting 7 orphaned files is a dead-code decision, not a tooling change): the 10 dead-caller domains resolve by deleting their callers, which would also drop the missing-edge baseline 44 -> 34 and make the ratchet's number mean what it says. role-dashboard-config.ts is the highest-value one (4 domains, zero importers). That belongs with the AUDIT-016 dead-code follow-ups. | VERIFICATION: check:routes green and now reports the split in its success line; audit:routes regenerated docs/route-parity-matrix.md with a new 'missing-edge, split by reachability' section and prints prod blockers as the LIVE 34 with the dead 10 listed separately as cleanup; the tool's split reproduces an INDEPENDENT scratch analysis exactly (same 34/10, same 10 domain names) — written before the tooling change, then cross-checked against it. check:edge-paths, check:proxy-overrides, check:nav, check:migrations, check:rootsql all green; ESLint holds at 11916; tsc untouched at 1067 (no app code changed — this story only touches scripts/ and generated docs). | HARDENING + A CORRECTION TO MY OWN ANALYSIS, same day, before this was called done. While pulling the evidence to decide delete-vs-wire on the 7 orphaned files, the reachability walk classified server/routes/workflow-automation-routes.ts as DEAD — which directly contradicts CLAUDE.md ('The registered router is server/routes/workflow-automation-routes.ts, mounted at /api by routes-registry.ts'). CLAUDE.md is right and the walk was wrong: routes-registry.ts mounts that router through `await import(modulePath)` iterating an ARRAY of string literals (asyncRootApiMounts, line ~552), and a regex walk that only follows a literal immediately inside import(...) cannot see it. Caught because the tool disagreed with the documentation and the documentation was checked, not assumed. | WHY THAT WAS URGENT RATHER THAN INTERESTING: this story had just changed the gate so a DEAD verdict SUPPRESSES a failure. That makes a false 'dead' the dangerous direction — it would silently de-gate a real prod 404, which is strictly worse than the over-reporting it replaced. So the walk is now FAIL-SAFE: it scans for the constructs it cannot follow (import.meta.glob, and import() with a computed specifier) and, if any exists in the client tree, treats EVERY file as live, disabling the split rather than emitting confident wrong answers. computeParity returns reachabilityTrusted + unfollowableImportFile, and check:routes PRINTS the disablement with the offending file, so a degraded split can never be silent. Verified today the client tree has neither construct, so the split is active and honest; the blind spot is server-side only and does not affect this story's client-side classification. | MUTATION-TESTED, third and fourth cases: adding `import.meta.glob(...)` to a live page disables the split (44 live / 0 dead, i.e. everything gates) and names the file; a computed `import(_p)` does the same; removing both restores 34/10. So the fail-safe is exercised, not just asserted. | THE DELETE-VS-WIRE QUESTION THIS STORY TEED UP IS NOW ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS *DO NOT DELETE ANY OF THEM*. My first pass at the evidence suggested /api/approvals and /api/assignment-groups had NO backend at all, which under the CLAUDE.md rule ('delete features with no backing implementation rather than fake them') would have made pages/my-approvals.tsx and pages/assignment-groups.tsx clean deletions. That was WRONG, and wrong via the exact blind spot above: both are fully implemented in server/routes/workflow-automation-routes.ts as router.get('/approvals') / router.get('/assignment-groups') inside a router mounted at /api, so a grep for "/api/approvals" finds nothing. Deleting those two pages would have destroyed working front-ends for live endpoints. Re-checked with that in mind, ALL SEVEN orphans have real, registered backends — equipment-disposal (routes-equipment-disposal.ts), record-layout-config (routes-record-layout.ts) and salesforce (routes-salesforce-integration.ts) are each LIVE and reachable from server/index.ts, and email-parser is mounted at routes-registry.ts:611. | SO THE FOLLOW-UP IS 'WIRE UP', NOT 'DELETE': seven implemented pages/components (3,480 lines) sit orphaned in front of working APIs — my-approvals, assignment-groups, email-parser-settings, EquipmentDisposalDialog, RecordPageLayout, SalesforceIntegration, and lib/role-dashboard-config.ts. That is unrouted product, not dead code, and it is a product decision about which to surface — deliberately NOT taken here. It also means the earlier framing in these notes ('the 10 dead-caller domains resolve by deleting their callers') is superseded: deleting them would resolve the ratchet number by removing working UI, which is the wrong trade. Route them and the domains become live prod 404s that genuinely need edge functions. | A THIRD INSTANCE OF THE SAME ROOT CAUSE, worth stating plainly because it has now caused three separate wrong answers in one day: the classifier's Express detection misses app.use(router)-mounted routers (EDGE-019: web-forms/email-sequences read as edge-only), the reachability walk misses await import(variable) (this story: workflow-automation-routes read as dead), and the evidence pass above nearly acted on the first of those. All three are the same shape — a regex that disagrees with the real module/route resolver. AUDIT-014's notes recorded the identical lesson about its own script. Any future tooling here should resolve routes/imports properly rather than pattern-match, and until then every 'X is dead/absent' verdict from these tools needs a second, differently-shaped check before anyone acts on it.

userStories.title: Fix Express detection for Router-mounted routes — 10 dev≠prod divergences were invisible to the parity tooling
userStories.description: As a maintainer relying on the route-parity tooling to decide what to port, I need it to see routes declared on an express Router, not just app.METHOD('/api/x'), so it stops reporting live Express handlers as absent and stops labelling still-divergent domains 'fully migrated'.
acceptanceCriteria: Detect routes declared on any router identifier with an absolute path (router.get('/api/x') mounted via app.use(router))
Detect routes declared with a relative path on a router mounted under a '/api' prefix (router.get('/x') via app.use('/api', router))
Exclude test files from the Express scan so supertest fixtures do not invent handlers
Hand-verify every newly surfaced domain before adding it to the baseline
Record in the baseline note why bothDivergent grew, so the growth is not misread as a regression
Mutation-test that the previously-blind combination now fails the guard
userStories.notes: Opened and DONE 2026-07-29, closing the root cause EDGE-019 and EDGE-020 each hit separately. The parity classifier detected Express handlers with ONE pattern — app.METHOD('/api/x') — which misses every route declared on an express Router object. That is not a corner case in this repo: 20 routers are mounted bare with app.use(router), and 11 more are mounted at '/api' through a loop over an array of module paths in routes-registry.ts. | WHAT IT WAS GETTING WRONG, concretely, and why it mattered three times in one day: (1) EDGE-019 — web-forms and email-sequences were reported `edge-only` while Express was actively serving them, so the tool's own column said the Express side did not exist; (2) EDGE-020 — while deciding delete-vs-wire on seven orphaned pages, /api/approvals and /api/assignment-groups looked like they had NO backend at all, which under the CLAUDE.md rule would have justified DELETING two working pages. Both are implemented as router.get('/approvals') inside the router mounted at '/api'. A tool that reports a live handler as absent is worse than no tool, because it launders a guess into evidence. | THE FIX, two mount shapes, both now covered: (a) ABSOLUTE — allow any identifier before the method, not just `app`, so router.get('/api/web-forms') is seen regardless of how the router is mounted; (b) PREFIXED — the module declares a RELATIVE path (router.get('/approvals')) and the registry supplies '/api' at mount time, so the module text contains no '/api' at all and NO amount of scanning that file can find it. Handled by reading the registry's array-of-literals module list and applying the prefix to each router's own paths. Express-served domains went 179 -> 244. | TESTS ARE NOW EXCLUDED FROM THE SCAN, a correctness bug the widening introduced and which was caught by hand-verification rather than by the tool. Widening to any identifier also picks up routers built inside supertest fixtures; the very first file matched for `ai-employees` was server/tests/unit/ai-employee-auth.test.ts. A test fixture's routes are not production surface, and counting them invents Express handlers that do not ship. Excluding test files dropped expressServed 246 -> 244 and express-only 71 -> 69, and did not change any of the 10 findings below (all have real production routers). | RESULT: bothDivergent 59 -> 69. THE BASELINE GREW, AND THAT IS A DETECTION FIX, NOT A REGRESSION — the reason is recorded in the baseline's own `note` field so it survives regeneration and nobody reads the growth as backsliding later. The 10 newly-visible dev-does-not-equal-prod traps: ai-employees, analytics, chart-of-accounts, email-campaigns, enabled-products, equipment-lifecycle, journal-entries, leases, sales-pipeline, social-media. Several had been sitting under an `edge-only` label, which the matrix glosses as 'fully migrated' — the most misleading possible state for a domain that still has a live Express handler. missingEdge is UNCHANGED at 44, as expected: classify() checks missing-edge before both-divergent and it does not depend on the Express side, so better Express detection cannot move it. | HAND-VERIFIED BEFORE BASELINING rather than trusted, because this is a tool I had just changed: journal-entries (routes-financial.ts declares /api/journal-entries absolutely, edge fn exists, not proxied), social-media (same absolute shape), and leases (routes/lease-routes.ts declares the RELATIVE /leases and is in the '/api' mount array — i.e. the branch-(b) path, confirming the prefixed case works end to end). All three have edge functions and no proxy entry, so all three are genuine traps. ai-employees is on the list because of EDGE-019's DELIBERATE decision not to proxy it (its edge fn covers only the read endpoints while Express keeps the agent-execution writes) — that is a documented, intentional divergence, and it is healthy that the tool can finally see it instead of silently calling it edge-only. | MUTATION-TESTED: adding router.get('/api/zzz-probe-domain') to an Express router, an edge fn dir of the same name, and a live frontend call makes check:routes exit 1 and name the domain — the exact combination the old detection was blind to. Removing all three restores green. Verified no probe artifacts survived in server/, client/, supabase/ or scripts/. | KNOWN REMAINING LIMITATION, stated rather than papered over: the scan does not check that a router is actually MOUNTED, so an unregistered router declaring /api/x could still produce a phantom Express handler. The known instance — server/routes-workflow-automation.ts, which CLAUDE.md documents as unregistered dead mock — declares only /api/workflow-automation, whose class is missing-edge and therefore unaffected by the Express side. This is consistent with the module header's standing contract ('Heuristic (regex over source) — treat as a worklist to confirm per-domain, not as ground truth'), and every finding here was confirmed by hand. A future version should resolve mounts properly rather than pattern-match; that is the same conclusion EDGE-020 reached about the import walk. | VERIFICATION: all six guardrails green; ESLint holds at 11916; tsc untouched at 1067 (scripts + generated docs only, no app code). docs/route-parity-matrix.md and docs/route-divergence.json regenerated.

userStories.title: Unbreak the sales forecasting pages in prod — edge fns for sales-forecasts + pipeline-forecast, and fix the bare-fetch call sites
userStories.description: As a sales manager, I need the Sales Command Center and Pipeline Forecasting pages to load real data in production, where both of their queries currently fail — there is no edge function behind either endpoint, and the calls bypass getApiUrl and auth entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a sales-forecasts edge function covering the reads the two pages make (list, and /:id/pipeline for parity)
Add a pipeline-forecast edge function reproducing the weighted deals+quotes+proposals aggregation, including the CRMX-005 stage probability and include_in_forecast rules
Replace the bare fetch() call sites in SalesCommandCenter.tsx and SalesPipelineForecasting.tsx with apiRequest so the calls reach the edge host with a Bearer token
Proxy only the prefix whose edge fn has full Express parity; document why the other is not proxied
Return camelCase rows matching what the pages read
check:routes stays green and the baseline movement is reviewed, not blanket-updated
userStories.notes: Opened and DONE 2026-07-29, the first story to USE the corrected tooling from EDGE-020/021 rather than fix it. Took the two highest-value single-endpoint entries off the LIVE prod-404 list: /api/sales-forecasts and /api/pipeline-forecast, both read by SalesCommandCenter.tsx and SalesPipelineForecasting.tsx. Live prod 404s 34 -> 32. | THE BIGGER FINDING: THE EDGE FUNCTIONS ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED THESE PAGES. All four call sites used bare `fetch('/api/...')` rather than apiRequest, which is broken in PROD in two independent ways. (1) ROUTING — getApiUrl (client/src/lib/config.ts) is what rewrites /api/x to <functions host>/x in production; a raw relative fetch skips it entirely, so the request goes to the Cloudflare Pages origin, which has no /api handler, falls through to the SPA shell, and `.then(res => res.json())` then throws on an HTML body. (2) AUTH — no Bearer header, so it would 401 even if it arrived (the exact trap CLAUDE.md records for invoice PDFs). So the port had to be paired with switching all four to apiRequest; shipping only the backend half would have left both pages just as broken and looked like progress. Anyone porting a missing-edge domain should check the CALL SITE first — an edge fn behind a bare fetch is dead on arrival. | PIPELINE-FORECAST, the interesting port. The Express handler is a weighted-pipeline aggregation over open deals + quotes + proposals vs active sales goals. Two things were preserved deliberately rather than simplified: (a) THE STAGE JOIN — Express does `LEFT JOIN pipeline_stages ps ON ps.legacy_stage_id = d.stage_id`, but PostgREST can only embed across a declared FOREIGN KEY and legacy_stage_id is not one, so an embedded select would ERROR rather than degrade; the edge fn fetches stages separately and joins in JS, which reproduces the same rows; (b) CRMX-005 SEMANTICS, which change the numbers and are easy to lose — the deal's own probability wins, else the stage default_probability, else 50; deals whose stage sets include_in_forecast=false are DROPPED entirely; quotes default to 50% and proposals to 70%. The sales_goals read keeps Express's tolerate-failure behaviour (its own try/catch) so a tenant without goals still gets a forecast instead of a 500. | PROXY DECISION, split per prefix on parity — the rule established for ai-employees in EDGE-019. /api/pipeline-forecast IS proxied because its edge fn has FULL parity (Express serves exactly one endpoint there). /api/sales-forecasts is NOT proxied: Express also owns a POST that the edge fn does not implement, and a crmProxies entry forwards the WHOLE prefix and falls through only on a network error, never a 404, so an entry would take that write from working-in-dev to 404-in-dev. No frontend caller POSTs it today, so porting a write nobody uses would add risk for no user benefit; reads were the whole problem. | SCOPE HELD DELIBERATELY: the edge fns cover reads only. GET /sales-forecasts and GET /sales-forecasts/:id/pipeline are ported (the latter for parity even though no page calls it yet); POST stays on Express. Rows are returned camelCase because the Express handlers return Drizzle rows and the pages read forecastName/revenueTarget/startDate and forecastData.pipeline.totalValue directly — raw PostgREST snake_case would render blank, the EDGE-005a failure mode. | A SEPARATE BUG FOUND AND DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN QUIETLY HIDDEN: SalesCommandCenter sends `owner=me` on the pipeline-forecast request when its scope toggle is set, but NEITHER backend implements it — the Express handler reads only period/startDate/endDate, and the edge fn mirrors that. So the 'my pipeline' toggle silently shows everyone's pipeline. I left the parameter on the URL and commented it at the call site instead of deleting it: dropping it would erase the only evidence that a real UI affordance is unimplemented. Fixing it needs server-side owner filtering, which is a feature, not part of unbreaking a 404. | BASELINE MOVEMENT, reviewed not rubber-stamped: missingEdge 44 -> 42 (pipeline-forecast and sales-forecasts both resolved) and bothDivergent 69 -> 70 (sales-forecasts moved INTO both-divergent, which is the expected consequence of adding an edge fn and deliberately not proxying — the same documented state as ai-employees, not a new problem). Nothing unrelated moved. | VERIFICATION: check:routes green, now reporting 32 LIVE prod 404s (down from 34) and 10 dead-caller domains; check:edge-paths green at 174 migrated, up from 172 — both new fns use normalizePath, so neither is born with the prod-only 404 bug; check:proxy-overrides, check:nav, check:migrations, check:rootsql green; tsc holds at 1067; ESLint holds at 11916; unit suite byte-identical to the clean tree (26 files / 10 tests failing before and after — DB-dependent). SAME HONEST LIMITATION AS EDGE-019: deno is not installed here and edge fns are outside tsconfig, so both new fns were syntax/type-checked with tsc --noResolve and hand-verified against the real schema columns (sales_forecasts in server/sales-forecasting-schema.ts) and the live _shared helper signatures. Treat prod behaviour as unexercised until someone curls GET /sales-forecasts and GET /pipeline-forecast.

userStories.title: Port the Contract P&L X-ray to an edge function, with the margin math extracted and test-locked first
userStories.description: As a dealer principal, I need the Contract Profitability page to work in production — all seven of its endpoints 404 there — and I need the margin numbers it shows to be identical whichever backend serves them.
acceptanceCriteria: Extract the P&L formulas to shared/contract-pnl-math.ts and have the Express router import them instead of its own copies
Pin the arithmetic with unit tests covering string-numeric coercion, explicit-zero rates, base-only financing, and null-vs-zero GP%
Add a contract-pnl edge function with parity for all seven endpoints, replicating the math inline with a keep-in-sync note
Add a Postgres function for the materialized-view refresh, which PostgREST cannot issue
Fix the CSV export download, which sends no auth header and 401s against an edge function
Proxy the prefix (full parity) and keep check:routes green with a reviewed baseline
userStories.notes: Opened and DONE 2026-07-29, continuing the live prod-404 burn-down from EDGE-022. /api/contract-pnl is the Contract Profitability X-ray (US-SUPER-003) — seven endpoints read by ContractProfitability.tsx and ContractPnlDetail.tsx, none of which had an edge function, so the whole feature 404'd in production. Live prod 404s 32 -> 31. | THIS ONE CARRIES MONEY, so it was done differently from the other ports. The risk in duplicating a handler into Deno is a subtly-wrong number that looks plausible — exactly what CLAUDE.md warns about repeatedly. So the FIRST move was not the port: the P&L formulas were extracted to shared/contract-pnl-math.ts (canonical, imported by the Express router, which lost 85 lines of now-duplicated code) and PINNED by 13 unit tests in server/tests/unit/contract-pnl-math.test.ts. Only then was the Deno replica written, against a tested specification rather than a second reading of the same prose. This is the arrangement CLAUDE.md already records for quote-math + the proposals fn; contract-pnl now follows it. | WHAT THE TESTS DELIBERATELY PIN, because each is a way the replica could have gone quietly wrong: (a) num() must coerce STRING numerics — Postgres returns numeric columns as strings through both drivers, so without it every multiplication is NaN or string concatenation; (b) ratesFrom guards on `!= null`, NOT truthiness, so a tenant who deliberately sets a ZERO rate gets 0 rather than silently having the default cost re-added to their contracts; (c) financing is charged on BASE (equipment) revenue only, never on clicks; (d) gpPercent is NULL, not 0, when there is no revenue — a 0 would sort a no-data contract in with genuine break-even ones and trip the below-threshold alert; (e) a cross-check that 12 identical months through computeMonthly equal one year through computePnl, which stops the two functions drifting apart. | THREE THINGS THE PORT COULD NOT DO LITERALLY. (1) THE VIEW->TABLE JOIN: Express does `FROM contract_pnl_v v LEFT JOIN business_records b ON b.id = v.customer_id`. PostgREST embeds only across a declared FOREIGN KEY and a MATERIALIZED VIEW has none, so an embedded select would ERROR rather than degrade — the customer columns are fetched separately and joined in JS. A real consequence, documented in the fn header: the industry/salesRep/territory/search filters span BOTH sides, so they are applied post-join instead of being pushed into the query. (2) REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW cannot be issued through PostgREST at all, so it became drizzle/functions/contract-pnl-refresh.sql. (3) The CSV export returns a text/csv body, so it bypasses createCorsResponse and echoes the Origin the way the other CSV endpoints in the tree (blog-ai-costs, blog-performance-dashboard) already do — my first draft called corsHeaders(req) as if it were a function when it is a const object, caught before commit. | THE REFRESH FUNCTION IS THE ONLY SECURITY DEFINER IN drizzle/functions/, and that is deliberate and bounded: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW requires OWNERSHIP of the view, which the API roles do not have. It takes NO arguments and names two hard-coded views, so there is no injection surface and nothing a caller can redirect; search_path is pinned. It is also NOT tenant-scoped and cannot be — a materialized view refreshes wholly. That exactly matches the Express behaviour: the per-tenant guard is the 60s cooldown in contract_pnl_settings, enforced by the CALLER before invoking, not by the refresh. It returns a jsonb marker instead of void so a missing view (undefined_table) comes back as data and the endpoint can answer 503 + viewMissing:true like Express, rather than raising. | A SECOND REAL BUG FOUND AT THE CALL SITE, the EDGE-022 lesson paying off again. The CSV export button was `window.open(getApiUrl(...))` — a browser NAVIGATION, which sends no Authorization header at all. That works in dev, where Express accepts the session cookie, and 401s in prod the instant the request reaches the edge function: the same prod-only shape as the edge path-normalization class. Fixed by extracting client/src/lib/authed-download.ts (fetchAuthedBlob + triggerBlobDownload + downloadAuthedFile), generalising what lib/invoice-pdf.ts already did for one endpoint, and wiring the button through it with an error toast. Worth reusing for every future authenticated download — its header comment spells out why BOTH window.open and fetch(credentials:'include') fail against edge auth. | PROXIED, unlike sales-forecasts and ai-employees: this edge fn has FULL parity — all seven Express endpoints (list, export.csv, GET/PUT settings, refresh, digest/preview, :contractId) are implemented, so forwarding the whole prefix in dev takes nothing offline. The routing gotcha is recorded in the fn header: export.csv / settings / refresh / digest are LITERAL first segments sharing a position with :contractId, so every literal branch must be matched before the :contractId fallthrough or /settings is read as a contract id. | SELF-CAUGHT REGRESSION, worth recording because the ratchet is what caught it: the first pass pushed ESLint 11916 -> 11919 (+3). Not pre-existing noise — all three were mine: a `catch (e: any)` I added, plus a now-unused `PnlComputed` import and an unused `DEFAULTS` alias left behind by the math extraction. Fixed rather than baselined (the catch narrows with `instanceof Error`), and the count is back to exactly 11916. | VERIFICATION: check:routes green at 31 LIVE prod 404s (down from 32), missingEdge baseline 42 -> 41 with contract-pnl the only removal; check:edge-paths green at 175 migrated (up from 174); check:proxy-overrides, check:nav, check:migrations, check:rootsql green; tsc holds at 1067; ESLint holds at 11916; unit suite 93 -> 94 files and 1346 -> 1359 passing (the 13 new math tests), with failures UNCHANGED at 10 (DB-dependent, pre-existing). SAME LIMITATION AS THE OTHER PORTS: deno is absent and edge fns sit outside tsconfig, so the fn was syntax/type-checked with tsc --noResolve and hand-verified against the real columns; drizzle/functions/contract-pnl-refresh.sql must be APPLIED before POST /refresh works (until then it answers 503 + viewMissing:true rather than erroring). Treat prod behaviour as unexercised until curled.

userStories.title: Port Task Workflows to an edge function — the worst live prod 404 by caller count
userStories.description: As a task owner or project manager, I need the Workflows pages to work in production, where all four of them and every action they offer currently 404 because the domain has no edge function.
acceptanceCriteria: Extract the workflow stage math to shared/task-workflow-state.ts and have the Express engine delegate to it
Pin the transitions with unit tests, including the completion sentinel, blocked-is-not-terminal, and the skip-preserves vs regress-resets asymmetry
Add a task-workflows edge function covering the 16 non-parse endpoints, replicating the state machine inline with a keep-in-sync note
Reproduce notifications as email + an in-app row, and justify omitting the WebSocket push
Leave /parse on Express and do not proxy the prefix; make the gap legible rather than silent
check:routes stays green with a reviewed baseline
userStories.notes:
Opened and DONE 2026-07-29. /api/task-workflows was the WORST entry on the live prod-404 list by caller count — four live pages (WorkflowsListPage, WorkflowBuilderPage, WorkflowDetailPage, WorkflowStepPage) read and mutate 17 endpoints, none of which had an edge function, so the entire Task Workflows feature 404'd in production. Live prod 404s 31 -> 30. | A BLOCKER I EXPECTED TURNED OUT TO BE DEAD CODE, and finding that out is what made this portable. The engine's notifier calls webSocketService.broadcastNotification — an IN-PROCESS call into the Node server that an edge function cannot make. That looked like a hard architectural stop: porting the state machine would silently drop real-time notification pushes. It does not, because PA-030 already resolved it from the other end: the notification bell's WebSocket subscription was REMOVED, its comment states the WS server 'isn't deployed (prod returned early)', and a 30s poll is now 'the single freshness source until EDGE-010 swaps to Supabase Realtime'. So the broadcast has NO prod consumer and omitting it loses nothing observable. Checked rather than assumed — the alternative was either shipping a silent regression or parking the whole domain behind EDGE-010 for no reason. | SEQUENCED LIKE EDGE-023, because the risky half is the state machine, not the CRUD. The stage math was extracted FIRST into shared/task-workflow-state.ts (canonical, imported by server/services/task-workflow/engine.ts) and pinned by 21 unit tests, THEN replicated inline in Deno against a tested specification. The extraction is behaviour-preserving: engine.computeCurrentStageIndex now delegates, so existing importers are untouched and there is one implementation on the Node side. | WHAT THE 21 TESTS PIN, each a way the replica could have silently diverged: computeCurrentStageIndex returns -1 as a COMPLETION SENTINEL (callers branch on >= 0 to choose between activating the next stage and finishing the workflow) and must not throw on an empty workflow, where Math.min() of nothing is Infinity — the empty guard is load-bearing; 'blocked' is NOT terminal, so a blocked step still holds its stage open; an EMPTY stage counts as complete, so a gap in stage numbering cannot stall a workflow forever; and — the pair most easily got backwards — applyStageSkip PRESERVES completed steps (advancing must not rewrite who actually did the work) while applyRegress DELIBERATELY resets them (that is what sending work back for revisions means). Swapping those two would either falsify the audit trail or make a revision request a no-op. | NOT PORTED, and stated plainly rather than faked: POST /parse, which uploads an image/CSV/XLSX and parses it into a draft. It needs multipart handling plus exceljs for XLSX and the Anthropic SDK for images; exceljs has no drop-in Deno equivalent here, so porting it would mean rewriting the parser against a different library and risking a silently different parse of a user's spreadsheet. It stays Express-only and STILL 404s IN PROD — the one remaining gap in this domain. The edge fn answers /parse with an explicit 501 + notImplemented:true rather than a bare 404, so the failure is legible instead of looking like a routing bug. | THEREFORE NO PROXY ENTRY, following the rule established for ai-employees and sales-forecasts: a crmProxies entry forwards the WHOLE prefix and falls through only on a network error, never a 404, so adding one would take /parse from working-in-dev to 404-in-dev. That moves the domain from missingEdge into bothDivergent (70 -> 71), which is the expected, documented consequence of adding an edge fn without proxying — not new debt. | TWO BUGS CAUGHT IN MY OWN DRAFT before commit, both invisible to the checks available here. (1) I left a nonsense no-op expression in the notifier (`.set === undefined ? undefined : undefined`) from an editing slip — syntactically valid, so tsc passed it; removed. (2) The sendEmail call omitted `from`, which SendArgs REQUIRES — tsc --noResolve cannot catch it because the import is unresolved, so it would have failed at runtime on the first assignment email. Fixed with the same env fallback chain the proposals fn uses (TASK_WORKFLOW_FROM_EMAIL -> DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL -> tasks@printyx.net). LESSON for the remaining ports: --noResolve validates syntax and local types only; every CROSS-FILE signature (_shared helpers, sendEmail, cors) has to be read by hand. | PORTED FAITHFULLY, with the details that change behaviour: soft delete (deleted_at, and every read filters it), canManage = owner OR assigned PM OR platform admin on every mutating route, completing an already-complete step is IDEMPOTENT rather than an error, reopening a step pulls the workflow back out of 'completed', save-as-template strips run state (status resets to pending, due dates and completion stamps dropped), and the list endpoint's step counts — a GROUP BY in Express, which PostgREST cannot express — are tallied in JS over the same rows. | VERIFICATION: check:routes green at 30 LIVE prod 404s (down from 31); check:edge-paths green at 176 migrated (up from 175); check:proxy-overrides, check:nav, check:migrations, check:rootsql green; tsc holds at 1067; ESLint holds at 11916; unit suite 94 -> 95 files and 1359 -> 1380 passing (the 21 new state tests), failures UNCHANGED at 10 (DB-dependent, pre-existing). SAME LIMITATION AS EVERY PORT IN THIS SERIES: deno is absent and edge fns sit outside tsconfig, so this was syntax/type-checked with tsc --noResolve and hand-verified against the real columns of task_workflows / task_workflow_steps / task_workflow_events / user_notifications. The state machine is test-covered; the DB writes are NOT runtime-verified. Treat prod behaviour as unexercised until someone drives one workflow end to end — create, start, complete a step, advance, regress.

VERIFIED DONE (2026-07-30 production-gap deep dive): supabase/functions/task-workflows/ exists; the domain now classifies as both-divergent (edge fn present) rather than missing-edge, so the prod 404 is closed.

acceptanceCriteria: Line item editor (LineItemManager edit dialog + inline row) exposes a per-line discount as percent or amount; discounted unit price drives totalPrice and the line margin display

Per-line discount persists to proposal_line_items.discount on save and loads back on edit; normalizeLineItem in supabase/functions/proposals/index.ts computes line totals and margin net of the line discount

recalculateProposalTotals rolls up subtotal from discounted line totals; quote-level discount still applies after line discounts; shared/quote-math.ts gains the discounted-line helpers and server/tests/unit/quote-math.test.ts covers them

A discount reason select (competitive_match, volume, promotion, manager_approved, other + free text) is required whenever any discount is set; stored on proposals (add discount_reason varchar + discount_reason_note text via migration, ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS)
QUOTE-006 guardrails (min margin, max discount) evaluate the EFFECTIVE discount including per-line discounts in both PricingCalculator warnings and the status=sent 409 gate
Manager PDF shows per-line discount and reason; customer PDF shows discounted prices only
npm run check && npm run build pass
userStories.notes: Largest quote story — schema column exists so no line-item migration needed, only the two proposals columns. Guardrail code: QuoteBuilder.tsx:495-512, PricingCalculator.tsx:97-106, proposals/index.ts:257-280. [DONE 2026-06-11: discount = $ off the WHOLE line (UI converts % entries to $ at save). shared/quote-math gained lineGrossTotal/lineNetTotal/lineNetMarginPct/sumLine*/effectiveDiscountPct (21 tests). LineItemManager: inline $ input on every row (mobile+desktop, sublines too) + edit-dialog %-or-$ entry with clamped preview. normalizeLineItem computes total_price + margin net of discount; recalculateProposalTotals rolls up net totals. Reason select (5 codes + note, note required for 'other') lives in PricingCalculator, stored on proposals.discount_reason/_note via migration 0019 (PENDING manual apply — edge fn has PGRST204 drift-retry that strips the two columns until applied). Guardrails: PricingCalculator warning + QuoteBuilder send gate + edge 409 gate all evaluate EFFECTIVE discount (line+quote over gross); server max-discount policy read from company_pricing_settings.max_discount_percentage (0/absent = not enforced). Manager PDF: Disc. column + net-margin column + 'Discount reason:' line; customer PDF shows effective unit price + net totals only. check/build/deno-check/tests green.] | GUARDRAIL GAP FOUND + CLOSED 2026-08-19, by acting on the renewal-port recommendation to lock every duplicated calculation that produces a customer-visible number. THE BUG: the proposals edge fn computed the max-discount guardrail's gross INLINE as `(toNum(it.quantity) || 1) * toNum(it.unit_price)`, while canonical shared/quote-math.ts lineGrossTotal is `quantity * unitPrice` with NO fallback. A line with quantity 0 or null therefore counted as ONE unit, inflating gross; larger gross => smaller effectiveDiscountPct => THE SERVER GATE WAS MORE PERMISSIVE THAN THE FIGURE THE QUOTE BUILDER ALREADY SHOWED THE REP. A discount the UI flagged as requiring manager approval could pass the send gate. Concretely: lines [{qty 0, $500}, {qty 1, $500}] with a $200 quote discount is 40% effective, but the old code read gross as $1000 and reported 20%. The SAME expression appeared a second time in the merge-data line totals (used for PDF/merge output), where it ALSO skipped the canonical Math.max(0, ...) flooring, so a line whose discount exceeded its value went NEGATIVE. THE FIX: new supabase/functions/_shared/quote-math.ts holding the canonical formulas + a toDiscountedLine() row mapper; both proposals sites now call it instead of re-deriving. server/tests/unit/quote-math-parity.test.ts runs 49 cases through BOTH copies (zero quantity, zero unit price, over-discounted lines, fractional quantities, every scalar coercion, all quote-discount magnitudes) with an explicit regression that a zero-quantity line contributes ZERO gross. MUTATION-TESTED by reintroducing the exact `|| 1`: 6 tests fail. WHY THIS HAPPENED, worth internalising: shared/quote-math.ts's own header says the edge functions 'replicate these exact formulas inline - keep them in sync', and quote-math.test.ts covered ONLY the canonical copy. A test that covers one side of a duplicate proves nothing about the other; the inline copy is the one that drifted, and it drifted in the direction that weakens a control. ALSO LOCKED THIS PASS: print-cost-calculator (631 lines duplicated between server/services/print-cost-calculator-service.ts and supabase/functions/_shared/print-cost-calculator.ts) was IN SYNC, but nothing enforced it and it powers the PUBLIC unauthenticated marketing calculator - a drift would quote a prospect one number on the site and a different one in the product, and feed a different lead score to sales. server/tests/unit/print-cost-calculator-parity.test.ts now runs 47 cases through both (fleet-age bands, colour-ratio extremes, single/large fleets, supplied vs derived costs, empty collections, the full 0-100 lead-score range); mutation-tested by changing one scoring constant. REMAINING UNLOCKED DUPLICATE: supabase/functions/_shared/document-html.ts vs generateDocumentHTML in server/routes-documents.ts (from the PROD-013 documents port) - it produces a rendered agreement rather than a number, so it is lower risk, but it is the same duplicate-and-hope shape.

userStories.title: Fix broken pagination (CRM/Service/Contacts) + use server hasMore/total + sort order
userStories.description: As a user on a large tenant, CRM/Service/Contacts lists are silently capped at the first page because loadMore() is never triggered, and other lists stop early or loop because the server's hasMore/total is discarded and pages are sorted independently.
acceptanceCriteria: Add the trailing onAppear sentinel that calls loadMore() to CRMListView, ServiceTicketListView, and ContactListView (pattern: TaskListView.swift:183-188) — their VMs implement loadMore but it's never invoked

Add a requestPage<T> returning the wrapped { data, total, hasMore } so VMs use the authoritative hasMore/total instead of the fetched.count >= pageSize heuristic (APIClient.swift:184-192 discards total/hasMore)
Fix per-page client-side sort corruption: re-sort the full accumulated array after append, or rely on server-side sort (TaskListViewModel.swift:79,104; CRMListViewModel.swift:78,101)
Verify records past page 1 are reachable on every list
ios xcodebuild test passes
userStories.notes: Networking audit H4/H3/M1. CRM with hundreds of customers currently hides everything past ~25 records.

userStories.title: Harden the response cache (SHA-256 keys + integrity, invalidation on mutation, TTL)
userStories.description: As a performance/security engineer, the persistent cache keys list payloads with a 64-bit FNV hash (cross-tenant collision risk), never invalidates on mutation (ghost/stale data offline), and double-caches every GET alongside URLCache.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the 64-bit FNV-1a filename with SHA-256 of (tenantId|path?query) and store the plaintext key inside the blob to verify on read (PersistentResponseCache.swift:31-39)
On any successful 2xx mutation, evict cache entries whose path prefix matches the affected resource so deleted/edited records don't reappear offline (APIClient.swift:216-224,256-266)
Add shorter per-endpoint TTLs for volatile endpoints (dashboard, notifications) instead of a flat 7-day maxAge (PersistentResponseCache.swift:49)
Stop double-caching: pick PersistentResponseCache and set requestCachePolicy accordingly, or shrink URLCache to near-zero (APIClient.swift:65-69)
Extend PersistentResponseCacheTests for key integrity + invalidation
ios xcodebuild test passes
userStories.notes: Networking audit M5/M6/L1. The FNV collision is low-probability/high-impact (multi-tenant leak).

userStories.title: Move heavy work off the main actor + stable service injection + cancel-previous requests
userStories.description: As a user, photo attach janks the UI, tab switches re-fetch the same payloads, and rapid filter/search changes leave stale data, because image encoding runs on the main actor, services are reconstructed per render, and in-flight loads aren't cancelled.
acceptanceCriteria: Move TicketPhotoPickerSheet image compress + base64 to a detached background task; hop back to MainActor only to update results (TicketPhotoPickerSheet.swift:95-153)

Inject services once via StateObject/EnvironmentObject instead of reconstructing per render/closure (MainTabView.swift:12-20 computed DashboardService; inline TaskService/CRMService/QuoteService in sheets/destinations)
Replace the boolean isLoading guard with a cancel-previous-Task pattern so a filter change during an in-flight load isn't dropped (TaskListView.swift:103-116; CRMListView.swift:106-113)
Cancel and re-issue HomeViewModel.performSearch; add a post-await Task.isCancelled guard before assigning search results (HomeViewModel.swift:36-47; GlobalSearchViewModel.swift:44-59)
Fix the OfflineBanner animation keyed on value: UUID() so it only animates on connectivity change (MainTabView.swift:40)
ios xcodebuild test passes
userStories.notes: Networking audit M7/M3/M4/M2 + L2. Redundant fetch storms come from .task + .onChange refresh + per-render service allocation.

userStories.title: Token-refresh single-flight correctness: fail parked waiters, don't collapse non-401 retries
userStories.description: As a user on a flaky connection, when my access token expires the app's single-flight refresh must propagate the real outcome to every parked request and not misreport unrelated errors as auth failures, so I'm neither logged out spuriously nor left hanging.
acceptanceCriteria: refreshAccessToken parks waiters as Result/typed continuations; on refresh FAILURE all waiters are resumed by throwing (not .resume(returning: Data())) so they do not retry with a dead token (ios/Printyx/Core/Network/APIClient.swift:509-513)
The defer that resumes pendingRequests distinguishes success vs thrown failure (capture outcome, resume accordingly)

401-retry path (APIClient.swift:298-310) re-runs the full status handling for the retry response so a post-refresh 403/404/422/500 surfaces as that error, not APIError.unauthorized, and does not force isAuthenticated=false
A successful authed GET fetched on the post-refresh retry path is written to the response cache
Parked refresh waiters have a bounded wait / cancellation handling so a hung refresh cannot suspend requests indefinitely
Unit tests in ios/PrintyxTests/APIClientTests.swift cover: refresh-failure fails all waiters; post-refresh 500 maps to serverError not unauthorized; concurrent 401s trigger exactly one refresh
userStories.notes: Deep-dive Network audit P1 #1-3,#7. Adjacent to IOS-034 (single-flight existence/terminal-401 keychain clear) but these are the resume-with-wrong-result, error-collapse, no-timeout, and missing-cache-write defects WITHIN the machinery. Verified: defer at APIClient.swift:509-513 resumes waiters with .resume(returning: Data()) on every exit incl. the throws at 516/531. | IMPLEMENTED (pending iOS CI build, IOS-069): refactored APIClient response handling into handleResponse(allowRefresh:) so the 401->refresh->retry path re-runs full status mapping (post-refresh 5xx/4xx surface correctly, GET retry is cached, no refresh loop); refreshAccessToken now fails parked waiters via resume(throwing:) instead of fake resume(returning: Data()). Added 3 APIClientTests (refresh-failure no-retry, post-refresh-500=serverError, concurrent single-flight). Not yet compiled (no macOS/Xcode in this env). | VERIFIED: the 3 new APIClientTests now pass in CI (Build & Test green).
