SURVEYED ALL 70 POLLING SITES FIRST, and the story overstates the problem: the distribution is 34 at 30s, 19 at 60s, 6 at 5min, and only a handful under 30s. More to the point, TanStack Query defaults refetchIntervalInBackground to FALSE, so an interval already pauses while the tab is hidden. That default is doing most of the work and none of the 30s sites needs touching. THE ONE GENUINELY UNBOUNDED POLL was DatabaseUpdaterPage.tsx, which explicitly set refetchIntervalInBackground: TRUE next to a 5-second interval — so a forgotten background tab kept hitting /api/database-updater/status every five seconds indefinitely, until someone remembered to switch autoRefresh off. Removed the override. Five seconds is the right cadence for watching a migration you are looking at, and the existing toggle already scopes that; no cadence is right for a tab nobody is looking at. BlogSettingsJobs.tsx polled TWO endpoints every 5s unconditionally — 1,440 requests an hour whether the queue was busy or empty. Now adaptive: 5s while anything is queued or active, 60s when the queue is idle. Implemented with refetchInterval as a FUNCTION, which react-query v5 supports and which reads the query's own latest data; my first version stored the interval in state and synced it from an effect, which needs an extra render to react to its own response and leaves two sources of truth for one number. TWO OF THE THREE FILES AC2 NAMES NEEDED NOTHING, which is worth recording so nobody re-opens them: SystemSecurity.tsx:26 was a 10s poll of /api/admin/system/health that nothing read and that resolved to no endpoint on either host — already removed under AUDIT-019, where it is filed as part of a page built entirely from literals. MobileLogsViewer.tsx:114 polls at 5s but ONLY behind a user-controlled autoRefresh toggle and without the background override, so it already stops when the tab is hidden and when the user says so. A 5-second poll is not a defect when the user asked for it and it pauses on blur; the defect is the one that does neither. AC1 (virtualize the CRM grids) NOT ATTEMPTED. It is a behavioural change to CrmDataTable and BusinessRecordsDataTable — the two components every CRM list renders through, and the ones AUDIT-014 part 10 found row-click regressions in twice — and it needs a measurement first (what row counts do real tenants actually hit?) that this environment cannot take. Swapping the table implementation under four list pages on a LOW-priority performance story, with no evidence anyone is hitting a slow grid, is the wrong trade. Left as the open half. VERIFIED: tsc holds at 496, build passes, 168 test files / 3658 tests, eslint on both touched files unchanged at 4 pre-existing errors, check:query-states unchanged.

userStories.title: Add loading and error states to data-fetching pages
userStories.description: As a user, I need pages to show loading and error UI instead of rendering blank on a failed/slow request. 24 pages call useQuery with no error handling.
acceptanceCriteria: Add isLoading + isError/error UI to the 24 identified pages (ExecutiveDashboard, FinancialIntelligenceDashboard, SalesCommandCenter, PlatformAnalytics, ...)
Guard data.map against undefined to prevent render crashes
Provide a retry affordance on error
Establish a shared query-state wrapper component
userStories.notes: [FRONTEND/MEDIUM] Source: automated code review 2026-07-11 (branch claude/web-app-code-review-y1eqny). | 2026-08-27 PASS 1. AC4 (the shared wrapper) is DONE and CI-gated; the per-page work is started, not finished, so passes stays false. THE COUNT IN THE DESCRIPTION IS WRONG AND LOW. It says 24 pages. Measured against files REACHABLE from the Vite entry - unreachable pages cannot show a user anything, and 39 of the files calling useQuery are orphaned per AUDIT-018 - the real figure is 226 components and 479 useQuery calls with no error handling. 23 of those read neither isError NOR isLoading, which is the sharp subset: they render their full layout the instant they mount, so a failed request, a slow one and a genuinely empty account are all the same screen. AC4 - client/src/components/ui/query-state.tsx. The primitives already existed (ErrorState with retry, LoadingState, EmptyState); what was missing was the thing that composes them and enforces an ORDER. QueryState takes the query and a render prop, so `data` is not in scope until it is defined - which closes AC2 by construction rather than by remembering a `data?.` guard - and an error can never fall through to the empty branch. QueryStates is the dashboard shape: several queries, one page-level state, retry refetches EVERY failed query rather than the first. It deliberately does not wrap itself in a Card; these pages already nest cards several deep. 20 tests, each branch pinned including the combinations a real query produces (loading WITH stale data, error WITH stale data). PAGES DONE (4 of the 23, all named in AC1): SalesCommandCenter, PlatformAnalytics, ExecutiveDashboard, FinancialIntelligenceDashboard. In each, the filters stay OUTSIDE the wrapper - re-picking a period or timeframe is how a user retries - and only the derived sections go inside. PlatformAnalytics is the case that justifies the story: every read is written `revenueMetrics?.mrr || 89000`, a hardcoded fallback per field, so a failed request did not render blank, it rendered a confident fake dashboard - $89,000 MRR, 14.1% growth, twelve months of invented chart data - with nothing on screen saying the request had failed. FOUND EN ROUTE, AND IT WAS NOT THIS STORY: a ~1-in-4 FLAKE IN THE FULL TEST SUITE, present on clean HEAD. server/tests/unit/crm-kpi-pagination.test.ts failed about half the time and passed in isolation. Root cause in client/src/lib/mobile-logger.ts: it builds its singleton at IMPORT time, so a throw in the constructor happens at module scope and takes down every file that transitively imports queryClient.ts. It had four separate `typeof window !== undefined` guards, each of which then reached for something else - document, window.location. That holds in a browser and in plain Node and fails in between, and vitest runs every file in ONE fork (singleFork: true) where something defines a global window with no document and no location. Verified directly with a probe test: window=object, document=undefined inside the suite, both undefined when the same file runs alone. Patching one guard just moved the throw to the next line, so the fix is one hasBrowserGlobals() predicate asking for the three globals this file actually uses. 8 consecutive full-suite runs green afterwards, against ~1 in 4 failing before. client/src/lib/mobile-logger.env.test.ts pins it, and was verified to FAIL 3 of its 4 cases with the fix reverted. ALSO: vitest.config.ts now sets esbuild.jsx=automatic. tsconfig says "jsx": "preserve" because Vite's React plugin does the real transform, esbuild reads that and falls back to the CLASSIC transform, and every .tsx test dies with "React is not defined" - including inside components that correctly do not import React. Nothing had hit it because query-state.test.tsx is the repo's first .tsx test. Component tests were not possible here before this line. RATCHET ADDED (check:query-states, wired into CI): fails when a REACHABLE component calls useQuery and neither reads isError nor uses the wrapper. Baseline 226. Mutation-tested both ways - a new unhandled page fails by path, and reverting SalesCommandCenter resurfaces it. This matters more than the four pages: without it the other 222 quietly become 230. Its blind spots are in its header - it checks for a NAME, not for good error UI; a file handling one of five queries counts as handled; error handling inside a child component is invisible to it. VERIFIED: tsc holds at 496, build passes, 167 test files / 3654 tests, check:orphans, check:nav and check:no-mocks green, eslint on the touched pages unchanged at 52 pre-existing errors with the two new files at zero. NEXT: the remaining 19 of the 23 blind-on-both pages, in rough order of what a wrong number costs - CrmGoalsDashboard (7 queries), AdvancedReporting (5), GdprComplianceDashboard (4), AdminCommandCenter, SecurityDashboard, admin/RootAdminSecurity (3 each). | 2026-08-27 PASS 2. Eight more of the blind-on-both pages: CrmGoalsDashboard (7 queries), AdvancedReporting (5), GdprComplianceDashboard (4), AdminCommandCenter, SecurityDashboard, admin/RootAdminSecurity (3 each), admin/TenantManagement, admin/UserManagement (2 each). Ratchet 226 -> 218; 12 of the original 23 are now handled. TWO OF THESE WERE ACTIVE ALL-CLEARS, NOT BLANK SCREENS, and they are the strongest evidence for the story. AdminCommandCenter guarded its pending-task list with nothing but `pendingTasks && length > 0`, so a FAILED poll rendered a green check and "All caught up! No pending administrative tasks" - on the page an admin opens precisely to find out what needs attention. CrmGoalsDashboard’s ConversionInsights did the same with "No conversion data available yet - data will appear once sales activities are tracked", which a manager reads as "my reps logged nothing". Both keep the exact same wording, now only when the request actually succeeded and came back empty. That is the whole point of the wrapper’s branch order. SecurityDashboard and RootAdminSecurity are the same shape with a worse blast radius: both poll every 30 seconds, and a failed poll rendered zero failed logins, an empty event feed and no active threats. On a security page that is not an empty state, it is an all-clear. PLACEMENT RULE APPLIED THROUGHOUT: the wrapper goes around the DERIVED sections only. Filters, date pickers and action buttons stay outside, because re-picking a period is how a user retries and a Create button has nothing to do with the failed read. AdminCommandCenter needed this at tab granularity rather than page level - only two of its four tabs consume the queries, so Quick Actions and Guided Workflows (static admin controls) stay usable while Pending Tasks and Monitoring show the failure. Wrapping the whole page would have hidden working controls. TWO REGRESSIONS I INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT BY DIFFING ESLINT BEFORE AND AFTER, worth recording because the second is a trap anyone doing the remaining pages will hit: (1) AdminCommandCenter kept a now-dead `pendingTasks` const after the rows moved to the render prop. (2) Converting `const { data: x = [] }` to `const x = q.data ?? []` moves the default INTO THE COMPONENT BODY, where it is a fresh array identity every render; CrmGoalsDashboard feeds goalProgress into two useMemo dependency arrays, so react-hooks/exhaustive-deps flagged it by name and the memos were defeated. Fixed with a module-level `const EMPTY: never[] = []` - never[] rather than any[], which is assignable to every array type and does not add a no-explicit-any error. Final eslint on the eight files is 100 errors / 0 warnings, exactly the pre-existing count. CORRECTION TO PASS 1’S NOTE: it recorded "167 test files / 3654 tests". That measurement was taken before mobile-logger.env.test.ts existed - the real figure with it is 168 files / 3658 tests. Both green; the count was stale, not the result. VERIFIED: tsc holds at 496, build passes in 43s, 168 test files / 3658 tests, check:query-states at 218, check:orphans, check:nav and check:no-mocks green. REMAINING of the original 23: components/analytics/{ConversionInsights,PipelineTrendWidgets}, components/dashboard/KpiSummaryBar, components/layout/{command-palette,enhanced-notification-bell}, components/quotes/quote-templates, components/workflows/AssigneeSelect, pages/AdminHub, pages/PlatformCohortAnalysis, pages/SetupWizard, pages/admin/SystemSecurity. Most are single-query components rather than dashboards, so QueryState (not QueryStates) fits them, and several are pickers where the right error UI is inline rather than a full-width panel. | 2026-08-27 PASS 3 — the blind-on-both list is CLEARED. All 23 files that read neither isError nor isLoading are now handled or documented; ratchet 218 -> 208. These eleven were components rather than dashboards, and each needed a different answer, which is the argument against doing this class with a codemod. INLINE, NOT PANELS: AssigneeSelect reports failure as a ROW INSIDE the dropdown (a picker cannot host a full-width ErrorState) — before, a failed /api/users left it holding only "Unassigned", indistinguishable from a tenant with no other users, so a workflow step silently could not be assigned. KpiSummaryBar keeps its four-tile shape and puts the reason underneath, because it is embedded in other pages and a panel would break the host layout. command-palette already handled loading via isFetching but told a failed search "No results found for X" — a claim about the user’s data, not the request. enhanced-notification-bell said "No unread notifications"; note its queryFn already falls back to /api/performance/alerts, so reaching isError means BOTH endpoints failed, which makes the error worth showing rather than swallowing. TWO WIDGETS VANISHED RATHER THAN FAILED. components/analytics/{ConversionInsights,PipelineTrendWidgets} inject fixtures through `select: (data) => data || {…invented numbers}`, and select only runs on SUCCESS — so an empty-but-successful response showed made-up conversion rates as measurements, while a real error left data undefined, hit `return null`, and removed the widget from the page entirely. A component that disappears is the hardest kind of wrong to notice. Error path fixed; the fixtures themselves are left and flagged on AUDIT-019, because deleting them changes what the component renders on a good day. ONE FILE STAYS BASELINED ON PURPOSE, and the reason is now a comment in the file so nobody "fixes" it: SetupWizard’s queryFn catches its own failure and returns { currentStep: 0, completedSteps: [], completed: false }, so the query can never reach isError. A first-time user whose saved wizard state cannot be read should start at step 0, not be shown an error about state they have never had. Adding a branch that cannot fire would be worse than the gap. AND ONE FILE TURNED OUT NOT TO BE A CR-033 PROBLEM AT ALL — see the new AUDIT-019. pages/admin/SystemSecurity.tsx is a routed 442-line page with ZERO dynamic values: every number, status and date is a literal, including "SSL/TLS Status: Active — Valid until 2025-12-31", a date eight months in the past rendered green. Its one useQuery polled /api/admin/system/health every 10 seconds, read by nothing, at a URL that exists on neither backend (the admin edge fn serves `system-health` as one segment; no Express route matches; /api/admin is not proxied). Only the dead poll was removed here. Adding an error state to a page with no data would be theatre, and rewriting a routed admin security console is a product decision, not a sweep. ALSO caught the `?? []` / useMemo trap a second time, in quote-templates — same fix, a module-level constant. It is now recorded twice because it will happen again to anyone converting `const { data: x = [] }`. VERIFIED: tsc holds at 496, build passes in 42s, 168 test files / 3658 tests, check:query-states at 208, eslint on the eleven touched files 48 errors / 0 warnings (from 49/0 — one dead const removed, and the one warning I introduced fixed rather than left). WHAT REMAINS on this story: 208 baseline entries, all of which DO render a loading state — the sharp subset that showed nothing at all is done. AC1 named 24 pages; the measured figure was 226 files, so the story is about a fifth complete by file count and complete by severity. The ratchet is what keeps the rest from growing. | 2026-08-27 THE FLAKE HAS A ROOT CAUSE, and it is the SOURCE of the one I patched earlier in this story rather than a second unrelated one. The previous pass recorded "one full-suite run reported 5 failing tests in 1 file; seven consecutive runs green; could not reproduce". Running `npx vitest run --sequence.shuffle` reproduced it on the FIRST attempt — the trigger is file ORDER, which vitest varies, so repeating the default run is close to useless for this class and shuffling is the tool. THE POLLUTER: client/src/lib/cookie-consent.test.ts installed `window`, `localStorage` and `navigator` on globalThis in beforeEach and its afterEach cleared only the localStorage store. vitest runs this repo in ONE fork (pool: forks, singleFork: true), so all three outlived the file and were visible to every file scheduled after it. Found by trapping assignment with a temporary defineProperty setter in server/tests/setup.ts that logged a stack — the stack named cookie-consent.test.ts:48 directly, which beat guessing. IT CAUSED BOTH FAILURES I HAVE SEEN THIS SESSION, and the earlier fix treated the symptom: (1) mobile-logger.ts guards on `typeof window !== undefined` then reaches for document and window.location — already fixed with hasBrowserGlobals(), which is still correct on its own merits since a window-without-document is a real environment; (2) isomorphic-dompurify picks its BROWSER implementation when a global window exists, and that implementation has no .sanitize without a document, so server/middleware/input-sanitization.ts threw "DOMPurify.sanitize is not a function" and took 4 tests with it. The second one is the more interesting failure mode: the security middleware did not silently skip sanitizing, it threw — which is the right way round, and it is worth noting that Node has no global window so production was never affected. FIX: cookie-consent.test.ts now captures the prior property descriptor for each of the three globals and restores it (or deletes the key) in afterEach. VERIFIED CAUSALLY, not just observationally: with the fix reverted, the first shuffled run fails; with it applied, six consecutive shuffled runs are 168 files / 3658 tests green, plus the default-order suite. LESSON FOR THE NEXT ONE: a test that writes to globalThis must restore it, because this repo shares a single fork. Grep for `globalThis as` assignments in test files before trusting an order-dependent failure to be anything more exotic. SWEPT FOR SIBLINGS, since the mechanism is now known: two other test files assign to globalThis without restoring — server/tests/unit/error-response-parity.test.ts:40 and server/tests/integration/edge-file-delete.test.ts:100, both setting a fake `Deno`. LEFT ALONE DELIBERATELY, having checked rather than assumed: nothing in server/, shared/ or client/ branches on `typeof Deno`, and the supabase/_shared modules read Deno.env unconditionally, so a leaked stub can only help them. Removing it risks breaking a test that depends on the leak for no present benefit. Recorded so the next order-dependent failure has a second suspect ready.

userStories.title: Type useQuery generics to stop silent contract drift
userStories.description: As a developer, I need useQuery calls typed with an explicit generic so field renames/contract drift are caught at compile time instead of silently rendering empty/mock data. ~115 untyped calls remain.
acceptanceCriteria: Add response-type generics to the 115 untyped useQuery calls, prioritizing pages that fall back to mock data
Derive types from shared schema where possible
Contributes to the QUALITY-002 typecheck ratchet
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes:
[FRONTEND/MEDIUM] Source: automated code review 2026-07-11 (branch claude/web-app-code-review-y1eqny). Same pattern documented in CLAUDE.md (BATCH 9/12). | 2026-08-27: FIRST BATCH, and typing five queries found three real defects, which is the argument for the rest of the story. COUNT CORRECTED: the story says ~115 untyped useQuery calls; it is 181 today against 527 typed. THE MECHANISM, for whoever picks this up: apiRequest is declared apiRequest<T = any>, so an untyped useQuery hands back `any` and every field read below it goes unchecked. Changing that default to `unknown` would surface the whole class at once, but it would add hundreds of errors and break the QUALITY-002 ratchet, so this is per-page instead. TYPES ARE TRANSCRIBED FROM THE HANDLER, not from what the page reads - client/src/types/sales-reports.ts records the five shapes supabase/functions/reports/handlers/sales.ts actually returns, including that quota and commissions are DEGRADED (no sales_quotas table, no commissions table), so a page showing 0% attainment is showing unknown rather than nothing-sold. A type asserted from the reading side would have locked in the bugs below instead of exposing them. DEFECT 1 - LEADERBOARD RENDERED BLANK. The report returns { userId, userName, revenue, deals, pipeline, activities, rank }; LeaderboardTable wants { userInitials, metricValue, metricLabel, dealsClosed, pipelineValue }. Only userId, userName and rank overlapped, so against live data every avatar showed blank initials and every metric cell was empty - the podium at the top of that tab reads userInitials directly. Now mapped, with metricLabel taken from the metric the server reports rather than hardcoded. DEFECT 2 - PIPELINE FUNNEL SHOWED $NaN. PipelineFunnel required averageDealSize and conversionRate; the report returns neither, so the detailed view printed Avg: $NaN and a conversion badge that never appeared. Both are derivable from what IS returned, so the component computes them when absent instead of demanding them - and the inline Win Rate column, which had its own copy of the conversion arithmetic (unguarded against an empty first stage), now uses the same one definition. DEFECT 3 - QUOTA CARD LIED WHEN LOADING. It read (quotaData?.quota?.actualRevenue / 1000 || 0): the optional chain sat INSIDE the division, so no data gave undefined / 1000 = NaN and the || 0 quietly turned that into a zero. It read as "you have billed nothing" when the truth was "the report has not loaded". All three were invisible while `any` flowed through, and all three were reported by tsc within seconds of adding the generics. VERIFIED: tsc holds at 496 (the three fixes cancel the errors the generics surfaced), npm run build passes, 157 test files / 3455 tests, check:nav and check:no-mocks green, eslint unchanged on the touched files (4 pre-existing errors, none new). REMAINING: 176 untyped calls. The dashboards/ directory is the richest seam - SalesManager, SalesSupervisor, ServiceManager, ServiceSupervisor, TeamLead and Technician all follow this exact shape against the team/ and service/ report handlers. | 2026-08-27 BATCH 2 - the manager and supervisor sales dashboards, 8 queries, and this batch found a CRASH rather than a blank. One handler serves both personas: supabase/functions/reports/handlers/scoped-sales.ts answers /sales-manager/regional-{pipeline,performance,quota,activity} and /sales-supervisor/location/{pipeline-overview,performance,quota,activity} with the same code and only the scoping unit changed, so client/src/types/scoped-sales-reports.ts is one set of types for both. Note the handler calls every unit collection `regions` even when the unit is a location; the type keeps that name because renaming it would lie about the wire. DEFECT 4 - THE SUPERVISOR QUOTA TAB THREW. LocationQuotaTracker took props as `any` and ran summary.overallAttainment.toFixed(0) inside a {summary && ...} guard. The endpoint does send a summary - { totalQuota, totalActual, averageAttainment } - so the guard passes, overallAttainment is undefined, and .toFixed throws a TypeError during render. Not a blank card: the tab threw. It also mapped a `quotas` array and an insights.attainmentDistribution that do not exist. DEFECT 5 - EVERY OTHER FIELD ON BOTH PAGES WAS WRONG TOO, and the pattern is that the pages were written against a design doc rather than the handler. The manager page read summary.totalRegions/totalPipeline, quota summary.overallAttainment/regionsOnTrack/regionsAtRisk, performance rows of ranking/regionName/locationCount/teamSize/dealsWon/totalRevenue, quota rows of regionId/regionName/locationCount/quotaAmount/actualRevenue/onTrack/attainmentPercent, and an `activities` collection with regionId/regionName/totalActivities/activitiesPerRep. Not one of those names appears in the handler. The supervisor page and its four presentational components (LocationPipelineGrid, LocationPerformanceTable, LocationQuotaTracker, LocationActivityChart, all typed `any`) were the same story, including a location x stage matrix built off a `pipelines[]` collection the endpoint has never returned - and cannot, since it sends per-stage totals across units (aggregated) and per-unit totals without stages (byUnit), so that matrix is not derivable here at all. All four components are now typed against the real contract and show the two cuts of the data that exist. DEFECT 6 - THE MANAGER DASHBOARD HAD NO DATE PICKER. All four of its queries key on a `dateRange` state that nothing ever set, so the range was frozen to the current month; format/subDays sat imported and unused as the leftovers. Added the picker the supervisor page already has. TWO PLACES WHERE THE HONEST RENDER IS "UNKNOWN", NOT A NUMBER: the quota endpoint has no non-degraded path at all (scoped-sales.ts:75 answers it with degradedQuota() unconditionally because there is no sales_quotas table), so both quota tabs now say quotas are not set up instead of drawing an empty list under a 0%; and the supervisor at-risk banner is gone rather than repointed - it was gated on a field that does not exist, and the only live substitute, attainmentRanges.atRisk, is set to regions.length unconditionally, so reviving it would have claimed every location was below 75% of a target nobody set. quotaAttainment columns are dropped for the same reason: a permanent 0% badge reads as failure. VERIFIED: tsc holds at 496, npm run build passes in 45s, 166 test files / 3634 tests passing, eslint on the six touched files goes 22 errors -> 0 (17 of those were the `any` props and unused imports this batch removed). PROCESS WARNING FOR THE NEXT BATCH: do NOT run `npm run format:write` - it is repo-wide and prettier is not clean at HEAD, so it rewrote 156 unrelated files (docs, mobile/, edge fns, a drizzle snapshot) into the working tree and had to be reverted file by file. Use `npx prettier --write <the files you touched>`. REMAINING: 168 untyped useQuery calls against 540 typed. Still in the dashboards/ seam: ServiceManager, ServiceSupervisor, TeamLead and Technician, against the service/ and team/ report handlers. | 2026-08-27 BATCH 3 - the manager and supervisor SERVICE dashboards, 8 queries. Same one-handler-two-personas structure as batch 2 (scoped-service.ts serves /service-manager/regional-* and /service-supervisor/location-*), so client/src/types/scoped-service-reports.ts is one set of types for both, and the per-unit collection is again `regions` under every scope. DEFECT 7 - THREE OF THE FOUR TABS COULD NEVER HAVE SHOWN ANYTHING, and not because of a renamed key: the data does not exist in the schema. (a) The Overview tab drew "Service Calls by Priority" off an `aggregated` array of { priority, avgCallsPerRegion, avgDuration }; the endpoint has no priority dimension at all, it buckets by unit and status. Repointed to the open/in-progress/completed volume it does return. (b) The SLA tab mapped `slaData.slas`; scoped-service.ts:70 answers `sla` with degradedSla() unconditionally because service_tickets has no sla_deadline column - the original SQL was speculative - so there is no non-degraded path and the tab was permanently blank. Now says so, and names what would have to be recorded to make the report real. (c) The Activity tab was an HOURS breakdown - travel, diagnostic, repair, documentation, total, utilization rate. Nothing in the schema records technician hours. The endpoint counts business_record_activities of type service_call/note/task per unit, so a count and a share is what it shows. DEFECT 8 - THE FIRST-TIME-FIX KPI WAS A DESIGN, NOT A METRIC. Both pages showed summary.avgFirstTimeFixRate over an insights.healthStatus caption, and the performance rows showed firstTimeFixRate/slaCompliance/utilizationRate. The handler sets ftfRate, slaCompliance and avgSatisfaction to null on EVERY row and returns degraded:{firstTimeFix,slaCompliance,customerSatisfaction}. Replaced with completion rate and mean resolution time, which are computed from real columns (scheduled_date -> resolved_at). DEFECT 6 AGAIN - both service dashboards had the same frozen date range as the sales manager page: four queries keyed on `dateRange`, nothing ever called setDateRange. Picker added to both. The two pages were near-identical modulo the region/location noun, so they are now generated from one template - they had already drifted apart in small ways (the manager read performanceData.regions, the supervisor performanceData.locations, for the same endpoint). VERIFIED: tsc holds at 496, build passes in 44s, 166 test files / 3634 tests passing, eslint clean on all three files. REMAINING: 160 untyped useQuery calls. Next in this seam: TeamLeadDashboard, TeamLeadDashboardNew (two copies - check whether both are routed), TechnicianDashboard, DirectorDashboard, ExecutiveDashboard. | 2026-08-27 CORRECTION TO BATCHES 2 AND 3, and a warning for whoever picks the next batch: THE ENTIRE client/src/pages/dashboards/ DIRECTORY IS UNROUTED. All 11 role dashboards (SalesRep, SalesManager, SalesSupervisor, ServiceManager, ServiceSupervisor, TeamLead, TeamLeadDashboardNew, Technician, Director, Executive, PlatformAdmin) are imported by nothing - zero references outside the directory itself, no React.lazy in App.tsx, no Route, no entry in navigation-permissions.ts - so they are tree-shaken out and no chunk for any of them appears in dist/assets. I checked this only AFTER batches 2 and 3. The defects those notes describe are real properties of the code and the fixes are correct, but nothing rendered blank and no tab threw FOR A USER, because no user can reach these pages. Read the impact claims in those two notes as "would, if routed", not as an outage. Batch 1 (SalesRepDashboard) has the same caveat. THE SAME CHECK APPLIES TO THE ENDPOINTS: outside pages/dashboards/, nothing in the client calls /api/reports/{sales-manager,sales-supervisor,service-manager,service-supervisor,director}/* at all. Those 8 scoped-sales + 8 scoped-service routes and the director routes have no live caller. The report surface that IS live is /api/reports/team/* (TeamStatsWidget, TeamLeaderboard, SalesPerformanceAnalytics), /api/reports/sales/personal/* (PipelineFunnel) and /api/reports/executive/dashboard (pages/ExecutiveDashboard.tsx - the ROUTED one at pages/ExecutiveDashboard.tsx, NOT pages/dashboards/ExecutiveDashboard.tsx, which is the dead copy). Two separate questions fall out of this and both are product calls, not mine: whether the role dashboards should be wired up (they are a coherent, mostly-working feature now that the shapes match) or deleted, and whether the scoped report endpoints should stay. PROCESS RULE ADDED: before typing a page under this story, confirm it is reachable - grep for an import outside its own directory. Typing a dead page is still a strict improvement but it is not the defect-finding this story is worth doing for. | 2026-08-27 BATCH 4 - Billing.tsx, the first ROUTED page under this story (/settings/billing, React.lazy at App.tsx:138). Four untyped queries in, two dead, two carrying user-visible bugs. DEFECT 9 - THE TRIAL BANNER TOLD EVERY TRIALING TENANT THEIR TRIAL ENDS "N/A". The queryFn bridged four key spellings - trial_end, trialEnd, is_trialing, isTrialing - and the endpoint sends none of them. TrialManagementService.getTrialStatus returns { userId, tenantId, trialStartDate, trialEndDate, daysRemaining, status }, so the bridge resolved trialEnd to null on every load and the card fell through to its N/A branch. status and daysRemaining, the other two fields the banner reads, DO exist - which is why the banner appeared at all and why the bug looked like a data problem rather than a key mismatch. The field is trialEndDate. DEFECT 10 - `response || {}` DEFEATED THE EMPTY STATE BELOW IT. GET /api/billing/info returns the default payment method’s billing_details jsonb, or NULL when the tenant has no default method. The queryFn coerced that null to {}, which is truthy, so `{billingInfo ? ... : "No billing address on file"}` always took the populated branch: a tenant with no address got the full address layout reading "Not set" and "No address on file" instead of the one-line empty state. null is the endpoint’s real answer and now reaches the render. DEFECT 11 - THE PAGE FETCHED PAYMENT METHODS ON EVERY LOAD AND THREW THEM AWAY. The Payment Methods card is a "coming soon" placeholder that renders neither the list nor a delete control, but the query and a delete mutation were both still wired. Removed rather than typed - the correct resolution for a dead query - and they are in git history if the card returns. DEFECT 12 - EDITING AN ADDRESS ON FILE OPENED A BLANK FORM. `useEffect` was imported and never used, the leftover of exactly this; changing one line of an address meant retyping all six. The form now resets from billingInfo when the dialog opens. The invoices query was already correct - normalizeInvoices (AUDIT-011) does the casing, the decimal-string coercion and the invoice_status-over-status pick - so it only needed the NormalizedInvoice generic, which removed the `invoice: any` from the table map. VERIFIED: tsc holds at 496, build passes in 43s, 166 test files / 3634 tests passing, check:routes green, eslint on both files 4 errors -> 0. REMAINING: 156 untyped useQuery calls. Highest counts on routed pages: RoleManagement (5), EnhancedOnboardingForm (5), TaskHub (4), GdprComplianceDashboard (4), hooks/useExternalIntegrations (4).
PROGRESS 2026-08-29 - A WORKED INSTANCE, AND IT WAS A CRASH RATHER THAN DRIFT. TaskHub.tsx did `const { data: tasks = [] } = useQuery({ queryFn: async () => apiRequest('/api/tasks') })` and passed `tasks` to MyTasksView, whose first statement is `tasks.filter(...)`. The tasks edge function answers GET / with `{ data, total, page, limit }`, so `tasks` was an object, an object has no .filter, and the default tab of the page threw on load. Six routes reach it - /tasks, /task-hub, /task-management, /basic-tasks, /my-tasks and /ai-task-scheduling - and /api/tasks is in crmProxies, so dev and prod both hit the same shape. Fixed by wrapping the tasks, projects and users queries in extractRecords, which accepts a bare array too and is therefore correct against either backend.

WHY NO EXISTING GUARD SAW IT, which is the story's whole thesis: apiRequest returns `any`, so tsc had nothing to compare; `= []` in the destructure makes it LOOK defended, and it only defends against undefined; and no test renders the page. A useQuery generic would have caught it, which is what this story is for - the untyped queryFn is the hole, not the missing generic on its own.

CASING WAS THE SECOND HALF OF THE SAME BUG. handlers/tasks.ts returned raw PostgREST rows while every component reads task.dueDate, task.completionPercentage, task.timeTracked and task.assignedTo, so those cells rendered blank next to a title that worked. mapTask already ACCEPTED camelCase on writes, so only the reads were asymmetric; toCamel now runs on all four read paths, matching handlers/time-entries.ts which already did it.

server/tests/unit/task-hub-list-shape.test.ts locks both halves and was mutation-tested against both reverts. The absence assertion in it strips comments first, since this repo has three times reported its own explanation as the defect.

userStories.title: Fix kpis / reporting / scheduled-reports dev-only pathPrefix proxies → hard 404 in production
userStories.description: As a user of KPI tiles, the Reporting Engine, and Scheduled Reports, I need those to work in production, not only in dev.
acceptanceCriteria: Add server.ts route overrides so kpis, reporting, and scheduled-reports resolve to the reports fn WHILE preserving the discriminator segment the reports dispatcher keys on (mirror dashboard->dashboard-widgets, not the segment-stripping public->public-calculator pattern).
Verify /kpis/summary, /reporting/reports/:id/data, /scheduled-reports/:id/toggle round-trip against functions.printyx.net.
Add a check flagging any crmProxies {fn,pathPrefix} entry whose URL segment lacks a matching server.ts override.
userStories.notes: [ROUTING/BLOCKER] Source: platform audit 2026-07-12 (branch claude/platform-audit-prd-e5lp6t). server/middleware/edge-function-proxy.ts:289-319 rewrite these via dev-only pathPrefix to the reports fn; no kpis/reporting/scheduled edge dir and no server.ts override exist, so prod resolves functionName=kpis -> 404. Callers: role-dashboard-config.ts:152, EnhancedReportsHub.tsx, ScheduledReportsDashboard.tsx. | COMPLETE 2026-07-23 — the prod-only 404 on KPI tiles, the Reporting Engine, and Scheduled Reports is closed. ROOT CAUSE confirmed: edge-function-proxy.ts routes /api/{kpis,reporting,scheduled-reports} to the reports fn via DEV-ONLY {fn:"reports",pathPrefix} entries; there is no kpis/reporting/scheduled-reports function directory, so in prod the Coolify dispatcher (supabase/functions/server.ts) resolved functionName=segment0 and 404ed. FIX (AC bullet 1): added a server.ts route-override block. The reports dispatcher keys firstSegment = pathParts[0] (after stripPrefix, which only strips a leading /reports and is idempotent) on "kpis"/"reporting"/"scheduled" — so the discriminator segment MUST survive the strip. Mirrored the leases / ai-employee pattern (rename + stripSegments = 0), NOT the segment-stripping public->public-* pattern: kpis and reporting map functionName -> "reports" with stripSegments = 0 (URL segment already equals the discriminator); scheduled-reports additionally rewrites pathParts[0] = "scheduled" (the reports fn keys on "scheduled", matching the dev proxy pathPrefix:"/scheduled"). Traced all three end-to-end: /kpis/summary -> reports firstSegment "kpis" -> handleKpis; /reporting/reports/:id/data -> "reporting" -> handleReporting; /scheduled-reports/:id/toggle -> "scheduled" -> handleScheduledReports. FIX (AC bullet 3): added scripts/check-proxy-overrides.mjs + npm run check:proxy-overrides, wired into ci.yml next to check:edge-paths. It parses every object-form crmProxies {fn,pathPrefix} entry and fails when the first URL segment (and, for multi-segment public/* prefixes, the sub-path discriminator) has no matching server.ts functionName override — the exact dev-works/prod-404s gap. Passes 6/6 now; mutation-tested: removing my override makes it exit 1 and name exactly kpis/reporting/scheduled-reports; restoring passes. VERIFICATION: check:lint ratchet holds at 12003 (server.ts is Deno/eslint-ignored; the new .mjs lints clean); the new check is green. NOT RUN (AC bullet 2): the /kpis/summary, /reporting/reports/:id/data, /scheduled-reports/:id/toggle round-trips against functions.printyx.net cannot be exercised from here (no prod/deploy access, and these prefixes are not proxied in a way dev routes to the edge fn) — the routing is proven statically by the segment trace + stripPrefix idempotency, but the handlers behind it have never been exercised in prod; confirm with one curl per prefix post-deploy.

userStories.description: As a user viewing a customer, I need the detail tabs (invoices, tickets, equipment, financials, supplies, meters, activities, 360) to load real data in production.
acceptanceCriteria: Add sub-resource routing to the customers edge fn (or dedicated fns) for /:id/{invoices,service-tickets,service-calls,equipment,contracts,financial-summary,payments,aging,supply-orders,devices,metrics/history,360-view,activities}, tenant-scoped.
Return the array/object shapes each component expects; no branch falls through to the single-customer response for a multi-segment path.
Smoke-test Customer Detail tabs against the functions host; remove the dev-only Express sub-routes once parity holds.
userStories.notes:
[ROUTING/BLOCKER] Source: platform audit 2026-07-12 (branch claude/platform-audit-prd-e5lp6t). supabase/functions/customers/index.ts implements only / and /:id CRUD; customerId=pathParts[1] ignores the sub-segment so /customers/:id/invoices returns the customer object. Sub-paths like /360-view,/financial-summary,/payments,/aging,/activities have no Express route either (broken in dev too). Not in the missing-edge baseline (parity heuristic stops at first segment).

--- 2026-08-30 --- DONE. Nine sub-resources routed, nine raw fetches converted,
and the shapes the tabs read are what they now get.

THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS HELD EXACTLY. customerId was
`pathParts[0] === 'customers' ? pathParts[1] : pathParts[0]` and nothing read
the segment after it, so every Customer Detail tab fell into the
single-customer branch and got the CUSTOMER OBJECT at 200. A component that maps
over an object renders an empty list and reports nothing, which is why this
survived an audit: there is no error to see.

TWO DEFECTS, NOT ONE. Nine of the calls were raw fetch(), which never passes
through getApiUrl - in production they hit the Cloudflare Pages origin, got
index.html at 200, and threw inside .json() (PROD-013). All nine were already in
docs/raw-api-fetch-baseline.json and nobody had connected the two entries. Both
are fixed; the raw-fetch baseline drops 78 -> 69.

WHAT IS SERVED NOW: invoices, equipment, contracts, service-tickets,
service-calls and supply-orders straight off their tables (customer_supply_orders
for the last); activities off business_record_activities, which keys on
business_record_id rather than customer_id because a customer IS a business
record here; and financial-summary, aging and payments DERIVED from the invoice
set, since PostgREST has no SUM. Rows go through toCamel - the components read
invoiceNumber, balanceDue, serialNumber and PostgREST answers snake_case.

WHAT IS ADMITTED RATHER THAN INVENTED. There is no `payments` table in any
schema or migration. Payment history is derived from invoices carrying an
amount_paid, which gives a real date and amount but no method and no cheque
number; the endpoint returns { payments, unbacked } and the component reads
.payments, so the gap is stated rather than showing two permanently blank
columns. averagePaymentDays is null when no invoice has settled (0 days reads as
a customer who pays instantly), and creditLimit / availableCredit are null when
the record carries none - the page shows "Not set" and hides the utilization bar
instead of drawing 0%.

AN UNKNOWN SUB-RESOURCE NOW 404s. That matters more than it looks: falling
through to the customer object is exactly what made the original defect
invisible, so the fallback had to go, not just be bypassed.

DEV FORWARDS THE SUB-PATHS EXPLICITLY rather than via crmProxies. /api/customers
is NOT a plain proxy entry: the bare list is special-cased to the `companies`
edge function (companies being the source of truth for the record), and adding
the prefix to crmProxies would have taken the list off that and sent it to a
function answering a different shape. The comment on that special case claimed
"there's no customers edge function", which has not been true for some time and
is corrected.

REMAINING from the AC, deliberately: /360-view, /devices and /metrics/history
are not implemented here. The first has no caller in any client tree; the other
two are routes-client-monitoring's, over device_registrations, and belong with
AUDIT-029's device-monitoring surface rather than with the customer record.

Hub 8, PlatformCohortAnalysis 7, AIHub 6, ExecutiveDashboard 6,
AdvancedBillingEngine 5, Contacts 4, AdvancedAnalytics 3, and eight pages with
one or two each. PlatformCohortAnalysis is the one to look at first - it is a
platform-admin analytics screen showing 79.4% retention and $20,605 LTV as typed

--- 2026-08-30 (second pass) --- PlatformCohortAnalysis IS REAL NOW, and the way
it failed is worth keeping.

THE PAGE DID CALL ITS ENDPOINT. That is what made it invisible to every guard
that looked: check:fabricated saw three `?? [...]` reads and baselined them,
check:no-static-posture saw four typed headline cards, CR-033 had already
annotated the shape - and none of them said the endpoint answers DIFFERENT KEYS.
It returned { cohorts, summary }; the page read cohortTable, revenueCohorts and
ltvData. All three resolved to undefined, so the fallbacks were not a
degradation path, they were the ONLY path, in dev and production alike. A
platform admin saw 79.4% three-month retention, 56.2% at twelve months, $20,605

recommendation to scale acquisition spend because "CAC has decreased by 18%
while LTV has increased by 23%".

A FALLBACK IS ONLY A FALLBACK IF THE PRIMARY PATH CAN WIN. Worth checking the
key names whenever a page has both a query and a `||`-fallback; that combination
reads as defensive and can be total.

WHAT THE TABLE CANNOT ANSWER, which decided most of the work.
platform_cohort_analysis holds ONE ROW PER COHORT - initial_size, current_size,
retention_rate, one MRR pair, average_ltv, average_cac, ltv_to_cac_ratio - and

revenue chart and an M0..M12 curve all need a row per cohort PER PERIOD, which
nothing records. All three are removed rather than wired, and the response says
so in `unbacked`, which the page renders. The 12-month and 3-month headline
cards went with them for the same reason.

current MRR, net revenue retention), the LTV/CAC/ratio table, and four summary
cards averaged across the cohorts that carry each value - null where none does,
because a 0% retention rate reads as every customer having left. No card carries
a "+3.2% vs. previous cohorts" delta any more: nothing records a previous
calculation to compare against.

TWO OF THE THREE SELECTORS WERE INERT. type= and metric= were sent on every
request and the endpoint reads neither - it filters on cohort_date and nothing
else - and one cohort definition per row means there is nothing to switch
between. Removed. timeframe is kept and now computes the startDate it sends, so
it does something for the first time.

Static-posture baseline 49 -> 42; fabricated-fallback baseline 34 -> 31.


--- 2026-08-30 (third pass) --- PlatformAnalytics, the sibling. Fabricated-
fallback baseline 31 -> 9.

SAME DEFECT AS THE COHORT PAGE, and the same reason it hid: the page DID query
its endpoints. /api/platform-analytics/revenue-metrics answered
{ metrics: {...}, counts: {...} } with every value .toFixed(2)'d into a STRING,
while the page read revenueMetrics.mrr, .arr, .grr and fourteen more at the top
level. Seventeen reads, none resolving, so `|| 89000`, `|| 1068000`, `|| 347`,
`|| 112` rendered on EVERY request. CR-033 had already wrapped these queries so
a failure would say so - correctly - but the literals were never a failure path.

CORRECTION TO CLAUDE.md's BATCH 9 NOTE, which said the platform-analytics edge
fn "returns a NESTED {metrics,counts} shape". Only revenue-metrics did.
conversion-metrics, pipeline-metrics, performance-metrics and growth-trends were
already flat and already matched what the page reads. Checking each endpoint
rather than generalising from one is what kept this from becoming a five-endpoint
rewrite.

TWO METRICS WERE WORSE THAN UNRESOLVED. estimatedCAC was `ltv / 3`, so
ltvCacRatio was `ltv / (ltv / 3)` - exactly 3.00 for every tenant on every
request, a tautology presented as a measurement, with paybackPeriod derived from
the same invented figure. All three are null now and named in `unbacked`, along
with NRR (expansionRate was hardcoded 0 because business_records has no
last_mrr_change column, so NRR was GRR under another name) and the growth rates
(this endpoint reads one window; growth-trends returns the real series). LTV is
null when nothing has churned - average lifetime is 1/churn, and the 24-month
default that stood there was a number somebody picked.

ALREADY RETURNED, NEVER READ: performance-metrics sends real activityTotals and
activityAvgPerDay off platform_activity_reports, and the page showed 1450 calls,
2340 emails, 687 meetings typed in beside them. Now wired.

Also removed: four chart datasets that fell back to six months of invented
revenue, a 1250-prospect funnel and a lead-source split; and every "vs. last
period" delta on the page - +14.1%, +16.4%, +8.7%, +2.3%, -8%, +4.2% - none of
which came from anywhere. A dash is shown where a value is unknown, because
$89,000 says the platform knows and a dash says it does not.

STILL IN THE BASELINE: 9 fabricated fallbacks across ConversionInsights (2),
PipelineTrendWidgets (2), AutoLeadRoutingDashboard (1), ContractProfitability
(1) and three others. Check the key names first on each - that is what made
these two total rather than occasional.

--- 2026-08-30 (2) --- THE FABRICATED VALUE WAS THE PRIMARY PATH, NOT THE FALLBACK.

analytics/ConversionInsights and analytics/PipelineTrendWidgets are now honest
not-connected gates, and server/analytics-routes.ts is deleted. Both render
inside live pages (LeadDeals, reached from the deals board), and both wrapped
every request in `select: (data) => data || { ...invented... }`.

The fallback looked like the safety net. It was the whole thing. In production
all four paths - /api/analytics/conversion-metrics, /activity-nudges,
/control-charts, /trend-widgets - 404, because the analytics edge function
answers only dashboard, sales, service and performance. In dev they were served
by server/analytics-routes.ts: 184 lines, four handlers, ZERO database access,
returning the same hardcoded objects the components already held. So the two
environments agreed, which is exactly why nobody looked: 65% lead-to-qualified,
45% qualified-to-proposal, 72% proposal-to-negotiation, 38% close, 8.2%
overall, a 45-day average cycle, four ranked loss reasons with percentages, and
control charts with upper/lower limits and sigma bands.

A control chart is a claim about process stability. Drawn over invented points
it asserts something specific and false, and it is the kind of chart a manager
screenshots into a QBR.

RULE THIS ADDS to the three fabricated-value guards: check whether the endpoint
behind a `|| literal` returns anything at all before treating the literal as a
fallback. check:fabricated flags the shape correctly but says nothing about
reachability, and the four entries it held here read as ordinary defensive
defaults. The tell was that the router had no db import.

Guard state: check:fabricated 9 -> 2 (the two PlatformAnalytics pipeline entries
and leadConversionRate were fixed in the same pass, deriving the caption and the
bar width from conversionMetrics.summary instead of a hardcoded "125 of 1,250").
Locked by server/tests/unit/analytics-fiction-removed.test.ts, mutation-tested
in four directions. Remaining in the baseline: AutoLeadRoutingDashboard's
maxLeadsPerRepPerDay and ContractProfitability's gpAlertThreshold, both of which
are configuration defaults rather than measurements.

userStories.title: Implement tenant-onboarding "Execute import" actual row insertion (imports nothing today)
userStories.description: As a new tenant importing data, I need Execute to actually create records, not report a fake success.
acceptanceCriteria: Execute inserts validated rows into the target tables scoped by tenant, transactionally.
importedRows reflects the real inserted count; failures roll back and surface errors.

userStories.notes: [FUNCTIONALITY/BLOCKER] Source: platform audit 2026-07-12 (branch claude/platform-audit-prd-e5lp6t). server/routes-tenant-onboarding.ts:396 "TODO: Implement actual data import execution" — sets importExecuted:true + importedRows from req.body but writes no rows. Silent data loss during onboarding. | COMPLETE 2026-07-23. ROOT CAUSE: the execute handler flipped importExecuted:true and echoed req.body.rowsToImport as importedRows while inserting NOTHING; worse, the validation record never persisted the parsed CSV rows, so execute had no data to insert even if it wanted to. FIX (3 layers): (1) SCHEMA — added rawRows jsonb to data_import_validations (shared/tenant-onboarding-schema.ts) + migration 0035_pa042_import_raw_rows.sql (ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS raw_rows jsonb; journaled idx 18, tag 0035 — clean per check:migrations); importDataWithValidation now stores rawRows: csvData at validate time. (2) EXECUTE ENGINE — rewrote POST /api/tenants/import/:validationId/execute to: load the validation (404 if absent, 409 if already executed), resolve the target from an IMPORT_TARGETS registry, resolve tenantId from validation.tenantId (fallback getTenantId/body), rebuild each row that PASSED validation (errors carry 1-based row numbers -> skip those) by translating columnMappings[*].mappedTo names to real target columns, and INSERT them inside db.transaction so a mid-insert failure rolls the whole import back (AC2). importedRows = real inserted count; failedRows = total - imported; response returns both. (3) TARGET SAFETY — the honest scoping decision: the onboarding auto-mapper (autoMapColumns) only ever produces a company name + contact/address fields, which cleanly satisfies business_records (companyName NOT NULL is mapped; recordType/status default). The other three dataTypes CANNOT be safely inserted from that CSV shape — equipment.customerId (FK) NOT NULL, contracts.customerId/startDate/endDate NOT NULL, inventoryItems.name/category NOT NULL are all absent from the field map — so 'customers' inserts into business_records (recordType='customer', status='active', email->primaryContactEmail, phone->primaryContactPhone, address->addressLine1, zipCode->postalCode) and equipment/contracts/inventory return an explicit 400 UNSUPPORTED_IMPORT_TYPE. This REMOVES the silent data loss for EVERY type: the supported type writes real rows, the unsupported types now fail loudly instead of reporting fake success (was the actual audit defect). TEST: server/tests/unit/tenant-onboarding-import.test.ts (5 tests, supertest over the mounted router, db + auth mocked): valid customers import inserts only the non-error rows with tenant+defaults and reports importedRows=1/failedRows=1; unsupported type -> 400 with no importExecuted; insert failure -> 500 with importExecuted never set (rollback); unknown validation -> 404; already-executed -> 409. VERIFICATION: vitest 5/5; tsc ratchet holds at 1083; lint ratchet DECREASED 11996->11995 (baseline tightened); prettier clean; migration guard's 25 pre-existing SUPA-002 drift files (0008-0028) untouched, 0035 journaled + not flagged. DEFERRED (separate story): equipment/contracts/inventory onboarding import needs a richer field map + FK/date resolution (customer lookup, name/category defaults) before those targets can be enabled.

userStories.title: Unify /api/customers list handler across dev and prod + honor sort/scope/filter params
userStories.description: As a dashboard user, I need regional-scoped and churn-risk customer views to actually filter, consistently in dev and prod.
acceptanceCriteria: Dev and prod resolve GET /api/customers list to the SAME backend (either proxy to the customers fn or delete the companies?recordType=Customer redirect).
The chosen handler honors sort, scope, filter (or explicitly rejects unknown params).
POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/customers resolve to the same backend in dev and prod.
userStories.notes:
[ROUTING/HIGH] Source: platform audit 2026-07-12 (branch claude/platform-audit-prd-e5lp6t). edge-function-proxy.ts:423-431 special-cases GET /api/customers (dev-only) to companies fn forwarding only search/limit/offset — drops sort/scope/filter; prod hits the real customers fn list (different backend). role-dashboard-config.ts:111,146 rely on the dropped params.
--- 2026-08-30 --- DONE. /api/customers is one backend on both hosts.

'/api/customers': 'customers' is a plain crmProxies entry now, and the two
special-cased forwards are gone. That settles the AC directly: the list, the
single record, POST/PATCH/DELETE and every sub-resource all run
supabase/functions/customers/ in dev exactly as they always have in production.

WHY THE REDIRECT WAS NEVER DEFENSIBLE, once looked at: dev sent the bare list to
the `companies` function with recordType=Customer, and production cannot reach
`companies` under this prefix at all - getApiUrl rewrites /api/customers
straight to functions.printyx.net/customers. So the same url was answered by
two different functions with two different SHAPES: `companies` returns
{ data, total, page, limit } and `customers` returns a bare array, which the
iOS client decodes as [BusinessRecord]. Both read the same `companies` table,
so the redirect bought nothing and cost the divergence. Every web consumer goes
through extractRecords and tolerates either, which is why nobody noticed.

THE STORY'S PREMISE HAD PARTLY EXPIRED. It says role-dashboard-config.ts:111,146
depend on the dropped sort/scope/filter params. That file no longer exists, and
grepping every client tree found NO caller sending sort, scope or filter -
what is actually sent is search/limit/offset from the web and page/limit/search/
status from iOS. The customers function reads search, status, recordType, limit
and offset, so the params in use are all honoured. Nothing needed adding.

THREE DEFECTS THE CONVERGENCE EXPOSED, all fixed here:

1. POST /api/customers/:id/supply-orders was writing junk CUSTOMERS. The edge
   function dispatched sub-resources on `req.method === 'GET' && customerId &&
   subResource`, so a POST fell past it into the create-customer branch, built a
   `companies` row out of the order payload and answered 201 - and
   CustomerSupplies reported "Supply order created successfully". Nothing in
   Express served that path, so production was the only host where the button
   did anything, and what it did was write a bogus company on every click.
   The dispatch now covers every method.

   The order itself is not implementable as the form stands, so this answers 501
   rather than dropping unknown keys: customer_supply_orders is an order HEADER
   (order_number NOT NULL UNIQUE, delivery_address jsonb NOT NULL,
   customer_portal_user_id NOT NULL referencing a portal login) with line items
   in customer_supply_order_items, while the dialog posted a flat {supplyId,
   quantity, unitPrice, totalPrice, orderType, notes} - not one a column - with
   status 'pending', which is not in the supply_order_status enum. A staff-side
   order has no portal user either. The dialog is removed, per the BATCH 7 rule
   (delete a feature with no backing column); the read side is untouched.

2. ONE PAGE, TWO BACKENDS, DECIDED BY SEGMENT COUNT. The dev sub-resource
   forward was app.get('/api/customers/:id/:sub'), which matches exactly three
   segments, so the Customer Detail meter-readings tab
   (/api/customers/:id/metrics/history, four segments) fell through to Express
   while its neighbour /devices did not. handleSubResource now takes the whole
   tail rather than one segment.

3. EVERY CUSTOMER SAW THE WHOLE FLEET. Both Express handlers behind those paths
   filtered device_registrations by tenant_id ONLY - despite
   device_registrations.customer_id existing, and despite each handler's own
   comment saying "get all devices for this customer". So the meter-readings tab
   showed every device in the tenant, labelled with whichever customer was open,
   with real numbers about the wrong customers. The ported version filters on
   customer_id and scopes device_metrics through those device ids. Metric rows
   go through toCamelShallow, because toner_levels, paper_levels and raw_data
   are jsonb.

ALSO REMOVED: a second query in CustomerMeterReadings for
/api/customers/:id/devices whose result nothing read (the device picker is built
from metricsHistory.timeline), so that endpoint was not ported.

FOURTEEN SHADOWED EXPRESS HANDLERS appeared the moment the prefix went into
crmProxies. Thirteen are deleted - routes-customers.ts entirely (one handler),
two in routes-crm-core.ts, three in routes-business-records.ts, two in
routes-enhanced-service.ts (which mounts at the /api root, so its bare
'/customers' and '/customers/search' were under this prefix; neither had a
caller) and five aliases in routes-workflow-mobile.ts. The fourteenth,
signature-routes.ts's /customers/:customerId/signature-requests, is RETAINED with
a reason: it is one of the twelve SEC-SESSION-001 files that read
req.session.user as their only identity and have never run on either host, and
deleting it means deciding the fate of the whole file.

ONE CONSEQUENCE WORTH KNOWING: server/lib/custom-field-validation.ts is now
unreachable, because the /api/customers write path in routes-business-records.ts
was its last caller - and that path never ran in production either. So
custom-field VALUES have never been validated on a write anywhere; the
custom-fields edge function validates field DEFINITIONS, which is a different
thing. Kept and baselined rather than deleted, with the gap recorded in its
header, because deleting it would drop the gap off the roadmap with the code.
Wiring it belongs to CRMX-004.

VERIFIED: check:shadowed-express back to 0 backlog (66 retained, was 65);
check:routes, check:nav, check:edge-paths, check:proxy-overrides,
check:phantom-cols, check:phantom-tables, check:orphans, check:server-orphans,
check:fabricated, check:no-static-posture, check:sql-string-tables all pass;
tsc 324 -> 322. Locked by server/tests/unit/customers-prefix-convergence.test.ts,
mutation-tested seven ways (GET-only dispatch, dropped customer_id filter, deep
jsonb conversion, restored companies redirect, re-added Express route, re-added
supply mutation, re-added devices query - all caught). Not verified against a
live deploy; no egress here (PROD-020).

UNRELATED DRIFT ABSORBED, so it is not mistaken for this story's: the four
commission tables CR-017 left reported by check:unwritten-tables
(commission_calculations, commission_calculation_details, commission_bonuses,
commission_adjustments) are baselined now. The commission edge function already
records why nothing writes them - POST /calculate answers 501 because the
calculation engine does not exist - so they are correctly unwritten rather than
a defect.


FOUR TESTS FROM EARLIER STORIES NEEDED CORRECTING, not deleting: three in
customer-sub-resources.test.ts pinned the PA-020 special cases this change
removes (the :id/:sub forward and the companies redirect), and one in
mobile-phantom-tables.test.ts asserted the five routes-workflow-mobile
/api/customers/:id/* handlers were "real and called". They read real tables but
were never called: PA-020 had already routed that sub-segment to the edge
function before that test was written, so all five were shadowed when it claimed
otherwise. Each assertion is inverted with a note saying what it used to assert
and why that was wrong, per the ratchet-annotation rule.

One assertion needed widening rather than inverting: "every query is scoped to
both tenant and customer" counted .eq(customerId) against .from(), and
device_metrics has no customer_id - the metrics/history branch scopes it
transitively through the customer's device ids. It now counts both forms, so the
invariant stays exact instead of being relaxed. Mutation-tested: dropping the
.in() fails it.

userStories.title: Resolve endpoints that live pages call but exist in NEITHER Express nor an edge function (dead in dev and prod)
userStories.description: As a user of Quote Templates, My Approvals, Sales Command Center, and Document Builder, I need their primary data to load somewhere.
acceptanceCriteria: For each dead-in-both prefix (/api/quote-templates, /api/approvals + /:id/respond, /api/sales-forecasts, /api/pipeline-forecast, /api/documents, and the rest: assignment-groups, content, equipment-disposal, financial-forecasting, lead-intelligence, lease-payments, sales-performance, system-monitoring, technician-sessions): build the edge fn (tenant-scoped + RBAC) or confirm-and-remove the dead page/query.
Prioritize prefixes backing shipped nav entries (quote-templates, approvals, sales-forecasts/pipeline-forecast, documents).
Split "dead-in-both" out of the generic missing-edge bucket in docs/route-ownership-baseline.json so they triage distinctly.
userStories.notes:
[ROUTING/HIGH] Source: platform audit 2026-07-12 (branch claude/platform-audit-prd-e5lp6t). Parity computeParity() dead-in-both subset. These present as working UI with empty/erroring data; grandfathered under the EDGE-014 umbrella with no per-domain AC.
--- 2026-08-30 --- DONE. The class exists in the tool now, and the fourteen
prefixes are resolved.

THE THIRD AC WAS THE ONE THAT STILL MATTERED. "Split dead-in-both out of the
generic missing-edge bucket so they triage distinctly" - route-parity classified
both as missing-edge, whose message is "add the edge function". That is right
when Express serves the path and production does not: the handler exists, port
or proxy it. It is wrong when NEITHER host serves it, because there is nothing
to port, the page is broken while you develop it too, and the fix is to build
the endpoint or delete the call. This story opened with fourteen prefixes it had
to separate by hand for exactly that reason.

`dead-in-both` is now its own class (fe && !edge && !exp), ordered before
missing-edge so the narrower rule wins, with its own message. It is GATED AT
ZERO rather than grandfathered: a missing-edge domain gets baselined because it
works in dev and can sit unnoticed, while a dead-in-both domain is broken for
everyone from the first commit, so baselining one would record a live defect as
accepted debt. Only a LIVE caller gates - a call inside an orphaned file can
never run, the same rule missing-edge and check-nav-targets already apply.

Mutation-tested five ways, all caught: dropping the `&& !exp` guard (which would
swallow every missing-edge domain and stop the prod-blocker message firing at
all), reordering CLASS_ORDER, removing it from the fail expression, making the
orphan branch gate, and putting an entry in the baseline. Behaviour verified
end-to-end too: pointing a live page at a made-up prefix fails the guard with
the build-or-delete message; pointing an ORPHANED page at one reports without
gating; and pointing a live page at an express-only domain still fails as
missing-edge, so the split did not swallow the older class.

THE FOURTEEN, RE-CHECKED RATHER THAN TRUSTED - the July list had gone stale the
same way PROD-010's did:
  gone entirely (no reference anywhere): quote-templates, financial-forecasting,
    lead-intelligence, system-monitoring
  express-only with no frontend caller (a dead-backend question, not this one):
    approvals, assignment-groups, equipment-disposal, sales-performance-metrics
  proxied and aligned: pipeline-forecast, documents, lease-payments,
    technician-sessions
  both-divergent, orphaned caller only: content-gap-analysis (ContentGapDashboard
    has no importers and is already in the orphan baseline)
  both-divergent and LIVE: sales-forecasts - the one real finding, fixed below.

sales-forecasts CONVERGED. SalesPipelineForecasting and SalesCommandCenter both
list forecasts from /api/sales-forecasts, which had an Express handler AND an
edge function with no proxy entry, so the two hosts ran different code for the
same routed page. The prefix is proxied now and the three Express handlers are
deleted. The POST is deliberately not ported: no file in any client tree creates
a forecast, and it could not have run in production anyway.

WHICH SURFACED THE HONEST CONSEQUENCE: check:unwritten-tables immediately flagged
sales_forecasts as a table nothing writes. That is correct and worth stating
plainly - the deleted POST was its only writer, it had no caller, and being
Express-only it could never have run for a deployed user. So both pages have
always listed a table no production user could fill. Recorded in the baseline
with the reason in the edge function's own header, rather than left looking like
a table nobody happens to use. Building a create path is a feature that starts
with a UI.

VERIFIED: check:routes (bothDivergent 58 -> 57, missingEdge 0, deadInBoth 0
gated), check:nav, check:edge-paths, check:proxy-overrides,
check:shadowed-express (0 backlog), check:orphans, check:server-orphans,
check:phantom-cols, check:phantom-tables, check:fabricated,
check:no-static-posture, check:unwritten-tables, check:sql-string-tables,
check:edge-rbac, check:unreferenced-edge-fns all pass. Locked by
server/tests/unit/dead-in-both-class.test.ts. eslint on the touched router: 12
unused-symbol errors -> 4, all pre-existing.

userStories.title: Add missing indexes (incl. tenant_id composites) to core CRM/ERP tables with zero indexes
userStories.description: As the platform scales across tenants, I need core tables indexed so tenant-scoped queries do not sequentially scan every tenant’s rows.
acceptanceCriteria: Add composite (tenant_id, ...) btree indexes to contracts, proposals, proposal_line_items, quotes, tasks, invoice_line_items, opportunities, purchase_orders, inventory_items (lead with tenant_id + common filter/FK cols: customer_id, status, created_at).
Add FK indexes for proposal_line_items.proposal_id and invoice_line_items.invoice_id.
Generate via db:generate, review SQL, apply via db:migrate; EXPLAIN confirms index scans on representative list queries.

userStories.title: Make a fresh database provisionable from versioned migrations alone (DR readiness)
userStories.description: As an operator doing disaster recovery, I need db:migrate on an empty DB to reproduce the running schema.
acceptanceCriteria: Generate a baseline migration reproducing the actual production schema (drift-diff the live DB) so db:migrate on an empty DB yields the running schema incl. the tables from PA-031.

Rename duplicate migration numbers (0008_client_enrollment_tokens vs 0008_pretty_rocket_raccoon; 0009_colorful_meggan vs 0009_monitoring_clients_customer_id) to unique ordered numbers; verify db:migrate:status replay.
Retire push-based provisioning (create-all-tables-from-drizzle.sh uses drizzle-kit push against the live container) in favor of db:migrate; document the DR runbook (ties LAUNCH-011).
userStories.notes: [DATABASE/HIGH] Source: platform audit 2026-07-12 (branch claude/platform-audit-prd-e5lp6t). Real schema was materialized via drizzle-kit push + manual SQL, not the 21 numbered migrations. Duplicate 0008/0009 sequence numbers make ordered replay ambiguous. | MEASURED 2026-08-26 (during COP-M00, no fix attempted). Ran the full 40-migration chain against an empty PostgreSQL 16 cluster. npm run db:migrate FAILS IN MIGRATION 0000 and, because it wraps the run in one transaction, rolls back and creates NOTHING: 'foreign key constraint api_key_rotations_tenant_id_tenants_id_fk cannot be implemented — Key columns tenant_id and id are of incompatible types: uuid and character varying.' Applying statement-tolerantly (psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=0, journal order) yields 667 tables and 30 errors: 0000 has 15 (FKs on api_keys/api_key_rotations/api_key_usage_logs, sso_login_attempts/sso_provider_configs/sso_sessions/sso_user_mappings, customer_maintenance_appointments, technician_availability_slots — all uuid-vs-varchar key columns), 0001 has 4 (type serial does not exist; tenant_id cannot cast to integer; export_format drop/recreate), 0002 has 10 (id cannot cast to uuid; tags cannot cast to text[]; the same two FKs; alert_severity/alert_status/duplicate_match_type/merge_strategy drop-recreate), 0043 has 1 (column o.template_type does not exist). The new 0057 contributes ZERO. So DR readiness is not a documentation gap — the baseline migration is genuinely unapplicable, and the fix is a repair to 0000/0001/0002/0043 or a regenerated baseline. | RESOLVED 2026-08-26. npm run db:migrate now SUCCEEDS on an empty database: 43 migrations, 668 tables, exit 0, and the seeder then runs against it. Measured, not argued - the same command was measured failing earlier the same day. The blocker was never documentation; 30 statements across four migrations could never execute, and because the migrator wraps the run in ONE TRANSACTION it rolled back and created nothing at all. CORRECTED IN PLACE rather than in a follow-up migration, which is safe for a specific reason worth stating: drizzle's migrator skips by created_at against folderMillis and NEVER by content hash (node_modules/drizzle-orm/pg-core/dialect.js:62), so editing an already-applied migration cannot cause a re-run on an existing database. A migration that has never executed anywhere has no history to preserve. WHAT WAS BROKEN. 0000 (15): foreign keys between columns whose types could not match - uuid columns pointing at the varchar tenants.id/users.id across api_keys, api_key_usage_logs, api_key_rotations and the four sso_* tables, plus two the other way round (customer_maintenance_appointments.portal_user_id and technician_availability_slots.appointment_id against uuid primary keys). Postgres rejects these outright, so NONE of those 15 constraints has ever existed in any environment. The SCHEMA files were wrong, not the migration, so both are fixed; the fresh database now carries all 15. 0001 (4): 'SET DATA TYPE serial' - serial is not a type, it is shorthand for integer plus a sequence - and a tenant_id-to-integer cast with no USING, both also contradicting the schema, which has those columns as uuid. Plus the first instance of the enum problem below. 0002 (10): the enum problem twice more, a jsonb-to-text[] cast with no USING whose DROP DEFAULT was emitted AFTER the cast rather than before, an id-to-uuid cast contradicting the schema (locationHistory.id is varchar), and two DROP TYPEs for enums the schema still uses. 0043 (1): a unique index on proposal_templates.template_type, a column that does not exist on a database built from these migrations. THE ENUM PROBLEM, which is a drizzle-kit gap worth knowing: to change an enum it converts dependent columns to text, drops the type and recreates it. Column DEFAULTS keep depending on the enum after that conversion - they stay as 'json'::export_format - so DROP TYPE fails with 'cannot drop type because other objects depend on it' and every statement after it unravels. drizzle-kit does not emit the DROP DEFAULTs that would make it work. Added them, and restored the defaults afterwards where the value is still a member of the new enum. AC2 was ALREADY SATISFIED before this pass: the duplicate 0008/0009 prefixes it names were fixed by SUPA-002 and check:migrations has been green on prefix uniqueness since. AC3: create-all-tables-from-drizzle.sh is DELETED - it hardcoded a container name and ran drizzle-kit push at production, which is how the 107-table drift COP-M00 had to reconcile got there - and docs/disaster-recovery-runbook.md replaces it with the migrate path, the seeding steps, the verification commands and the two seeder traps (refuses a second run per tenant; tenant-independent ids mean a second tenant in the same database writes nothing). 0059_pa032_fk_column_types.sql brings an EXISTING database to the corrected shape; it is a no-op on one built from the chain, and the two uuid casts carry the explicit USING that varchar-to-uuid needs. db:generate reports no drift, so schema and migrations now agree. TWO CONTRADICTIONS SURFACED AND DELIBERATELY NOT RESOLVED, because they are schema decisions rather than migration repairs, both recorded in the runbook: alert_severity/alert_status are each declared TWICE with different members (team-alerts-schema vs intelligent-alerts-schema, the barrel skips the first), and alert_instances defaults to 'warning'/'active' which are not members of the enum the migrations create - those two defaults are dropped and not restored, and since both columns are NOT NULL an insert omitting them now fails rather than storing a value outside the enum; and proposal_templates is declared twice with template_type vs category. VERIFIED: db:migrate exit 0 on an empty database twice over (before and after adding 0059), 668 tables, 43 migrations recorded, all 15 previously-impossible foreign keys present, seed:demo then runs clean, check:stage-resolution green against the result, check:migrations/check-phantom-cols/check:dup-tables/check:rootsql pass, 3435 tests pass, tsc holds at 506.

userStories.notes: [DATABASE/HIGH] Source: platform audit 2026-07-12 (branch claude/platform-audit-prd-e5lp6t). routes-products-crud.ts:1645/1658 parse insertMeterReadingSchema without createdBy; meter_readings.created_by is NOT NULL -> parse throws -> 500. CLAUDE.md BATCH 8 flagged this as still-open server debt; pattern recurs across schema.ts lines 1394/1815/2021/2218/2281/2566/2700/2807/2871. PROGRESS 2026-07-12: meter-readings POST fixed (createdBy injected at both parse sites); systemic sweep of other NOT-NULL created_by insert-parse sites + integration test still pending a tsc/live-DB environment. | COMPLETE 2026-07-23 — bullet 1 (meter-readings) was already done; this closes the systemic sweep (bullet 2) + adds a regression test (bullet 3). THE AUDIT was done authoritatively, not by the shared-schema heuristic (which had a ~5x false-positive rate from schema/DDL drift): scanned the actual migration DDL for every table with created_by/tenant_id NOT NULL (no default), mapped table -> insertXSchema via createInsertSchema/pgTable, and matched parse sites — CRUCIALLY shorthand-aware (`tenantId,` counts as injected, not just `tenantId:`; missing that inflated a first pass to 62 bogus hits, e.g. routes-tasks.ts which injects via shorthand and works fine). TRUE list: 10 sites. RESOLVED ALL 10: FIXED 8 real bugs — 5 INSERT via `.omit({tenantId[,createdBy]:true})` before parse (routes-knowledge-base.ts:122 category + :395 article [both tenantId+createdBy] + :695 feedback, routes-enhanced-service.ts:157 phone-in-ticket, routes-warehouse-fpy.ts:26 kitting — each injects the field at .values() downstream, so omit is safe); 1 INSERT via INJECT (routes-manufacturer-integration.ts:50 -> `.parse({...req.body, tenantId})` rather than .omit, because createIntegration(tenantId, data) is typed Omit<Insert,"tenantId"> and the Zod-omit inferred type mismatched it — injecting keeps the type aligned and was the +1 tsc regression I caught and fixed); and 2 UPDATE routes via `.partial()` (routes-social-media.ts:263 post + :409 cron-job — these misuse an INSERT schema to validate a PUT, so the full-required-fields parse 500s any partial update; .partial() is the correct update contract, matching the existing knowledge-base category PUT). EXCLUDED 2 with rationale: routes-client-monitoring.ts:538 is a FALSE POSITIVE (tenantId is spread into the `clientData` object BEFORE parse; the audit missed it only because the parse arg is a variable, not a literal); routes-seo-core.ts:57 (seo_settings) is the KNOWN broken settings contract tracked under EDGE-002e (batch 15 — missing NOT NULL siteUrl etc.), a separate story, deliberately not touched here. TEST (bullet 3): server/tests/unit/insert-schema-server-injected.test.ts asserts on the REAL schemas that each base schema required the server field (safeParse({}) reports a tenantId/createdBy issue = the bug) and that `.omit(...)` removes it from both `.shape` and the parse contract — 24 tests, all pass. Chose a schema-level test over a route test because it validates the exact fix on the real schemas with zero db/route mocking (robust, not brittle). VERIFICATION: vitest 24/24; tsc ratchet holds at 1083 (the manufacturer-integration omit briefly pushed it to 1084 — caught by the ratchet, fixed by switching to inject); lint ratchet holds at 12000.

userStories.notes: [FUNCTIONALITY/HIGH] Source: platform audit 2026-07-12 (branch claude/platform-audit-prd-e5lp6t). server/routes/chrome-extension-routes.ts:467 "TODO: Store API key in database (create extension_api_keys table)"; :481 expiresAt:null TODO; :522 zoominfo:false TODO.
