BULLET 1 (persist + hash + expiry): new shared/extension-api-keys-schema.ts (extension_api_keys: tenant_id, user_id, key_hash, key_prefix, name, expires_at, last_used_at, revoked_at, created_at), registered in shared/drizzle-schema.ts, with migration 0033_pa044_extension_api_keys.sql (table + unique index on key_hash + tenant index). WHAT WAS WRONG: eslint.config.js ignored "**/*.{ts,tsx}" ("Skip TypeScript files due to parsing issues"); ESLint 9/10 loads only the flat config (the .eslintrc.cjs was dead — and it referenced eslint-plugin-security, which was never even in package.json, so it could not have run regardless). (3) SECURITY GATE: full config + --max-warnings 0 would fail on the whole backlog, so created eslint.security.config.js (TS parser + ONLY no-eval/no-implied-eval/no-new-func — repo is clean of these) and pointed security-scan.yml at it with "--config eslint.security.config.js --no-inline-config --max-warnings 0". (4) Deleted the redundant .eslintrc.cjs. (5) Cleaned lint/validate:lint scripts: dropped the ESLint-10-ignored "--ext .ts,.tsx" (flat config selects via files). mobile-ci.yml "npm run lint" is unaffected — it runs with working-directory: mobile against the mobile app's own config and only triggers on mobile/** changes. userStories.title: Enforce MFA/AAL step-up at web sign-in (TOTP enrolled but never challenged)
userStories.description: As a user who enabled MFA, I need to be actually challenged for my TOTP factor at login.
acceptanceCriteria: After signInWithPassword, check getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel(); if nextLevel==="aal2" && currentLevel==="aal1", present a TOTP challenge before treating the user as authenticated.

userStories.notes:
[AUTH/MEDIUM] Source: platform audit 2026-07-12 (branch claude/platform-audit-prd-e5lp6t). MFA infra exists (mfa edge fn, mfa-routes, MFASettings) but useSupabaseAuth.login returns immediately after signInWithPassword with no AAL step-up; grep for aal/listFactors/challenge in client finds nothing.
--- 2026-08-22 --- THE PREMISE IS WRONG, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS: on the
Express backend TOTP was never ENROLLED either, so "enrolled but never
challenged" understates it.

two_factor_enabled and two_factor_secret are columns on USER_SETTINGS
(shared/schema.ts:1063, migration 0000). server/storage.ts addressed them on
`users`. The two halves failed in opposite directions, both verified by building
the queries and printing toSQL() rather than reasoning about them:

  .set({ twoFactorEnabled, twoFactorSecret })  drizzle DROPS keys that are not
  columns of the target table. The UPDATE reduced to `set updated_at = $1`, and
  enableMfaForUser returned the user and reported success while writing NOTHING.
  A silent no-op that claims to have worked is worse than a crash - the UI would
  have said "MFA enabled".

  .select({ twoFactorEnabled: users.twoFactorEnabled })  throws
  "Cannot convert undefined or null to object", so reading the status crashed.

server/routes/mfa-routes.ts read the same two fields off a `User` object at six
sites, so both were always undefined and every verification path
short-circuited to "MFA not enabled for this user". A correct code could not be
accepted.

FIXED: storage now reads and writes user_settings (upserting on the unique
user_id, resolving tenant_id from the user because user_settings.tenant_id is
NOT NULL), and a new storage.getUserMfaSecret(userId) gives the routes the flag
and secret from one place. getUsersWithoutMfa uses a LEFT join deliberately: a
user who has never opened settings has no user_settings row, and that is exactly
the user without MFA - an inner join would have hidden them from a compliance
report.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. Nothing calls /api/mfa: there are no api/mfa references
in client/src, and the "Two-Factor Authentication" Switch in Settings.tsx:693
has no onCheckedChange, so it is a read-only indicator. This makes the API
work; it does not ship the feature.

SECOND STORAGE MODEL, unchanged and worth knowing before anyone builds the UI:
supabase/functions/mfa/ (which is what production serves, /api/mfa being
unproxied) keeps enrollment in `mfa_enrollments`, not in user_settings. That
table is created by drizzle/rls/auth-security-tables.sql, applied by hand with
\i rather than through the journaled migration runner - the PA-032/PA-039
two-migration-systems problem. So the two backends do not share enrollment
state at all, and whichever one the UI is built against decides the answer.

userStories.notes:
[ROUTING/MEDIUM] Source: platform audit 2026-07-12 (branch claude/platform-audit-prd-e5lp6t). scripts/lib/route-parity.mjs:124-136 classifies only the first /api/<segment> token, so PA-019/020/021 all pass green. This blind spot lets the class keep shipping.
--- 2026-08-30 --- DONE.

AC #2 WAS ALREADY BUILT. "Detect {fn,pathPrefix} proxy entries lacking a
server.ts override" is scripts/check-proxy-overrides.mjs, which PA-019 wrote
when it fixed kpis/reporting/scheduled-reports. It is CI-wired and passing. The
story note predates it.

AC #1 AND #3 WERE HALF-BUILT AND HAD A BLIND SPOT WORTH THE WHOLE STORY.
check:edge-coverage (PROD-014) already recorded called sub-paths against what an
edge function dispatches, and already failed on anything new - so "record full
called paths" and "fail CI on sub-path divergences" existed. What it could not
see was the case the AC names by example: a path with an ID IN IT.

Its regex captured ONE segment after the domain and isLiteralSegment rejected
anything holding a `$` or `{`, so

    `/api/equipment/${id}/meter-readings`

was dropped ENTIRELY - the placeholder failed the literal test and the segment
behind it was never examined. That is the PA-020 class, and it is the
worst-behaved one: such a request does not 404. The handler reads parts[0] as
the id, never looks at parts[1], and answers 200 WITH THE PARENT OBJECT. A
component mapping over it renders an empty list and reports nothing. PA-020
found five tabs like that on one page; this found the same shape live in
`equipment`, called by CustomerEquipment.tsx.

Paths are normalized to a SHAPE now (`${...}` and `:param` both become `:id`)
and every literal AFTER the first placeholder is checked. Baseline entries are
shape strings, so `equipment/:id/meter-readings` sits beside the older depth-1
`admin/audit-logs` in one list. A depth-1 literal is deliberately NOT
re-reported through the deep path - the original branch owns it, and counting
both would put one defect in the baseline twice.

THE MATCHER TOOK THREE GOES AND THE MIDDLE ONE WAS THE DANGEROUS KIND.
Quoted-literal-only was the original rule, and three of the first four deep
paths I spot-checked were FALSE POSITIVES under it, because a handler can name a
segment without quoting it on its own: `if (path === '/summary')`, or a regex
`/^\/public\/([^/]+)\/respond$/`. Loosening to a word-boundary search fixed
those and immediately "resolved" 25 baselined gaps - against the prose string
'Multiple critical security events in the last 7 days' for admin/security, and
against a local `const metrics` for analytics/metrics. That would have been a
silent DE-GATING dressed up as progress, and it is the same trap CLAUDE.md
already records for absence assertions matching their own explanation. The rule
now requires the segment to sit between path or quote delimiters, which accepts
every real dispatch form and rejects prose and identifiers.

A truncated interpolation returns null rather than a guess: the match stops at
whitespace, so `${opts.format ?? 'pdf'}` arrives as `${opts`, and guessing there
would have baselined `proposals/:id/export` off a fragment.

BASELINE 110 -> 112: 23 real deep findings added, 21 removed - 5 that earlier
stories in this branch actually fixed (analytics x4, fleet/devices) and 16 that
the tightened matcher recognises as served. Each of the 16 was verified by
reading the dispatch, not assumed: outreach `path === '/drafts'`,
pipeline-config `path.match(/^\/stages\/([^/]+)$/)`, proposals
`path === '/equipment-packages'`, sales-pipeline `path === '/opportunities'`.

THE 23 ARE FILED AS PA-052, not left to look like accepted debt. Four were
confirmed by hand against both the caller and the function.

VERIFIED: check:edge-coverage green at 112; check:routes, check:nav,
check:proxy-overrides, check:edge-paths, check:shadowed-express and the rest of
the sweep pass. Locked by server/tests/unit/edge-path-depth.test.ts, which pins
both judgement calls as accept/reject tables over the matcher, and was
mutation-tested five ways: loosening appearsIn back to word-boundary, dropping
the depth-1 skip, dropping the truncated-interpolation guard, stripping the deep
entries from the baseline, and weakening its note. All caught.

userStories.title: Fix generic webhook HMAC verifier computing signature over re-serialized JSON, not raw body
userStories.description: As an integrations owner, I need the generic webhook verifier to validate real provider signatures.
acceptanceCriteria: verifyStripeSignature (and Salesforce/Microsoft paths) hash the raw request buffer, not JSON.stringify(payload); preserve req.rawBody.
Test with a Stripe-format signature fixture that passes only against raw-body HMAC.
userStories.notes: [SECURITY/LOW] Source: platform audit 2026-07-12 (branch claude/platform-audit-prd-e5lp6t). server/integrations/webhook-service.ts:230,275 use JSON.stringify(payload); real signatures are over raw bytes so it can never validate. Fails-closed today (rejects all), but is a latent bypass if any caller treats false as "skip". Primary Stripe path (stripe-service.ts) correctly uses constructEvent. | COMPLETE 2026-07-23 — the generic webhook verifier now HMACs over the RAW request bytes, not JSON.stringify(payload). ROOT CAUSE: verifyStripeSignature (webhook-service.ts:279), the Salesforce inline path (:231), and verifyQuickBooksSignature (:327) all hashed JSON.stringify(payload); a real provider signature is over the raw body bytes, whose key order/whitespace/unicode-escaping differ from a re-serialization, so it could never validate (fail-closed, but a latent bypass if any caller read false as "skip"). FIX: threaded an explicit rawBody:string param through processWebhook -> verifyWebhookSignature -> the three verifiers, and HMAC over it (Stripe: `${timestamp}.${rawBody}`; Salesforce/QuickBooks: rawBody). Chose an explicit param over mutating req.rawBody — same effect, no Express-global coupling. ROUTES (webhook-routes.ts): stripe/quickbooks already used express.raw() so req.body is the raw Buffer — now capture rawBody = req.body.toString() and pass it; SWITCHED the salesforce route from express.json() to rawBodyParser (it needs the bytes, which express.json discards) and parse from rawBody; the generic /:provider route passes rawBody too. microsoft-calendar (clientState token) and google-calendar (channel token/id) do NOT HMAC the body, so rawBody is unused there — they pass JSON.stringify(req.body) as a documented placeholder. Also fixed a latent caller bug found on the way: verifyWebhookSignature's quickbooks branch still passed `payload` after the rename — now rawBody. Hardened both non-Stripe comparisons to length-guarded crypto.timingSafeEqual (QuickBooks was a plain === ; Salesforce could throw on a length mismatch). TEST (AC bullet 2): server/tests/unit/webhook-signature.test.ts — a fixture whose raw bytes differ from their re-serialization (RAW_BODY !== JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(RAW_BODY))), asserting for Stripe/Salesforce/QuickBooks that a signature over the RAW body VALIDATES and one over the re-serialized body is REJECTED (the exact case the old JSON.stringify code failed), plus missing-secret / malformed-signature negatives. 7/7 pass. VERIFICATION: vitest 7/7 green; tsc ratchet holds at 1083; lint ratchet DECREASED 12003->12001 (two `payload: any` params became `rawBody: string`) — baseline tightened. Note the primary Stripe path (stripe-service.ts constructEvent) was already correct; this fixes the secondary generic path.

Grep the whole supabase/functions tree for "req.headers.get('x-tenant-id') ||" and confirm no handler orders the header before the JWT claim (12 files match today; 9 are genuine offenders, the 3 blog/monitoring ones already order app_metadata first)
Add a regression test (or edge smoke test) proving a JWT for tenant A + header x-tenant-id: tenantB returns 403, not tenant B's rows

Typecheck passes: npm run check

Verified: grep shows no header-first ordering remains; deno check net-zero on all 9 (admin 0->0 after casting header fallback to preserve string typing at 7 downstream call sites). userStories.title: [SECURITY/MEDIUM] Harden root-admin raw SQL executor with a read-only DB role instead of regex parsing
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need the root-admin SQL console to be safe by construction rather than by a home-grown keyword/semicolon regex, so that a crafted query using escaped quotes or dollar-quoting cannot slip past the filter.
acceptanceCriteria: server/routes-root-admin.ts (~lines 483-508): run the submitted query inside a read-only transaction (SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY) using a dedicated low-privilege DB role with SELECT-only grants
Remove reliance on the .replace(/'[^']*'/g,'') literal-stripping regex as the sole safety gate (it does not handle '' escapes or $$ dollar-quoting)
Add a test that a query with a dollar-quoted or escaped-quote payload cannot execute a second statement or a write
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by security audit 2026-07-14. Defense-in-depth: route is already requireRootAdmin-gated and SELECT-only, so this hardens rather than fixes an external break. | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. (1) THE REAL FIX — the console statement now runs inside a transaction with `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY`, so write capability is removed BY THE ENGINE rather than by text matching: Postgres raises SQLSTATE 25006 ("cannot execute INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL in a read-only transaction") for anything that slips past the static gate, including payloads nobody thought of. SET LOCAL scopes the settings to the transaction so the pooled connection is unaffected once it returns to the pool. This is the "safe by construction" the story asks for. (2) NEW server/lib/sql-console-guard.ts replaces the `.replace(/'[^']*'/g, '')` literal stripping with a real lexer implementing Postgres's rules for '' escapes, E'' backslash strings, "quoted idents", $$ / $tag$ dollar quoting, -- line comments and NESTED /* */ block comments. The gate (SELECT/WITH-only, single-statement, dangerous-keyword denylist, 1000-row cap) now runs against text that agrees with the server about what is code and what is data. The denylist is deliberately KEPT even though the read-only transaction covers writes, because it also blocks things a read-only transaction happily permits: pg_read_file, pg_sleep, pg_terminate_backend, SET ROLE. (3) TESTS (AC bullet 3): server/tests/unit/sql-console-guard.test.ts, 30 tests, driven by the exact payload classes the AC names — a second statement hidden after a dollar-quoted literal, after an escaped-quote literal, after an E-string, and behind a comment-terminated line; plus every write verb, a write disguised by a leading comment, and the non-write dangers above. Full unit suite green (60 files / 1263 tests); tsc holds at the 1315 baseline. | AN HONEST CORRECTION TO THE STORY'S PREMISE — the old regex was NOT exploitable in the way the description claims ("a crafted query using escaped quotes or dollar-quoting cannot slip past the filter"). I diffed the OLD stripping against the NEW lexer across the named payload classes and every divergence went the SAFE way: the old regex OVER-blocks, it does not under-block. `SELECT $$a;b$$ FROM t` — the old regex never strips dollar quotes, so it sees the data semicolon and REJECTS a legitimate query; `SELECT $x$ DELETE FROM users $x$ FROM t` — it leaves the literal visible so the DENYLIST fires on data; nested block comments likewise. On the escaped-quote cases (SELECT 'a''; SELECT 1; --') the old and new strippers AGREE. I could not construct a payload where the old regex MISSED a real second statement. So this story is genuinely what its own note says — defence-in-depth hardening, not an open hole — and the practical user-visible effect of the lexer is FEWER FALSE REJECTIONS (dollar-quoted and nested-comment queries now work). The security value comes from the read-only transaction, and from no longer depending on a parser that disagrees with Postgres about what a string is — which is worth doing precisely because "it happens to fail safe today" is not a property anyone should be relying on. | NOT DONE — the AC's "dedicated low-privilege DB role with SELECT-only grants" is an OPS change, not a code change: it needs a role created in Postgres (CREATE ROLE ... ; GRANT SELECT ...) and a SECOND connection string for the app to use for this endpoint (e.g. READONLY_DATABASE_URL), plus pool wiring. That cannot be done from here — the DB is unreachable (the pooler rejects the checked-in credentials) and the role/grants live in the target environment, not the repo. The read-only TRANSACTION delivers the same protection against WRITES with no infra change, so the remaining gap the dedicated role would close is READ SCOPE: the console still connects as the app role, so any SELECT can read across tenants and bypass RLS. That residual is documented in the route header as a TODO(prod) and is unchanged by this story. Worth a follow-up if cross-tenant read via the console is considered unacceptable.

userStories.title: [PERF/HIGH] Eliminate the edge-router per-response double JSON parse + recursive date walk
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need the edge dispatcher to stop buffering, JSON.parsing, recursively walking, and re-stringifying every response body, so that the platform-wide CPU/memory tax on 100% of prod JSON traffic is removed and large list responses stop paying an O(payload)-twice cost.
acceptanceCriteria: supabase/functions/server.ts (lines 172-182 + recursive walker 19-38): stop unconditionally doing const body = await response.json(); normalizeDates(body); re-stringify on every response
Gate date normalization to only the callers that need it (e.g. iOS User-Agent/header), or move it into the specific handlers/PostgREST that emit PG timestamps
At minimum, skip normalization for bodies over a size threshold and add a cheap length/charAt prefilter before running PG_TIMESTAMP_RE.test on every string value
Verify streaming responses are no longer buffered by the router
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by performance audit 2026-07-14. Highest-leverage single change: every prod response currently pays this. Confirm no handler depends on the router mutating its dates before changing the default. | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. CRITICAL FINDING FIRST — AC BULLET 2 ("gate date normalization to only the callers that need it, e.g. iOS User-Agent/header") MUST NOT BE IMPLEMENTED. It would be a silent, platform-wide DATA CORRECTNESS regression. Reason: NOTHING in shared/schema.ts uses withTimezone — all 432 timestamp columns are `timestamp WITHOUT time zone`, so PostgREST emits NAIVE strings ("2024-01-15T10:30:00.123456"). JavaScript parses a naive timestamp as LOCAL time, so new Date("2024-01-15T10:30:00") in a browser at UTC-5 is SIX HOURS off. The Z this router appends is exactly what makes the WEB frontend render correct times — it is a correctness dependency of every browser client, not an iOS convenience, despite the comment naming iOS. Gating it behind an iOS User-Agent would shift every timestamp for every web user by their UTC offset, with no error and no test failure. This is precisely what the story's own note asked to confirm ("Confirm no handler depends on the router mutating its dates before changing the default") — the answer is that the entire web client does. So normalization stays UNIVERSAL and was made CHEAP instead, which achieves the story's actual goal (remove the CPU/memory tax) without the regression. WHAT CHANGED: the old path ran JSON.parse -> a recursive walk that REBUILT every object/array -> JSON.stringify, on 100% of JSON responses (3 full passes + a complete object-graph allocation). Replaced with (a) a single regex pass over the RAW TEXT — no parse, no rebuild, no re-stringify — matching only quoted JSON tokens that are exactly a PG timestamp, (b) a Date-free fast path: for naive/+00:00/-00:00 (the overwhelming majority) the result is just ts.slice(0,19)+'Z', so no Date object is constructed at all; only a genuine non-zero UTC offset takes the Date path, (c) a cheap prefilter (text.indexOf('T') === -1 -> skip the scan entirely, which covers date-free payloads). MEASURED on a real 934KB list response: 23.91ms -> 7.50ms per response = 3.2x, on 100% of prod JSON traffic. EQUIVALENCE PROOF (this is a hot, subtle path, so it was verified not argued): a harness EXTRACTED both implementations from source — the new one from the patched file, the old one from `git show HEAD` — so neither was retyped by hand, then fuzzed 80,000 randomly generated timestamps (all fraction widths 0-6 digits, and zones '', Z, +00:00, -00:00, +05:30, -05:00, +14:00, -11:00, +09:45) => 0 mismatches, plus 8 whole-document shapes (single row, 200-row list, bare array, nested, empty object/array, unicode+escapes, no-dates) => all byte-identical. TWO SUBTLETIES DELIBERATELY PRESERVED, both verified by the fuzz: (i) a value already ending in Z is returned UNTOUCHED — the old code appended a SECOND Z, got an Invalid Date and fell through to the original string, so "...T10:30:00.123Z" keeps its fractional seconds. That is arguably a latent bug for iOS ISO8601DateFormatter, but it is EXISTING behavior and out of scope to change here; flagged for a follow-up. (ii) object KEYS are never rewritten — the recursive version only normalized values, so the text pass checks whether the next non-space char after the token is ':' and skips it. Without that guard a timestamp-shaped key would have been silently rewritten. BONUS BUG FIXED: the old code did `await response.json()` inside a try, and on parse failure fell through to `return new Response(response.body)` — but .json() had ALREADY consumed the body, so the "pass through the original response" fallback itself threw. Now the body is read once via .text() and reused, so the fallback is real. Also drops a stale content-length header (timestamp rewriting changes byte length). STREAMING (AC bullet 4): only application/json is buffered, which is unavoidable if the bytes must be rewritten. Everything else — text/event-stream (SSE), PDFs, octet-stream — still streams straight through via `new Response(response.body)` and is not buffered. That was already true and is preserved. deno check: identical error profile before/after (2 TS18046 + 1 TS2307 + 1 TS2345, all pre-existing); tsc unaffected (supabase/ is outside tsconfig include). Removed the now-orphaned PG_TIMESTAMP_RE constant. | FOLLOW-UPS: (a) The Z-ending-keeps-fraction quirk above means iOS may still receive "...T10:30:00.123Z" from any handler that emits an already-Z-suffixed timestamp; if iOS decode failures are ever reported, that is the first place to look — the fix is one line in normalizeTimestamp, but it is a behavior change and wants its own story + iOS verification. (b) The REAL structural fix is upstream: make the 432 timestamp columns `withTimezone: true` (or have handlers emit ISO-8601 UTC), after which this router pass could be deleted outright rather than optimized. That is a migration, not a router change. (c) If a size ceiling is ever wanted (AC bullet 3), the natural knob is now a single early return in normalizeDatesInJsonText — but note that skipping normalization on large bodies would reintroduce the timezone bug selectively for big lists, which is worse than the cost; the text pass is cheap enough that a threshold is not needed.

userStories.title: [PERF/HIGH] Cut two serialized auth round-trips per request (local JWT verify + role cache)
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need edge functions to avoid an HTTP round-trip to GoTrue (auth.getUser) plus a second role-lookup query on every request, so that per-request latency across the whole platform drops.
acceptanceCriteria: Verify the JWT signature locally in supabase/functions/_shared/auth.ts (jose + GoTrue JWKS/secret) using claims already in the token, instead of calling supabase.auth.getUser(jwt) on every request; OR cache getUser results by token-hash with a short TTL

For functions that additionally query users->roles for gating (e.g. platform-analytics/index.ts:70-86, platform-cs/index.ts:32-43, deployment-readiness/index.ts:53-57), cache the role row by token-hash/user-id with a short TTL
Confirm platform-admin / role-level gates still hold after the change (add/keep a test)
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by performance audit 2026-07-14. Two serialized network hops on every prod request in ~212 functions. Local verification must still honor token revocation expectations — document the TTL tradeoff. | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. KEY MEASUREMENT FIRST — the AC pointed at _shared/auth.ts, but that is NOT where the tax lives: only 52 of the 255 function dirs import _shared/auth.ts, while 214 call supabase.auth.getUser(jwt) DIRECTLY (that is the story's "~212 functions"). Fixing only requireAuth would have optimized the minority path and left the real cost untouched. The choke point is _shared/supabase.ts createSupabaseClient(req) — the shared factory all 214 already go through — so the cache is installed THERE and every one of them benefits with ZERO call-site edits. CHOSE CACHING OVER LOCAL JWT VERIFY (the AC offered either). Local jose/JWKS verification would remove the hop but CANNOT see a revoked or signed-out session at all, so a stolen token stays valid for its whole lifetime; it also puts hand-rolled crypto in front of ~212 functions. Caching keeps GoTrue as the source of truth and bounds staleness to a short TTL — strictly safer for the same win on repeat traffic. WHAT LANDED: (1) NEW supabase/functions/_shared/auth-cache.ts — a token-hash-keyed TTL cache for getUser plus cachedRoleLookup for the second hop. Deliberately import-clean (no supabase-js, no Deno APIs at module scope) so it is unit-testable under the repo vitest runner. (2) _shared/supabase.ts wraps the returned client so getUser(jwt) is cached for all 214 direct callers; a NO-ARGUMENT getUser() is passed straight through UNCACHED, because it resolves against the client's own session/header state which we are not keying on — caching it could return the wrong user. (3) _shared/auth.ts requireAuth routed through the same cache (the other 52). (4) The second serialized hop: the users->roles gate is cached by user id in ALL SEVEN functions that run it (database-updater, platform-activities, platform-analytics, platform-crm, platform-cs, platform-deals, root-admin) — the AC named only three; the query is byte-identical in all seven. deployment-readiness (also named) does NOT do a role query, only getUser, so it is already covered by the factory wrap. TRADEOFF, per the story note: a revoked token keeps working for up to AUTH_CACHE_TTL_MS (default 30s), and a role change lands within ROLE_CACHE_TTL_MS (default 30s). Both are env-tunable and both accept 0 as a full kill switch (no redeploy needed, TTL is read at call time). The cache is per-isolate, so a restart clears it. TESTS (AC bullet 3): new server/tests/unit/auth-cache.test.ts, 17 tests. This sits in front of authentication for ~212 functions, so the four safety invariants are PINNED rather than assumed: (1) errors are NEVER cached — a failure cannot be replayed and a transient GoTrue blip cannot lock a user out (both tested); (2) a cache entry never outlives the token — TTL is capped at the JWT exp, so a token expiring in 5s under a 30s TTL is re-verified rather than served stale (this one would be an auth bypass if wrong); (3) keys are SHA-256 hashes, not raw bearer tokens; (4) the cache is bounded. Gate behavior is pinned too: role rows key by user id, and a low-privilege user still gets level 1 on a cache hit even when an admin row is cached (no cross-contamination), a null role row is never cached (a missing role re-checks instead of pinning a user in or out), and a role change is picked up after the TTL. VERIFICATION: deno check clean (0 errors) on all 10 touched edge files; full unit suite green (58 files / 1220 tests); tsc holds at the 1335 baseline. | TWO TYPE GOTCHAS worth remembering for anyone touching this: (a) `T extends ReturnType<typeof createClient>` does NOT work as a constraint — with no type args that resolves to SupabaseClient<unknown, never, GenericSchema> and the real client is not assignable to it (TS2345 "public is not assignable to never"). Constrain structurally instead (`T extends { auth: unknown }`). (b) cachedRoleLookup takes `() => T | PromiseLike<T>`, NOT `() => Promise<T>`: supabase's PostgrestBuilder is a THENABLE, not a real Promise (no .catch/.finally), so a Promise-typed callback rejects a bare `admin.from(...).single()` and breaks T inference at every call site (TS2739 + TS2339 on .data). | FOLLOW-UPS / NOT DONE: (i) createSupabaseClient(req) still builds a NEW supabase client per request (an allocation per call, on top of the hop this story removed). Reusing one anon client and passing the jwt explicitly would cut that too, but it changes the shape of a factory 214 files depend on — separate story. (ii) The 214 direct auth.getUser callers are still an architectural smell: they each re-implement auth+tenant resolution rather than using requireAuth, which is why the tenant-resolution fallbacks in _shared/auth.ts do not protect them. Migrating them onto requireAuth would be the real consolidation (and would make this cache redundant at the call sites). (iii) No integration test exercises a REAL platform-admin gate end-to-end — the edge functions are Deno and the repo runner is node/vitest, so the gate logic is pinned at the cache layer only. A deno-test harness for the edge functions is a genuine gap worth its own story.

userStories.title: [PERF/HIGH] Replace full-table scans with SQL aggregates + pagination in analytics, billing, AP/AR
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need dashboard and ledger endpoints to compute counts/sums in Postgres and paginate list results, so that they stop fetching entire tables into JS (which also silently truncates at PostgREST's 1000-row cap and produces wrong numbers as data grows).
acceptanceCriteria: platform-analytics/index.ts: replace select('*') + JS reduce/filter (helpers ~100-114 used at 121-129, 441, 537-543, 627-633, 685-688, 761-763) with { count: 'exact', head: true } for counts, narrowed selects for sums, or a Postgres RPC/view; run the independent fetches in revenue-metrics (121-129) and churn-analysis (737-763) via Promise.all
billing/index.ts (141-186): compute revenue/outstanding/overdue/MRR via SQL aggregates/RPC instead of loading every invoice row for the tenant

account-payable/index.ts (132-141) and account-receivable/index.ts (150-160): add .range() pagination (frontend already handles { data, total }); compute /summary buckets with filtered aggregate queries instead of fetching all rows
platform-cs/index.ts (75-82) and platform-analytics health-trends (627-657): average overall_score with a SQL avg() rather than fetching every health-score row
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by performance audit 2026-07-14. These are the biggest data-volume time bombs as tenants grow, and the 1000-row cap makes the metrics wrong (not just slow). platform-cs already does head-count Promise.all correctly — mirror that pattern. | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. HOW THE APPROACH WAS CHOSEN (not guessed): the AC offers "count/head, narrowed selects for sums, or a Postgres RPC/view". Checked what is actually PROVEN in this codebase before picking: `{ count: exact, head: true }` is used in 51 files; `.rpc()` in 11 files with SQL functions living in drizzle/functions/*.sql (a documented convention — idempotent CREATE OR REPLACE, applied out of band via \i, SECURITY INVOKER, tenant-scoped by explicit parameter, deliberately kept OUT of drizzle/migrations per that dir's README). PostgREST aggregate selects (.sum()/.avg()) have ZERO usage anywhere, so that feature is unproven here and was NOT used. THE REAL BUG IS CORRECTNESS, NOT SPEED — worth restating because it drove every decision: PostgREST silently caps a response at db-max-rows (1000 by default) and does NOT error. So every one of these "SELECT * then reduce in JS" sites produced WRONG MONEY NUMBERS for any tenant past 1000 rows (revenue, outstanding, MRR/ARR, AP/AR aging buckets) — quietly under-reported, with no failure to notice. Narrowing a select does not fix that; only aggregating in SQL or paging explicitly does. | WHAT LANDED: (1) NEW drizzle/functions/billing-aggregates.sql — ap_aging_summary(tenant), ar_aging_summary(tenant), billing_analytics(tenant), using SUM(...) FILTER (WHERE ...) so each bucket is one pass. The bucket boundaries reproduce the JS they replace EXACTLY (AP: due<now -> overdue, <=now+7d -> dueThisWeek, else current; AR: days past due <=0/30/60/90/90+), so applying it must not move any number. README.md updated with the file + its consumers, per that directory's convention. (2) billing/index.ts /analytics, account-payable /summary and account-receivable /summary now call the RPC and FALL BACK to the existing JS scan when it is missing — drizzle/functions is applied OUT OF BAND, so the code can legitimately deploy before the SQL exists; a missing function must not 500 the page. (3) AP + AR list endpoints now .range() paginate via a new shared readRange() helper in _shared/http.ts (there was no pagination helper; now both AP/AR share one). Their `total` already came from an exact count, so the frontend's { data, total } contract is unchanged. (4) platform-analytics revenue-metrics: churnedTenants and newCustomers were full row fetches used ONLY for `.length` -> now { count: exact, head: true } DB counts; activeTenants still needs values but the select is narrowed to just current_mrr; all three now run via Promise.all instead of serialized. Added countRecords() + fetchAllRows() helpers (fetchAllRows pages explicitly so a sum is correct at any size). (5) platform-cs health average: was a plain select of every overall_score, so past 1000 rows it averaged an ARBITRARY SUBSET. Now paged. Its counts were already correct head:true + Promise.all (as the AC noted) and were left alone. VERIFICATION: deno check clean (0 errors) on all 5 touched edge functions; tsc holds at the 1335 baseline; full unit suite green (59 files / 1233 tests). | IMPORTANT CAVEATS / NOT DONE — read before closing this out: (a) THE SQL IS NOT VERIFIED AGAINST A LIVE DATABASE. The pooler rejects the checked-in credentials ("Tenant or user not found" — the CLAUDE.md note that the committed keys are rotated/stale), so billing-aggregates.sql has never been executed. It must be applied (\i drizzle/functions/billing-aggregates.sql) and SPOT-CHECKED against the JS fallback on a real tenant before being trusted — compare /billing/analytics and both /summary endpoints with the RPC present vs absent and confirm the numbers match. The fallback means a MISSING function is safe; it does NOT protect against WRONG SQL. (b) A PRE-EXISTING ODDITY PRESERVED DELIBERATELY: billing analytics reports averageInvoiceAmount = totalRevenue / totalInvoices, i.e. PAID revenue divided by ALL invoices (not paid-over-paid, and not total-over-total). That is almost certainly a bug, but changing it would silently move a number the story did not ask about; it is reproduced exactly and flagged here (billing_analytics also returns paidCount so a future fix has what it needs). (c) platform-analytics still has other select(*) + JS-reduce sites the AC lists (441, 537-543, 627-657, 685-688, 761-763 in the original numbering) plus the churn-analysis Promise.all — revenue-metrics was done as the pattern and the helpers (countRecords/fetchAllRows) are now in place for the rest, but they are NOT all converted. fetchDeals is also still an unpaged select(*). Worth a follow-up pass; the mechanical part is done. (d) fetchAllRows pages in the client, which is correct but still transfers every row — it fixes the WRONG-NUMBER bug, not the transfer cost. The full fix for the platform_* sums is an RPC like the billing one.

userStories.title: [PERF/HIGH] Fix backend N+1 query fan-out across dashboards and list endpoints
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need list/dashboard endpoints to batch their per-row lookups into single grouped/IN queries, so that response time stops scaling linearly with fleet/team/pipeline size and the connection pool stops being hammered.
acceptanceCriteria: server/routes-remote-monitoring.ts (29-52, 450): replace 2-queries-per-device with one DISTINCT ON (device_id) latest-metrics query + one grouped 24h aggregate via inArray(deviceId, ids)
server/routes-technician-management.ts (92-118): replace 2 count queries per technician with a single GROUP BY technicianId using count(*) FILTER (WHERE ...)
server/routes-root-admin.ts (317-333, and enrich loops at 165/398/608/741): select roles.name/level and tenants.name in the existing joined base query and delete the per-row enrichment lookups
server/routes-service-dispatch.ts (699-729): collect all part numbers and do one inArray(partNumber, all) query for batch-check-parts
server/routes-address-books.ts (218-227): replace per-book count with one GROUP BY bookId over inArray(bookId, ...)
server/routes-today-dashboard.ts (137-148): add a limit and push the stale (>7 days) predicate into SQL
server/routes-chatbot.ts (313-326): replace up-to-50 per-rep proposal scans with one GROUP BY assignedTo count(*)/max(updatedAt) over inArray(assignedTo, repIds)
server/routes-predictive-maintenance-hub.ts (40,61,117): batch per-unit metrics with inArray(serialNumber, [...]) and paginate the equipment base query
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by performance audit 2026-07-14. Grouped here because they share one fix pattern (batch with GROUP BY / inArray). Also add limits to unbounded storage.ts list methods (getEquipment :2871, getContracts :2883, getServiceTickets :2895, getMeterReadings :2957, getInvoices :2997) called on request paths (e.g. routes-workflow-mobile.ts:2059-2060 loads the whole equipment table to find one row). | PROGRESS 2026-07-16 (passes stays FALSE — 5 of the 9 named sites remain; see REMAINING). FOUR SITES BATCHED, all following the same recipe: run ONE grouped query over the ids already in hand, build a Map, then default the misses to zero (a row with no matches produces no GROUP BY row, which is exactly what the per-row COUNT returned — that default is what keeps the output identical). (1) server/routes-technician-management.ts: ran TWO count queries PER TECHNICIAN (2N round-trips growing with the team). Collapsed to one GROUP BY assigned_technician_id using count(*) FILTER (WHERE ...) for both buckets in a single pass. Predicates reproduced byte-for-byte (active = status NOT IN (completed,cancelled); completedThisMonth = status completed AND updated_at >= the 1st of the current month). (2) server/routes-address-books.ts: entryCount(b.id) per book -> one GROUP BY book_id over inArray(books). (3) server/routes-chatbot.ts: up to FIFTY per-rep queries, each pulling up to 200 proposal rows, purely to derive a count and a max(updated_at) -> one GROUP BY assigned_to with count(*) + max(updated_at). (4) server/routes-workflow-mobile.ts:2059 (called out in the story notes): did `(await storage.getEquipment(tenantId)).find(e => e.id === equipmentId)` — pulling the tenant's ENTIRE equipment table across the wire to satisfy a PRIMARY-KEY lookup. Added storage.getEquipmentById(id, tenant) (a tenant-scoped SELECT ... LIMIT 1) to IStorage + DatabaseStorage and used it. Grepped for other `await storage.getEquipment(tenantId)` callers: that was the only one. VERIFICATION: tsc holds at the 1335 baseline (routes-technician-management still has its 9 PRE-EXISTING TS2769s on the requirePermission([...]) route-registration lines — verified identical count at HEAD, so none are mine); full unit suite green (59 files / 1233 tests). | ONE DELIBERATE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, called out because it is a user-visible number: in routes-chatbot.ts `openDeals` was `open.length` taken from a query with .limit(200), so it silently SATURATED at 200 — a rep with 500 open proposals reported 200. count(*) now reports the true figure, which can exceed 200. That is a fix rather than a regression, but it will move the number on screen for very busy reps. | REMAINING (all 5 files verified to still exist — these are real, not stale AC entries): (a) server/routes-remote-monitoring.ts (29-52, 450) — 2 queries per device; wants one DISTINCT ON (device_id) latest-metrics query + one grouped 24h aggregate via inArray. (b) server/routes-root-admin.ts (317-333 + enrich loops at 165/398/608/741) — select roles.name/level and tenants.name in the existing joined base query and delete the per-row enrichment lookups. (c) server/routes-service-dispatch.ts (699-729) — collect all part numbers, one inArray(partNumber, all) for batch-check-parts. (d) server/routes-today-dashboard.ts (137-148) — add a limit and push the stale (>7 days) predicate into SQL. (e) server/routes-predictive-maintenance-hub.ts (40,61,117) — batch per-unit metrics with inArray(serialNumber, ...) and paginate the equipment base query. ALSO NOT DONE: the story notes ask for limits on the unbounded storage.ts list methods (getEquipment:2871, getContracts:2883, getServiceTickets:2895, getMeterReadings:2957, getInvoices:2997 — the line numbers have drifted but the methods are all still `select().from(x).where(eq(tenantId))` with no limit). Adding a limit to those CHANGES THEIR CONTRACT for every existing caller (a caller that today gets the full list would silently start getting a page), so it needs a caller-by-caller audit rather than a blanket edit — that is why only the getEquipmentById fix landed here, which removes the worst caller without touching the shared method. | PROGRESS 2026-07-16 (part 2) — 2 more sites batched; 6 of 9 AC bullets now done. (5) server/routes-service-dispatch.ts batch-check-parts — the worst fan-out in this story: a NESTED Promise.all running one inventory query PER PART, PER TICKET (N tickets x M parts round-trips) to answer a single batch question. Now collects every DISTINCT part number across the whole batch, asks once via inArray(inventoryItems.partNumber, all), and resolves each ticket from a Map. Behaviour preserved exactly: a part with no inventory row is unavailable, which is what the old `(item?.quantityAvailable || 0) > 0` produced on an empty result — the Map lookup defaults to false for the same reason. (6) server/routes-today-dashboard.ts — loaded EVERY open deal for the tenant (prospecting/qualification/proposal/ negotiation), computed "days since update" in JS, filtered to stale (>7 days), sorted and kept 5. So the work grew with the entire pipeline to render a 5-row panel. The staleness predicate, the ordering and the limit all run in SQL now. Two details that keep it identical: COALESCE(updated_at, created_at) mirrors the JS fallback to createdAt when updatedAt was null; and ordering by that ASC puts the OLDEST first, which is what the JS `sort desc by daysSinceUpdate` produced. Both verified not to move the ratchet: tsc holds at 1314, and each touched file has the SAME pre-existing error count as at HEAD (today-dashboard 29, service-dispatch 29 — all phantom-column/activities errors that predate this work, none introduced). Full unit suite green (61 files / 1269 tests). | REMAINING (3 of 9): (a) server/routes-remote-monitoring.ts (29-52, 450) — 2 queries per device; wants one DISTINCT ON (device_id) latest-metrics query + one grouped 24h aggregate via inArray. (b) server/routes-root-admin.ts (317-333 + enrich loops at 165/398/608/741) — select roles.name/level and tenants.name in the existing joined base query and delete the per-row enrichment lookups. userStories.title: [PERF/HIGH] Fix N+1 writes and loop-invariant re-fetches in invoice/meter billing generation
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need billing runs to bulk-insert invoices and hoist loop-invariant reads, so that a run over hundreds of meter readings does not take minutes and does not re-read/re-write the same customer balance N times (a race hazard).
acceptanceCriteria: supabase/functions/billing/handlers/generate-invoices.ts (152-173): replace per-reading insert(...).single() + meter_readings.update(...) inside the for loop with a bulk insert([...]) and a batched update per invoice-id group (or an RPC)

server/routes-workflow-mobile.ts (2154-2224): hoist getContractTieredRatesByContract and the customer fetch out of the loop (they are loop-invariant for a contract), batch-insert invoices, and apply one summed balance update instead of N sequential updates
Confirm produced invoice amounts/totals are unchanged by the batching (test against a known set of readings)
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by performance audit 2026-07-14. The reads are already batched in generate-invoices.ts (60-88); only the writes are N+1. The mobile path does 5 sequential queries per reading incl. an invariant tieredRates re-fetch. | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. EDGE PATH (supabase/functions/billing/handlers/generate-invoices.ts): the reads were already batched; the WRITES were the N+1 — an insert(...).single() PLUS a meter_readings update per reading, i.e. 2N serialized round-trips. Split the pipeline into a PURE prepareInvoiceRows() (no I/O — this is what makes the billing math testable, which AC bullet 3 demands) and an I/O half that does ONE bulk insert for the whole batch, then marks the readings processed with bounded concurrency (chunks of 25) instead of strictly one-at-a-time: 2N serialized becomes 1 + ceil(N/25) waves. WHY NOT A SINGLE UPDATE: each reading needs a DIFFERENT invoice_id/billing_amount, so it cannot collapse into one UPDATE. A PostgREST upsert of the full rows WOULD be one statement, but it rewrites every column from values read earlier and would clobber any concurrent change — rejected deliberately in favour of chunked concurrency. RESILIENCE PRESERVED: a bulk insert is all-or-nothing, so one bad row would fail the ENTIRE run — strictly worse than the old per-row behaviour, which failed only that reading and kept going. The bulk path therefore FALLS BACK to per-row inserts on error, keeping the old per-reading fault isolation while the fast path stays the norm. Inserted invoices are mapped back to their readings by invoice_number (unique within the batch by construction) rather than by array position, so nothing depends on the driver preserving input order. MOBILE PATH (server/routes-workflow-mobile.ts POST /api/contracts/:contractId/process-meter-billing): hoisted getContractTieredRatesByContract OUT of the loop (contractId is fixed for the whole endpoint — it was N identical queries returning identical rows) and hoisted the customer fetch out too. The balance is now summed locally and applied as ONE update after the loop instead of N read-modify-write cycles on the same row — that was the race hazard called out in the description: any concurrent balance write landing between a read and its write was silently lost. Final state is identical (starting balance + sum of every invoice). VERIFICATION: new server/tests/unit/generate-invoices.test.ts (13 tests) asserting amounts are unchanged by the batching, with every expected number COMPUTED BY HAND from the tiered-rate rules rather than snapshotted from the implementation (a snapshot would happily lock in a wrong number): flat-rate 1000*0.01 + 500*0.08 + 100 base = 150; tiered banding 500@0.02 + 500@0.01 + 100 base = 115; a 3-reading batch grand total of 390 matching the old per-row accumulator; zero-copy readings still billing the base; and the skip semantics (no contract_id / contract missing from the map are skipped silently and NOT marked failed, exactly as the original loop did). tsc holds at the 1335 baseline; deno check clean; full unit suite green (59 files / 1233 tests). | TWO REAL BUGS FOUND AND FIXED WHILE DOING THIS (neither is in the AC): (1) SEVERE — server/routes-workflow-mobile.ts built its invoice number with a template literal that was BROKEN BY A LINE BREAK between the dollar sign and the opening brace, so the Date.now() placeholder NEVER INTERPOLATED. Every invoice from that endpoint got the same literal string ("INV-<contractNumber>-$" + newline + the raw placeholder text). invoice_number is UNIQUE, so the FIRST reading inserted fine and the SECOND always violated the constraint and 500'd the endpoint — meaning this path could never bill more than one reading per contract, and nobody noticed because the perf problem it was filed under masked it. Fixed to a real interpolation plus a trailing index for intra-run uniqueness. (2) The edge path built `INV-${Date.now()}-${random}` per row. Under a BULK insert every row is written in the SAME millisecond, so Date.now() is identical across the batch and uniqueness rested entirely on a 5-char random suffix — one collision would fail the whole batch. The row index is now part of the number, making intra-batch uniqueness structural rather than probabilistic. A test generates 200 rows under one frozen clock and asserts all 200 numbers are distinct. | FOLLOW-UPS (found, deliberately NOT changed — this is a perf story and these are behaviour changes): (i) In the mobile path, lastMeterReadingDate ends up as the OLDEST processed reading, not the newest: readings are ordered by readingDate DESC and the old loop overwrote the field on every iteration, so the LAST one written is the last element = the oldest. The batched version reproduces that exactly (deliberately), but it looks like a latent bug worth its own story — a field named lastMeterReadingDate almost certainly wants MAX(readingDate). (ii) Neither billing path is transactional: invoices can be inserted and then a meter_readings update can fail, leaving a reading pending against an already-issued invoice (double-billing on the next run). The old code had the same hole; batching does not widen it, but an RPC/transaction is the real fix. (iii) The mobile path still does one createInvoice + one updateMeterReading per reading (2N); it uses the storage layer rather than a raw client, so a bulk insert there needs a new storage method — worth doing, but larger than this story.

userStories.title: [PERF/HIGH] Add missing indexes on 10 hot tables (tenant/status/created_at + FK columns)
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need composite indexes on the hottest multi-tenant tables, so that the most common list/join/aggregate queries stop doing sequential scans that get slower with every row added.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Drizzle index blocks + a generated migration for: proposal_line_items (proposal_id, line_number) and (tenant_id); proposals (tenant_id, proposal_type, status) and (tenant_id, created_at DESC); audit_logs (tenant_id, timestamp DESC) and (tenant_id, resource, resource_id); invoices (tenant_id, invoice_status), (tenant_id, customer_id), (external_customer_id); equipment (tenant_id, customer_id) and (tenant_id, equipment_status); contracts (tenant_id, customer_id) and (tenant_id, status)

Also index: accounts_payable (tenant_id, status, due_date); accounts_receivable (tenant_id, status, due_date); business_record_activities (business_record_id, created_at DESC) and (tenant_id); users (tenant_id); inventory_items (tenant_id)

Verify against the live DB with pg_indexes which of these already exist before generating the migration (journal reportedly stops at 0009 — but the schema files define NO indexes for these 10 tables, so new index blocks are required, not just applying pending migrations)
npm run db:generate produces the migration SQL; review it; do not db:push to production
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by performance/index audit 2026-07-14. business_records, service_tickets, meter_readings, signature_requests, blog_audit_log ARE already indexed (baseline 0000) — do not duplicate. proposals is the live quotes table (proposal_type='quote'); its only index today is proposals_share_token_key (pending migration 0017). | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. THE AC'S CENTRAL CLAIM WAS FALSE. It states "the schema files define NO indexes for these 10 tables, so new index blocks are required" — in fact 6 of the 11 named tables were ALREADY indexed by the earlier CR-028 and PA-026 stories (whose migrations are literally 0010_cr028_perf_indexes.sql / 0011_pa026_perf_indexes.sql). Blindly following the AC would have created DUPLICATE indexes, which cost write amplification for zero read benefit. Verified per-table by paren-matching each pgTable block (a regex bleeds across adjacent table blocks and gave plainly wrong answers — e.g. reporting purchase_orders_* indexes under accounts_payable). ALREADY COVERED, deliberately NOT touched: equipment (tenant_id,customer_id)+(tenant_id,equipment_status) and contracts (tenant_id,customer_id)+(tenant_id,status) are complete; invoices already had (tenant_id,invoice_status) and (tenant_id,customer_id); proposals already had (tenant_id,created_at); proposal_line_items already had (tenant_id). inventory_items (tenant_id) is ALREADY SERVED by the existing (tenant_id,category) index via the leftmost-prefix rule — adding a bare (tenant_id) index there would be pure redundancy, so it was not added. ADDED — 10 genuinely missing indexes, in shared/schema.ts + shared/security-schema.ts AND in a hand-authored migration: proposals (tenant_id,proposal_type,status) [proposals is the live quotes table and callers filter by type BEFORE status, which the existing (tenant_id,status) cannot serve — different leftmost prefix, so not redundant]; proposal_line_items (proposal_id,line_number) [QUOTE-020 makes line_number the ordering source of truth and every read path orders by it]; invoices (external_customer_id) [doubles as the service-ticket ref and backs the ?ticketId= filter, queried WITHOUT a tenant prefix]; audit_logs (tenant_id,timestamp) + (tenant_id,resource, resource_id) [this table had ZERO indexes despite being append-heavy — the single worst case found]; accounts_payable and accounts_receivable (tenant_id,status,due_date) [AP/AR aging]; business_record_activities (business_record_id,created_at) + (tenant_id); users (tenant_id). ONE INDEX DROPPED: proposal_line_items_proposal_idx (proposal_id) is fully covered by the new (proposal_id,line_number) via leftmost prefix, so it is replaced rather than left alongside it as a redundant write cost. audit_logs also needed `index` added to its drizzle-orm/pg-core import (security-schema.ts imported none, since the table previously had no indexes). SORT DIRECTION: the AC asks for DESC on created_at/timestamp. Used plain btree (ASC) deliberately — PostgreSQL scans a btree BACKWARDS at the same cost, so DESC only matters for MIXED-direction multi-column sorts, which none of these queries do. It also matches the existing *_created_idx convention from CR-028/PA-026. VERIFICATION: the DB is unreachable from here (the pooler rejects the checked-in credentials with "Tenant or user not found" — consistent with the CLAUDE.md note that the committed keys are rotated/stale), so the AC's pg_indexes check could NOT be performed and is left for whoever applies this. Instead the migration was cross-checked against Drizzle's own getTableConfig(): every CREATE INDEX names a real table and real PHYSICAL column names, every index is declared in the schema, the DROPped one is gone from the schema too, and all 10 appear in both schema and migration. tsc holds at the 1335 baseline; full unit suite green (58 files / 1220 tests). | MAJOR INFRASTRUCTURE FINDING — `npm run db:generate` IS UNUSABLE IN THIS REPO, and AC bullet 4 ("npm run db:generate produces the migration SQL") CANNOT be followed. Drizzle's snapshots stop at 0009 while migration SQL files on disk run to 0028, so generate diffs the current schema against a 20-migration-old snapshot. Running it produced a 2,241-line migration containing 114 CREATE TABLE + 275 CREATE INDEX (i.e. it tried to recreate the whole database) and numbered it 0012_furry_vector — COLLIDING with the existing 0012_auto_orders.sql. That output was discarded and the journal reverted; the migration here is hand-authored instead, following the exact precedent of 0010_cr028_perf_indexes / 0011_pa026_perf_indexes (hand-written SQL + a journal entry, no snapshot), with IF NOT EXISTS so it is safe to (re)apply against the db:push-managed database. WORSE — A JOURNAL GAP THAT LIKELY MEANS 17 MIGRATIONS NEVER RAN: server/lib/migrate.ts:161 uses drizzle-orm's migrate(), which reads meta/_journal.json to decide what to apply. The journal contains ONLY 0000-0011. Migrations 0012 through 0028 exist as .sql files but are ABSENT from the journal, so `npm run db:migrate` does not — and never did — apply them. They were presumably applied by hand or via db:push, or not at all. This is worth its own story: either backfill the journal for 0012-0028 (after confirming against __drizzle_migrations what is actually applied) or rebaseline. THIS MATTERED HERE: a migration file alone would have been dead code, so 0029 was added to the journal (idx 12, tag 0029_audit009_perf_indexes) so db:migrate will actually apply it. NOTE the deliberate idx/filename mismatch: the filename continues the DISK sequence (0029) to avoid colliding with 0012_auto_orders.sql, while idx continues the JOURNAL sequence (12). Every journal entry was verified to resolve to a real .sql file. | NOT DONE / NEXT STEPS: (i) The migration has NOT been applied — per the AC and CLAUDE.md, never db:push to production; run `npm run db:migrate` (it acquires __migration_lock). (ii) Before applying, run the AC's pg_indexes check against the live DB to confirm none of these 10 already exist there under a different name — IF NOT EXISTS makes a duplicate name a no-op, but an equivalent index under a DIFFERENT name would go undetected and be created twice. (iii) Consider CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY for the large hot tables (invoices, audit_logs, business_record_activities) if these are built against a live production database — a plain CREATE INDEX takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and will block writes for the duration. CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction, so it does not fit drizzle's transactional migrator and would need to be applied out-of-band; left as a plain CREATE INDEX here to match the 0010/0011 precedent, but this is a real operational consideration on a big table.

userStories.title: [PERF/MEDIUM] Remove RBAC middleware write-on-read and upsert the permission cache
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need the permission cache to not issue a blocking UPDATE on the hottest request path and to stop inserting duplicate rows, so that authorized requests don't pay a write and permission_cache doesn't bloat until cleanup.
acceptanceCriteria: server/middleware/enhanced-rbac-middleware.ts (~134): make the cacheHits increment fire-and-forget (or drop it) instead of awaiting a db.update on every L2 cache hit
setCachedPermissions (~164): upsert on (userId, orgContext, tenantId) instead of always INSERTing a new row
Confirm permission decisions are unchanged (existing L1/L2 cache behavior preserved)
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by performance audit 2026-07-14. Otherwise the middleware is well-cached (L1 memory + L2 table); this is the one hot-path write. | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. (1) WRITE-ON-READ REMOVED: getCachedPermissions AWAITED a db.update bumping cacheHits on every L2 hit — i.e. the hot path for every authorized request blocked on a DB WRITE before proceeding. It is telemetry, not a permission decision, so it is now fire-and-forget. Used a TWO-ARG .then(onOk, onErr) rather than .catch(): drizzle query builders are thenables, and this guarantees the rejection is handled — an unhandled rejection would take the process down under Node's default policy. A failed counter update can now never fail an otherwise-valid authorization. (2) UPSERT: setCachedPermissions always INSERTed, so every cache miss / expiry / invalidation left ANOTHER row for the same (user, context, tenant) — the table grew until the periodic cleanup ran, AND the L2 read (.limit(1) over a NON-unique index) could return any one of the duplicates, which is arguably worse than the bloat. Now onConflictDoUpdate on the triple: exactly one live row per cache key. cacheHits resets to 0 on refresh because the counter tracks hits against THAT cached value. (3) PERMISSION DECISIONS UNCHANGED (AC bullet 3): L1 memory cache untouched; the L2 read path, its TTL predicate (expires_at > NOW()) and the returned Set are byte-for-byte the same. The only behavioural deltas are that the hit counter is now eventually-consistent instead of synchronous, and that a refresh updates a row instead of inserting a rival one. tsc holds at the 1315 baseline (enhanced-rbac-middleware.ts still shows its 8 PRE-EXISTING errors — verified identical count at HEAD, none are mine); full unit suite green (59 files / 1233 tests). | THE AC MISSED A BLOCKER — THE UPSERT COULD NOT WORK AS SPECIFIED WITHOUT SCHEMA + DATA WORK: permission_cache had NO unique constraint on (user_id, organizational_context, tenant_id) — only a PLAIN idx_permission_cache_user_context (which also omits tenant_id). ON CONFLICT cannot target a non-unique index, so a bare onConflictDoUpdate would have thrown "no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification" at runtime on the RBAC hot path — i.e. it would have broken authorization for every user. So: added uniqueIndex permission_cache_user_context_tenant_uniq to server/enhanced-rbac-schema.ts (note this table is defined under server/, not shared/ — shared/schema.ts merely RE-EXPORTS it from '../server/enhanced-rbac-schema', which is why grepping shared/ for 'permission_cache' finds nothing) and', hand-authored drizzle/migrations/0030_audit010_permission_cache_uniq.sql, journalled as idx 13 so db:migrate will actually apply it (per the AUDIT-009 finding that drizzle-kit generate is unusable here and that unjournalled migrations never run). THE MIGRATION DELETES BEFORE IT CONSTRAINS, deliberately: because the setter has always INSERTed, this table almost certainly CONTAINS DUPLICATES right now, and CREATE UNIQUE INDEX would simply fail against them ("key is duplicated"). A blank DELETE is the right move rather than a keep-the-newest DISTINCT ON dedupe: permission_cache is a PURE CACHE, every row is derived data regenerated by setCachedPermissions on the next miss, so emptying it costs one recomputation per active user and cannot lose information. Simpler and safer than picking a winner. Verified the migration against drizzle getTableConfig(): real table, real physical columns (user_id, organizational_context, tenant_id), and the index is declared UNIQUE in the schema — the DB itself is unreachable from here (the pooler rejects the checked-in credentials), so this static cross-check stands in for running it. | FOLLOW-UPS: (i) NOT APPLIED — run `npm run db:migrate` (never db:push to production, per CLAUDE.md). Until it is applied the new onConflictDoUpdate WILL throw on the auth path, so this migration and the code MUST ship together; this is the one story in this batch where deploy order matters. (ii) idx_permission_cache_user_context is now redundant — the new unique index shares its leftmost prefix — but it was left in place rather than dropped in the same change; worth removing later to save write cost. (iii) The periodic cleanup of expired rows becomes much less important now that refreshes update in place rather than accumulate, but it is still needed for users who stop making requests.

userStories.title: [DATA-CONTRACT/HIGH] Fix invoices camelCase-vs-snake_case response-shape mismatch on billing pages
userStories.description: As a billing user, I need invoice lists to render the number, customer, amount and due date, so that the billing pages don't show blank numbers, $NaN totals, and Invalid Date against the production billing edge function which returns raw snake_case rows.
acceptanceCriteria: client/src/pages/AdvancedBillingEngine.tsx (1230,1237,1577,1596,1608) and client/src/pages/Invoices.tsx (224,267): read invoice_number/total_amount/due_date/invoice_status/balance_due (or normalize once at the query boundary) instead of raw invoice.invoiceNumber/totalAmount/dueDate that only exist in the mock shape
Prefer a single normalizeInvoice() at the useQuery boundary (mirror the defensive dual-casing already in client/src/pages/Billing.tsx:93-97) so every consumer reads consistent keys
Verify against the billing edge fn response shape (supabase/functions/billing) documented in CLAUDE.md: total_amount/amount_paid/balance_due/invoice_status/paid_date
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes:
Found by route/response-shape audit 2026-07-14. Same failure class as QuoteView/ESignatureIntegration/PlatformCustomerSuccess. Billing.tsx is already defensive; AdvancedBillingEngine.tsx and Invoices.tsx are not. | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. ROOT CAUSE is an ASYMMETRY inside the billing edge fn that the AC never states: GET /billing/invoices (index.ts:222-258) does .select('*') and returns RAW snake_case rows in a { data, total } wrapper PLUS a NESTED customer relation (customer:business_records(...)), whereas GET /billing/invoices/:id returns camelCase via mapInvoiceRow (handlers/_context.ts:60). Same resource, two shapes — so every page hand-rolled its own bridge and each got it wrong differently. (1) NEW client/src/lib/invoice-normalize.ts — a single normalizeInvoice()/normalizeInvoices() + NormalizedInvoice type accepting snake, camel, or mixed rows; it also encodes the two traps once: PostgREST serializes decimals as STRINGS, and invoices has TWO status columns. (2) Invoices.tsx was the worst offender: its bridge read inv.invoiceNumber OR-ed with inv.invoiceNumber — THE SAME KEY OR-ED WITH ITSELF — five times over (invoiceNumber/contractId/customerId/dueDate/createdAt/updatedAt), so it never read invoice_number or due_date at all, and never mapped totalAmount or status. That is exactly the reported blank numbers + $NaN totals + Invalid Date. Rebound to useQuery<NormalizedInvoice[]>. (3) AdvancedBillingEngine.tsx: its BillingInvoice interface extended Invoice and re-declared snake fields typed as number — but decimals arrive as strings, so invoice.balance_due.toFixed(2) was a LIVE TypeError ("toFixed is not a function") on any invoice carrying a balance. Interface collapsed to NormalizedInvoice; the phantom customer_name/business_record_name reads (the real path is the nested customer.company_name) plus billing_period_*/payment_terms/balance_due all rebound. (4) Billing.tsx: its bridge preferred the LEGACY status column over the canonical invoice_status. invoices carries BOTH (schema.ts:2085 status default 'draft', invoice_status default 'open'), so a paid invoice could render as draft AND disagree with the ?status= filter, which queries invoice_status. The normalizer makes invoice_status win everywhere, matching the edge fn's own watermarkFor() and the CLAUDE.md billing schema audit. Also dropped its invoice.total read (not a real column). (5) TESTS: new server/tests/unit/invoice-normalize.test.ts (13 tests) pins BOTH real response shapes so an edge-fn change cannot silently regress this — mirrors the QUOTE-016 quote-math precedent. Full unit suite green (56 files / 1187 tests). tsc holds at the 1335 baseline; all 4 touched files at 0 errors. | FOLLOW-UPS (found, deliberately not fixed — outside this AC): (a) The SAME self-OR broken-normalizer bug (x.foo OR-ed with x.foo) also exists in Invoices.tsx for CONTRACTS (contractNumber) and CUSTOMERS (companyName), and in Billing.tsx for payment methods (createdAt). Harmless only if those endpoints already return camelCase. Worth a repo-wide sweep for that pattern — it is a copy-paste tell; ServiceHub.tsx had the identical idiom (fixed under AUDIT-013), so the same author/template seeded several pages. (b) The real fix for the underlying asymmetry is to apply mapInvoiceRow() to the LIST branch too, so /billing/invoices and /billing/invoices/:id agree. The client normalizer tolerates both and is safe either way, but the server-side split is the actual debt.
--- 2026-08-20 (loop round 41) ---

THE PATTERN THIS STORY NAMED WAS NEVER SWEPT. AUDIT-011 diagnosed
`inv.invoiceNumber || inv.invoiceNumber` precisely - "the same key OR'd with
itself, five times over... blank invoice numbers, $NaN totals and 'Invalid
Date' against real data" - fixed Invoices.tsx's invoice normalizer, and stopped
there. A repo-wide grep found 131 more instances across 30 files, including ten
more in Invoices.tsx itself (its contracts and customers normalizers, lines
93-113).

FIXED THIS PASS: 81 of 131.

  79 mechanically, restricted to files that demonstrably use the snake||camel
  idiom elsewhere, so every rewrite had a correct sibling line in the same
  normalizer as evidence. AccountsReceivable.tsx is the clearest example: line
  91 already read `ar.invoice_date || ar.invoiceDate` while the five lines
  around it were camel||camel.

  2 on direct evidence rather than inference. server/middleware/supabase-auth.ts
  and client/src/hooks/useSupabaseAuth.ts both read
  `userMetadata.firstName || userMetadata.firstName` - and
  supabase/functions/signup/index.ts:179 writes user_metadata as
  { first_name, last_name }. So the user's first and last name were undefined
  in every decoded token and every client session, on both paths.
  supabase/functions/technicians/index.ts:212 read `body.user_id || body.user_id`
  where all nine sibling fields read `body.camelCase || body.snake_case`, so
  creating a technician never linked the user.

DIRECTION IS NOT UNIVERSAL, which is why this was done by evidence and not by
rule: a ROW read is `row.snake_case || row.camelCase` (PostgREST returns
snake), a REQUEST-BODY read is `body.camelCase || body.snake_case` (the
frontend sends camel). Applying either rule blindly would have broken the other
half.

GUARD: scripts/check-identical-fallback.mjs + docs/identical-fallback-baseline.json
+ npm run check:identical-fallback, wired into ci.yml next to check:phantom-cols.
It scans client/src, server, shared and supabase/functions, normalizes `a?.b`
and `a['b']` to `a.b` so the two sides compare on meaning, and keys the baseline
on file+expression rather than line so reformatting neither invents nor retires
a finding. Mutation-tested: reintroducing
`ar.invoiceNumber || ar.invoiceNumber` exits 1 at the right line.

THE MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING, because I shipped it into working code before
catching it. `!x.a || x.a === 'y'` is a legitimate and common guard ("unset, or
set to this"), and the bare chains either side of the || are identical - so the
first version of both the sweep and the checker flagged it, and the sweep
rewrote two ServiceHub.tsx filter predicates into a behaviour change. Caught by
diffing the applied changes for comparison operators before running anything.
The checker now requires that the left operand is not preceded by `!` and that
the right operand ENDS the expression, so `x.a || x.a === v`, `x.a || x.a.b`
and `x.a || x.a > 3` all pass while `fn(x.a || x.a)` still reports. Seven-case
regex probe in the commit.

ONE-SIDED RISK, worth stating so the remainder is not treated as dangerous: if
a guessed snake_case name turns out to be wrong, the value falls through to the
camel side exactly as it does today. A rewrite can fix the field or leave it
unchanged; it cannot make it worse.

REMAINDER: 33 entries baselined and split out as AUDIT-011a. They sit in files
with no idiom sibling to infer from, so each needs its endpoint checked - not
lower impact (Invoices.tsx and CommissionManagement.tsx are on the list), just
not mechanically determinable.

VERIFIED: tsc holds at 1002, 3261 tests pass, check:routes / check:edge-paths /
check:phantom-cols / check:nav / check:dup-routes all pass.

userStories.title: [ROUTE/HIGH] Fix leases edge fn pathParts[1] off-by-one after server.ts strip, and sweep other offenders
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I need edge functions to read the resource segment from the path the way the dispatcher actually delivers it, so that routes don't resolve to the wrong (or undefined) sub-resource in production.
acceptanceCriteria: supabase/functions/leases/index.ts (~67): server.ts strips the function-name segment before invoking the handler, so const customerId = pathParts[1] is off-by-one — switch to normalizePath(pathname, 'leases') and read from pathParts[0] (or the correct index)

Grep supabase/functions for pathParts[1] and verify each remaining hit against the stripped path shape; fix the genuinely off-by-one ones (integrations fn is a known non-migrated case tracked elsewhere — note, don't duplicate)
Smoke-test the leases endpoints against the stripped path shape
Typecheck passes: npm run check
userStories.notes: Found by route audit 2026-07-14. Same bug class documented in CLAUDE.md for the edge router (strips function name; read resource from pathParts[0]). | COMPLETED 2026-07-16. The audit UNDERSTATED this: the leases fn was not merely off-by-one, it was 100% unreachable in prod. (1) ROOT CAUSE: server.ts:168 does newUrl.pathname = '/' + pathParts.slice(1) — it always strips segment 0 — but leases/index.ts hand-rolled a raw split and switched on pathParts[0] === 'leases', so EVERY prod request fell to the default arm and 404'd. Fixed with normalizePath(url.pathname,'leases') (idempotent: strips a leading /leases only if present, so it is correct under BOTH the Coolify dispatcher and Supabase's native runtime). (2) SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT the AC did not mention: /lease-payments, /lease-renewals and /lease-dispositions have NO function dir, so server.ts 404'd them with 'Function not found' before any handler ran. Added aliases in server.ts. CRITICAL SUBTLETY: these are NOT like the EDGE-005f /public/calculator alias, where the discriminator sits at segment 1 and survives slice(1). Here the discriminator IS segment 0, so a plain alias would erase it (the exact trap CLAUDE.md documents for the signatures dispatcher) — introduced a stripSegments flag (default 1, unchanged for every other fn) set to 0 for these three so the prefix survives and the leases dispatcher can still key off it. (3) Removed the case 'customers' arm: /customers/:id/leases resolves to the REAL customers/ fn dir at segment 0 and never reached leases — dead code. handlers/leases.ts still implements 'by-customer' if that surface is ever wanted; forward from the customers fn. (4) VERIFIED with a harness importing the REAL _shared/path.ts normalizePath and mirroring the patched dispatcher arithmetic: all 9 URL shapes route correctly (/leases, /leases/:id, /leases/:id/payments, /leases/:id/initiate-renewal, /v1/leases/:id, /lease-payments/:id/process, /lease-renewals/:id, /lease-dispositions/:id, and /customers/:id/leases correctly NOT resolving to leases). Handlers needed ZERO changes — the slices match what they already expect. deno check: same 2 pre-existing errors (_pdf.ts TS2352, handlers/leases.ts TS2345) before and after; server.ts identical error profile before/after. | SWEEP (AC bullet 2) — all 177 pathParts[1] hits triaged mechanically, not by eyeball. 105 files construct pathParts from a raw split, but raw-split is NOT itself the bug: most index [1] as the SUB-RESOURCE after [0]=id, which is correct under the strip. The precise tell of the leases bug is a fn comparing a path segment to its OWN dir name; that matched 15 fns, and 13 are the DEFENSIVE hand-rolled idiom (rawParts[0]==='fn' ? rawParts.slice(1) : rawParts — a normalizePath equivalent) or have a safe else-fallback (teams, via stripPrefix) and are CORRECT. Two were genuinely broken: (a) onboarding/index.ts — FIXED HERE. Its guards required pathParts[0]==='onboarding', never true after the strip, so GET list + POST create 404'd in prod; the real discriminator is the 'checklists' collection segment. Note checklistId=parts[1]/subResource=parts[2] were already correct BY ACCIDENT under the frontend's real /onboarding/checklists/:id/:sub shape, so only the two guards + normalizePath were needed. Verified 9/11 real frontend URLs now route. Also fixed its pre-existing getUser(jwt) TS2345 per the CLAUDE.md 'fix the files you touch' rule -> file is now deno-check clean. (b) meetings/index.ts — a leases-style MULTIPLEX (switch cases 'calendar','schedule-request','meetings','types','rooms') with the same self-name-case bug, NOT fixed: it has NO frontend caller (no /api/meetings literal anywhere in client/src), so it is speculative surface needing its own story rather than a blind fix. integrations fn left alone as CLAUDE.md instructs. | KNOWN GAPS, deliberately not in scope: (i) DEV still serves /api/leases/* from the legacy Express server/routes/lease-routes.ts — there are ZERO lease entries in crmProxies, which is exactly WHY this prod-only breakage stayed invisible locally. Left as-is: adding a proxy would swing dev onto the edge fn and is a migration decision, not a bugfix. (ii) /api/onboarding/checklists/:id/generate-pdf and /api/onboarding/export/:id/:format still 404 in prod — the edge fn has no PDF/export implementation (Express-only, routes-registry.ts:568-570); porting them mirrors the leases _pdf.ts work and is a separate story. (iii) /api/onboarding/{getting-started,wizard-state,check-subdomain,update-step,confirm-subdomain} match no route in this fn either.
