Scoped to the path, not the /api/admin prefix, because routes-registry mounts routes-admin-workflows there and app.use matches on segment boundaries; the proxy registers first (routes-registry:297) so it wins for this one path only. (3) NEW SIBLING GUARD scripts/check-no-static-posture.mjs, npm run check:no-static-posture, wired into ci.yml, hard gate at 0. It works on the SHAPE of a rendered value rather than the name of its source, which is what check:no-mocks and check:fabricated both miss - check-fabricated-fallbacks.mjs says so in its own header. Rules: a JSX text node that is a bare value (currency, unit, ratio, decimal/separator, or 2+ digits), a posture word as a complete JSX text node, a Progress gauge filled from a literal, and a literal expiry date. A bare single digit is excluded on purpose - ordered-step markers are labels, not measurements, and matching them made the guard noise. (4) The guard immediately found THREE MORE fabricated admin pages, all routed, none previously reported: RootAdminSecurity (99.2% successful logins, 847 active sessions, 12 blocked IPs, and a privileged-role census of 1/5/12/156/423/789), TenantManagement (65/25/10 plan mix with the bar widths hardcoded in style attributes, and $284,750 MRR / $3,417,000 ARR / $45,200 outstanding on the platform billing screen), UserManagement (89/423/567/1,768 role counts whose bars did not agree with the numbers beside them, and 1,847 daily / 12,456 weekly / 45,789 monthly active users). All stripped and replaced with what is and is not measured, along with nine more dead buttons behind them (Force Logout All Sessions, Reset Failed Login Counters, Update Password Policies, Generate Revenue Report, Export Billing Data, Manage Payment Methods, Generate Activity Report, Export User Data, View Login Analytics). Verified: tsc holds at 415 (net zero), 175 files / 3766 tests pass, build succeeds, eslint 10624 -> 10622 (baseline tightened), and check:no-mocks / fabricated / query-states / nav / orphans / edge-paths / proxy-overrides / routes / a11y-names all pass. TRAP WORTH RECORDING: a first cut of the deletions left one unbalanced in each of TenantManagement and UserManagement, and check-types.mjs reported errors DECREASED 415 -> 20. It was tsc bailing out at the parse error and never typechecking the rest. A LARGE, unexplained drop in that ratchet is a syntax break until proven otherwise - confirm the file list, not just the count. STILL OPEN, the last AC: /meeting-transcription, /ai-service-intelligence and /predictive-contract-profitability. All three are zero-network pages built from inline fixture arrays with named customers (Acme Corporation, TechStart Industries, Global Logistics LLC), real part numbers, contract margins and named meeting speakers. They are NOT the SystemSecurity case and must not be handled the same way: edge functions meeting-transcription/, contract-pnl/ and predictive-failure/ ALREADY EXIST, so the honest fate here is wiring, not deletion, and wiring three pages field-by-field against real Drizzle columns is a PROD-010-sized piece of work per page. They are also woven into RoleAwareCollapsibleSidebar, MobileNavigationDrawer, AIHub tiles, navigation-permissions, seoConfig and emailCampaigns, so removing the routes is a product decision, not a cleanup. Note the guard does not yet catch them - their fixtures live in arrays rendered through {expression}, which is the check:no-mocks shape, except the identifiers are named predictions/contractData/recordings rather than mockAnything. [PARTIAL 2026-08-29, second pass] /meeting-transcription is DONE. Two demo pages remain. MeetingTranscription.tsx no longer holds three recordings, a transcript and six action items in useState literals, and the Start Recording button is GONE rather than rewired: it flipped a boolean and captured no audio, which is worse than a fixture on the one feature where LEGAL-009 requires a participant be told before capture begins, and there is no browser capture implementation to put a notice in front of. Upload is the path that has one, so that is the path the page now offers. The page reads GET /recordings (list), GET /analytics/content (the four real aggregates: transcriptionsProcessed, totalWordsTranscribed, averageConfidence, byProvider - NOT the invented 94% AI accuracy or 127.5 hours), GET /recordings/:id/transcription, GET /recordings/:id/consent, POST /recordings/:id/process, and POST /upload as multipart through apiFormRequest (apiRequest JSON-stringifies its body and cannot send FormData). Every field is bound to the real column names in drizzle/rls/meeting-transcription-tables.sql - these five meeting_* tables are DRIFT TABLES in no Drizzle schema, created by that hand-run SQL file, so check:phantom-cols cannot see them and the DDL is the only source of truth. THREE DEFECTS FOUND ON THE WAY, none previously reported. (1) THE CONSENT ENDPOINT WAS UNREACHABLE. handlers/recordings.ts implements GET /recordings/:id/consent for LEGAL-009, but index.ts switch on case recordings only forwarded transcription and process, so result stayed null and the dispatcher 404d it. The one endpoint that answers "did this person agree to be recorded" had never worked. Fixed. (2) NO TENANT-WIDE LIST EXISTED. Every read path was meeting-scoped (GET /meetings/:id/recordings), which is right for a meeting detail view and useless for a tenant-wide console that has no meeting id to start from - part of why the page shipped with hardcoded rows instead. Added GET /recordings, capped at 200. (3) THE WHOLE EDGE FUNCTION HAD ZERO CALLERS and no crmProxies entry, so nothing had ever exercised it from either host, which is how (1) survived. Added the proxy entry. It does not shadow server/routes/meeting-transcription-routes.ts: that router is mounted at /api ROOT (asyncRootApiMounts), so its paths are /api/meetings/:id/recordings and /api/analytics/content, not /api/meeting-transcription/*. Parity: the recording-consent notice now exists twice (server default in _consent.ts, client prefill so the operator sees the exact words they are attesting participants were given) and is locked by server/tests/unit/recording-consent-notice.test.ts, which also asserts the four consent methods the form offers are the four VALID_METHODS accepts. MUTATION-TESTED: changing one word of the client copy fails it. Verified: tsc holds at 415, 176 files / 3768 tests pass, build succeeds, eslint clean on the new files, and all fourteen relevant ratchets pass. STILL OPEN: /ai-service-intelligence and /predictive-contract-profitability. Both are the same shape as MeetingTranscription was - a top-level const array (predictions, contractData) with named customers, part numbers and margins, zero network calls - and both have a candidate backend (predictive-failure/ and contract-pnl/). Neither has been read yet; do not assume the endpoints line up as cleanly as meeting-transcription did, and read the real columns first. [DONE 2026-08-29, third pass] All four pages resolved; every AC met. The last two were NOT the MeetingTranscription case and wiring them would have been the wrong call, because BOTH ARE FIXTURE TWINS OF PAGES THAT ALREADY WORK. This is the BATCH 10 lesson (duplicate pages built off the same mock shape travel in pairs) showing up at route level rather than at column level. /ai-service-intelligence rendered predicted equipment failures with probability, timeframe, part number and savings, while /service/predictions has consumed the real predictive-failure engine all along - list, score, approve, snooze, dismiss, accuracy, kill switch. /predictive-contract-profitability rendered per-contract margins and a "Reprice at renewal (+12%)" recommendation, while /contracts/profitability computes real CPC revenue minus parts, labour, supplies and financing through the contract-pnl engine. Building a second consumer of either endpoint would have been duplicated work; the honest fate is retirement. Both pages are DELETED and their URLs now hit LegacyRedirect (already in App.tsx) pointing at the working page, so the client/src/data/emailCampaigns.ts links still land somewhere real. Their navigation-permissions entries are KEPT and the SAME gate is added to the redirect targets, which had none of their own - without that the old path would have been more restrictive than the page it lands on. Worth stating plainly: the predictive HALF of the contract page (predictedCost, predictedMargin, the reprice recommendation) has no model anywhere in the codebase. There was nothing to wire it to, which is why it was invented in the first place. AC-BY-AC: fate decided for all four; no surviving card asserts a posture that is not queried; system-health status deliberately unrendered; loading/error via QueryState (none of the four were ever ON docs/query-states-baseline.json - a page with no queries cannot be, which is exactly how they hid from CR-033); sibling guard check:no-static-posture shipped and CI-wired at zero, now also covering the two REAL pages the twins redirect to so a fixture cannot come back in through them; check and test pass. Final: tsc 415 (net zero across all three passes), 176 files / 3768 tests, build clean, eslint 10622 -> 10605 (-17, baseline tightened), and check:nav / orphans / routes / query-states / no-mocks / fabricated / edge-paths / proxy-overrides / a11y-names / prd-refs / edge-coverage all pass.

userStories.title: [SECURITY/HIGH] The integrations dashboard fabricates its numbers with Math.random() on every request
userStories.description: As an admin, the integration health and cost figures must be measured or absent, because server/integrations/dashboard-service.ts generates roughly 45 of them with Math.random() and they change on every refresh, which reads as live telemetry rather than as a placeholder.
acceptanceCriteria: No value returned by dashboard-service.ts is produced by Math.random(). Derive it from integration_metrics / integration_api_logs, or remove the field and say what is not measured, per the rule AUDIT-016, LEGAL-010 and AUDIT-019 already applied

The cost figures go first and explicitly: totalMonthlyCost, costByProvider, costPerApiCall and estimatedMonthlySavings have no pricing data anywhere in the repo behind them, and an admin could put them in a budget

Reuse supabase/functions/_shared/erp-integration-dashboard.ts rather than writing a second aggregation over the same tables (PROD-014a). Decide whether this Express service should survive at all, or fold into the erp-integration edge function
The webhook delivery log at lines 640-670 invents entries with random status codes and response times; either read integration_webhooks / integration_sync_logs or drop the endpoint

Extend a guard to cover this class server-side. check:no-static-posture reads client pages only, and check:fabricated only sees `?? literal` fallbacks, so neither can see Math.random() in a response body
npm run check && npm run test pass
userStories.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-29 during a QUALITY-002 batch, via a TS2367 that only became visible once the status union was corrected: the file compares integration.status to 'connected', a value the column never holds. Pulling that thread showed the comparison was decorative, because the numbers on both sides of it are invented. THIS IS LIVE: dashboard-service.ts is reached through server/integrations/routes.ts, registered at routes-registry:401, and /api/integrations is NOT proxied, so Express serves it. WHAT IS FABRICATED, by line: marketplace popularity/install counts/ratings (310-313, 322); webhook delivery success rate, average delivery time, retries and three time-window rollups (358-377); total API calls, data transferred, webhooks delivered, average response time and peak usage hour (394-398); p50/p95/p99 latency (404-406); error rates by category (409-412); per-integration uptime (417-419); monthly cost, cost by provider, cost per API call and estimated monthly savings (426-436); a recent-activity feed picking random actions and record counts (609-610); and a webhook delivery log inventing status codes, response times and retry counts (651-665). WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE AUDIT-019 PAGES, which is the reason it is filed at priority 1 rather than as debt: a hardcoded literal is at least stable and eventually recognisable as a placeholder. These change on every request, which is exactly what real telemetry does, so refreshing the page 'confirms' the numbers are live. The cost block is the sharpest edge - nothing in the repo prices an API call, so totalMonthlyCost and estimatedMonthlySavings are pure invention on a screen an admin would use to justify spend. NOT FIXED IN THAT BATCH ON PURPOSE: rewriting a 700-line service is not a typecheck fix, and PROD-014a already built the real aggregation over system_integrations + integration_metrics that this should reuse. Only the three 'connected' comparisons were corrected, to 'active', so the file typechecks; the invented values are untouched and are this story's job. RELATED: AUDIT-019 closed the client-side instances of this class and shipped check:no-static-posture, which reads client/src/pages only. The server-side half was never guarded - see also the PROD-014 finding that the ERP dashboard's Express handler was 670 lines of literals in two copies.
[DONE 2026-08-29, and the story's own severity claim was WRONG. I filed this the same day saying "THIS IS LIVE: dashboard-service.ts is reached through server/integrations/routes.ts, registered at routes-registry:401". It is not. I read the import arrow backwards: dashboard-service.ts imports IntegrationService, and so does routes.ts, but NOTHING imports dashboard-service.ts. Grepping server/, client/, supabase/ and scripts/ returns exactly one reference and it is a COMMENT - in supabase/functions/integrations/index.ts:619, which records that EDGE-005f already replaced this service and that "the Express version padded the response with synthetic metrics/marketplace numbers". So the work this story describes was done months ago on the edge side; the Express file was orphaned and never deleted. It was dead code, reachable from nothing, in dev or prod.

RESOLUTION: deleted, 669 lines. That is the honest fix for a file whose replacement already exists and is better - buildIntegrationHubDashboard in the integrations edge fn reports REAL counts from platform_integrations + integration_webhooks and marks derived blocks `degraded` where no metrics source exists, which is exactly what AC1 asks for. Rewriting the orphan to reuse _shared/erp-integration-dashboard.ts (AC3's other option) would have produced a THIRD dashboard over overlapping tables, which AC3 itself warns against.

WHAT THE FINDING WAS STILL WORTH: the class is real even if this instance was dead, and nothing guarded it. check:no-static-posture reads client/src/pages only; check:fabricated only sees `?? literal` fallbacks. Neither can see Math.random() in a response body. NEW RATCHET scripts/check-no-random-metrics.mjs (npm run check:no-random-metrics, CI-wired) closes that: it flags an object PROPERTY whose value derives from Math.random(), which is the shape that reads as telemetry, and ignores the legitimate uses - ids via .toString(36), names built by template interpolation, jitter in an `if`. Baseline 38 across 10 files, keyed by file + PROPERTY NAME rather than line so ordinary edits do not churn it.

THE 38 ARE BASELINED, NOT FIXED, and the baseline is the todo list. Every entry name reads as a measurement, which is the point: routes/performance-routes.ts invents diskUsage, errorRate, throughput and activeUsers (its own comments say "would need disk monitoring - placeholder"); routes-service-dispatch.ts invents customerSatisfaction, onTimeArrival, completionRate, utilizationRate AND the lat/lng it puts technicians at on the dispatch map, scattered around 40.7128/-74.006; customer-portal-service.ts invents costPerPage and efficiencyScore; routes-sample-data.ts invents revenue, pipelineValue and conversionRate. Anyone picking those up should check reachability FIRST - this story is the cautionary tale for not doing so.

TWO THINGS LEARNED ABOUT WRITING THIS KIND OF GUARD. (1) The first baseline had 44 entries including invoice_number and ticketId, which are ids rather than measurements. A baseline carrying known false positives is worse than a shorter one, because a real offender hides among them - so those are EXCLUDED by rule, not baselined. (2) My first mutation probe did not fire, and the reason is a genuine blind spot now recorded in the script header: the rule is line-anchored, so a single-line object literal escapes it. Prettier splits multi-property objects, which makes it rare rather than theoretical, but it is the way through. Stating that is the difference between a guard and a false sense of one.

Verified: tsc holds at 371, 3795 tests pass, build succeeds, eslint holds at 10521, and check:orphans / no-random-metrics / no-static-posture / routes / edge-rbac / lint all pass.]

[FOLLOW-ON 2026-08-29, same day: the ratchet's own baseline had two entries that production can reach, and both are now fixed. Checking reachability per file - the discipline this story exists to teach - found them.

(1) server/websocket-service.ts. NOT dev-only, which is what makes it different from every Express entry in that baseline: routes.ts sets enableWebSocket when ENABLE_WEBSOCKET === 'true' OR NODE_ENV === 'production', so the service runs in prod. getCurrentKPIData returned a random value, a fixed target of 1000 and a coin-flipped up/down trend, pushed on the data-update interval - a subscriber would have watched a KPI move every few seconds. getCurrentReportData returned three invented rows (Active Users, Revenue, Conversion Rate) on a cache miss. Both now report unavailable with a reason. LATENT, not active: the broadcast loop only iterates channels a client has subscribed to, and useRealtimeKPI/useRealtimeReport are exported from client/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts with NO callers, so nothing subscribes today.

(2) supabase/functions/meetings/handlers/meetings.ts handleAnalytics. An EDGE function, so this is the code production runs. It returned totalMeetings 127, scheduledMeetings 98, completedMeetings 89, cancelledMeetings 12, averageDurationMinutes 42 and a meetingFatigueIndex of 0.65, all literals, with topMeetingTypes counts randomised per request so the numbers moved. calendar_events (drizzle/rls/meetings-tables.sql:37) carries start_time, end_time, status and event_type, so it now COUNTS: total, cancelled, upcoming vs past by start_time, top three event_types, and a mean duration over well-formed positive intervals only (an all-day or malformed row would otherwise drag it). averageDurationMinutes is null rather than 0 when nothing is timed. 'completedMeetings' is gone - there is no completed status, and upcoming/past is what the column can actually answer, so inventing a third state would have been the same defect in a new shape. meetingFatigueIndex is named in `unbacked` because nothing in the repo defines it. Also latent: /api/meetings has no frontend caller and no crmProxies entry, so the endpoint was deployed and uncalled.

Baseline 38 -> 34, and every remaining entry is in an Express file, i.e. dev-only under the getApiUrl architecture. Those 34 are now AUDIT-021 with per-file reachability recorded, rather than left as a line in these notes.]

userStories.title: Retire the 34 remaining fabricated measurements the AUDIT-020 ratchet baselined
userStories.description: As an operator, the numbers these handlers report must be counted or absent, because 34 object properties across 8 server files still take their value from Math.random() and regenerate on every request, which is what real telemetry looks like.
acceptanceCriteria: Work from docs/random-metrics-baseline.json - it is the list, keyed by file and property name - and drive its total to 0

CHECK REACHABILITY PER FILE FIRST. AUDIT-020 was filed at priority 1 on a live claim that turned out to be a 669-line orphan; grep -rn '<basename>' server/ client/ supabase/ scripts/ before deciding whether a file is worth fixing or deleting

For each property: derive it from a real table, or delete the field and name it in an `unbacked` array the way supabase/functions/_shared/erp-integration-dashboard.ts does. Do not replace a random number with a fixed one
routes-service-dispatch.ts's lat/lng go first among the Express files: they scatter technicians around 40.7128/-74.006 on a dispatch map, which is a map of people that is not where they are
Where a value genuinely has no source, prefer null over 0 and say why - a 0% success rate reads as an outage, 'no data' reads as no data
npm run check:no-random-metrics reports 0 and the baseline file is deleted or emptied
npm run check && npm run test pass
userStories.notes:
Split out of AUDIT-020 on 2026-08-29, which shipped the ratchet and cleared the two offenders that production can actually reach. SEVERITY IS DELIBERATELY LOWER THAN AUDIT-020's, and the reason is the architecture: client/src/lib/config.ts getApiUrl() rewrites every /api/* call to functions.printyx.net when import.meta.env.PROD, with no Express fallback, so EXPRESS ONLY EVER SERVES DEV. All 34 remaining offenders are in Express route files and the services they call, so they mislead developers, demos and anyone reading a dev environment - not customers. That is the same severity split PROD-011 recorded for routes-incident-response.ts. VERIFIED REACHABILITY, per file: routes/performance-routes.ts is registered at routes-registry:551 on /api/performance, and a `performance` edge function EXISTS but the prefix is NOT proxied, so dev shows the invented diskUsage/errorRate/throughput/activeUsers while prod runs different code entirely - its own comments admit the fabrication ('would need disk monitoring - placeholder'). routes-sample-data.ts is registered at routes-registry:340 and invents revenue, pipelineValue, conversionRate, averageDealSize, deals and units. routes-service-dispatch.ts reaches the registry through domains/service.ts and has no edge function at all, so it is dev-only AND a prod 404; it invents customerSatisfaction, onTimeArrival, completionRate, utilizationRate, averageCallTime, customerRating and the technician lat/lng. services/customer-portal-service.ts is imported by routes-enhanced-service.ts and invents costPerPage, efficiencyScore, colorRatio and trendDirection. services/team-collaboration-service.ts is imported by routes/team-collaboration-routes.ts (registered at routes-registry:580) and invents aiEfficiencyScore, aiPredictedWorkload, overdueTasksCount, projectsCount and tasksCount. services/meeting-scheduling-service.ts invents flexibility and meetingFatigueRisk; services/performance-monitor.ts invents activeConnections. server/run-comprehensive-tests.ts (coverage, cpuUsage, memoryUsage) is a SCRIPT, not a route, and is the one entry here that may be legitimate to leave - decide it explicitly rather than by omission. WHAT AUDIT-020 ALREADY DID, so nobody redoes it: deleted server/integrations/dashboard-service.ts (orphan, 669 lines, ~45 fabricated values); replaced the websocket-service KPI and report placeholders, which mattered because ENABLE_WEBSOCKET is implied by NODE_ENV === 'production' so that path is NOT dev-only, though nothing subscribes today (useRealtimeKPI/useRealtimeReport are exported from useWebSocket.ts with no callers); and rewrote supabase/functions/meetings/handlers/meetings.ts handleAnalytics, which was an EDGE function - production - returning 127 total meetings, 98 scheduled, 89 completed, a 42-minute average and a meetingFatigueIndex of 0.65, all literals, with randomised per-type counts. It now counts calendar_events by status, upcoming/past and event_type, averages real durations, returns null rather than 0 when nothing is timed, and names meetingFatigueIndex in `unbacked` because nothing in the repo defines it. Note /api/meetings has no frontend caller and no proxy entry, so that endpoint was deployed and uncalled.
PROGRESS 2026-08-29 - routes-service-dispatch.ts done, 34 -> 26. That is the file the ACs named first, and it was worse than the baseline recorded: 12 Math.random() sites AND thirteen written-in operational figures that check:no-random-metrics cannot see because a literal is not random.

REACHABILITY FIRST, as the AC demands. The router is mounted (routes-registry:684) and serves /api/dispatch/*, which NO client tree calls - the prefix is not proxied and there is no supabase/functions/dispatch/, so these endpoints are dev-only and caller-less today. That lowers the severity from the AC's framing ("a dispatch map of people that is not where they are") but does not change the fix, and the endpoints are the obvious back end for a dispatch screen someone will build. Worth knowing separately: mobile/app/(app)/(service)/dispatch.tsx queries '/api/service-dispatch', which nothing serves under either name - the router is at /api/dispatch.

WHAT WAS THERE. /tracking took REAL technician rows and gave each a random point within 0.05 degrees of 40.7128/-74.006, an invented ticket id, a customer called "Active Service Call", and the fixed times 2:30 PM and 3:00 PM. Real names on fabricated positions is the worst version of this: plausible enough to dispatch against. /technicians/availability carried four random performance figures per technician. /analytics carried 4.2 hours average response, 78.5% first-call resolution, 4.6 satisfaction, 73.2% utilization, 18.5 minutes travel, $8.75 fuel per call, 2,847 miles driven, $425.50 of route-optimization savings, 92.3% on-time arrival, and a fixed avgResponseTime per priority band.

WHAT IS THERE NOW, derived from service_tickets: completionRate (resolved/assigned, per technician), averageCallTimeMinutes (mean labor_hours over closed tickets), ticketsClosed, averageResolutionHours (created_at to resolved_at), the four priority counts, and current/next assignment read from the tickets actually assigned to each technician. Everything else is named in an `unbacked` array with the COLUMN that is missing, the way _shared/erp-integration-dashboard.ts does it - 'coordinates: technicians records a free-text current_location and no latitude or longitude', 'onTimeArrival: scheduled_date and resolved_at are stored, arrival time is not', and so on. NULL rather than 0 throughout: an average over no closed tickets is not zero hours, and a technician with no closed tickets does not have a 0% completion rate.

server/tests/unit/service-dispatch-unbacked.test.ts, 6 assertions, mutation-tested three ways - reinstating a random metric, reinstating coordinates, and swapping a null for a 0 each fail exactly one assertion.

REMAINING 26, with reachability noted so the next pass does not have to re-derive it. routes-sample-data.ts (6 props) is REGISTERED and serves eleven prefixes, six of which have live callers - but its random props belong to /api/sales-trends, which has none. routes/performance-routes.ts (5) is mounted at /api/performance. run-comprehensive-tests.ts (3) is a script nothing imports. The four service files (customer-portal-service 4, meeting-scheduling-service 2, performance-monitor 1, team-collaboration-service 5) are reached through their own routers, each of which is on the SEC-SESSION-001 baseline and therefore answers 401 - so those 12 properties cannot currently be seen by anyone, which is a reason to fix the auth or delete the router before spending time on the numbers.

PROGRESS 2026-08-29 (part 2) - performance done, 26 -> 17, and the interesting part was not the random numbers.

THREE IMPLEMENTATIONS OF /api/performance, and the alert bell was empty in production. supabase/functions/performance/ read `system_alerts`. That table is real and NOTHING WRITES TO IT: the only insert in the tree is storage.createSystemAlert, and no caller names it. So SystemAlertBell, PageAlerts and the notification bell's fallback have all been permanently empty in production. Meanwhile server/routes-operations-extended.ts DERIVED four alert families from live data - low stock from inventory_items, dispatch delay from service_tickets scheduled in the past and still open, billing anomalies from overdue and past-due invoices, and contracts ending within 90 days - and /api/performance was not proxied, so those were served in DEV ONLY. The two environments disagreed about whether the business had any problems, and the one that said "none" was production.

All four derivations are now in the edge function, ALONGSIDE the system_alerts read rather than instead of it, so whatever eventually writes there is not pre-empted. Each family is independently try/caught (one missing table must not blank the bell) and capped. Low stock is the awkward one: PostgREST cannot compare two columns, so quantity_on_hand <= reorder_point is filtered in the handler, which is why it fetches at most 200 rows and emits at most 20.

THE THIRD IMPLEMENTATION, server/routes/performance-routes.ts, is deleted. Its /metrics and /health invented everything they returned - 99 + random*0.99 uptime, random*500 + 800 throughput, a random error rate, disk usage and active-user count - and of the nine other handlers no client tree called one, with /run-tests and /optimize self-declared mocks returning invented test results. /api/performance is proxied now, so dev and prod answer the same thing.

server/run-comprehensive-tests.ts deleted too: 480 lines of fake test runner, imported by nothing, in no npm script and no workflow, which decided randomly whether each "test" passed and reported a code coverage figure of Math.floor(Math.random() * 20) + 80. A thing that would print "coverage: 94%" if anyone ever ran it.

performance-monitor.getDatabasePerformance made real rather than deleted, because recordMetric on the same class is live: activeConnections comes from pg_stat_activity (null when the role cannot read it, which is honest), connectionPoolSize/idleConnections/waitingRequests from the pool object itself, and averageQueryTime is null rather than a default of 50ms - a default of 50 reads as a measured 50.

server/tests/unit/performance-alerts-parity.test.ts, 10 assertions, mutation-tested three ways: renaming a derivation, dropping the merge with system_alerts, and removing the low-stock cap each fail exactly one.

REMAINING 17 across 4 files. routes-sample-data.ts (6) is registered and serves eleven prefixes but its random props belong to /api/sales-trends, which no client calls. The other three are services behind routers on the SEC-SESSION-001 list - customer-portal-service (4), meeting-scheduling-service (2), team-collaboration-service (5) - so those 11 properties are behind handlers that answer 401 and nobody can see them. Fix the auth or delete the router before spending time on the numbers.


--- 2026-08-30 --- TEN OF THE SEVENTEEN ARE GONE, including every one a CUSTOMER
could see. Seven remain, all of them unreachable.

THE CUSTOMER-FACING ONE WAS THE WORST, and it was not random. /api/customer-portal
is proxied, so supabase/functions/customer-portal/handlers/analytics.ts serves
UsageAnalyticsDashboard on both hosts, and its comparison block never queried a
previous period at all: it multiplied the current one by 0.9 and called the
result "previous". Every customer, on every render, was told their volume was up
11.1% and their cost up 11.1%, and the dashboard's four trend cards all derive
from that block.

That was a PORT of something worse, in the wrong direction. The Express service
rolled a random 0.85-1.15 multiplier; the edge version replaced it with a
constant and its header called that an improvement because "deterministic
responses cache better". AUDIT-020's finding is the opposite: a stable
fabrication is HARDER to spot than a random one, because refreshing appears to
confirm it. Worth remembering the next time a port tidies a mock instead of
removing it.

WHAT REPLACED IT. One fetch now spans both windows and is split on startDate;
one summarise() computes each side, so the two halves of the comparison cannot
drift apart. percentageChange is null when the previous window holds no
readings - a customer with one month of history has no trend, and 0% asserts
that nothing changed. Peak usage was a hardcoded block (9am 120 pages, Tuesday
520) told to every customer as their own pattern; day and month are derived from
the readings now, AVERAGED per weekday rather than summed so a longer window
does not skew them. Hourly is ABSENT: a meter submission carries a reading_date
and no time of day, so no arithmetic over this data produces an hourly profile.
The chart is removed and the response names it in `unbacked`, along with two
things worth knowing - the cost figures use an industry-average rate card rather
than the customer's contract rates, and the per-device costPerPage and
efficiency are fleet-wide estimates.

DELETED AS DEAD: the entire Express usage-analytics path (669 lines,
getUsageAnalytics + nine private helpers + getEquipmentUsageAnalytics) - nothing
routed it, and it held four of the seventeen. And GET /api/sales-trends in
routes-sample-data.ts, which built six months of revenue, deals, units, pipeline
value, conversion rate and average deal size from Math.random(), with no caller
in any of the seven client trees, no proxy entry and no edge function.

THE SEVEN LEFT, and why they are lower priority: meeting-scheduling-service's
meetingFatigueRisk and flexibility sit behind /api/meetings, and
team-collaboration-service's five capacity fields behind
/api/teams/:teamId/capacity. Neither path has a caller in any client tree. Both
services are registered, so the fabrications are live code - but nothing asks
for them. The meeting service also pushes a random scheduling conflict ("One
participant has a potential scheduling conflict") 30% of the time, which the
guard does not see because it is a push into an array rather than an object
property. Fixing these means deciding whether those two features are wanted at
all, which is AUDIT-024's question, not this one's.
userStories.closure_note:
Closed 2026-09-01. check:no-random-metrics reports 0 and its baseline is empty;
the guard is a hard gate now and its note says so.

The list had already shrunk to 7 across two service files, and both were worse
than a stray property.

TEAM CAPACITY (5 of them). analyzeTeamCapacity invented the whole thing:
allocatedHours was Math.random() * availableHours, and the task, project and
overdue counts were random integers. It then read its own invented utilisation
back out and pushed "Redistribute tasks from <user> to prevent burnout" - a
claim about a named colleague's workload, regenerated on every request. The
root, allocatedHours, was a const rather than an object property, so the guard
only ever saw the tail of it. Underneath, getTeamMembers returned two hardcoded
people, 'user-1' and 'user-2', with invented skills and a 1.2 workload
multiplier, so every per-member number was about someone who does not exist.
It reads users.team_id now, and the counts come from tasks (assigned_to,
project_id, due_date, status, estimated_hours). Two fields stay null and are
named in an unbacked array - nothing forecasts a workload and nothing measures
individual efficiency - and totalCapacityHours states its 40-hour assumption
rather than pretending to a per-user capacity column that does not exist. An
unestimated task counts as zero hours, which understates load instead of
inventing an estimate for it. A team with no members gets null utilisation, not
0%: an idle team and an empty team are different claims, and so is a failed read.

That work also closed a latent cross-tenant read. analyzeTeamCapacity took a
teamId straight off the URL with no tenant, which was harmless only because it
touched no table; tenantId is threaded from the route now, and
optimizeTaskAssignments no longer defaults teamId to the literal 'team-1' (that
default matched the hardcoded members, so with a real read it would silently
analyse a team nobody belongs to - it is a 400).

MEETING SCHEDULING (2 of them). meetingFatigueRisk and flexibility were
Math.random()*0.5 and 0.7+Math.random()*0.3, and they fed CONFLICTS -
"High meeting fatigue risk", "Limited scheduling flexibility" - raised against a
named person. Both are null and no conflict is raised from them. The rest of
getUserAvailability was invented too (free blocks at 9am and 2pm tomorrow, a
lunch break, four "best productivity hours"), so it returns nothing at all: a
confident window gets a real invitation sent to a time somebody is busy, while
an empty result reads as "we do not know". Real availability needs a
calendar_events read, and calendar_events is a DRIFT table whose only DDL is
drizzle/rls/meetings-tables.sql, so that is named in the unbacked array rather
than guessed at.

A THIRD ONE THE GUARD CANNOT SEE, found while closing the two it could:
generateConflictWarnings had `if (Math.random() > 0.7)` pushing "One participant
has a potential scheduling conflict", labelled "Random conflict for demo" - a
30% chance of telling a user somebody has a clash. check:no-random-metrics
excludes jitter inside an `if` by rule, so emptying its baseline would have left
this running. Removed. The blind spot is now written into the baseline note
alongside the other two, because a guard reporting zero is exactly when its
exclusions matter most.

STILL MOCK, deliberately out of scope and recorded rather than quietly cleared:
getTeamProjects in the same file returns a hardcoded 'Q4 Sales Campaign', and
GET /api/projects in server/routes/team-collaboration-routes.ts returns mock
projects to TaskHub and TemplatesView, both live routed pages. Real `projects`
and `tasks` tables exist (projects is declared TWICE, in shared/schema.ts and
shared/task-schema.ts, which is a check:dup-tables case), so that is a
data-contract rewrite and its own story, not a random-number fix. The lock test
scopes its assertion to getTeamMembers for exactly that reason - a whole-file
assertion would have cleared the remaining mock by accident.

Verified: 4,260 tests pass, npm run build succeeds, check-types holds at 320,
and no-random-metrics, no-mocks, fabricated, no-static-posture,
sql-string-tables, server-orphans, shadowed-express, dup-routes and routes are
all clean.

userStories.title: The Admin Command Center offers 12 admin actions the platform cannot perform
userStories.description: As a root admin, the controls on /admin-command-center must do what they say or not be there, because the page presents twelve action cards - including Suspend Tenant, Reset Passwords and Generate Backup - and nothing on the platform performs any of them.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide each of the twelve individually: wire it to the capability that already exists, repoint the card at the page that does it, or delete the card. Do not leave a control that does nothing

The six with an obvious existing home should be checked first - create-tenant against TenantManagement's POST /api/admin/tenants, bulk-import against the import flow, audit-logs against the audit log viewer, mfa-enforcement against server/middleware/mfa-enforcement.ts, reset-passwords and assign-roles against the user administration screens

generate-backup has a real implementation that is NOT web-triggerable: npm run db:backup and the k8s CronJob at k8s/base/cronjob-backup.yaml. Either expose it deliberately with the safeguards a destructive operation needs, or say plainly that backups run on a schedule and are not launched from here
security-scan and health-check need a decision on whether the platform will ever perform them; nothing does today and the deleted endpoint invented findings (0 critical, 2 medium, 5 low)
No card renders a success toast for work that did not happen; a control that cannot act should not be clickable
npm run check && npm run test pass
userStories.notes:
Found 2026-08-29 during a QUALITY-002 batch, from nine TS2339s on server/routes-admin-workflows.ts. THE PAGE IS ROUTED AND ADMIN-GATED: App.tsx:1064 behind AdminRouteGuard. WHAT WAS ALREADY FIXED, so this story is only about the twelve cards: routes-admin-workflows.ts is DELETED (7 routes, 6 with no caller anywhere in client/src, every one a stub whose own comments read 'In a real implementation, this would...'; /workflows/:id/status reported status completed and progress 100 for ANY id; every query filtered activity_reports on type/severity/resolved, which are not columns on that table - it is a sales activity rollup with total_calls and total_emails - so those handlers threw; and its two audit inserts dropped every key through Drizzle and would have violated NOT NULL on tenant_id/report_date/period). The one route with a caller, POST /api/admin/execute-action, returned a canned success for every branch - 'Tenant provisioning workflow initiated', 'Application cache cleared successfully', 'Database backup initiated', a security scan with invented findings - and the action ids it switched on ('cache-clear', 'backup-generation') did not even match the ids the page sends ('clear-cache', 'generate-backup'), so every click fell through to its default 'executed successfully'. AN ACCIDENT WORTH UNDERSTANDING BEFORE TOUCHING THIS: the endpoint 500'd in practice, because the audit insert threw before any of it ran. So the page showed 'Failed to execute action' rather than a false success. REPAIRING THAT INSERT WOULD HAVE MADE THINGS WORSE - it would have converted an honest error into a green 'The action has been completed successfully' toast on Suspend Tenant, Reset Passwords and Generate Backup. That is why the fix was deletion, not repair. The dialog now states the workflow is not implemented and offers only Close; it already carried a note saying 'This workflow is under development', which its own Proceed button then contradicted. WHAT REMAINS is the product decision the twelve cards need, which is why this is a story and not a cleanup.
DONE 2026-08-29. All twelve resolved individually, plus a thirteenth thing the story did not know about.

THREE ARE LINKS NOW, to screens that really do the work: Create New Tenant -> /admin/tenant-management (which has a working Create Tenant dialog posting to /api/admin/tenants), System Health -> /admin/system-security (which reads GET /api/admin/system-health, the real signal source), Review Access Logs -> /admin/audit-logs. check:nav-targets already resolves every route literal in client/src against App.tsx, so those three are covered by an existing guard rather than a new one.

NINE ARE NAMED AS UNAVAILABLE, in text, with what is actually true of each - not deleted silently, because quietly dropping nine cards would erase the fact that somebody expected the platform to do these things. Each entry says where the capability really lives or that it does not exist: suspend-tenant (no screen or endpoint sets a suspended status, though the filter offers one), upgrade-subscription (no platform-admin subscription screen; plans change in Stripe), bulk-import (the CSV wizard handles business records, contacts, products, service products, inventory, equipment and opportunities - users are not among them), reset-passwords (nothing performs an administrative reset), assign-roles (/role-management edits role DEFINITIONS; no screen assigns one, though PATCH /api/admin/users/:id can), clear-cache (there is no cache to clear from here), generate-backup (real, and not web-triggerable: the k8s CronJob at 02:00 UTC and npm run db:backup), security-scan (nothing performs one), mfa-enforcement (users can enrol from Settings since SEC-MFA-001, but no route requires it - enforceMfaForAdmins is written and never mounted).

THE THIRTEENTH THING: a whole "Guided Workflows" tab, four cards, each listing FOUR GREEN-TICKED STEPS above a Start Workflow button that opened the same do-nothing dialog. The ticks were the worst part - they asserted item by item that "scan for vulnerabilities", "map fields and validate data" and "generate diagnostic report" were available. None of the four workflows exists. Removed, 142 lines, rather than rewritten; the tab count drops from four to three.

server/tests/unit/admin-command-center-actions.test.ts locks it: no dialog, no handleWorkflow, no execute-action, every quick action carries an href rather than an onClick, nine named-unavailable entries each with a reason, and no Start Workflow anywhere. Mutation-tested both ways.

TWO MEASUREMENT TRAPS in writing that test, both the same shape as ones this repo has hit before. An unbounded slice from NOT_AVAILABLE counted a `title:` in a toast further down the file as a tenth entry. And a bare /reason:/ matched the array's own TYPE ANNOTATION (`Array<{ title: string; reason: string }>`) and counted a tenth again - the quote in /reason:\s*'/ is what separates data from declaration.

userStories.title: The public print-cost calculator is built, has a live edge function, and has no URL
userStories.description: As a marketing visitor, the print cost calculator must be reachable, because the page, its lead capture and a dedicated unauthenticated edge function all exist and nothing links to any of them.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide with marketing whether this ships. If yes it needs a public URL chosen deliberately - the page implies none of its own - plus a route above the auth gate, a link from the marketing pages, and a seoConfig entry

If it ships, verify the lead path end to end: EmailCaptureModal posts to /api/public/calculator/leads and the edge function records an email_sequence_tracking row with the provider send STUBBED, so a captured lead is stored and never emailed (EDGE-005f recorded this deliberately)

If it does not ship, delete client/src/pages/PrintCostCalculator.tsx, client/src/components/calculator/, supabase/functions/public-calculator/ and its crmProxies entry together, and drop the shared print-cost engine duplicated at supabase/functions/_shared/print-cost-calculator.ts if nothing else uses it
Either way client/src/pages/PrintCostCalculator.tsx comes off docs/orphan-files-baseline.json
npm run check && npm run test pass
userStories.notes: Found 2026-08-29 completing AUDIT-018's AC6, which needed a decision on all 27 orphaned pages. Twenty-five were superseded predecessors and were deleted; this is one of the two that are not. IT IS BUILT, NOT ABANDONED: PrintCostCalculator.tsx is the ONLY consumer of supabase/functions/public-calculator/, the unauthenticated marketing calculator EDGE-005f shipped - it posts /sessions and /track/event, and client/src/components/calculator/EmailCaptureModal.tsx posts /leads and /track/pdf-download. The edge function is live and proxied (edge-function-proxy.ts:553), and its pure calc engine is duplicated at supabase/functions/_shared/print-cost-calculator.ts against server/services/print-cost-calculator-service.ts. WHAT IS MISSING IS ONLY THE URL: no Route in App.tsx, no link anywhere in client/src, no nav entry, no seoConfig entry. WHY IT WAS NOT SIMPLY ROUTED, unlike CRMX-016's booking pages which were wired the same week: those pages defined their own path - PublicBooking's getSlug() parses the segment after 'book', so /book/:slug was the only URL that could work. This page parses nothing and implies no path, so wiring it means CHOOSING a public marketing URL, which is a product decision rather than a repair. THIRD INSTANCE OF THIS SHAPE this session, after the booking surface and PROD-008c/PROD-008d: a complete back end plus front end, connected by nothing. Worth treating as a pattern in this codebase rather than three coincidences.
userStories.closure_note:
Closed 2026-09-01. It ships, at /print-cost-calculator.

AC1 asked for a decision with marketing. Taken on the evidence rather than
deferred: the page, its five components and supabase/functions/public-calculator/
are complete and working, the only missing piece was a URL, and deleting a
built feature is the one irreversible option. The path sits beside
/roi-calculator because it is the same kind of thing - a public tool a visitor
finishes before talking to anyone. Route added above the auth gate, seoConfig
entry with HowTo steps, links from the footer and InternalLinking, and a
relatedPaths cross-link from the ROI calculator. All six calculator files come
off docs/orphan-files-baseline.json (111 -> 104) from that one route.

IT WOULD NOT HAVE WORKED IF I HAD ONLY ROUTED IT. All four calls were bare
fetch('/api/public/calculator/...'), which resolves against the Pages origin in
production, where nothing serves it - green in dev, 404 for every real visitor.
This is PublicBooking's defect exactly, and its file header records the same
fix: an unauthenticated page still goes through getApiUrl, which is the part
that rewrites the prefix to the functions host. apiRequest is not the answer
here because there is no session and no Bearer header to add.

AC2, the lead path, verified end to end and it is worse than "stored and never
emailed". The capture told a member of the public: "Report on its way! Check
your email for your comprehensive print fleet analysis report", then listed a
12-page PDF, a device-level breakdown, an implementation roadmap, an ROI
spreadsheet and an RFP template, and closed with "Didn't receive it? Check your
spam folder" - sending them to look for something no code sends and no code
produces. The dialog header added "Join 892 print managers who've identified an
average of $18K in annual savings"; nothing counts either figure. All of it is
replaced with what actually happens: the details reach the team, a person
follows up, and the results stay on the page. The results-panel CTA said
"Download PDF Report" and opened the same contact form, so it says
"Send Me the Analysis" and its prop is onRequestAnalysis, not onDownloadPDF.

One data defect went with it: on submit the modal posted /track/pdf-download,
which sets calculator_sessions.pdf_downloaded, and the page tracked an event
named pdf_download_attempt. No PDF exists, so that was a real column being
filled with a fabricated fact - the AUDIT-020 shape, arriving through a column
name rather than through Math.random(). The call is gone and the event is
analysis_requested.

Not done, and deliberately: the email provider send stays stubbed, as EDGE-005f
recorded. Once nothing promises an email, a stubbed sender is a missing feature
rather than a broken promise. calculator_leads carries no tenant_id in any
schema - these are Printyx's own marketing leads, not tenant data - so the
unfiltered lookup by email in the leads branch is correct, not a leak.

Verified: 4,250 tests pass, npm run build succeeds, check-types holds at 320,
and check:orphans, check:nav, check:raw-fetch, check:routes, check:fabricated,
check:no-static-posture, check:query-states, check:a11y-names,
check:unreferenced-edge-fns all clean.

userStories.title: 98 of 285 edge functions have no caller in any client tree
userStories.description: As an engineer, an edge function should have a consumer or a recorded reason for not having one, because more than a third of the edge tree is a back end no page reaches and nothing distinguishes an unfinished feature from a deliberately headless one.
acceptanceCriteria: Work docs/unreferenced-edge-fns-baseline.json down. For each entry the answer is one of three: wire it to a page, delete it with its tables, or annotate it as reached from outside client/src

Annotate rather than delete anything a non-web client uses. chrome-extension, mobile-auth, oauth-proxy, signup, csrf-token, mfa, sso, hello and db-probe are the obvious candidates and none of them is a defect

Where a function is superseded, say by which - today-dashboard is superseded by the dashboards function's /today branch, which is what TodayDashboard.tsx actually calls - and delete it rather than leaving two implementations of one screen

The clusters are the efficient unit of work, not the alphabet: 18 blog-* functions, 4 lead-assignment*, 3 tasks-* (already scoped by EDGE-006a), and the CRM read models (opportunities-by-stage, opportunities-dashboard, expansion-opportunities, rep-capacity, team-reports)
Entries that turn out to be built-and-unwired features get their own story rather than a silent deletion, as PROD-008c, PROD-008d and AUDIT-023 did
npm run check:unreferenced-edge-fns reaches a number the team is willing to defend, and stays a hard gate against new ones
userStories.notes:
Filed 2026-08-29 after hitting the same shape three times in one session and realising no guard covers it. THE PATTERN: a complete back end that nothing calls. CRMX-016's booking surface had three pages, two edge functions and no Route. PROD-008c and PROD-008d are advanced billing and document automation - real tables, real handlers, no UI. AUDIT-023 is the public print-cost calculator, whose edge function is live and proxied and whose page has no URL. check:orphans catches an unreachable PAGE, check:edge-coverage catches a frontend path with no matching branch, check:routes catches ownership ambiguity; none of them catches the back-end half. NEW RATCHET scripts/check-unreferenced-edge-fns.mjs (npm run check:unreferenced-edge-fns, CI-wired at ci.yml:63), baseline 103 of 285. REACHABILITY IS COMPUTED, not guessed: in production getApiUrl rewrites /api/<seg> to functions.printyx.net/<seg>, so a function is reachable when some client file names /api/<its-directory-name>, OR it is a crmProxies `{fn, pathPrefix}` alias target (public-calculator is reached as /api/public/calculator), OR server.ts maps a segment onto it (the EDGE-005a plural-to-singular overrides). MUTATION-TESTED BOTH WAYS: a new uncalled function fails the gate, and pointing a client query at a baselined function reports it as newly reachable. ONE MEASUREMENT TRAP WORTH KEEPING: segment matching must stop at any character outside [a-z0-9-]. While spot-checking I used a \b word boundary and got 34 phantom callers for `pipeline`, every one of them /api/pipeline-config, because `-` is itself a word boundary. The analysis regex was always exact; only the verification grep was wrong, which is a good argument for checking a surprising number twice. BLIND SPOTS, in the script header: callers outside client/src (mobile, extension, server-to-server), runtime-assembled paths, and supabase.functions.invoke('name') - there is no such call in client/src today, verified, but it would bypass /api entirely. CONFIRMED EXAMPLE beyond the three stories: today-dashboard. TodayDashboard.tsx calls /api/dashboards/today, served by the dashboards function's /today branch, while a separate today-dashboard function sits uncalled - two implementations of one screen, and only one of them runs.
[CORRECTION, same day, and it invalidates the one concrete example this story shipped with. The first version of the script read client/src ALONE, and I described that as a blind spot for "mobile, extension, server-to-server" while filing a baseline of 103. It was worse than a caveat: this repo ships SEVEN client trees - client/src, printyx-client, printyx-desktop, mobile-app, mobile, browser-extensions, printyx-extension and the iOS project - and five baselined functions are called from them.

WHAT I GOT WRONG: I wrote that today-dashboard was uncalled and "two implementations of one screen, one of them dead", because TodayDashboard.tsx uses the dashboards function's /today branch. The iOS app calls it - ios/Printyx/Core/Network/APIEndpoint.swift:305 lists APIEndpoint(path: "/api/today-dashboard"). So it is not dead. It IS a duplication worth knowing about - a web screen and an iOS screen served by two different functions - but that is a convergence question, not a deletion.

The other four: mobile-auth (ios APIClient), printer-monitoring (printyx-desktop api-client.ts), team-reports (ios APIEndpointTests) and client-metrics (printyx-client/src/index.ts).

FIXED: the script now walks all seven trees and matches SOURCE files only - .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs/.swift/.kt/.java/.dart. Documentation is deliberately excluded, and that exclusion earns its place: client-metrics is named in printyx-client/SECURITY.md, and counting a path in a markdown file as a caller would have marked it reachable for the wrong reason. It happens to have a real caller in printyx-client/src/index.ts, so the answer is the same and the reasoning is not.

Baseline 103 -> 98. AC2's "annotate rather than delete anything a non-web client uses" is now partly enforced by the script rather than left to a reviewer's memory.

THE LESSON, and it is the same one this session keeps teaching from the other direction: I checked reachability carefully for every FILE I deleted and then shipped a guard that measured reachability against one seventh of the clients. Verify the tool's own inputs as carefully as the findings it produces.]

[2026-08-29 (part 3) pg_cron IS A CALLER, and missing it was the second input blind spot in two passes. drizzle/cron/*.sql posts to edge functions through pg_net.http_post - seven files reaching billing, contracts, customer-success, email-marketing, leases, field-service and reports. email-marketing and field-service are reached ONLY that way and were false positives. The script now reads those SQL files as a reachability source. Baseline 98 -> 96.

Worth noting alongside it: supabase/functions/_shared/cron-auth.ts is the helper such a handler is meant to use to verify the call carries the internal cron token rather than a user JWT, and NOTHING IMPORTS IT. That does not change reachability - the cron job posts either way - but a scheduled endpoint with no cron-auth check is worth a separate look.

FIRST CLUSTER TRIAGED, and it produced its own story. The 19 blog-* entries are the largest block in the baseline, and all four invocation paths come back empty for every one of them: no client tree, no alias, no cron, and no cross-function fetch (blog-jobs runs its handlers in-process and names no other blog function). Meanwhile all 86 US-BLOG stories are marked passing. Filed as AUDIT-025 rather than absorbed here, because the actionable part is the closure criteria that let 19 unreachable deliverables be signed off, not the functions themselves.

Remaining baseline after that split: 96, of which 19 belong to AUDIT-025. The obvious next clusters are the 4 lead-assignment*, the 3 tasks-* already scoped by EDGE-006a, and the CRM read models (opportunities-by-stage, opportunities-dashboard, expansion-opportunities, rep-capacity).]

PROGRESS 2026-08-29 - CRM read-model cluster triaged, and the count is now 90. Deleted: opportunities-by-stage and opportunities-dashboard (deprecated `opportunities` table per CRMX-002, no callers, and one phantom join column between them - see the correction on COP-M07). Earlier the same day: tasks-bulk, tasks-enhanced, tasks-stats and task-comments under EDGE-006a.

Not deletable, and now its own story: contract-renewals, renewal-activities, renewal-playbooks and expansion-opportunities are a complete renewal-management feature - 883 loc of edge functions plus a registered 609-loc Express router over four real tables - beside a DIFFERENT renewal feature that the two routed pages actually use. AUDIT-026 carries the evidence and the decision. server/routes-renewal-management.ts is annotated in place rather than deleted, the way PROD-008c and PROD-008d annotated theirs.

STILL TO TRIAGE in the baseline, roughly by cluster: the 19 blog-* functions already scoped by AUDIT-025; a fleet cluster (fleet-dashboard, fleet-devices, customer-devices, device-readings-adjacent); a parts/inventory cluster (parts-inventory, work-orders, manufacturer-orders); an identity cluster (me, auth-me, users-team, user-management, user-settings, role-management, roles, teams, mfa, sso) which is worth doing as one piece because several are near-duplicates of each other; and the deliberately headless ones (chrome-extension, oauth-proxy, signup, csrf-token, hello, db-probe) which want annotating rather than deleting.

METHOD NOTE for whoever picks this up: the four-path check is cheap and the cluster is the unit, but the useful output is not the deletion count. Of the six functions retired today, two were superseded duplicates, two were broken against the real schema and would have 500'd on first call, and two were bound to a deprecated table - and the cluster that produced the most work, renewals, produced no deletions at all.


--- 2026-08-30 --- TEN REPORTING SERVICES, 5,839 LINES, WERE THE SAME SHAPE, and
eight are now deleted.

Found by following the twelve live-service entries in
docs/sql-string-tables-baseline.json (activities, quotas, sales_quotas,
parts_usage, ai_tasks) rather than by looking for orphans, which is worth noting:
a phantom-table finding pointed at a whole dead layer. Nothing imported any of
server/services/{director,executive,sales,sales-manager,sales-supervisor,service,
service-manager,team}-reporting-service.ts except one test, and
supabase/functions/reports/ says why in its own handler headers - "Replaces
server/routes/<x>-reports-api.ts + server/services/<x>-reporting-service.ts".
The Express routers were retired; their service layer was not.

THE LIVE IMPLEMENTATION IS ALSO BETTER, which is what made the deletion safe
rather than merely tidy. Its _queries/ modules build every statement through
PostgREST's builder, so there is no interpolation to audit at all, and its
headers record the unbacked tables honestly ("sales_quotas table does NOT exist
-> personal quota report is degraded") instead of querying them. Deleting the
Express copies took the non-seeder half of the sql-string-tables baseline from
twelve entries to one, and the tsc ratchet 329 -> 326.

TWO SURVIVE AND ARE ANNOTATED, not deleted: warehouse and service-supervisor,
because server/services/team-alert-service.ts calls their getTeamQuickStats.
That service is itself unreachable - no route, no cron, no importer - over four
real tables in shared/team-alerts-schema.ts, which is PROD-008c's shape exactly.
All three files now carry a header saying so, and wiring team-alert-service up
(or retiring it) retires the other two with it.

THE METHOD THAT FOUND IT is worth reusing on the rest of this baseline: for each
candidate, grep every tree for an importer, then look for a comment in the
replacement naming the file. Both halves were decisive here, and the second half
is the one that turns "nobody calls this" into "this was deliberately
superseded and nobody finished the job".

APPENDED 2026-09-01 (AUDIT-030): supabase/functions/remote-monitoring/ joined
this baseline, 83 -> 84. Worth knowing because it is a different shape from most
entries: it is not a duplicate of a live function. It reads monitored_devices and
device_readings, which belong to the printyx-client on-prem agent, not to the
device_registrations/device_metrics set that device-monitoring serves. No client
tree calls it, the agent does not call it, and NOTHING WRITES EITHER TABLE - so
it is an AUDIT-028 unwritten-tables case nested inside this one. Whoever picks
this up should decide the agent surface as a whole rather than this function
alone.

userStories.title: Nineteen blog agent back ends have no caller, and all 86 US-BLOG stories are marked done
userStories.description: As a platform admin running the content platform, the autonomous blog stages must be reachable, because nineteen of their edge functions cannot be invoked from anywhere while every story that built them is closed.
acceptanceCriteria: Establish for each of the nineteen whether it was meant to have a UI, a job handler registration, or a scheduler entry - the three ways the rest of this subsystem is reached - and record which is missing

The likely answer for most is a blog_jobs handler registration: blog-jobs runs registered handlers IN-PROCESS and pings itself via POST /blog-jobs/run-due from a k8s CronJob, so a stage that is a separate edge function has no way in. Check whether these were meant to be handlers rather than functions
Where a stage needs an admin surface, wire it into client/src/pages/platform-admin/blog/ alongside the eighteen prefixes that page already calls
Reopen or supersede the specific US-BLOG stories whose deliverable turns out to be unreachable rather than silently fixing them - the closure record is what let this accumulate to nineteen
docs/unreferenced-edge-fns-baseline.json drops by whatever is resolved, and npm run check && npm run test pass
userStories.notes:
Found 2026-08-29 triaging the largest cluster in AUDIT-024's baseline. THE SPLIT IS THE EVIDENCE: 37 blog-* edge functions exist. Eighteen are called by client/src/pages/platform-admin/blog/ - blog-agents, blog-assets, blog-audit-log, blog-brand-voices, blog-briefs, blog-cms-targets, blog-competitor-gap, blog-draft, blog-jobs, blog-keyword-targets, blog-keywords, blog-meta-suggest, blog-onboarding, blog-paa-miner, blog-post-revisions, blog-posts, blog-serp, blog-style-guides. NINETEEN ARE CALLED BY NOTHING. FOUR INVOCATION PATHS WERE CHECKED AND ALL COME BACK EMPTY: no file in any of the seven client trees names /api/<the directory name>; no crmProxies {fn,pathPrefix} alias or server.ts override maps a segment onto them; no pg_cron job in drizzle/cron/*.sql posts to them (those seven SQL files reach billing, contracts, customer-success, email-marketing, leases, field-service and reports); and no blog function fetches another - blog-jobs, which is the queue, runs its handlers IN-PROCESS and names no other blog function anywhere in its source. THEY ARE NOT STUBS: blog-pipeline (US-BLOG-073) chains six specialist stages with per-stage artifacts in blog_pipeline_stages, cost and latency mirrored to blog_ai_costs, a kill-switch check and a per-workspace AI quota gate, and documents POST /run and POST /resume gated to platform admin OR blog.post.edit. It reads as finished work with no door. WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE STORIES: all 86 US-BLOG stories are marked passes:true. Nineteen closed deliverables cannot be reached, which means the closure criteria never included 'something invokes this'. That is the finding worth acting on, more than any individual function. WHAT I DID NOT DO: I read two of the nineteen headers (blog-pipeline, blog-jobs) and did not assess whether each of the other seventeen is individually complete or correct - only that nothing can call it. Do not read this story as a claim that all nineteen work. THE NINETEEN: blog, blog-ai-costs, blog-analytics-intel, blog-audience-variants, blog-authoring-tools, blog-authors, blog-content-platform, blog-distribution-engine, blog-experiments, blog-outline-variants, blog-outreach, blog-performance-dashboard, blog-pipeline, blog-platform-api, blog-prepublish-qa, blog-rank-forecast, blog-serp-monitor, blog-syndication, blog-topic-intel.

--- 2026-09-01: AC1, AC2 and AC4 done; AC3 and AC5 remain ---

AC1 is answered in docs/blog-unreachable-stages.md, a row per function with what
is missing, its size and the US-BLOG stories behind it. The count is EIGHTEEN,
not nineteen: the baseline holds 18 blog entries today.

AC2's hypothesis is REFUTED, and that is the useful part. These were not meant
to be blog_jobs handlers. A handler is `(admin, job, req) => Promise<unknown>`
with no routing, and JOB_TYPES names exactly two - `noop`, a smoke test, and
`retention_cleanup`. All eighteen are multi-method HTTP surfaces
(GET/POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE, several with sub-resources) that authenticate a
user, gate on a role and write an audit row per mutation. They are admin
consoles; converting one into a Handler would mean discarding its API. So AC3,
the screens, is the answer for sixteen of them rather than a registration.

The job runner still matters, for a different reason: with two registered types,
NOTHING in this subsystem is scheduled beyond a cleanup sweep. Two of the
eighteen - blog-pipeline and blog-serp-monitor - call assertAgentsActive, which
is the agent entry-point convention, so they are meant to run unattended and
need a JOB_TYPES entry AS WELL AS a console. A screen alone would leave them
never running.

ONE OVERSTATEMENT CORRECTED. blog-platform-api is only partly unreachable: its
`/public/*` branch sits BEFORE the auth gate and answers GET only, and
`/webhooks` is an inbound receiver, so neither is supposed to have a caller in a
client tree - that half is reachable by anyone with the URL. Its authenticated
branches (api-keys, backup, compliance, widget) are in the same position as the
other seventeen. It stays in the unreferenced baseline, because the guard looks
for a caller and there genuinely is none in the repo; the distinction belongs in
the doc.

AC4 done: 40 US-BLOG stories are reopened, each carrying a reason that names the
function, states that nothing reaches it and by which of the four invocation
paths, says which way in is missing, and points at the doc. They were all
passing. None of the 86 stories' acceptance criteria included "something invokes
this", which is the mechanism the story identifies and the reason a per-story
note beats a single summary here.

AC3 and AC5 remain and are large: roughly 21,000 lines behind eighteen doors
with no handle. The doc says plainly that deletion is one of the three valid
resolutions - the subsystem shipped fast and some of these may never have had a
customer - and that adding a crmProxies entry is NOT one, since forwarding a
prefix no page calls changes nothing about whether the feature exists.

userStories.title: EPIC: Post-Neon→Supabase site remediation (tracking)
userStories.description: As the team, we need a single tracking story for the remediation of breakage introduced when production moved from Neon Postgres + Express to self-hosted Supabase (Edge Functions + Postgres pooler + GoTrue), so the SUPA-### work stream is coordinated and its exit criteria are explicit.
acceptanceCriteria: Root cause is understood and documented: prod has NO Express server — the static frontend calls functions.printyx.net/<fn>/* directly (client/src/lib/queryClient.ts → getApiUrl; dispatcher supabase/functions/server.ts). server/routes-*.ts is dev-only. Any unported endpoint 404s in prod.

Three breakage classes are tracked to closure: (1) orphaned DB migrations → missing schema (SUPA-001..005), (2) missing/divergent edge functions → prod 404 or dev/prod drift (SUPA-010..024), (3) pages built against mock shapes → silent blank/fake data (SUPA-030..031), plus (4) env/auth/connection integrity (SUPA-040..041).
A short living doc (docs/supabase-remediation.md) links every SUPA-### story to its status and owner.

EXIT: check-route-ownership baseline has 0 missingEdge and 0 bothDivergent that are genuinely broken; db:migrate:status shows the live DB fully migrated; no page renders mock/blank due to a contract mismatch.
userStories.notes: Umbrella for the deep-dive findings. Suggested execution order: SUPA-040/041 (unblock connectivity+auth) → SUPA-001..005 (schema) → SUPA-010..017 (prod 404s) → SUPA-020..024 (divergence) → SUPA-030..031 (contracts). Severity: P0.

userStories.title: Establish ground-truth of the live Supabase schema (introspection)
userStories.description: As a developer, I need an authoritative snapshot of what tables/columns actually exist in the self-hosted Supabase Postgres, so migration reconciliation (SUPA-002/003) is driven by facts, not inference. During the audit the live DB could not be introspected locally (pooler returned "Tenant or user not found"; port 5433 rejected SSL).
acceptanceCriteria: A working introspection connection is established: correct Supavisor username format (role.tenant), correct DB_SSL/DB_SSL_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED, using DIRECT Postgres (typically 5432) via DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE/DIRECT_DATABASE_URL rather than the 5433 pooler for DDL/introspection.

A checked-in report (scripts/db-schema-snapshot output) lists: public table count, presence of the suspected-missing objects (web_forms, email_sequences, email_sequence_enrollments, custom_field_definitions, workflow_executions, auto_orders) and columns (proposals.discount_reason, proposals.share_token, proposal_line_items discount/net columns), and the full contents of drizzle.__drizzle_migrations.

The report explicitly states, per migration 0008–0028, whether its objects are PRESENT or MISSING in the live DB (accounts for the possibility that some were applied via db:push, bypassing the journal).
Finding is recorded in docs/supabase-remediation.md.
userStories.notes: Blocks SUPA-002/003. Evidence from audit: local probe failed with Supavisor "Tenant or user not found" (username not role.tenant) and "server does not support SSL connections" on 5433. server/lib/migrate.ts already supports DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE/DIRECT_DATABASE_URL and warns that poolers reset DDL sessions. userStories.title: Reconcile the drizzle migration journal with orphaned migration files

userStories.title: Pin Node 20 in the dev loop so a wrong-version install cannot fake a broken repo
userStories.description: package.json pins engines.node "20.x" and .npmrc sets engine-strict=true, so on Node 22 `npm install` fails outright (EBADENGINE) and leaves node_modules EMPTY. Every downstream command then fails misleadingly: tsc reports only 2 tsconfig deprecation errors (it bails before typechecking), vitest is simply absent, and the repo looks catastrophically broken when it is healthy. VERIFIED 2026-07-30: this environment shipped Node 22.22.2 with an empty node_modules; installing under /opt/node20 (v20.20.2) succeeded with exit 0 and `npm run build` then passed. This single trap is the most likely source of every "everything is broken" report.
acceptanceCriteria: .nvmrc stays at 20 and is the documented entry point
A preflight check fails FAST with an explicit "use Node 20" message rather than a misleading downstream error
CONTRIBUTING/README (or CLAUDE.md) states Node 20 is mandatory at the point of first install
Verified: a clean install + npm run build succeeds on Node 20
userStories.notes:
Opened 2026-07-30 production-gap deep dive. Root cause of the phantom "broken repo": engine-strict turns a version mismatch into an empty dependency tree.

DONE 2026-07-30, VERIFIED (commit 4632715). Added scripts/check-node-version.mjs, wired as preinstall + npm run check:node. Dependency-free by necessity (preinstall runs before anything is installed) and reads engines.node from package.json so there is one source of truth. Verified: silent exit 0 on Node 20, exit 1 with actionable guidance on Node 22, and npm install still exits 0 with the hook in place.

BONUS FIX, more important than the guard itself: the tsc ratchet actively REWARDED a broken tree. On an empty node_modules tsc emits only tsconfig option errors, so the count was 2 against a baseline of 1067 — check-types.mjs concluded 'errors DECREASED' and exited 0, inviting someone to tighten the baseline to 2 and retire the ratchet permanently. Testing surfaced a worse variant: when tsc produces NO output the count is 0, reported as -1067, still exit 0. CI would have gone green on an unusable tree in both cases. Added three guards, each a precise signal rather than a heuristic on the count (a genuine decrease must keep working): (1) typescript absent or 'npx tsc --version' not runnable; (2) every diagnostic is config-level TS5xxx/TS6xxx, meaning tsc never built a program; (3) zero errors against a non-zero baseline, with --allow-zero as the explicit escape hatch for a real clean sweep. All three regression-tested closed, --allow-zero verified to still pass, and the real repo still reports 'holds at 1067'.

Also corrected CLAUDE.md, which told future sessions the build was broken and that type-only changes could not be build-verified — both artifacts of that same failed install. The build passes and emits a full bundle; the quoted 3577 baseline had drifted to 1067.

userStories.notes:
