Every path the new text names was checked to exist. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: CLAUDE.md is the file every session reads before touching the repo, and its instruction was to wire new automation into a file that is not there. The next person adding a trigger would have followed it to a deleted path or, worse, imported the Node dispatcher into an edge handler and shipped a seam that never fires — which is precisely the defect this story was opened for, reintroduced by its own stale documentation. VERIFIED: 168 test files / 3658 tests, tsc holds at 496, prettier clean on CLAUDE.md.

userStories.title: CSV lead import is unreachable: orphaned component, shadowed endpoint, wrong host
userStories.description: As a sales manager, importing leads from a CSV must work, because the feature is fully built on both sides and reachable from neither.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide first whether the feature is wanted. client/src/components/leads/LeadsImport.tsx has NO importers - a repo-wide search finds only the file itself - so nothing renders the upload UI today. If the answer is no, delete the component and the endpoint together rather than leaving half of each

If it is wanted, three separate things are broken and all three need fixing. (1) The component uses a raw fetch('/api/business-records/import') rather than getApiUrl, so in production it targets the Cloudflare Pages origin instead of functions.printyx.net and never reaches a backend. (2) It sends credentials: 'include' with no Authorization header, which an edge function rejects. (3) The Express handler at server/routes-crm-core.ts:282 is under the proxied /api/business-records prefix, so it does not run in dev either

Port the handler to supabase/functions/business-records as a multipart branch. It is a real implementation, not a stub: CSV parse, per-row companyName validation, duplicate detection against existing records, and imported/skipped/duplicates/errors counters the UI renders
Multipart handling on the edge side is the shared blocker EDGE-002l tracks - check whether that has landed before starting
Wire the component into a routed page, or the fix is invisible
The import handler comes out of docs/shadowed-express-baseline.json when it is ported and deleted
userStories.notes:
Found 2026-08-20 while checking what retiring the /api/business-records cluster would lose. The endpoint looked like a live gap - the frontend does call it - until the caller turned out to be orphaned, which is the same shape as the trackContentView beacon in PROD-013: a reachable module holding an unreachable function. Recorded rather than deleted because the implementation is substantial and the tables exist; this is an unfinished feature, not dead code from a port. NOTE the ordering trap: fixing only the proxy shadowing would make it work in dev and stay broken in production, because the raw fetch does not go to the functions host at all. All three defects have to land together or the fix reads as done and is not. | 2026-08-27 ASSESSED. AC1 (decide whether the feature is wanted) HAS AN EVIDENCE-BASED ANSWER, and it is not the one this story frames: CSV import is wanted, is already built, and is already ROUTED — just not through LeadsImport. client/src/pages/CSVImportWizard.tsx is registered at /import (App.tsx:901), is not in the orphan baseline, and is backed by a real edge function, supabase/functions/import/, which does multipart, CSV parsing, entity types (business_records, contacts, products), column mapping, duplicate detection and job execution. So the choice is not "build it or delete it" — it is "delete the redundant second implementation", which is what AC1 says to do when the answer is no. LeadsImport.tsx (13.9 KB) is still orphaned, still has zero importers, and is recorded in docs/orphan-files-baseline.json. RECOMMEND deleting it together with the Express handler at routes-crm-core.ts:282, per this story's own wording; not done in this pass because it is a delete of a substantial component plus a server handler that interacts with the /api/business-records retirement, and that is worth one explicit yes. THE BLOCKER THIS STORY NAMES IS CLEARED: EDGE-002l (multipart bodies through the proxy) passed 2026-05-04, and four edge functions already call formData() today. THE ROUTED WIZARD HAS THE SAME DEFECT AND IT MATTERS MORE, because a user can actually reach it. All three of its multipart POSTs used raw fetch — the exact defect AC2(1) and AC2(2) describe for LeadsImport: getApiUrl rewrites /api/x to the functions host and a raw fetch skips it, so in production the request hit the Cloudflare Pages origin, fell through to the SPA shell and .json() threw on HTML; and credentials:'include' sends no Authorization header, which the edge function rejects. FIXED this pass: all three now go through apiFormRequest, which resolves the host, attaches the bearer token, handles the 401 refresh, and strips Content-Type so the browser keeps the multipart boundary. check:raw-fetch 86 -> 83. TWO DEEPER PROBLEMS FOUND WHILE MAPPING IT, both out of scope here and both needed before /import actually works end to end. (1) THREE ENDPOINTS THE WIZARD CALLS DO NOT EXIST ANYWHERE: POST /api/import/preview-mapping, POST /api/import/ai/map-columns and /api/import/jobs/:id/mappings. The edge function serves entity-types, templates/:t[/download], ai/status, upload, jobs/:id/validate, jobs/:id/duplicates[/resolve-all] and jobs/:id/execute — and there is NO Express /api/import router at all, so these are not shadowed, they are absent. After this pass they fail as honest 404s rather than "Unexpected token < in JSON", which is better but is not working. (2) THE EDGE FUNCTION KEEPS JOB STATE IN PROCESS MEMORY: `const importJobs = new Map()` at supabase/functions/import/index.ts:7, with its own comment saying "temporary - should use database in production". Edge invocations are stateless and multi-instance, so a job created by /upload is not visible to the /validate and /execute calls that follow it. The wizard is a multi-step flow over a backend that cannot remember step one. That is a schema + handler task, not a transport fix. SO THE HONEST STATE OF CSV IMPORT: the entry point is reachable, the upload path now reaches a real backend, and the flow still cannot complete. Worth its own story rather than being folded into this one, which is about the orphaned component. VERIFIED: tsc holds at 496, build passes, check:raw-fetch 83, eslint on CSVImportWizard unchanged at 36 problems. TEST NOTE, recorded rather than smoothed over: one full-suite run during this pass reported 5 failing tests in 1 file; seven consecutive runs before and after were 168 files / 3658 tests green, no test in the repo references CSVImportWizard, and I could not reproduce it or identify it. Unexplained, not dismissed.
--- 2026-08-27 --- TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE 08-27 ASSESSMENT ABOVE, and the job-state defect fixed.

CORRECTION 1. That note says "THREE ENDPOINTS THE WIZARD CALLS DO NOT EXIST ANYWHERE ... there is NO Express /api/import router at all". There is: server/routes-csv-import.ts, registered at routes-registry.ts:422 through domains/crm.ts, serving eighteen paths under /api/import including all three (preview-mapping at :203, ai/map-columns at :638, jobs/:jobId/mappings at :314). They exist in Express and were missing from the edge function, which is a dev/prod divergence, not an absence — and /api/import is NOT in crmProxies, so Express really does serve them in dev while production gets the edge function. The three now exist on both sides.

CORRECTION 2. The in-memory Map was not the only reason the edge executor could not work. Its row-processing loop reads job.tenant_id and job.user_id — snake_case — while the Map stored tenantId and userId. So every .eq('tenant_id', ...) in that loop filtered on undefined and every insert sent a null tenant into a NOT NULL column. The import could not have completed even within a single invocation. Reading the job from PostgREST fixes this as a side effect, because the row IS snake_case; both spellings are now correct against the same object.

FIXED. supabase/functions/import/index.ts no longer keeps job state in process memory. csv_import_jobs already existed (shared/csv-import-schema.ts, migration 0000) and the Express side already wrote to it; only the edge side kept its own copy. upload inserts a row and returns its id; jobs/:id, validate and execute read it back scoped by tenant_id; execute persists cumulative imported/skipped/merged counters per batch, so the 100-row batching the wizard drives actually accumulates instead of restarting from zero on a different instance.

ONE SHAPE FOR raw_data, and it is the part most likely to be broken by a later edit. Express stores rows as objects keyed by CSV header; the edge function stored arrays of cells and its executor indexed into them with headers.indexOf(sourceColumn). Both now produce objects. supabase/functions/import/_csv.ts holds the parser, and server/tests/unit/csv-import-row-shape.test.ts imports BOTH it and the Express parseCSVContent and asserts they return identical headers and rows for the same file — quoted commas, CRLF, blank rows, short rows and header-only files included. Mutation-tested: changing the edge parser to leave a missing cell undefined instead of '' fails it.

THREE ENDPOINTS ADDED to the edge function, matching the Express response shapes field by field: POST /preview-mapping (totalRows, headers, mappings, unmappedColumns, overallConfidence, sampleData), PUT /jobs/:id/mappings (merges the user's targetField/confirmed onto the auto-mapper's confidence, as Express does), and POST /ai/map-columns, which returns 503 with the Express message because there is no AI client in this runtime — which is exactly what GET /ai/status already reports. A 503 is the honest answer; a 404 made the wizard show a transport error for a feature that is simply not deployed there.

VALIDATE NO LONGER LIES. It used to set validRows = totalRows unconditionally and report zero invalid rows for any file. It now checks that every row has a value in whichever column is mapped to companyName/businessName — weaker than the Express validator, which also type-checks and looks for duplicates, and deliberately not dressed up as more. Rows with an empty company name are what actually break this import, and they are counted now rather than waved through.

STILL OPEN. AC1's recommendation stands and still needs one explicit yes: delete the orphaned LeadsImport.tsx and the Express handler at routes-crm-core.ts:282 together. Duplicate detection is still a stub on the edge side (GET /jobs/:id/duplicates returns [] and validate reports needsDuplicateReview:false), so /jobs/:id/duplicates/:dupId/resolve was NOT added — there is nothing for it to resolve, and csv_import_duplicates has no writer on that host. Express also serves jobs (list), jobs/:id/cancel and jobs/:id/ai-process, which the wizard does not call; /api/import stays bothDivergent.

VERIFIED: 10 new tests, 3698 pass; tsc holds at 496; build passes; lint holds at 10626; the edge function is syntax-clean under esbuild; check:phantom-cols covers csv_import_jobs and every column literal in this file passes — mutation-tested by pointing one .eq at a column that does not exist and watching it fail; edge-path and route-ownership guards green. NOT VERIFIED: no SQL ran and no request was made — this container has no database, so the insert/select/update path has never executed.
[DONE 2026-08-29. The one explicit yes this story was waiting on: LeadsImport.tsx and the Express handler at routes-crm-core.ts:282 are DELETED, together, exactly as AC1's recommendation stated.

Nothing else was needed. AC2 through AC6 were all conditional on "if it is wanted" being answered by fixing THIS path, and the 2026-08-27 assessment already established it is not: CSV import is wanted, is built, and is routed at /import through CSVImportWizard against supabase/functions/import/, which handles business_records and leads directly (index.ts:496, 569, 1073). So there was no handler to port, no multipart blocker to wait on (EDGE-002l), and no component to wire into a page - the working path needs none of them. Those ACs are void rather than skipped.

Removed with it: the multer upload config, parseCSV, and the multer/csv-parser/stream imports left dead behind them. Ratchets: shadowed-express 3 -> 2 in the backlog and 58 -> 57 retained (AC6), orphan-files 137 -> 136, eslint 10475 -> 10469, tsc holds at 345, 3799 tests pass, build succeeds.

I reached this independently from the other end - working the shadowed-express tail - and only found this story afterwards, when check:prd-refs flagged that CRMX-011a names a file I had just deleted. Worth noting for the next person: docs/shadowed-express-baseline.json still annotated the entry as a "LIVE BROKEN FEATURE... the only implementation", which this story had ALREADY disproved two days earlier. The assessment was right and the baseline was never updated to match it. When a story corrects a ratchet's annotation, correct the annotation too, or the next reader trusts the ratchet.]

userStories.title: Establish a runnable production smoke check against a deployed environment
userStories.description: The entire route-parity analysis is STATICALLY derived. CLAUDE.md is explicit that the prod-404 mechanism is proven but nothing has been executed against a live deploy, and asks for one curl per prefix before treating any of it as an incident. No claim in the gap analysis has been confirmed against a running production environment: npm run check:drift exits with "DATABASE_URL is not set", and npm run audit:pages needs a live app plus browser auth and a current anon key (CLAUDE.md notes the committed anon keys are rotated/stale — GoTrue /auth/v1/health returns 401). Until one authenticated request per domain is actually made, the 29 prod 404s remain high-confidence inference rather than measured fact.
acceptanceCriteria: A committed script issues one authenticated request per /api prefix against a deployed environment and reports status per domain
The 29 statically-derived prod 404s are confirmed or corrected against a real deploy
A current anon key is available to the check (documented as a reference, never a committed value)
Output is committed as a dated summary — audit-reports/ is gitignored, so an uncommitted report does not survive
userStories.notes:
Opened 2026-07-30 production-gap deep dive. This is the honesty gate on the whole analysis: static parity cannot distinguish "404" from "returns 200 with the wrong shape", and CLAUDE.md flags the latter as strictly worse.

STRENGTHENED 2026-07-30: the need for this is now demonstrated rather than theoretical. A purely static audit produced one confirmed false positive out of 29 (quote-templates — an api-shaped CACHE KEY, no network call). The architecture premise itself (getApiUrl -> functions.printyx.net with no Express fallback in PROD) has now been verified by reading the code, but still not by a single real request. Static parity also cannot distinguish a 404 from a 200 carrying the wrong shape, which is the more dangerous outcome.

PROGRESS 2026-08-01 — TOOL DELIVERED, NOT YET RUN. Story stays OPEN: 2 of 4 acceptance criteria require measuring a real deploy, and this session had no egress to one. Do not close it on the strength of the script alone.

DONE:
 * AC1 (committed script, one authenticated request per /api prefix, status per domain) — scripts/prod-smoke-check.mjs, wired as `npm run smoke:prod`. Domains come from computeParity() in scripts/lib/route-parity.mjs — the SAME source the gap analysis uses — so the check cannot drift from the claims it tests. 182 live domains by default; --all widens to orphaned callers too. Flags: --base/--out/--json/--strict/--all/--concurrency/--timeout.
 * AC3 (current anon key available to the check, documented as a reference and never a committed value) — .env.example gained a "Production smoke check" block naming PRINTYX_SMOKE_TOKEN / PRINTYX_SMOKE_ANON_KEY / PRINTYX_FUNCTIONS_URL, where each comes from, and the rotation caveat. No values committed.

NOT DONE (blocked, not deferred):
 * AC2 (confirm/correct the 28 static prod 404s against a real deploy) and AC4 (commit the dated output of an actual run) — the sandbox refuses egress by policy: every CONNECT to functions.printyx.net and api.printyx.net returns 403 at the agent proxy, and https://example.com is refused identically, so there is no general egress to compare against. Nothing about production was measured, and docs/prod-smoke-2026-08-01.md states that in its first line so the artifact cannot be mistaken for results.

KEY DESIGN — WHY IT NEEDS NO CREDENTIALS: requiring auth is exactly what kept this analysis unverified (the committed anon keys are rotated/stale, 401 from GoTrue /auth/v1/health). It does not need them, because the Coolify dispatcher resolves the function from URL segment 0 BEFORE any handler runs and enforces auth PER HANDLER. So: 404 carrying {"error":"Function not found"} proves the function is NOT deployed; 401/403/2xx proves it IS. Distinguishing that marker 404 from a handler's own 404 on an unhandled sub-path is what makes the verdicts trustworthy — a status-only check would report every function that simply does not serve GET / as missing. A token is still worth supplying: it upgrades 2xx responses into evidence about RESPONSE SHAPE, the failure mode static parity cannot see and that CLAUDE.md calls strictly worse than a 404. Bonus: the marker body carries available[], so ONE request to an impossible function name enumerates every deployed function (reported as corroboration only — server.ts aliases like accounts-payable->account-payable mean a prefix can resolve while its literal name is absent from that list).

TRAP FOUND AND FIXED — READ BEFORE TRUSTING ANY SMOKE OUTPUT: the first working version REPORTED A FABRICATED CLEAN BILL OF HEALTH against the blocked host, and the run looked completely normal. The proxy answers every path with 403; a status-only classifier reads 403 as "deployed, refused auth", so all 182 domains came back exists-auth — a confident report that production was healthy, produced without one packet reaching it. ANY uniform interceptor (proxy, WAF, CDN, captive portal, login wall) produces the same lie, and its natural answers (401/403) are precisely the ones that read as fine. Fix: a HANDSHAKE — before reporting anything, probe a function name that cannot exist and require the dispatcher's marker; only server.ts emits it, so receiving it proves the far end is the real dispatcher. Without it the run aborts (exit 1) saying plainly that nothing was measured. Deliberately NO override flag: every failure mode this catches produces plausible-looking output, and "wrong but confident" is the outcome this story exists to prevent. This is the story's own thesis reproduced in miniature — worth keeping in mind for PROD-010..014, where a wrong response SHAPE fails the same way.

VERIFIED: classifier exercised against a local mock reproducing all four dispatcher response shapes (marker 404 / 401 / 200 / bare sub-path 404) — all classified correctly, including the bare 404 that must NOT read as missing. Both failure paths confirmed: handshake refuses the blocked host with exit 1, --strict exits 2 on contradicted predictions. That verifies the classifier, not production. All five ratchets still pass (check:routes, check:nav, check:edge-paths, check:proxy-overrides, check:migrations); eslint clean; prettier applied.

TO FINISH: from any host with egress, `npm run smoke:prod -- --out docs/prod-smoke-$(date +%F).md` (add PRINTYX_SMOKE_TOKEN to also exercise shapes), then COMMIT the generated file — audit-reports/ is gitignored, so a report written there does not survive. | NEW RATCHET 2026-08-19 (from the PROD-013 documents port): scripts/check-raw-api-fetch.mjs + docs/raw-api-fetch-baseline.json + npm run check:raw-fetch, wired into ci.yml next to check:nav. A bare fetch('/api/...') in client code is broken in PRODUCTION two independent ways and works fine in dev, so local testing never catches it: (1) the relative path skips getApiUrl (client/src/lib/config.ts), which in prod rewrites /api/x to the edge-function host - a relative path instead hits whatever origin serves the static bundle; (2) credentials:'include' sends COOKIES, but edge functions authenticate with a Bearer JWT, so even a correctly-addressed call 401s. COUNT: 120 LIVE call sites (file reachable from App.tsx, a user can trigger it) plus 22 on unreachable files. That is a far wider blast radius than the one page that surfaced it and is multi-session work, so it is BASELINED to stop new ones while the existing set is worked down - shrink it, never grow it. The fix per site is apiRequest() from lib/queryClient for JSON, or a helper modelled on lib/invoice-pdf.ts for blob downloads. Detection rule: the URL argument must be a RELATIVE /api literal with only whitespace between it and the paren, so fetch(getApiUrl('/api/x')) and fetch(url) correctly do NOT report (verified against invoice-pdf.ts, quote-pdf.ts, document-export.ts). MUTATION-TESTED: reintroducing the exact raw fetch this was written for exits 1 at the right line; restoring the apiRequest call passes. This is a good candidate for a smoke-check assertion too - a prod smoke test that exercises any of these 120 sites would have caught the class years ago. | RAW-FETCH BURN-DOWN 2026-08-19, ROUND 1: live call sites 128 -> 121, baseline (deduped by file:url) 120 -> 113. THE TRIAGE RULE THAT MATTERS, learned the hard way: converting a raw fetch to apiRequest only FIXES production if the edge function actually implements that path. Otherwise you trade a wrong-origin request for a 404 and the page is just as broken, but now it LOOKS fixed. So check two things per cluster before touching it: (a) does /api/<prefix> have a crmProxies entry, and (b) does the edge fn have a branch for the specific sub-path. MEASURED TABLE of the remaining live sites by prefix, n = live sites, with proxy status: seo 17 (no proxy), subscriptions 16 (no), platform-crm 16 (PROXIED), public 9 (no), knowledge-base 9 (PROXIED), customers 8 (no), oid-mappings 7 (no), import 6 (no), integrations 5 (no), rbac 5 (no), social-media 4 (no), device-monitoring 3 (no), manufacturer-integrations 3 (no), admin 2, validate 2, then singletons (equipment, tasks, content, auth, auto-supply-replenishment, contract-renewal, leads, devices, pricing). CONVERTED THIS ROUND, both fully covered: the 7 platform-deals mutations on PlatformDealDetail + PlatformDealsPipeline (PATCH /:id, POST /:id/{move-stage,close-won,close-lost} - all four branches exist in supabase/functions/platform-deals/index.ts and the prefix is proxied) and the 5 ratings/votes sites in ArticleRatingWidget (the knowledge-base engagement dispatch covers GET /ratings/:id, GET /ratings/user/:id, POST /ratings, GET /votes/user/:id, POST /votes). CAVEAT ON THAT SECOND ONE, do not count it as a user-facing fix: client/src/components/knowledge-base/ArticleRatingWidget.tsx is imported by NOTHING - it is an orphan, so those 5 were in the ratchet's DEAD bucket and the live count did not move for them. Belongs to AUDIT-016. DELIBERATELY NOT CONVERTED, each because the endpoints do not exist edge-side: useSubscription's 16 sites (the subscriptions fn implements only plans + usage -> EDGE-002c); SEODashboard's 17 (the seo fn implements settings/pages/analytics/redirects/sitemap, the dashboard calls audit/crawl/content-*/images/links/mobile/performance/security/semantic/structured-data -> EDGE-002e); the 11 platform-crm assignment-rules/scoring-rules/territories sites (prefix IS proxied but platform-crm has NO branch for any of them - it only handles business-records, leads, activities, stats); and tasks/ai-schedule (absent, and its caller already swallows the failure on purpose). ALSO NOTED: the knowledge-base call sites in ArticleEditor/KnowledgeBaseAdmin use an /articles/ path segment (/api/knowledge-base/articles/:id) but the edge fn treats parts[0] as the ARTICLE ID directly, with no 'articles' segment - so those are a path-shape mismatch, not just a call-site fix. Verify that contract before converting them. | RAW-FETCH BURN-DOWN ROUND 2 (2026-08-19): baseline 111 -> 102, by fixing the knowledge-base admin cluster. WORTH READING BEFORE THE NEXT ROUND, because the pattern generalises: converting a raw fetch to apiRequest was only step THREE of three here. The KB admin pages were broken in three independent ways and only one was production-specific. (1) DEV-AND-PROD BUG: publish + archive PATCHed /api/knowledge-base/articles/:id/publish and /archive. NEITHER endpoint exists on the canonical Express router (server/routes-knowledge-base.ts) NOR the edge fn - those buttons 404'd EVERYWHERE. Fixed by routing both through PUT /articles/:id, which already accepts a status change, with changeType/changeDescription so the revision history records why. The same dead /publish call was also in ArticleEditor's save-and-publish path. (2) PATH SHAPE: the edge fn addressed articles FLAT (/ and /:id) while every caller uses /articles and /articles/:id - all of them 404'd in prod. Fixed by stripping an OPTIONAL leading `articles` segment (the EDGE-005e signatures idiom for its optional `signature-` prefix), so both shapes resolve and no caller has to change. (3) RESPONSE SHAPE: the edge list returned { data, total, page, limit } while Express returns { articles, pagination } and KnowledgeBaseAdmin reads articlesData?.articles - the table would have rendered EMPTY against a 200, the same failure mode as the platform-crm pages. The edge response now carries BOTH shapes (`data` kept as an alias) rather than swapping one for the other. Verified nothing else consumes the flat list before changing it. ALSO ADDED: a /analytics branch, which the admin dashboard calls and the edge fn never had; PostgREST has no COUNT FILTER or AVG so the tenant's articles are read once and reduced in JS rather than issuing five counts. `analytics` had to be RESERVED alongside categories/popular/search or the :id branches would treat it as an article id - watch for that whenever adding a named route to a function with a flat /:id shape. DEAD FILE FOUND: server/routes/knowledge-base-routes.ts is imported by NOTHING (the mounted one is server/routes-knowledge-base.ts, registry line 348). Do not mistake it for the canonical implementation - it has its own /analytics and /articles routes that never execute. TAKEAWAY FOR THE REMAINING 102: check whether the endpoint exists on EITHER backend before converting a call site; a 404 in dev means the fix is a feature, not a call-site change.
--- 2026-08-22 --- EGRESS RE-TESTED AND STILL BLOCKED. Recording the measurement
so the next session does not spend a round rediscovering it.

  curl https://functions.printyx.net/  -> curl (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, 403
  curl https://example.com             -> curl (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, 403

The agent proxy's own status endpoint confirms it is policy, not a transient
failure: GET $HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status lists both attempts under
recentRelayFailures as 'connect_rejected - gateway answered 403 to CONNECT
(policy denial or upstream failure)', and its noProxy allowlist covers only
package registries and Anthropic APIs. There is no general egress to compare
against, so AC2 and AC4 cannot be measured from this environment - unchanged
from the 2026-08-01 attempt.

scripts/prod-smoke-check.mjs (npm run smoke:prod) is ready and needs no
credentials to produce its primary verdict. What it needs is a runner with
egress.

userStories.title: Close prod 404s: AI, analytics & predictive surfaces
userStories.description:
VERIFIED 2026-07-30 via scripts/lib/route-parity.mjs: each domain below is called by a page REACHABLE from App.tsx/main.tsx and has NO edge function, so it works in dev (Express serves it) and returns 404 in production (which hits the edge function directly). 7 of these have an Express handler that is the port source; 1 have no handler on either side and are dead in dev AND prod.

  - /api/ai -> pages/GPT5Dashboard.tsx
  - /api/ai-analytics -> pages/AIAnalyticsDashboard.tsx
  - /api/predictive-analytics -> pages/PredictiveAnalytics.tsx  [NO Express handler either]
  - /api/predictive-failure -> pages/ServicePredictions.tsx
  - /api/business-process -> pages/BusinessProcessOptimization.tsx
  - /api/daily-briefing -> pages/DailyBriefings.tsx
  - /api/churn-risk -> pages/CustomerRisk.tsx
  - /api/qbr -> pages/CustomerQbrs.tsx

The no-handler domains (predictive-analytics) need a decision first: implement the endpoint, or remove the frontend call. Do not port a handler that does not exist.

Per CLAUDE.md, porting is not just route creation: use normalizePath(url.pathname, '<fn>') (an edge handler NEVER sees its own name in the path — the dispatcher strips segment 0), filter every query by tenant_id, and match the RESPONSE SHAPE the page actually reads. Returning the wrong shape is worse than a 404, because pages fall back to mock data with || and silently render fabricated numbers.
acceptanceCriteria: An edge function exists for every domain listed, resolving under the URL prefix the frontend already calls
Routing uses normalizePath so it behaves identically whether or not the function-name segment is present
Every query filters by tenant_id, and auth is enforced per handler
Response shape matches what the consuming page reads, verified field by field against the real Drizzle columns (not an assumed/mock shape)
Each domain is removed from the missingEdge list in docs/route-ownership-baseline.json
npm run check:edge-paths stays at 0 offenders
No regression in the ratchets: npm run check:routes, check:nav, check:migrations, check:edge-paths, check:proxy-overrides all still pass
userStories.notes:
Opened 2026-07-30 production-gap deep dive from the verified live-prod-404 set (29 domains across 30 pages). Confirm against a real deploy per PROD-020 before treating any single one as an outage.

SCOPE REFINED 2026-07-30 — the premise was VERIFIED and the count corrected 29 -> 28.

(a) PROD-ARCHITECTURE CONFIRMED (this had never been checked, and everything here depends on it): client/src/lib/config.ts getApiUrl() rewrites /api/x -> https://functions.printyx.net/x whenever import.meta.env.PROD, with NO Express fallback anywhere in the path. So a domain with an Express handler and no edge function DOES hard-404 in production. The porting work is genuinely required; it is not an artifact of the audit tool.

(b) ONE FALSE POSITIVE FOUND AND ELIMINATED: quote-templates. components/quotes/quote-templates.tsx has a CUSTOM queryFn that reads localStorage and never touches the network — the api-shaped string was only a TanStack Query CACHE KEY. route-parity greps reachable client files for api paths and cannot distinguish a cache key from a URL.
