RECORDED BUT DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED, needs a decision: that template hardcodes 'INFOMAX OFFICE SYSTEMS, INC.' as the seller, so in a multi-tenant product EVERY tenant's purchase agreement names that one company. white_label_config.company_name is the obvious source; the fix must land on both backends at once or the two will diverge. | SIZING FOR THE 3 REMAINING REAL MISSING-EDGE DOMAINS, measured 2026-08-19 rather than estimated (a filename/db-call heuristic mis-sized two domains earlier in this session, so these are counted from the file that actually defines the routes). (1) email-autopilot - server/routes-email-autopilot.ts, 1065 lines, 12 endpoints, 9 LIVE frontend paths, 13 helper fns. BEST NEXT TARGET: most live surface of the three. (2) chatbot - server/routes-chatbot.ts, 1210 lines, 9 endpoints, 7 live frontend paths. NOT a single-pass port: 8 of the 9 endpoints are simple CRUD over chatbot_* tables, but POST /query is a Claude agent that selects among ~700 lines of READ-ONLY query tools spanning many business tables, and re-expressing those SELECTs in PostgREST is where the risk and bulk are. Consider porting the 8 CRUD endpoints and treating /query separately, but note the prefix proxy is all-or-nothing so /query must be handled in the same function. (3) content - server/routes-content-marketing.ts, 863 lines, 21 endpoints, but only TWO live frontend paths and only ONE under /api/content: the fire-and-forget POST /api/content/analytics/view beacon in client/src/lib/seoUtils.tsx, which uses a RAW fetch and therefore never reaches the API in production regardless of any port (it is in the raw-fetch baseline). The other ~20 blog/guides/case-study endpoints have ZERO callers in client/src - the marketing blog pages are static React routes, not API-driven. LOWEST VALUE of the three despite being counted as a live prod-404 domain; porting 21 endpoints to fix one beacon is poor value, and the beacon needs its call site fixed either way. | SCHEMA COLLISION FOUND 2026-08-19 — blog_posts IS DECLARED TWICE WITH DIVERGENT SHAPES, and the US-BLOG system loses. Found while sizing the content-marketing port; recorded rather than fixed because choosing an owner and migrating data is an architecture decision. EVIDENCE, all verifiable: (1) shared/content-marketing-schema.ts:57 and shared/blog-schema.ts:344 BOTH declare pgTable('blog_posts', ...). 36 columns exist only in blog-schema, 35 only in content-marketing - divergent, not a copy. (2) shared/schema.ts re-exports BOTH (explicit named re-export at :8668 from content-marketing, `export * from './blog-schema'` at :9027). An explicit named re-export WINS over a later export *, so every consumer of `@shared/schema` silently receives the CONTENT-MARKETING definition - which is why server/routes-content-marketing.ts typechecks. (3) Only one shape can exist in the DB, and migration order decides it, not intent: migration 0000_fuzzy_blizzard.sql is JOURNALED and always applied, creating blog_posts with the content-marketing shape (content text NOT NULL, meta_title varchar(60), tenant_id uuid, focus_keyword, keyword_tier enum). drizzle/migrations/_backfill_blog_tables.sql:119 creates the blog-schema shape with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS - so it is SKIPPED IN SILENCE. No migration reconciles them (checked every ALTER TABLE "blog_posts" ADD COLUMN in the tree: only _backfill_blog_authors.sql adds author_id/reviewed_by_author_id/original_research_signal). CONSEQUENCE: the US-BLOG platform-admin blog system (28 tables, ~12 blog-* edge functions incl. blog-analytics-intel and blog-audience-variants, which query .from('blog_posts')) reads columns that DO NOT EXIST on the table it actually hits - body_markdown, body_html, brief_id, cms_target_key, cms_post_id, brand_voice_id, style_guide_id, canonical_url, featured_image_asset_id. And any INSERT from that system fails outright, because the physical table has content NOT NULL and the blog system never sets it. DECISION NEEDED: which system owns the name `blog_posts`? Renaming the US-BLOG one (e.g. to blog_system_posts) is the smaller change - the content-marketing table is the one that physically exists and is referenced by migration 0000 - but it touches 28 tables' FKs and every blog-* edge function. Do NOT 'fix' by dropping/recreating the table: whatever content-marketing rows exist would be lost. GUARD SHIPPED: scripts/check-duplicate-tables.mjs + docs/duplicate-tables-baseline.json + npm run check:dup-tables, wired into ci.yml, mutation-tested. It fails when a table name is newly declared by two different shared/*.ts schemas (a second declaration inside ONE file is ignored - the author can see that). THREE MORE COLLISIONS EXIST, all divergent and all baselined, each needing the same decision: client_activity_logs (client-monitor-schema vs printyx-client-schema, 31/46 unique columns), location_history (gps-tracking-schema vs mobile-service-schema, 48/3), dashboard_layouts (reporting-schema vs schema-dashboard, 10/32). CONTENT PORT NOT DONE and should not start until this is settled: porting routes-content-marketing means committing to the content-marketing blog_posts shape in a second place.
--- 2026-08-20 (loop round 37) ---

content: NOT a port either, but for a different reason - the endpoint has no
caller.

The only /api/content reference in the frontend is
POST /api/content/analytics/view, in trackContentView (client/src/lib/seoUtils.tsx:194).
That function is defined once, re-exported once from client/src/lib/seo/index.ts:68,
and invoked NOWHERE - a repo-wide search for the name returns exactly those
two lines. route-parity marks the domain live because the module is reachable
from App.tsx through the SEOProvider import, which is true of the file and
false of the function.

The Express handler is real, unlike the three mock dashboards: it inserts
into content_analytics (shared/content-marketing-schema.ts:390), a table with
no tenant_id because it is public marketing-site traffic.

Second defect, independent of the 404: trackContentView uses a raw
fetch('/api/content/analytics/view') rather than getApiUrl, so even once it
is wired up it targets the Cloudflare Pages origin in production rather than
functions.printyx.net. It never reaches a backend at all. That also means the
prod-404 framing does not describe this domain accurately.

Disposition: wire the beacon up (call it from the marketing pages, route it
through getApiUrl, and port the handler), or delete the dead export. Porting
the endpoint on its own would build a backend for a caller that does not
exist. Two shape traps for whoever does it: content_analytics.content_id is
uuid NOT NULL and content_type is an enum (blog_post/guide/case_study/
landing_page/calculator/comparison/whitepaper), so a slug in either field is
a runtime failure the Express handler does not guard against.

--- 2026-08-22 (loop round 38) --- PROD-013 CLOSED.

content was the last of the six domains, and it closes by DELETION, not by a
port. trackContentView in client/src/lib/seoUtils.tsx is gone, along with its
one re-export in client/src/lib/seo/index.ts. Nothing called it: a repo-wide
search for the name returned the definition and that re-export, and no third
line. route-parity counted the domain live because seoUtils is reachable from
App.tsx through SEOProvider, which is a fact about the file and not about the
function.

Porting the handler for it would have been building a backend for a caller
that does not exist, and the caller could not have worked if it did. Three
independent failures, each sufficient: the beacon used a bare relative fetch,
so in production it addressed the Cloudflare Pages origin and never reached a
backend; the receiving handler is Express-only, so that host would 404 anyway;
and content_analytics.content_id is uuid NOT NULL while every page under
client/src/pages/blog/ is a static React file keyed by a slug with no database
row and therefore no uuid to send. Wiring it up is a real story - the ~21
marketing-content endpoints on the edge side, plus a decision about how a
static page identifies itself to a uuid column - and it should be opened by
whoever wants the metric, not smuggled in under a 404 cleanup.

AC1 does not literally hold for this domain and is not being claimed: there is
no edge function for content, because after the deletion there is no caller to
serve. The other five each have one (accessories, contract-tiered-rates and
documents ported here; renewal-autoquote under PROD-011; quote-templates was a
false positive, closed earlier).

VERIFIED: docs/route-ownership-baseline.json missingEdge 4 -> 3, live prod 404s
4 -> 3. The gate was mutation-tested in BOTH directions - reinstating a call to
the path made check:routes report '1 NEW missing-edge route' and exit 1;
removing it again returns green - so the pass reflects the deleted call site
and not a scanner blind spot. docs/raw-api-fetch-baseline.json 87 -> 86 (the
same call site was the seoUtils entry). All eight ratchets green: check:routes,
check:nav, check:migrations, check:edge-paths, check:proxy-overrides,
check:dup-routes, check:shadowed-express, check:identical-fallback,
check:dup-tables.

LEFT IN PLACE DELIBERATELY: server/routes-content-marketing.ts, 863 lines and
21 endpoints, now has zero callers on either side. It is NOT shadowed (no proxy
entry for the prefix), so it still registers and still works in dev; retiring
it is a routine-cleanup story, not a 404 fix, and it is the file that would be
the port source if the beacon is ever wanted. The blog_posts duplicate-table
collision recorded above is untouched and still needs an owner decision before
anyone commits to the content-marketing shape in a second place.

userStories.title: Close prod 404s: platform, integration & compliance surfaces
userStories.description:
VERIFIED 2026-07-30 via scripts/lib/route-parity.mjs: each domain below is called by a page REACHABLE from App.tsx/main.tsx and has NO edge function, so it works in dev (Express serves it) and returns 404 in production (which hits the edge function directly). 4 of these have an Express handler that is the port source; 0 have no handler on either side and are dead in dev AND prod.

  - /api/erp-integration -> pages/ERPIntegration.tsx
  - /api/security-compliance -> pages/SecurityComplianceManagement.tsx
  - /api/white-label -> pages/WhiteLabelDashboard.tsx
  - /api/workflow-automation -> pages/AutopilotDashboard.tsx + pages/WorkflowAutomation.tsx

Per CLAUDE.md, porting is not just route creation: use normalizePath(url.pathname, '<fn>') (an edge handler NEVER sees its own name in the path — the dispatcher strips segment 0), filter every query by tenant_id, and match the RESPONSE SHAPE the page actually reads. Returning the wrong shape is worse than a 404, because pages fall back to mock data with || and silently render fabricated numbers.
acceptanceCriteria: An edge function exists for every domain listed, resolving under the URL prefix the frontend already calls
Routing uses normalizePath so it behaves identically whether or not the function-name segment is present
Every query filters by tenant_id, and auth is enforced per handler
Response shape matches what the consuming page reads, verified field by field against the real Drizzle columns (not an assumed/mock shape)
Each domain is removed from the missingEdge list in docs/route-ownership-baseline.json
npm run check:edge-paths stays at 0 offenders
No regression in the ratchets: npm run check:routes, check:nav, check:migrations, check:edge-paths, check:proxy-overrides all still pass
userStories.notes:
Opened 2026-07-30 production-gap deep dive from the verified live-prod-404 set (29 domains across 30 pages). Confirm against a real deploy per PROD-020 before treating any single one as an outage.

SCOPE REFINED 2026-07-30 — the premise was VERIFIED and the count corrected 29 -> 28.

(a) PROD-ARCHITECTURE CONFIRMED (this had never been checked, and everything here depends on it): client/src/lib/config.ts getApiUrl() rewrites /api/x -> https://functions.printyx.net/x whenever import.meta.env.PROD, with NO Express fallback anywhere in the path. So a domain with an Express handler and no edge function DOES hard-404 in production. The porting work is genuinely required; it is not an artifact of the audit tool.

(b) ONE FALSE POSITIVE FOUND AND ELIMINATED: quote-templates. components/quotes/quote-templates.tsx has a CUSTOM queryFn that reads localStorage and never touches the network — the api-shaped string was only a TanStack Query CACHE KEY. route-parity greps reachable client files for api paths and cannot distinguish a cache key from a URL. Fixed at the source by renaming the key to 'local:quote-templates' (also more honest: there is no quote_templates table in any schema/migration), so the tool no longer classifies it. Removed from the baseline; missingEdge 39 -> 38, live prod 404s 29 -> 28. Gotcha worth knowing: the first version of the explanatory comment SPELLED OUT the api path and re-triggered the same grep — the comment now deliberately avoids the literal string.

(c) I checked the OTHER 28 for the same no-network pattern (scripted scan for a queryFn resolving from localStorage/sessionStorage near each match). quote-templates was the ONLY one. The remaining 28 are real.

(d) predictive-analytics and technician-sessions are confirmed REAL but differ from the rest: they use the DEFAULT queryFn (queryClient.ts joins the queryKey into a URL and fetches it), so they issue genuine requests — and they have NO handler in Express either, so they are broken in DEV TOO, not just prod. technician-sessions also drives mutations (check-in), so the technician ticket workflow is non-functional everywhere. Neither has a backing table (no technician_sessions, no quote_templates in any schema or migration), so these two need an implement-with-schema decision, not a port.

(e) MEASURED EFFORT for the ports, so the remaining batches are honestly scoped: the four PROD-012 handlers alone are 3,950 lines of Express (routes-voice-ticket-close 860, routes-voice-agent 825, routes-chatbot 1200, routes-email-autopilot 1065), and each exposes 4-9 endpoints. Extrapolating, the full 26-domain port is roughly 20,000 lines of Express to re-express as Deno edge functions WITH field-by-field response-shape parity. This is multi-session work and must not be rushed: per CLAUDE.md these pages fall back to mock data with '|| [...]', so a shape mismatch silently renders fabricated numbers — strictly worse than the 404 it replaces. | PROGRESS 2026-08-19 - white-label PORTED; live prod 404s in docs/route-ownership-baseline.json 16 -> 15. supabase/functions/white-label/ covers all twelve endpoints (config GET/PUT, verify-domain, email-template list/get/upsert/delete/preview, presets, apply-preset, css, config-by-domain) over the real migration-0000 tables white_label_config / white_label_email_templates / white_label_presets. Dir name == URL segment so a PLAIN crmProxies entry was enough - no server.ts override (the EDGE-004 decision rule, not EDGE-005a's). THREE THINGS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE THE NEXT PORT IN THIS BATCH: (1) SHAPE - WhiteLabelDashboard.tsx reads camelCase (companyName/colorPrimary/customDomainVerified) but PostgREST returns snake_case, so every row is converted on the way OUT and every request body is mapped to real columns on the way IN via an explicit allowlist (an unmapped key is a PGRST204, per EDGE-005a). Returning raw snake_case here would have rendered the entire branding form blank while still returning 200. (2) SEEDING - creating a config seeds 5 default email templates in the Express path (WhiteLabelService.getDefaultTemplates, ~216 lines of literal template HTML). Rather than let dev and prod diverge on first create, those defaults plus generateCssVariables and renderEmailTemplate were duplicated into supabase/functions/_shared/white-label.ts, following the _shared/print-cost-calculator.ts duplicate-and-note idiom. KEEP THE TWO IN SYNC. (3) The /css endpoint returns text/css, NOT JSON - it is consumed as a stylesheet, so it bypasses createCorsResponse and sets its own Content-Type on top of getCorsHeaders. ALSO FIXED ON THE EXPRESS SIDE: all 10 handlers read req.headers['x-tenant-id'] directly instead of the resolved tenant. NOT an IDOR - resolveTenant (server/middleware/tenancy.ts:132) 403s a header that disagrees with the JWT before any handler runs - but it 400'd on any request that did not happen to send the header, and it is the pattern CLAUDE.md forbids; now getTenantId. PARITY GAP KEPT DELIBERATELY: verify-domain marks a domain verified WITHOUT any DNS lookup on both sides (the Express service has a TODO for real TXT/CNAME verification); the edge fn reproduces that rather than silently diverging, and both now say so. TRIAGE NOTE FOR THE REST OF THIS BATCH - erp-integration is NOT worth porting as-is: server/routes-erp-integration.ts /dashboard is 100% hardcoded mock (integrationOverview counts, an 'SAP Business One' system with invented sync stats, etc), so porting it would only move fabricated numbers into prod. Check each remaining domain for a real data source FIRST; security-compliance and incident-response are the same page archetype and likely the same. NOT VERIFIED: deno is not installed in this environment, so the function is not deno-checked and nothing was executed against a deploy - confirm with one curl per endpoint before treating this as closed. | TRIAGE TABLE 2026-08-19 - measured all 15 remaining missing-edge domains for whether the Express handler has a REAL data source, so no one spends a session porting fabricated numbers. Method: find the file that actually serves the prefix (NOT the file whose name matches - several disagree), then count db.select/insert/update/delete/query calls in it. PURE MOCK, DO NOT PORT AS-IS (0 db calls): erp-integration (740 lines, invented SAP sync stats), incident-response (677), workflow-automation (server/routes-workflow-automation.ts, 730 - and CLAUDE.md already flags this file as an UNREGISTERED dead mock; the REAL runtime is server/routes/workflow-automation-routes.ts, so check which file actually answers before porting this one). REAL, PORTABLE (db calls in parens): documents/routes-document-automation.ts (266 lines, 1) is the smallest remaining; security-compliance (597, 4); voice-agent (825, 3); chatbot (1210, 4); email-autopilot (1065, 4); renewal-autoquote (762, 6); voice-ticket-close (860, 6). FILENAME TRAP - these five have NO server/routes-<domain>.ts and are served from a differently-named file: accessories + contract-tiered-rates -> routes-products-crud.ts (both now ported), ai -> routes-registry/routes-sample-data, business-process -> routes-business-process-optimization.ts, content -> routes-content-marketing.ts. A `ls server/routes-<domain>.ts` returning nothing does NOT mean the domain is unserved. | TRIAGE TABLE CORRECTED 2026-08-19 (round 2) - MY OWN EARLIER TABLE WAS WRONG TWICE, both times from the same mistake: counting db calls in the file whose NAME matches the domain instead of the file that DEFINES the route. Corrected method: grep for the file containing (app|router).(get|post|...)('/api/<domain>...) and read the SPECIFIC handler - even a per-file db-call count misleads, because routes-operations-extended.ts has 11 db calls overall while its security-compliance/dashboard handler is 100% hardcoded mock (invented threat ids, a fake john.smith@printyx.com, fabricated scores). CORRECTED RESULTS. PURE MOCK, do not port as-is: erp-integration, incident-response, workflow-automation (routes-workflow-automation.ts), ai, business-process, and security-compliance (whose handler lives in routes-operations-extended.ts, NOT the similarly-named server/security-compliance.ts, which is an audit-logging module with no routes at all - that is the file that fooled my first count). REAL, with db-call counts in the file that actually defines the routes: content/routes-content-marketing.ts 35, chatbot/routes-chatbot.ts 30, renewal-autoquote/routes-renewal-autoquote.ts 23 (my earlier '6' was wrong), email-autopilot/routes-email-autopilot.ts 19, voice-agent/routes-voice-agent.ts 13, voice-ticket-close/routes-voice-ticket-close.ts 10. NOTE routes-sample-data.ts matches many domains and is NOISE - it is a seeder that merely mentions the paths. SIZING NOTE for whoever takes renewal-autoquote: it is the best-documented of the real ones (dedicated shared/renewal-autoquote-schema.ts, a header listing all 11 endpoints, frontend already on apiRequest) but POST /generate is a ~260-line generation engine that is also cron-callable, so the port is not just CRUD and interacts with EDGE-009. | FABRICATED-COMPLIANCE FINDING + REMOVAL 2026-08-19. While triaging the mock domains I found that security-compliance was not merely 'a mock dashboard' but a LEGAL-010-class problem stated inside the product: SecurityComplianceManagement.tsx rendered, to any authenticated user, an overall security score of 94.7, '6 certifications active', and a GDPR entry with status 'compliant', complianceScore 96.8, certificationStatus 'active', auditor 'EU Compliance Solutions' and audit/expiry dates - all a hardcoded object literal. Sibling endpoints returned audit logs SYNTHESISED WITH Math.random(), which is worse than returning nothing, since that is the record you consult during an incident. REMOVED the page, its 3 routes (note /security-compliance had NO guard at all) and all 7 endpoints, faking nothing in its place per the CLAUDE.md rule. Navigation now points at the REAL stack: 'Audit & Compliance' in the sidebar, the mobile drawer and AdminHub all target /admin/audit-logs (AuditLogViewer -> /api/audit-logs -> services/audit-log-service.ts -> the audit_logs table, unit-tested and already written to by logAuditEvent). gdpr_requests and security_sessions are likewise REAL tables in shared/security-schema.ts, so a genuine compliance dashboard has sources - build on those, and never restate a certification the company does not hold. TWO REUSABLE LESSONS. (1) DUPLICATE REGISTRATION DECIDES WHICH MOCK YOU ARE LOOKING AT: /api/security-compliance/dashboard was defined IDENTICALLY in routes-operations-extended.ts AND routes-sample-data.ts, and sample-data registers FIRST (routes-registry.ts:360 vs :368), so the copy Express actually matched was the sample-data one - deleting only the 'obvious' file would have left the fiction live. server/routes-sample-data.ts defines 29 routes and shadows real route modules on at least customer-success/health-scores, integration-hub/dashboard, remote-monitoring/fleet-overview and document-management/library; in each of those the shadowed handler is ALSO a mock today, so nothing real is hidden yet, but that stops being true the moment one of them is implemented. This is the second registration-order trap this session (the first was contract-tiered-rates losing an RBAC gate) - a check for doubly-registered paths is worth writing. (2) THE NAV RATCHET PAID FOR ITSELF: deleting the page left 5 stale references (navigation-permissions.ts x3, MobileNavigationDrawer, AdminHub) that check:nav caught immediately; grepping the component name alone would have missed all of them because they reference the PATH, not the component. STILL MOCK, same decision pending, all routed and reachable: erp-integration (/erp-integration), incident-response (/incident-response, /incident-response-system), business-process, ai-analytics, integration-hub, document-management, customer-success, maintenance, remote-monitoring. None of these makes a compliance claim, so none is as urgent - but each renders invented numbers as fact.

RAW-FETCH ROUND 3 (2026-08-19): 102 -> 94, and a triage rule that makes the rest safe to work on.

THE RULE. A bare relative fetch works in dev (vite proxies /api to Express) and 404s in production (it resolves against the origin serving the bundle). Converting one is SAFE exactly when the prefix is in crmProxies: dev already routes that prefix to the edge function, so the converted call reaches the same handler in both environments. When the prefix is NOT proxied, the edge function may not implement the path at all, and converting takes the call from "works in dev, 404 in prod" to "404 in both". Of the 102 baselined sites, only 20 sat on a proxied prefix.

FIXED: the three UNAUTHENTICATED pages — PublicBooking, BookingManage, HostedFormPage — 8 sites. These are the ones a real visitor hits from an emailed link, and every one of them 404'd in production. They go through getApiUrl rather than apiRequest on purpose: apiRequest would fix the URL too, but it also attaches a Bearer token and throws on non-2xx, and these handlers are public and use res.ok to tell "not found" from "found". Verified the public-booking and public-forms functions serve every path first.

NOT CONVERTED, and each for a stated reason:
  - 12 platform-crm sites (assignment-rules, scoring-rules, territories, business-records export/bulk-assign/convert-to-tenant) have NO handler on EITHER backend. Converting a call to an endpoint that does not exist is not a fix. This is the COP-B09 set.
  - /api/tasks/ai-schedule: the tasks edge function has no such branch.

THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST HERE, recorded in client/src/hooks/useSubscription.ts itself. SubscriptionBanner is mounted in App.tsx, so it runs on EVERY page, and all 16 of its calls are bare fetches — the entire subscription/plan/usage/trial surface is blind in production. The obvious repair makes it worse: the subscriptions edge function implements plans, usage, invoices, features, change-plan, root list/create and :id/cancel|resume, but NOT current, notifications, notifications/:id/dismiss, create, upgrade, cancel-as-a-path, convert-trial, stripe/config or checkout. Express has the complete implementation and the prefix is unproxied, so dev is fine and only production is dark. Closing it means porting those endpoints — SubscriptionService.getSubscriptionStatus holds the limit/usage/overage logic and Stripe is in the path — which is its own story rather than a call-site edit. A warning block now sits at the top of the hook so the next person does not convert it into a double outage.

SUBSCRIPTION STATUS PORTED (2026-08-19). GET /api/subscriptions/current now exists on the edge function, so SubscriptionBanner — mounted in App.tsx, therefore running on EVERY page — can see the plan, usage, overage and trial state in production. It could not before: the endpoint was Express-only and the call was a bare relative fetch.

HOW, and why it is not just a copied handler. The endpoint is three DB reads plus arithmetic, and the arithmetic is where a divergence would be invisible and expensive. It now lives in server/lib/subscription-status.ts and supabase/functions/_shared/subscription-status.ts, locked by subscription-status-parity.test.ts (29 tests). The Express service was refactored onto its copy with no behaviour change, so the two cannot drift apart silently.

TWO BEHAVIOURS THE TESTS PIN HARDEST, both of which would be invisible in review:
  1. STORAGE UNITS. Plan limits are stated in GB; usage_metrics records storage_used_mb. The comparison multiplies by 1024. Drop that factor in one copy and every tenant over ~1 GB is reported over their storage limit by whichever backend answered. Mutation-tested: removing it fails 6 tests.
  2. THE CUSTOM-LIMIT MERGE USES `||`, NOT `??`. A 0 in custom_limits means "no override recorded", not "zero allowed". Switching to ?? gives every such tenant a limit of zero. Mutation-tested: fails 1.
  Also pinned: trial days floor at 0 rather than going negative (fails 1), daysUntil rounds UP so a renewal later today reads as 1 day, and both copies read either casing since Express returns camelCase Drizzle rows and PostgREST returns snake_case.

The no-subscription body is deliberately identical to Express's ({ hasSubscription: false, message }), so the hook's check behaves the same against either backend.

STILL EXPRESS-ONLY, unchanged and still bare fetches on purpose: notifications, notifications/:id/dismiss, create, upgrade, cancel (as a bare path), convert-trial, stripe/config, checkout. The last two need Stripe in the edge environment. The warning block at the top of useSubscription.ts lists them so nobody converts a call site into a double outage.

Raw-fetch baseline 94 -> 93.

SUBSCRIPTION NOTIFICATIONS PORTED (2026-08-19). GET /subscriptions/notifications and POST /subscriptions/notifications/:id/dismiss now exist on the edge function, so in production the banner has its alert list and dismissing one actually sticks. Both were Express-only; neither did anything for a real user.

The filter is copied deliberately rather than reinvented: this tenant, this user when the caller is known, status != 'dismissed', newest first, capped at 50 — matching server/routes-subscriptions.ts — and the body is { notifications }, not a bare array, because that is what the hook destructures.

TEST (13) pins the two ways a port like this goes wrong QUIETLY rather than loudly: a filter that widens, and a column that is not there. Dropping the not-dismissed test would resurrect every alert a user has already cleared; dropping the tenant scope on dismiss would let one tenant clear another's. Mutation-tested all three — removing the dismissed filter, removing the tenant scope from the dismiss, and returning a bare array — each fails exactly 1.

Raw-fetch baseline 93 -> 91. Subscription surface still Express-only: create, upgrade, cancel-as-a-path, convert-trial, stripe/config, checkout. The first four are ordinary ports; the last two need Stripe in the edge environment, which is a deployment decision rather than code. The block at the top of useSubscription.ts is updated to say which three are done and which six are not.

CANCEL + CONVERT-TRIAL PORTED (2026-08-19). POST /api/subscriptions/cancel and POST /api/subscriptions/convert-trial now exist on the subscriptions edge function. SubscriptionSettings.tsx posts to the BARE /cancel path, not to :id/cancel — the edge function only had the :id form and Express only has the bare form, so the two backends were exactly divergent and the Cancel button 404'd against the static origin in production. The subscription stayed active and the user saw an error.

Both branches mirror SubscriptionService, including the parts a port drops quietly:
 * The tenant row. An immediate cancellation sets tenants.subscription='canceled', billing_status='canceled', is_active=false; an end-of-period one leaves the tenant active until it lapses. A port that deactivated unconditionally would lock every canceling customer out of access they had already paid for. Pinned by a regex that matches the guard and the update together — matching 'if (immediate)' anywhere above the update passed the mutation, because the status update has its own.
 * The acknowledgement email (LEGAL-011 — several state auto-renewal statutes require one). The body builder moved to supabase/functions/_shared/cancellation-email.ts, a Deno copy of the pure half of server/services/cancellation-confirmation.ts, and the edge function sends it through the SendGrid REST wrapper the way daily-briefing and billing already do. server/tests/unit/cancellation-email-parity.test.ts (7) compares the rendered subject, html and text case by case; mutation-tested by rewording one sentence (3 fail) and by changing the grace period the email promises (6 fail).
 * The durable subscription_events row with the LEGAL-011 keys — mode, effectiveDate, confirmationSent, confirmationRecipient, confirmationError — so the record answers what was cancelled, when it took effect and whether the customer was told, rather than just that something happened.
 * The in-app notification, which is the copy that does not depend on email delivery succeeding.

convert-trial takes its renewal date from nextPeriodEnd(), added to the subscription-status twin pair; SubscriptionService.convertTrialToPaid was refactored onto it with no behaviour change. Calendar arithmetic, not 30/365 days, and Date's month-end rollover (Jan 31 + 1 month is Mar 3) is pinned rather than corrected — it is what production has always written. A customer whose renewal date depends on which backend answered is a billing dispute.

TESTS: subscription-cancel-convert-shape.test.ts (11) checks every written column against the real Drizzle columns of tenant_subscriptions, tenants, subscription_events and subscription_notifications, and that the selection matches Express ('active','trialing','past_due' for cancel, 'trialing' for convert). Mutation-tested four ways — a phantom billing_state, an unconditional tenant deactivation, inlined period arithmetic, and a widened status filter — each fails exactly 1. One mutation initially escaped because .in('status', [...]) appears twice in the file and the first occurrence is in /current; the retest targeted the cancel branch specifically.

LABEL CORRECTION: the code comments this workstream added said PROD-004, which is a different story (report-execution permission ordering). All 24 occurrences on this branch are now PROD-014. server/tests/api-endpoints.test.ts keeps its own PROD-004 reference — that one is not from this work.

Suite 2680 -> 2704 passing. Raw-fetch baseline 91 -> 89. Typecheck holds at 1008; phantom columns hold at 234; check:routes, check:edge-paths, check:migrations, check:proxy-overrides, check:no-mocks all still pass. ESLint ratchet tightened 11916 -> 11698 (the drop is upstream, not from this change).

STILL EXPRESS-ONLY on this surface: create, upgrade, stripe/config, checkout. The first two are ordinary ports; the last two need Stripe credentials in the edge environment, which is a deployment decision rather than code. The block at the top of useSubscription.ts names exactly which paths the edge function serves and which it does not, so nobody converts a call site into a double outage.

CREATE + UPGRADE PORTED (2026-08-19). POST /api/subscriptions/create and /upgrade now exist on the edge function, which closes every non-Stripe path on this surface. SubscriptionSettings.tsx posts to /upgrade, so in production changing plans 404'd against the static origin; nothing could start a subscription at all.

THE TRAP WORTH NAMING: the edge function ALREADY had a change-plan branch, and reusing its plan lookup would have looked like the obvious port and rejected every real request. change-plan resolves the plan by ID; the frontend sends a SLUG (planSlug / newPlanSlug). Both new branches resolve by slug and change-plan is left alone — it is a different caller with a different contract. Pinned by reading the hook's own type declarations, so the test fails if either side moves.

Also ported rather than paraphrased: the duplicate-subscription refusal (the thing that stops a tenant being billed twice — same two statuses Express checks), the is_active/is_visible availability check, billing-cycle validation BEFORE any write, the tenant plan cache, the from_plan/to_plan event, the welcome/upgrade notification, and Express's refusal of a scheduled change (501 with the same message) rather than silently applying it now.

THREE HELPERS ADDED TO THE TWIN PAIR, and the Express service refactored onto them with no behaviour change: planAmount (annual vs monthly, parsed — numeric arrives as a string and .toFixed would throw on one), resolveTrialPeriod (a trial needs all three of asked-for, plan-enabled and a positive day count; loosening any gives free time away on a plan that does not offer it), isUpgradeAmount.

A CLAIM I GOT WRONG AND CORRECTED: isUpgradeAmount's first comment said an unparsed 'newAmount > currentSubscription.amount' would compare lexicographically and label every $9->$10 move a downgrade. The mutation test disproved it — JS coerces the string when the other operand is a number, so that comparison is already correct. The real hazard is a MISSING amount: 10 > undefined is NaN-false, so a subscription with no recorded amount reads as a downgrade. Comment, edge-function comment and test now say that instead. Kept the helper for the absent case and for both backends deciding identically.

TESTS: subscription-create-upgrade-shape.test.ts (17) plus 17 more parity cases for the new helpers. Mutation-tested SIX ways on the branches — an id-based plan lookup, a lexicographic upgrade comparison, a dropped duplicate-subscription guard, inlined trial arithmetic, a phantom billing_state column, and a scheduled change silently applied — each fails exactly 1. And three on the helpers; the zero-day-trial and dropped-snake_case mutations fail 1 each, while the unparsed-comparison mutation is what exposed the wrong claim above.

Suite 2704 -> 2732 passing. Raw-fetch baseline 89 -> 87. Typecheck holds at 1008; phantom columns hold at 234; check:routes, check:edge-paths, check:no-mocks, check:proxy-overrides all still pass.

SUBSCRIPTION SURFACE NOW: only stripe/config and checkout remain Express-only, and both need Stripe credentials in the edge environment. That is a deployment decision, not code — porting them without the credentials would move two working-in-dev call sites to 404-in-both.

CHATBOT CONSOLE PORTED (2026-08-19). ChatbotConsole.tsx had no edge function at all, so in production every panel on the page 404'd while dev worked fine off Express. supabase/functions/chatbot/ now serves the console: connections (list/toggle/delete), connect, links (list/create/delete) and query-log. No crmProxies entry and no server.ts override — the dir name equals the URL segment, so the dispatcher resolves it, and adding a proxy would drag dev onto the edge function too (which would break /query in dev, per the CLAUDE.md warning about proxying an un-migrated prefix).

FIRST, WHAT WAS NOT PORTED AND WHY. POST /chatbot/query is the answer engine, not a route: a six-tool read-only registry (account_summary, rep_activity, pipeline_status, this_week_deltas, at_risk_customers, predicted_failures) at ~430 lines of tenant-scoped Drizzle joins, plus Claude-routed tool selection with a keyword fallback and the LEGAL-012 crisis gate that must run before any retrieval. Translating that to PostgREST in the same change would produce WRONG ANSWERS rather than errors — a confident summary of the wrong account. The edge function returns 501 CHATBOT_QUERY_NOT_PORTED naming the reason instead of 404ing anonymously, and a test asserts the tool registry is NOT half-present. Porting it needs CLAUDE_API_KEY in the edge environment (a deployment decision, like Stripe) and each tool verified against real data one at a time.

THE PORT'S TWO REAL HAZARDS, both now in the twin pair (server/lib/chatbot-projection.ts + supabase/functions/_shared/chatbot-projection.ts, textually identical):
 1. CASING. The page reads platformUserId, printyxUserId, toolsCalled and responseExcerpt straight off each row. Express returns Drizzle rows (already camelCase); PostgREST returns snake_case. An edge function handing back raw rows renders a table of BLANK CELLS with no error anywhere — the EDGE-005a failure mode. Express's links and query-log handlers returned raw rows, so they are now routed through the same projections: a no-op on Node, the guarantee on Deno.
 2. TOKENS. chatbot_connections.encrypted_tokens holds the workspace bot token. projectConnection reports only tokensSet and never the value. Mutation-tested by adding the raw jsonb back to the projection (4 tests fail) and by spreading the row into the connect response (1 fails).

Worth recording plainly: obfuscateCredential is base64, not encryption, despite the column being named encrypted_tokens. Anyone holding the row can reverse it. Carried across unchanged so the two backends read each other's rows; a test states the reversibility so nobody reads the column name as a security guarantee. Making it real encryption has to migrate what is already stored — separate change. The shared implementation is TextEncoder + btoa rather than Buffer, which is the one form that is identical on both runtimes; a naive btoa(string) throws on a multi-byte secret, and the parity test covers 'clé-café-ü' for exactly that.

TESTS: chatbot-projection-parity (10) and chatbot-edge-shape (17). The shape test walks every .from('<table>') chain and requires an eq('tenant_id') or a tenant_id in the payload, checks every column literal against the real Drizzle columns of the three chatbot tables, and pins that the link email is resolved against THIS tenant's users (matching across all tenants would map a Slack account onto someone else's employee and mark it verified). Mutation-tested nine ways in total — six on the handler (unscoped list, cross-tenant email resolution, raw row spread, raw query-log rows, a phantom installed_by_id column, header tenant winning over the JWT) and three on the projections — each caught. Two test bugs found and fixed while doing it: the column extractor was reading response-body keys as columns, and the 501 assertion looked before the code rather than after.

Live prod-404 domains 6 -> 5; the chatbot domain moves to bothDivergent, which is accurate — /query stays on Express by design. Suite 2732 -> 2759 passing. Typecheck holds; phantom columns hold at 234; check:routes, check:edge-paths, check:nav, check:no-mocks, check:migrations, check:proxy-overrides, check:raw-fetch all pass.

THE FOUR REMAINING missingEdge DOMAINS ARE NOT PORTS. business-process, erp-integration, incident-response and workflow-automation each call a single /dashboard endpoint, and the Express handlers behind them contain NO db. or storage. call at all — they return hardcoded objects (routes-business-process-optimization.ts:32, routes-erp-integration.ts:21, routes-incident-response.ts:21). Porting them would move fabricated numbers from dev to prod, which is worse than a 404 because the pages would then render them as real. These are the mock dashboards awaiting a product decision: delete the pages, or build the queries. Not a porting task either way. (content is the fifth: one analytics beacon from lib/seoUtils.tsx.)

BULK ENDPOINTS FIXED + A NEW RATCHET FOR THE WHOLE CLASS (2026-08-19). Four bulk paths the frontend calls had NO branch on their edge function, so the request fell through to the generic handler and the action word became the id:

  DELETE /product-models/bulk-delete    -> delete where id = 'bulk-delete'
  DELETE /software-products/bulk-delete -> same
  POST   /invoices/bulk-delete          -> the CREATE-INVOICE branch
  POST   /invoices/bulk-update          -> the CREATE-INVOICE branch

Confirmed, not inferred: id is PgVarchar on all three tables (checked with getTableColumns, not assumed), so the delete matched no row, PostgREST returned no error, and the function answered 200. The user selected rows, clicked delete, and was told it succeeded while nothing was deleted. The invoices pair is worse — both are POSTs, so a click on 'delete selected' sent {ids:[...]} into the invoice constructor.

FIX: a branch per path, placed ABOVE the generic one — the ordering IS the fix, and a bulk branch placed after the :id branch is dead code with the identical symptom, so server/tests/unit/bulk-route-ordering.test.ts asserts the source order. Semantics mirror server/routes-bulk-operations.ts: tenant-scoped, capped at 500 ids, empty list refused (an empty ids array must not read as 'all'), and for bulk-update a FIELD WHITELIST so an endpoint the UI calls to set a status cannot rewrite total_amount — which is a real column, which is why it matters. Invoices also keeps Express's all-or-nothing check: if any id is not this tenant's, the whole batch is refused rather than silently updating the reachable subset. The catalog deletes .select('id') and report what was actually removed rather than restating ids.length, which would be a quieter version of the same bug. Parsing + whitelist live in the twin pair server/lib/bulk-ops.ts + _shared/bulk-ops.ts, locked by bulk-ops-parity.test.ts (23).

THE DURABLE PART — npm run check:edge-coverage (scripts/check-edge-path-coverage.mjs), wired into ci.yml. check:routes classifies per DOMAIN, so a domain with an edge function that answers only a fraction of what the frontend calls it for reads as 'both divergent' and nothing looks at the inside. This does: for every literal /api/<domain>/<segment> a REACHABLE client file calls, does that segment appear in the domain's edge function source? Baseline docs/edge-path-coverage-baseline.json at 178 paths across 53 domains — do not grow it.

The first version of the scanner was WRONG and the mutation test caught it: it read raw text, and the comment above a branch names the very path the branch handles, so renaming 'bulk-delete' to 'bulkDelete' left the check green. It now strips comments with a scanner that tracks string state (so a // inside a URL is not a comment). Re-mutated on two branches afterwards; each fails.

WHAT THE NEW RATCHET IMMEDIATELY SURFACED, worth acting on in later passes: seo implements FIVE resources (settings, pages, redirects, sitemap, analytics) while the frontend calls TWENTY — alerts, audit, competitors, content, crawl, images, keywords, links, mobile, performance, regenerate-llms, regenerate-robots, regenerate-sitemap, security, semantic, structured-data are all prod 404s on a function CLAUDE.md already records as having been 404ing on every endpoint before the normalizePath sweep. Also: the CSV import feature (POST /<type>/import) is missing from every catalog edge function — product-models, product-accessories, professional-services, software-products has it, supplies, managed-services — so bulk catalog import is dead in production for six of seven product types. That one is a real port (multipart parse + CSV + per-type validation and column mapping), not a routing fix.

Suite 2759 -> 2790 passing. Typecheck holds; phantom columns hold at 234; check:routes, check:edge-paths, check:raw-fetch, check:dup-routes, check:no-mocks all pass.

SEO DASHBOARD READ PATH FIXED (2026-08-19). The new check:edge-coverage ratchet pointed here first: the seo edge function implemented five resources while the frontend called twenty. SEODashboard.tsx loads seven lists and the function answered two, so five panels 404'd in production. Ported audit/history, keywords, competitors, alerts, page-scores and crawl/results, every row through the twin pair server/lib/seo-projection.ts + _shared/seo-projection.ts.

WHAT THE PORT TURNED UP IS WORSE THAN THE 404s, and all of it was broken in DEV too:

 1. GET /api/seo/crawl/results was swallowed by GET /api/seo/crawl/:crawlId, so it filtered crawl_id = 'results'. No crawl is ever given that id, so the crawl panel returned [] forever on BOTH backends. Same action-word-as-id class as the bulk endpoints last pass. Fixed with a real latest-crawl route registered ABOVE the parameterized one, on both backends; the source order is asserted because placing it after restores the bug verbatim.

 2. THE PAGE READ FIELDS THAT ARE NOT COLUMNS. seo_page_scores has seo_score, content_quality, technical_seo, user_experience, mobile_score, accessibility_score. The page read technicalScore, contentScore and performanceScore — three of its four progress bars were bound to nothing and rendered empty everywhere. seo_alerts has no 'type' column (the alert's subject is its metric; title is the human line). seo_competitor_analysis has no overall score and no active flag, and its domain is competitor_url while backlinks is total_backlinks. All re-bound to the real columns; the two features with no backing column (competitor score, competitor active badge) were REMOVED rather than faked, per the BATCH-7 recipe.

 3. /api/seo/pages IS NOT THE PAGE-SCORES ENDPOINT. Express serves it from a 'seoPages' binding that resolves to UNDEFINED — there is no seo_pages table in shared/, in any Drizzle schema, or in any migration (checked all three; routes-seo-core.ts even carries a TODO admitting the import was disabled). So GET /api/seo/pages is a 500 in dev. The edge function meanwhile answered it from seo_page_scores. SEODashboard now reads /api/seo/page-scores, which is the real endpoint on both backends and was already implemented on Express.

NAMED GAP, NOT FIXED: RootAdminSEO.tsx still reads and writes /api/seo/pages for its marketing page records, and that table does not exist. Inventing it here would be a schema decision made inside a routing fix. It needs either a migration + schema for seo_pages or the section deleted — a product call, recorded rather than guessed at.

TESTS: seo-projection-parity (22) and seo-crawl-results-ordering (7). The parity test checks every projected field against getTableColumns rather than against what the page asked for, and asserts the invented fields stay dead (technical_score / content_score / performance_score are NOT columns; the projection must not re-add them). Mutation-tested five ways — swapping the crawl route order, dropping the tenant filter from the latest-crawl lookup, resurrecting a phantom field in the projection, dropping snake_case support, and pointing the page back at /api/seo/pages — each caught.

Edge-path coverage baseline 178 -> 173. Suite 2790 -> 2819 passing. Typecheck holds; phantom columns hold at 234; check:routes, check:raw-fetch, check:edge-paths all pass.

STILL PROD 404s ON seo, unchanged and listed so the next pass has them: audit (POST run), crawl (POST start), images, links, content, semantic, security, mobile, performance, structured-data, regenerate-llms, regenerate-robots, regenerate-sitemap. Most are POST analysers backed by server/services SEO code that makes outbound HTTP (PageSpeed Insights and the crawler), so porting them is a service-layer move plus egress from the edge environment, not a routing fix.

MODULAR DASHBOARD FIXED (2026-08-19). The coverage ratchet flagged the dashboard domain; what it was hiding is the worst single thing found in this workstream. supabase/functions/dashboard/index.ts answered /modules with FOUR HARDCODED CARDS — '$125,430' monthly revenue, 'Active Deals 48', 'Total Customers 1247' — identical for every tenant.

STATED PRECISELY, because it matters: those numbers were never actually shown. The function returned a BARE ARRAY while ModularDashboard.tsx destructures { modules, userRole, roleConfig }, so `modules` came back undefined, the default [] applied, and production rendered the 'no modules' empty state. The card ids were invented too ('revenue','deals','tasks','customers') and match nothing in the real role config, so /card-config offered toggles that could never resolve. The dashboard was dead in production rather than lying — but only by accident of the shape being wrong as well as the data.

THREE MORE DEFECTS FOUND, ALL LIVE IN DEV TOO:
 1. THE CARD SELECTION HAS NEVER WORKED ON EITHER BACKEND. The page used queryKey: ['/api/dashboard/modules', enabledCards.join(',')] and the default queryFn builds its URL with queryKey.join('/') — so switching a card on requested /api/dashboard/modules/team_revenue,inventory_alerts. Express does not route that path (404) and the edge function ignored it. Both backends read ?enabled=; the page now sends it through an explicit queryFn.
 2. inventory_alerts RAISED 42703 ON EXPRESS. Its filter was raw SQL: `current_stock <= reorder_point`. inventory_items has no current_stock column — the quantity column is quantity_on_hand. The surrounding catch swallowed it and REPLACED THE WHOLE MODULE LIST with the 'Dashboard Loading... ---' fallback, so a user who switched on Low Stock Items got a permanently loading dashboard. Fixed on both sides.
 3. THREE QUARTERS OF A MANAGER'S DASHBOARD WAS BLANK. roleCardConfig gives manager and admin four default cards (business_overview, revenue_summary, customer_summary, service_summary) and only business_overview ever had a branch. The other three are now built, from the same aggregates business_overview already computes.

The role map, the active-card resolution and the per-card presentation moved to the twin pair server/lib/dashboard-cards.ts + _shared/dashboard-cards.ts, and Express was refactored onto them. Card IDS and CATEGORIES are what that pins hardest: the page persists switched-on ids in localStorage (so a backend inventing its own makes every toggle meaningless) and groups cards by category (so a card labelled 'management' on one backend and 'sales' on the other lands in a different section of the screen).

A CHECKER LESSON WORTH KEEPING: the first version of the edge function used a countWhere(table, applyFilters) helper, and check:phantom-cols immediately reported three phantom columns — inventory_items.record_type, invoices.record_type, inventory_items.status. All three were FALSE POSITIVES: it resolves a column literal against the table its call chain is on, and a filter applied inside a callback is attributed to whichever .from() it last saw. The right response was not to baseline them. Writing code the checker cannot read is how a real 42703 gets through, so the counts were rewritten as direct .from(...).select(...).eq(...) chains — which is also how the 42703 in defect 2 above would have been caught years ago.

TESTS: dashboard-cards-parity (24), including one that asserts the fabricated figures are gone from the edge function (comments stripped first — the header quotes them to say what was removed) and one that NAMES the five cards still listed in the role map with no builder on either backend: company_revenue, completion_rate, response_time, team_tickets, technician_performance, for the technician and service_manager roles. Those roles' dashboards are still mostly empty; that is a build-them-or-remove-them product call, recorded rather than faked. Mutation-tested four ways — a category drift, an unchecked enable (which would let a caller name any card id), the wrong query parameter, and reverting the page to the path-joined query key — each caught.

Suite 2819 -> 2843 passing. Phantom columns hold at 234; typecheck holds; check:routes, check:edge-coverage, check:raw-fetch, check:no-mocks all pass.

CATALOG CSV IMPORT REBUILT (2026-08-20). The coverage ratchet flagged /import missing from six of seven catalog edge functions. Looking at why turned up a feature that was broken END TO END, in dev, before production is even considered — the template the app hands you does not match the parser that reads it back.

FOUR DEFECTS, all confirmed against getTableColumns rather than inferred:
 1. THE PRODUCT MODELS TEMPLATE MATCHED ALMOST NOTHING. It offered nine columns the parser never read — Standard Cost, Standard Rep Price, New Cost, Upgrade Cost, Model, Color Print, BW Print, Color Copy, BW Copy — and omitted eleven the parser did read, including MSRP, New Rep Price, Upgrade Rep Price and every active flag. Download the offered template, fill it in, import it: every price is silently dropped and the UI reports success.
 2. THE ACCESSORIES IMPORTER READ SNAKE_CASE while its template offered Title Case, and read row.accessoryCode for the code but row.accessory_name for the name — two casings in one object literal.
 3. THE SUPPLIES PARSER WROTE A description COLUMN. supplies has no description (it has summary/note/ea_notes).
 4. TWO OF THE SEVEN WERE STUBS. professional-services and service-products returned { success:false, imported:0, errors:['... not yet implemented'] } — and ProductImport.tsx renders that as a completed import of zero rows.

FIX: one spec per product type in shared/catalog-import.ts (+ the Deno twin), bound to the real columns, and BOTH the downloadable template and the upload parser are generated from it. A column that does not exist cannot be offered; a header that is offered cannot be ignored. Header matching is case- and separator-insensitive, so 'Product Code', 'product_code' and 'productCode' all land — the three spellings the old importers each accepted a different subset of. The CSV parser is written out rather than taken from csv-parser, because Deno has no equivalent and both sides must parse identically (quoted fields, doubled quotes, embedded newlines, CRLF).

Seven Express handlers collapsed to one loop over the spec; seven MORE dead duplicates in routes-catalog-csv.ts were deleted (registerProductsCrudRoutes runs first, so those never ran — a second, differently-broken copy of the same feature), along with the six helpers that deletion orphaned. All seven edge functions gained an /import branch.

TWO BUGS I INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT:
 * The import branch initially named the id variable (modelId, accessoryId...) which in the three normalizePath functions is declared BELOW it — a temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError at runtime that esbuild does not flag. Now reads parts[0] directly, and a test asserts it.
 * An explicit UTF-8 BOM strip in the CSV parser turned out to be DEAD CODE: removing it changed nothing, because headers are trimmed and String.trim() removes U+FEFF. Removed rather than kept as a guard that guards nothing; the test now says what actually handles it.

TESTS: catalog-import-spec (32) and catalog-import-routing (41). The spec test checks every column, constant and dedupe key of all seven specs against getTableColumns, and round-trips each type's own template through its own parser — which is the check that would have caught defects 1-3 the day they were written. Mutation-tested four ways: moving the import branch after the create branch, pointing a spec at a phantom column, truncating the template's headers, and the BOM case (the one that revealed the dead code).

Suite 2843 -> 2916 passing. Typecheck 1007 -> 1003. ESLint 11698 -> 11656. Coverage baseline 173 -> 168 across 48 domains (5 fewer domains). Duplicate-route baseline 69 -> 62. Phantom columns hold at 234; check:routes and check:raw-fetch pass.

STILL NOT PORTED on this surface: /api/catalog/import-enhanced and /api/catalog/models/import, which are separate endpoints in routes-catalog-csv.ts with their own semantics.

PRICING ENDPOINTS PORTED + A MARGIN FORMULA CORRECTED (2026-08-20). /api/pricing/{calculate-rep-cost, approvals/pending, approval/:id, margin-report} were Express-only, so in production the rep-cost preview on the product pricing form, the approvals badge, the pending-approvals widget and the margin-trends widget all 404'd. All four now exist on the pricing edge function, with the role gate and the markup arithmetic in the twin pair shared/pricing-math.ts + _shared/pricing-math.ts.

THE ROLE MAP IS THE PART THAT NEEDED CARE. My first draft of the shared module INVENTED a role map (platform_admin, company_admin, sales_rep...) instead of copying the real one, which is hyphenated ('platform-admin', 'super-admin', 'read-only') and is compared against role names already stored. That would have dropped every manager to level 999 and hidden dealer cost from exactly the people these endpoints exist for. Caught by reading pricing-service.ts rather than by a test — so a test now pins the hyphenated keys and asserts the underscored spellings do NOT resolve.

A MARGIN FORMULA WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED, with the impact stated honestly. server/services/pricing-service.ts:calculateMarginPercentage computed (price - cost) / COST, which is MARKUP, and so does product-pricing-service.calculateMarginPercentage. shared/quote-math.ts — the canonical definition used by the quote builder, the proposals edge fn and both PDFs — computes (price - cost) / PRICE. On a $110 price against $100 cost that is 10% versus 9.09%, so a minimum-margin floor built on the old function passes prices that break the policy it states.

NOT A LIVE DEFECT, and I checked before claiming otherwise: validateMinimumMargin and product-pricing-service.validatePriceChange are BOTH imported and never invoked — every call site grepped, no callers anywhere. So this is a latent trap being removed rather than a number changing under anyone. calculateMarginPercentage now returns gross margin, calculateMarkupPercentage exposes the old quantity under the name that describes it (it is genuinely needed — rep cost is derived from a markup), and a test locks the margin function to lineMarginPct from quote-math so the two cannot drift again.

The margin REPORT deliberately does not compute anything: it reports total_margin_percentage as stored on enhanced_quote_pricing. A third margin formula is how the two that disagreed got here, and a test asserts the branch contains no margin maths.

ALSO FIXED — THE COVERAGE RATCHET'S OWN BLIND SPOT: check-edge-path-coverage stripped comments from the edge function but not from the CLIENT, so a path named in a comment counted as a live call. usePricingVisibility.ts explains in prose that /api/pricing/visibility used to route wrongly, and that comment alone put a phantom entry in the baseline. A phantom entry is worse than a missing one because a real gap can hide among them. Client files are stripped now; exactly one phantom disappeared, so the rest of the baseline was honest. Re-mutation-tested afterwards (renaming every occurrence of a segment still fails the check; renaming ONE of several occurrences does not, which is the documented limit of a presence test).

TESTS: pricing-math-parity (18) and pricing-edge-shape (18). Mutation-tested five ways — dropping the canSeeDealerCost gate from the approvals branch, tidying a hyphenated role key, reverting margin to markup, ignoring the category markup override, and letting a snake_case key reach the badge — each caught.

Suite 2916 -> 2952 passing. Coverage baseline 168 -> 163 across 47 domains. Typecheck holds at 1003; phantom columns hold at 234; check:routes, check:edge-paths, check:raw-fetch pass.
--- 2026-08-20 (loop round 37) ---

workflow-automation: CLOSED. supabase/functions/workflow-automation/ now
serves /dashboard from the CRMX-008 runtime tables, crmProxies forwards the
prefix in dev, and the domain is off missingEdge (5 -> 4). Aggregation lives
in _shared/workflow-dashboard.ts because PostgREST expresses no GROUP BY, SUM
or AVG; it is pure, and server/tests/unit/workflow-dashboard.test.ts asserts
21 cases against it (drift-verified). No server.ts override was needed - dir
name equals URL segment, per the EDGE-004 rule.

The Express handler was NOT the port source, and this is the part worth
carrying forward. server/routes-workflow-automation.ts is the unregistered
dead mock CLAUDE.md already names. The two handlers that DO register -
routes-workflow-mobile.ts:360 and routes-sample-data.ts:1801 - return
hardcoded figures identical for every tenant. Neither consuming page has a
`|| mock` fallback, so porting that would have put fabricated numbers on a
production dashboard where the 404 at least showed nothing. Fields the schema
cannot support (time saved, cost savings, workflow priority, template rating,
per-rule execution history) return zero and are listed in an `unbacked` array
on the response.

One crash to know about: WorkflowAutomation.tsx calls status.toLowerCase()
and priority.toLowerCase() unguarded, and `workflows` has no priority column.
The response sends priority: 'unset', which falls through getPriorityColor to
its neutral default rather than throwing on undefined.

erp-integration: NOT a port. server/routes-erp-integration.ts is 740 lines
with ZERO database calls and 48 hardcoded date literals - it imports db and
the drizzle operators and never uses them. It invents 18 integrations, a
98.7% sync rate, an SAP Business One instance and 45,672 records processed,
per tenant. Unlike the other two mocks this one COULD be backed by real data:
system_integrations, integration_metrics, integration_api_logs and
integration_setup_logs all exist, and the integrations edge fn already reads
platform_integrations / integration_sync_logs / integration_webhooks. That is
a build against real tables, not a port, so it is split out as PROD-014a.


[DONE 2026-08-29] All four domains resolved, but only ONE of them by writing an edge function, and the reasons matter. white-label and workflow-automation had already been ported in earlier rounds (fn + proxy entry both present). security-compliance IS DEAD, not missing: its consumer SecurityComplianceManagement.tsx no longer exists (only client/src/pages/_archived/SecurityCompliance.tsx.backup), nothing in client/src calls /api/security-compliance, server/routes-security-compliance.ts is UNREGISTERED (its only remaining reference is a filename string in fix-data-consistency.ts), and the domain was already off docs/route-ownership-baseline.json. Building an edge function for a page that does not exist would be inventing work, so the AC is recorded as satisfied by the domain being retired rather than served. NOTE FOR LATER: routes-security-compliance.ts is 597 lines of REAL queries (audit_logs, gdpr_requests, security_sessions, compliance_settings) - unlike the ERP fixture it is not junk, just unwired. Deleting it is a separate call; it is left in place deliberately.

erp-integration was the real work, and it was NOT a port. THE EXPRESS HANDLER WAS A 670-LINE FIXTURE: "SAP Business One", 18 integrations, 16 active, 98.7% sync success, 99.94% uptime, 234ms latency, 2.4M data points, plus data-quality scores for accuracy, completeness, consistency and timeliness. It existed TWICE - the LIVE copy in routes-sample-data.ts (registered via routes-registry:340) and a byte-similar UNREGISTERED duplicate in server/routes-erp-integration.ts (740 lines, referenced by nothing). That makes /api/erp-integration/dashboard the AUDIT-019 class on the server side, and PROD-011 already ruled that porting a mock handler is the wrong fix. Both copies are deleted.

What replaced it: supabase/functions/erp-integration/ GET /dashboard over the REAL tables system_integrations and integration_metrics (both in shared/schema.ts:5749/5767), filtered by tenant_id, normalizePath-routed, plus the /api/erp-integration proxy entry so dev matches prod. THREE DECISIONS WORTH KEEPING. (1) NULL IS NOT ZERO: successRate and averageLatencyMs return null when no metrics rows fall in the 30-day window, because a 0% success rate reads as a total outage while "no data" reads as no data; the page renders them as "No traffic" / "No data". (2) LATENCY IS WEIGHTED BY CALL COUNT, not a mean of the per-period means - averaging avg_latency_ms across periods would weight a quiet hour the same as a busy one. (3) The metrics query is SKIPPED ENTIRELY when the tenant has no integrations, because PostgREST would otherwise be handed integration_id=in.() which is a syntax error, not an empty set.

ERPIntegration.tsx went 1348 -> 270 lines. It read a deep invented shape - businessProcessAutomation.workflowOrchestration, dataSynchronization.conflictResolution.resolutionRules, dataQuality.{accuracy,completeness,consistency,timeliness}, a field-mapping tab and a per-system authentication tab. NO TABLE ANYWHERE IN THE REPO BACKS ANY OF IT, so those four tabs are deleted rather than ported, and the page states what it does not show. Only integrationOverview and the systems list survived, because only they had columns. Verified: tsc holds at 415, 176 files / 3768 tests pass, build succeeds, eslint 10605 -> 10534 (-71, baseline tightened), route-ownership missingEdge 3 -> 2 (only business-process and incident-response remain, both PROD-010/011), and check:nav / orphans / query-states / edge-paths / proxy-overrides / edge-coverage / no-mocks / fabricated / phantom-cols / phantom-tables / a11y-names / shadowed-express / unwrapped-response / no-static-posture all pass.

userStories.title: Build the ERP integration dashboard from real integration tables
userStories.description: As an admin, I need /api/erp-integration/dashboard to report this tenant's actual integrations, sync outcomes and error rates, because the only handler that exists today invents all of them.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace, do not port: server/routes-erp-integration.ts is 740 lines with zero database calls and 48 hardcoded date literals, returning 18 integrations, a 98.7% sync rate, an SAP Business One instance and 45,672 records processed for every tenant

Derive the dashboard from the tables that exist: system_integrations, integration_metrics, integration_api_logs, integration_setup_logs, and the platform_integrations / integration_sync_logs / integration_webhooks the integrations edge fn already reads

Decide first whether ERPIntegration.tsx should keep its own prefix or fold into the existing integrations edge function, which already serves /dashboard for the integration hub (EDGE-005f). A second dashboard over overlapping tables is the thing to avoid

Every field ERPIntegration.tsx reads is either backed by a real column or returns a zero named in an `unbacked` array on the response - the page has no `|| mock` fallback, so a wrong shape renders as fact

Aggregations go in a pure module under supabase/functions/_shared/ with vitest coverage, because PostgREST expresses no GROUP BY, SUM or AVG (see _shared/workflow-dashboard.ts from PROD-014 for the pattern)
erp-integration comes off missingEdge in docs/route-ownership-baseline.json; check:routes, check:edge-paths, check:phantom-cols and check:proxy-overrides all still pass
userStories.notes:
Split out of PROD-014 on 2026-08-20 during the loop pass that closed workflow-automation. Kept separate because it is a build against real tables rather than the port PROD-014 describes, and because the fold-into-integrations question is a design decision someone should make deliberately. The sibling mocks found in the same sweep - business-process (PROD-010) and incident-response (PROD-011) - have no backing tables at all and stay 404 pending a product decision; this one is the only one of the three with real data behind it.

[DONE 2026-08-29] Every AC met. AC1 replace-not-port: BOTH fixture copies deleted - the live one in routes-sample-data.ts (registered via routes-registry:340, 232 lines) and the unregistered 740-line duplicate server/routes-erp-integration.ts this story names. The duplicate was referenced by nothing but a filename string in fix-data-consistency.ts. AC2 real tables: system_integrations + integration_metrics. integration_api_logs and integration_setup_logs are DELIBERATELY NOT READ and the edge fn header says why - api_logs is per-call debug detail that integration_metrics already aggregates and would fetch an unbounded row set for a dashboard, setup_logs is onboarding history, a different question. AC3 THE PREFIX DECISION, made deliberately: keep /api/erp-integration separate, do NOT fold into the integrations fn. They read DIFFERENT TABLES - integrations serves the hub from platform_integrations / integration_sync_logs / integration_webhooks (the platform connector catalogue), this serves system_integrations / integration_metrics (the per-tenant registry of connected business systems and their API traffic). The overlap the AC warns about turns out to be in the naming, not the data; folding them would put two unrelated row sets behind one /dashboard and force callers to know which half they wanted. AC4: unbacked fields are NAMED on every response in an `unbacked` array (businessProcessAutomation, dataSynchronization.conflictResolution, dataSynchronization.dataQuality, fieldMapping, systemAuthentication) and the page RENDERS that list, so the gap is visible rather than reading as nothing-to-report. The page has no || mock fallback and never did, which is exactly why a wrong shape would have rendered as fact. AC5: all aggregation is in supabase/functions/_shared/erp-integration-dashboard.ts, pure, following the _shared/workflow-dashboard.ts pattern, with 10 vitest cases in server/tests/unit/erp-integration-dashboard.test.ts. The edge fn is 140 lines and does nothing but fetch and delegate. AC6: erp-integration off missingEdge (3 -> 2, leaving business-process and incident-response); check:routes, check:edge-paths, check:phantom-cols, check:proxy-overrides all pass.

THREE THINGS THE TESTS PIN, each a way this could have gone quietly wrong. (1) NULL IS NOT ZERO - successRate and averageLatencyMs are null with no metrics in the window, because a 0% success rate reads as a total outage while "no data" reads as no data; the page shows "No traffic" / "No data". (2) LATENCY IS WEIGHTED BY CALL COUNT. avg_latency_ms is a per-period average, so averaging the averages weights a quiet hour the same as a busy one: one call at 1000ms plus 999 calls at 10ms is 11ms weighted and 505ms unweighted. MUTATION-TESTED - swapping to a mean of means fails that case with "expected 505 to be 11". A period carrying zero calls contributes nothing whatever its stored latency. (3) METRICS FOR A DELETED INTEGRATION ARE EXCLUDED from the tenant roll-up - rows outlive the system they measured, and counting them reports traffic for a connector the tenant removed. Also tolerates numeric STRINGS, which is what PostgREST returns for a bigint column. Verified: tsc holds at 415, 177 files / 3778 tests pass, build succeeds, eslint 10534 (new files clean).

userStories.title: Resolve the canonical-table contradiction: production CRM runs on `companies`, not `business_records`
userStories.description: As an architect, I need one decided direction of travel for the account model, because docs/crm-canonical-model.md declares `business_records` canonical and `companies` deprecated, while the deployed edge functions do the exact opposite — they read and write `companies` and treat `business_records` as the legacy fallback. Until this is settled, every downstream CRM story risks being built against the wrong table.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm the finding in a running environment before deciding anything: supabase/functions/business-records/index.ts lists FROM `companies`, creates INTO `companies`, maps rows through mapCompanyToBusinessRecord(), and its own comment on the by-id branch reads 'Fallback: try business_records table for unmigrated records'. Express server/routes-business-records.ts meanwhile queries the real `businessRecords` table. Both are reachable: edge-function-proxy.ts maps '/api/business-records' -> the business-records edge fn.

Quantify the split per tenant: row counts in `companies` vs `business_records`, how many rows exist in only one, and whether any record ids appear in both. This determines whether the tables are a fork or a completed migration.

Record the dev/prod divergence explicitly: in dev Express serves the canonical table, in prod the edge fn serves `companies`, so the SAME page shows different data depending on environment. This is the CLAUDE.md 'both-divergent' class and must be stated in the decision.

Pick ONE canonical account table and write the decision into docs/crm-canonical-model.md, superseding the CRMX-002 ruling if the evidence goes the other way. Do not leave the doc and the runtime disagreeing.
Re-scope COP-E06 to match the chosen direction — it currently assumes folding `companies` INTO `business_records`, which is backwards if production has already migrated the other way.
State the blast radius for the consuming pages before any migration: LeadsPage, Contacts.tsx, and CustomersPage all read /api/companies, while CrmLeadsPage reads /api/business-records.
userStories.notes: [PHASE 0 / BLOCKER] Found 2026-08-11 while implementing COP-M01; not visible in the original audit, which read the Express routes and the Drizzle schema but not the deployed edge functions. This BLOCKS COP-M01 (nav repoint), COP-M03 (lifecycle views), COP-E03 (retiring the legacy index pages) and re-scopes COP-E06 / CRMX-007. Nothing that moves account data should ship until this is decided. Evidence is static (file reads); acceptance criterion 1 requires confirming against a real deployment before acting. [RESOLVED BY EVIDENCE 2026-08-11 — the DIRECTION is settled; what remains is a data migration, not an architecture decision. Written up as an addendum in docs/crm-canonical-model.md. I originally framed this as 'production migrated the other way, so the canonical choice is unsettled'. The dates disprove that. mapCompanyToBusinessRecord() and scripts/migrate-business-records-to-companies.ts both date to 2026-06-26 (the business_records -> companies direction). CRMX-002 — the canonical doc AND the @deprecated banner on `companies` — landed 2026-07-14 and reversed it. The edge function's `companies` binding therefore PREDATES the decision by ~3 weeks and was simply never updated; CRMX-007, the implementation, was never started. So `business_records` stands as canonical: the most recent authority says so and every artefact contradicting it is older than it. WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINS (needs DB access, no decision required): (1) repoint the business-records edge fn at business_records and retire mapCompanyToBusinessRecord — until then Express reads business_records in dev while the edge fn reads companies in prod, and THAT dev/prod split is the real thing blocking COP-M01, not any ambiguity about which table wins; (2) migrate the rows (CRMX-007 / COP-E06) — count both tables per tenant, find rows in only one, check for id overlap; (3) ORDER MATTERS — repointing the edge fn before migrating rows would hide records that currently live only in `companies`.]

userStories.title: Repoint the sidebar at the CrmIndexShell pages for leads, contacts, and companies
userStories.description: As a sales rep, I need the CRM list pages to have saved views, a board/table toggle, inline editing, and bulk operations, because those were already built in CRM-001..010 but the sidebar still points at the older hand-rolled pages so nobody can reach them.
acceptanceCriteria: RoleAwareCollapsibleSidebar.tsx 'Sales Hub' children point Leads at /crm/leads (CrmLeadsPage), Contacts at /crm/contacts (CrmContactsPage), and Companies/Customers at /crm/companies (CrmCompaniesPage) — replacing /leads-management (LeadsPage), /contacts (Contacts.tsx), and /customers (CustomersPage).

Before switching, confirm each shell page has parity on the capabilities the legacy page provided (create dialog, CSV export, the filters reps actually use); file any true parity gap as a follow-up rather than silently dropping it.

Each shell page renders saved-view tabs, the table/board toggle where the object supports a board, advanced filters, the column picker, bulk selection, and inline cell editing — i.e. the CrmIndexShell feature set is live for all four object types, not just deals.
matchPatterns on the Sales Hub nav entry still highlight the hub for every legacy path so deep links keep the correct section expanded.
Legacy pages are left routed (not deleted) in this story — COP-E03 retires them once parity is confirmed in a running environment.
npm run check && npm run lint pass.
userStories.notes:
[PHASE 0 / NAV] Source: docs/crm-copier-overhaul.md (copier CRM overhaul audit, 2026-08-10), grounded in a direct read of the CRM client/server/schema trees rather than the docs. Highest ratio of impact to effort in the whole report: a one-line-per-object nav change that instantly upgrades three object types. Audit evidence: CrmLeadsPage (261 lines) / CrmContactsPage (176) / CrmCompaniesPage (174) are routed under /crm/* but absent from the sidebar, while nav points at LeadsPage (661), Contacts.tsx (1959), CustomersPage (877). Only deals reaches the shell, via /opportunities. [BLOCKED 2026-08-11 — investigated while starting this story. The repoint is NOT a one-line nav change; four defects gate it. (1) PARITY: the shell had no bulk operations, no CSV export, and hardcoded View/Edit row actions, while the legacy pages have convert / deactivate / assign-owner / delete + export. CLOSED by commit 'feat(crm): add row actions, bulk operations, and CSV export to the CRM shell'.
