userStories.title: Standardize stage semantics on pipelineStages and remove remaining legacy dealStages reads
userStories.description: As an admin, I need one stage model, because CRMX-005 bound the board to pipelineStages via a legacy_stage_id map but other surfaces (forecasting, reports, automations, the API) may still read deal_stages, leaving two sources of truth for what a stage means.
acceptanceCriteria: Inventory every read of deal_stages/dealStages across client, server, and edge functions, and record the result in the story.

Every surface that needs stage config (name, order, probability, forecast weighting, SLA, closing/won flags) reads pipelineStages; deal_stages survives only as the identity map CRMX-005 established, if at all.
Forecast math uses per-stage defaultProbability/weightedValue/includeInForecast rather than the free-text deals.probability column.
Any remaining writer of deal_stages is either removed or documented as the sync-staging exception with a comment pointing at docs/crm-canonical-model.md.
Existing deals do not orphan: verify stage resolution for every deal in a seeded tenant before and after.
npm run check && npm run lint pass.
userStories.notes:
[PHASE 1 / ARCH] Source: docs/crm-copier-overhaul.md (copier CRM overhaul audit, 2026-08-10), grounded in a direct read of the CRM client/server/schema trees rather than the docs. Finishes what CRMX-005 started. Blocks COP-I06 (forecast accuracy), which needs one authoritative stage weighting. [AC1 INVENTORY DONE 2026-08-11; REST BLOCKED ON DB ACCESS. Full inventory of deal_stages/dealStages references (count, file): 28 server/storage.ts; 9 shared/schema.ts; 8 supabase/functions/pipeline-config/index.ts; 5 supabase/functions/pipeline/index.ts; 5 server/routes-deals-management.ts; 3 supabase/functions/proposals/index.ts; 3 supabase/functions/opportunities/index.ts; 3 server/routes/admin-seed-routes.ts; 2 supabase/functions/reports/handlers/frontend-stubs.ts; 2 shared/pipeline-configuration-schema.ts; 2 server/seeds/seed-all-demo-data.ts; 2 client/src/components/crm/EnhancedPipelineBoard.tsx (comments only); 1 supabase/functions/reports/handlers/second-tier.ts; 1 server/routes-sales-forecasting.ts. Plus GET/POST /api/deal-stages served from server/routes-workflow-mobile.ts:763 and consumed by client/src/components/leads/LeadDeals.tsx:156. ALREADY SATISFIED — AC3 is largely done: routes-sales-forecasting.ts already LEFT JOINs pipeline_stages via legacy_stage_id and reads ps.default_probability + ps.include_in_forecast, with the deal's own probability as an override (deal.probability ?? stage_probability ?? 50). Judgement call for the implementer: that deal-level override is arguably CORRECT (a rep adjusting one deal should win) and I did not strip it. SANCTIONED USE — pipeline-config/index.ts is the CRMX-005 identity mirror and should KEEP reading deal_stages. WHY THE REST IS BLOCKED: AC5 requires verifying stage resolution for every deal in a seeded tenant before and after, and this container has NO .env and CANNOT reach the DB (209.145.59.219:5433 refused). Per CRMX-005 deals.stage_id is keyed on the LEGACY deal_stages.id, with pipeline_stages.legacy_stage_id as the map — so repointing any writer to the pipeline_stages id space without that verification ORPHANS deals. That risk applies even to the seemingly-trivial LeadDeals.tsx fix, because it feeds a stage picker that writes back. Do this story in an environment with DB access.] | 2026-08-26: UNBLOCKED. The blocker was 'no DB access'; a scratch PostgreSQL 16 built from this repo's own migrations is enough, and standing one up turned AC5 from a promise into a measurement. THREE DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED, all confirmed against that database rather than read: (1) pipeline_templates.pipeline_type is NOT NULL with no default, and the LAZY BOOTSTRAP in supabase/functions/pipeline-config/index.ts omitted it. The insert always failed, 'created' came back null, and ensureTemplate returned { template: null, stages: [] } - so ANY tenant without a template got an empty pipeline board forever. That is every freshly seeded tenant, because the demo seeder created deal_stages and no template at all. Reproduced by running the handler's exact insert: 'null value in column pipeline_type violates not-null constraint'. Fixed with pipeline_type: 'new_business' (there is no 'sales' member; the enum is new_business|renewals|expansions|upsell|cross_sell|custom). (2) The explicit POST /templates wrote stage_type and allowed_transitions, NEITHER of which is a column on pipeline_stages. PostgREST answered 42703, so every template create through the UI returned 'Template saved but stage insert failed' and left an ORPHAN template. Confirmed: 'column stage_type of relation pipeline_stages does not exist'. stageType now maps onto the real booleans (is_final_stage/is_closed_won/is_closed_lost/is_active) via supabase/functions/_shared/pipeline-stage-type.ts; allowedTransitions is DROPPED, because it has no column and no reader anywhere in the tree - inventing one to store what nothing reads is how this drift started. (3) The read paths returned raw rows, so PipelineConfiguration.tsx's Stage Type select read undefined every time; stageType is now derived on read, and the round trip is locked by a unit test. AC5 MEASURED, BEFORE AND AFTER, on a database built from the migrations and seeded by npm run seed:demo. BEFORE: 3 deals resolving to NO canonical stage, 6 legacy stages with no mirror, 0 pipeline_stages rows. AFTER: 6 canonical stages, every deal resolving to exactly one, zero ambiguous. The seeder now mirrors deal_stages into pipeline_templates + pipeline_stages keyed by legacy_stage_id, so a demo tenant is in the state the canonical model assumes instead of half of it. New scripts/check-stage-resolution.mjs (npm run check:stage-resolution) makes that verification repeatable rather than a one-off; it exits 2 rather than 0 when it cannot connect, so 'did not run' is never mistaken for 'passed', and both failure modes were mutation-tested by orphaning a deal and by dropping a mirror. SEPARATE SEEDER DEFECT FOUND, NOT FIXED: generateId() produces tenant-independent ids ('stage-demo-001'), and every insert is onConflictDoNothing, so seeding a SECOND tenant into the same database silently writes NOTHING for any table with fixed demo ids - it reports success and creates nothing. That cost a verification round before I noticed. It needs its own story. STILL OPEN on this one: the AC2 sweep of the remaining deal_stages readers (storage.ts 28, routes-deals-management.ts 5, opportunities/proposals/reports edge fns) and the GET/POST /api/deal-stages picker in routes-workflow-mobile.ts that LeadDeals.tsx writes back through. Those are now DOABLE - check:stage-resolution is the before/after gate the earlier note said was missing - but each is a live write path and belongs in a pass that can run the check between every step. | 2026-08-26 (part 2): AC4 CLOSED and AC2 done for the picker, each verified by calling the real storage methods against the scratch database rather than by reading. THE GAP AC4 NAMES, made concrete: POST /api/deal-stages and POST /api/deal-stages/initialize both write deal_stages through storage.createDealStage and created NO canonical mirror, so every stage an admin added opened a hole in the CRMX-005 bridge. Demonstrated the cost end to end: inserted an unmirrored legacy stage (check:stage-resolution reported 'Active legacy stages with no canonical mirror'), moved a real deal into it, and the same check then reported the deal resolving to NO canonical stage - it would simply stop appearing on any surface bound to pipeline_stages, with no error anywhere. FIX: server/lib/pipeline-stage-mirror.ts, one place both writers call. mirrorLegacyStage() creates or refreshes the pipeline_stages row keyed by legacy_stage_id, creating the tenant's default template if it has none (with pipeline_type set - the omission that made the edge function's own bootstrap unable to succeed). It NEVER throws: an unmirrored stage is recoverable by re-running the write, a 500 in the middle of stage admin is not. Confirmed live - storage.createDealStage('Legal Review') produced the mirror, and storage.updateDealStageById renaming it to 'Legal & Security Review' propagated to name AND display_name AND colour. canonicalFieldsFor() derives the probability deal_stages cannot carry (100 won / 0 lost / neutral 50), pinned by 8 unit tests including the won-without-closing combination the legacy table allows. AC2 for the picker: getDealStages now LEFT JOINs pipeline_stages on legacy_stage_id and returns canonical display_name, colour, default_probability and include_in_forecast. The id STAYS the legacy deal_stages.id, deliberately - LeadDeals.tsx writes stage.id straight into POST /api/deals and the deals edge function's resolveStageId looks it up in the legacy space, so returning a pipeline_stages.id here is precisely the repoint COP-M07 warns orphans deals. Verified BOTH directions: with a mirror, the picker returns legacy ids carrying canonical config; with an unmirrored legacy stage, name and colour still render from the legacy row and defaultProbability comes back NULL rather than a fabricated 50, so the gap is visible instead of papered over. STILL OPEN: the two leftJoin(dealStages) reads in storage.ts that resolve a deal's stageName/stageColor for the list and detail (they work, but read the legacy row rather than the canonical mirror), routes-deals-management.ts, and the opportunities/proposals/reports edge functions. None of them writes, so none can orphan a deal - they are display consistency, not correctness, which is why they are last. 153 test files / 3416 tests pass; tsc holds at 506; check:stage-resolution, check:chained-where, check:phantom-cols, check:spread-insert-keys and check:migrations all green. | 2026-08-26 (part 3): AC1 inventory RE-RUN and reconciled, AC2 finished where it changes an answer, AC4 documented. THE INVENTORY HAS MOVED since 2026-08-11: server/routes-deals-management.ts is GONE (deleted under PROD-008b), so 5 of the listed references no longer exist. What is left splits three ways. (a) SWITCHED TO CANONICAL: the reports pipeline-funnel now takes its stage LIST from pipeline_stages (display_name, order, is_active) and buckets deals by the legacy id through legacy_stage_id, falling back to deal_stages for a tenant whose stages predate the mirror. Bucketing extracted to supabase/functions/_shared/pipeline-funnel.ts with 9 tests. Two behaviour fixes came with it: stages are ordered by the canonical 'order' rather than trusting arrival order, and an INACTIVE stage is dropped ONLY when it holds no deals - dropping it outright would stop the funnel counts adding up to the pipeline, and deals parked in a retired stage are still real money. Verified the join against real seeded data: all 7 canonical stages carry their legacy id and the 3 deals bucket into Qualification/Proposal/Negotiation at 28k/45k/85k. (b) SANCTIONED, now commented in place rather than left to be re-litigated: the four stage-ID resolvers in supabase/functions/proposals/index.ts resolve an id that is then WRITTEN to deals.stage_id, so they MUST read the legacy space - returning a pipeline_stages.id there is precisely the repoint this story warns about. Same for _shared/deal-stage.ts (already documented) and pipeline-config's mirror source. (c) DELIBERATELY NOT SWITCHED, with the reason recorded at the call site: supabase/functions/opportunities/index.ts embeds deal_stages through a real FK. PostgREST can only embed across a declared FOREIGN KEY and legacy_stage_id is not one, so going canonical means a second query plus an in-memory join. That is worth doing when it changes an answer and today it does not - the mirror COPIES name and colour from the legacy row, so both tables say the same thing. Doing it for the checkbox would be churn on a working list endpoint. KNOWN LIMITATION, stated because it decides when (c) stops being true: the mirror is ONE-WAY, legacy -> canonical. An edit made on the canonical side (pipeline-config PUT /stages/:id renaming a stage) is not durable - the next write to the legacy stage overwrites it. That is acceptable while deal_stages is the only stage-admin surface, and it is the thing to fix first if canonical stages ever become independently editable. 154 test files / 3425 tests pass; tsc holds at 506; check:stage-resolution, check:edge-paths and check:phantom-cols green. | 2026-08-26 (part 4): AC3 CLOSED, and it was a live defect rather than the bookkeeping item the earlier note implied. STALE NOTE CORRECTED FIRST: the 2026-08-11 entry said 'routes-sales-forecasting.ts already LEFT JOINs pipeline_stages via legacy_stage_id and reads ps.default_probability + ps.include_in_forecast'. That file no longer does anything of the kind - PROD-008b moved the handler out to supabase/functions/pipeline-forecast/, which is where the canonical weighting actually lives. The substance survived the move; the file reference did not. THE DEFECT: the forecast read 'd.probability ?? stage.prob ?? 50'. deals.probability DEFAULTS TO 0, not null, so the ?? NEVER fell through - default_probability was fetched, mapped into stageByLegacyId, and then never used by anything. MEASURED on the seeded demo tenant: three open deals worth 45,000 + 85,000 + 28,000 = 158,000, every one at probability 0, every one in a stage configured at 50%. The weighted pipeline came out at ZERO. It now comes out at 79,000. FIX in supabase/functions/_shared/deal-probability.ts, one tested function: a CLOSED stage decides outright (won = 100, lost = 0, because a deal sitting in Closed Won is not 30% likely just because a stale field says so); otherwise the deal's own probability wins but ONLY when it is > 0; otherwise the stage default; otherwise the fallback. Values are clamped, so a nonsense 250 forecasts at 100 rather than 250%. 10 unit tests including the exact 158k -> 79k reproduction. THE AMBIGUITY IS STATED, NOT HIDDEN: with a default of 0 and no null, 'the rep said 0%' and 'nobody ever touched this' are the same stored value, and no backfill can recover the intent of existing rows. Reading 0 as unset is what makes stage weighting work at all; the alternative is making the column nullable, which fixes future rows and still cannot interpret the ones already there. That trade-off is written at the top of the module so the next reader does not have to rediscover it. FOUND AND NOT FIXED - the same class, a different surface: supabase/functions/opportunities-dashboard/index.ts:49 weights with '(o.probability || 0)' and joins no stage at all, so a deal at probability 0 contributes nothing there too. Fixing it means adding the stage join that function does not currently have, which is a bigger change than this story's AC3 and belongs with whatever owns that dashboard. Worth knowing the write side is already correct: pipeline-config's stage transition PATCHES deals.probability from the stage (100 won / 0 lost / default otherwise), so deals dragged across the board do carry a real number - it is deals created directly (the deals edge fn POST defaults to 10) and seeded ones (0) that relied on the broken read. 155 test files / 3435 tests pass; tsc holds at 506; check:phantom-cols and check:edge-paths green. | 2026-08-26 (part 5): the last two AC2 reads. storage.ts getDeals and getDeal resolved stageName/stageColor from the legacy row; both now LEFT JOIN pipeline_stages on legacy_stage_id and coalesce onto the legacy name and colour, so a stage predating the mirror still renders instead of going blank. Verified both directions by calling the storage methods against the seeded database: with a mirror they return the canonical display (Negotiation #EF4444, Qualification #8B5CF6, Proposal #F59E0B); after pointing a deal at a deliberately unmirrored legacy stage, getDeal returned 'Legacy Only Stage' / #FF00FF rather than nulls. WHERE THIS STORY STANDS. AC1 inventory: done and re-run, with the stale entries corrected. AC2: done for the picker, the reports funnel, and both deal reads, with ONE deliberate exception - opportunities/index.ts keeps its deal_stages FK embed. The reasoning got STRONGER this round, not weaker: the mirror is one-way (legacy -> canonical), so the legacy row is the authoritative value, and paying a second query plus an in-memory join to read a copy of it would be strictly worse. AC3: closed, and it was a live defect - the forecast never used its stage weighting. AC4: both writers mirror; the sanctioned identity-lookup reads are commented in place. AC5: verified before and after on a real database, and made repeatable as npm run check:stage-resolution. AC6 is the repo-wide typecheck/lint ratchet, not something this story can move. passes STAYS FALSE on one honest point: AC2 says 'every surface that needs stage config reads pipelineStages', and opportunities still does not. That is a judgement call rather than unfinished work - if the exception is accepted, this story is done.
CORRECTION 2026-08-29 - the deferred item in part 4 pointed at work that should not be done. That note said: "FOUND AND NOT FIXED - supabase/functions/opportunities-dashboard/index.ts:49 weights with (o.probability || 0) and joins no stage at all... Fixing it means adding the stage join that function does not currently have, which is a bigger change than this story's AC3 and belongs with whatever owns that dashboard." The probability observation is right and the prescription is wrong, for a reason the note could not have seen from that line: the function does not read `deals` at all. It reads `opportunities`, the table docs/crm-canonical-model.md marks deprecated for net-new work under CRMX-002, and it had no caller in any of the seven client trees. Adding a canonical stage join to it would have been careful work on a dead read model over a deprecated table.

It is deleted, together with opportunities-by-stage, which had the same three properties plus a phantom column - it embedded `owner:owner_id (id, full_name)` and users has first_name/last_name, no full_name, so the query would have answered 42703 the first time anything called it. The canonical replacements already exist and are live: supabase/functions/sales-pipeline/ serves /opportunities, /summary and /rep-metrics for SalesPipelineWorkflow, and supabase/functions/opportunities/ (which /api/opportunities/convert-to-deal reaches) already reads `deals`.

THE GENERAL POINT, worth more than the two files: a deferred fix inherits the assumption that the code is live. Neither of these was, and the note is what a later reader would have trusted. Check reachability at the moment you defer, not only at the moment you fix.

userStories.title: Rebuild the Deal record page — timeline, notes, tasks, quotes, equipment, next step
userStories.description: As a sales rep, I need the deal page to be where I actually work the deal, because DealDetail.tsx is 238 lines of read-only fields with no timeline, notes, tasks, quotes, email, next step, or stage advance — while Lead and Customer detail are 2,287 and 2,935 lines.
acceptanceCriteria: The deal record is built on the record-layout engine (server/routes-record-layout.ts, CRM-008) so its layout is configurable like the other object types.

A unified activity timeline shows notes, emails, calls, meetings, tasks, stage changes, and quote events in one chronological stream, sourced through the crm_associations layer (CRMX-006) and the single ActivityTimeline component from COP-E05.
Inline creation from the record: add a note, log an activity, create a task, all without leaving the page and all appearing immediately in the timeline.
Associated records are shown and navigable: contacts, the account, quotes/proposals, and (once COP-M05 lands) the equipment the deal places or replaces.
The header carries stage with one-click advance (writing deal_stage_history and firing the pipelineStages triggers), amount, close date, owner, probability, and an explicit Next Step field.
A right-hand panel is present and structured to receive the COP-B11 insights — rendering an honest empty state until then, never fabricated scores.
Every read is tenant-scoped; every write validated with Zod.
npm run check && npm run lint pass.
userStories.notes: [PHASE 1 / CORE] Source: docs/crm-copier-overhaul.md (copier CRM overhaul audit, 2026-08-10), grounded in a direct read of the CRM client/server/schema trees rather than the docs. The single most important screen in the product and the biggest single build in Phase 1. Depends on COP-E05 (one timeline) and COP-M07 (one stage model); COP-M05 and COP-B11 extend it later. [INPUT from COP-E05, 2026-08-11: the surviving components/ActivityTimeline.tsx is a container hardwired to `businessRecordId: string` and fetches its own data, so it CANNOT render a deal timeline as-is — generalize it to a polymorphic parent (parentType + parentId over crm_associations / crm_notes, per CRMX-006) before building the deal record on it. A presentational variant taking ActivityItem[] existed and was deleted as dead code; recover with `git show 9c30f93:client/src/components/ui/activity-timeline.tsx` if a container/presentational split is wanted. Also: the survivor has a console.log on every render (line 87) — drop it while you are in there.] [SUBSTANTIALLY DONE 2026-08-11, story stays open for two panels. Rebuilt DealDetail from a 238-line read-only field dump into a working record: header with amount / monthly value / close date / probability / owner / next step, a stage-advance Select and Mark won|lost, an Activity timeline, Notes, and a right column with primary contact + click-to-email/call, an Insights slot and Details. REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED: COP-E04 made /crm/deals/:id canonical, but this page matched only useRoute('/deals/:id') — so on the canonical URL params was null, dealId undefined, and the page rendered 'deal not found'. It now matches BOTH routes. BUG AVOIDED: /api/pipeline-config/deals/:id/move expects `toStageId` (the legacy deal_stages.id), NOT `stageId` — verified against how EnhancedPipelineBoard calls it; the wrong key silently 400s. Stage advance deliberately reuses that same endpoint so the record and the board drag fire identical history + automation. Verified every endpoint before building on it: /api/deals/:id/activities exists on Express (routes-workflow-mobile.ts:886) AND the deals edge fn; 'deal' is a valid CrmRecordType so NotesPanel needed no change; board.stages is the shape the board already reads. STILL OPEN: (1) Tasks panel — tasks have NO dealId column, they must attach via crm_associations, so it renders an honest stub rather than a fake list; (2) Equipment panel — stubbed, needs COP-M05 (blocked on COP-M00); (3) Quotes — proposals have no deal linkage either, same association work as tasks; (4) the record-layout engine (server/routes-record-layout.ts) is NOT yet driving this page's layout, so it is not user-configurable. Insights renders an honest empty state for COP-B11 — no fabricated score, per CRMX-001.]

userStories.title: Repair drizzle migration generation — meta snapshots are 22 behind the journal
userStories.description: As a developer, I need `npm run db:generate` to emit a migration containing only my change, because today it emits 151 statements of already-applied drift and numbers the file into a collision — so no story that needs a schema change can ship.
acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce first: `DATABASE_URL=<any> npm run db:generate` after any schema edit emits ~2,281 lines / ~151 statements and writes 0040_<name>.sql, which collides with the existing 0040_auto_orders.sql and fails `npm run check:migrations`.

Root cause is the snapshot set, not the journal: drizzle/migrations/meta holds only 15 snapshots (highest 0018_snapshot.json) against 40 journal entries (highest tag 0056_email_sequence_enrollments). drizzle-kit diffs the schema against the LATEST snapshot, so every change made after 0018 is invisible to the differ and gets re-emitted.
The journal itself is healthy — check:migrations passes on a clean tree, all 40 files are journaled, prefixes unique, idx contiguous. Do not 'fix' the journal.

Second defect to fix in the same pass: drizzle-kit names the new file from the journal LENGTH (0040) while the files on disk are numbered up to 0056, so a fresh generate always collides. Reconcile the two numbering schemes.
Rebuild or backfill the meta snapshots so a no-op `db:generate` (schema unchanged) produces an EMPTY migration. That is the pass/fail test.
Then verify the real case: add one nullable column and confirm the generated SQL contains only that column.
Do not hand-author migrations as the fix — CLAUDE.md forbids dropping a .sql into drizzle/migrations, and the journal guard exists to enforce it.
userStories.notes: [PHASE 1 / BLOCKER] Found 2026-08-11 while implementing COP-M04. BLOCKS every story that needs a schema change: COP-M04, COP-M05, and through them the whole Phase 3 copier wedge (COP-B04 Opportunity Radar, COP-B05 Fleet Assessment, COP-B06 installed-base quoting). Related to the SUPA-005 journal-integrity work, but distinct: that guard checks the JOURNAL, which is currently healthy — this is the SNAPSHOT set, which the guard does not check. Consider extending check-migration-journal.mjs to also assert snapshots == journal entries, so this cannot silently regress again. [DIAGNOSED + GUARDED 2026-08-11; RECONCILIATION NEEDS DB ACCESS. Full write-up: docs/COP-M00-migration-tooling.md. ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED: 15 snapshots (highest 0018) vs 40 journal entries; drizzle-kit diffs against the LAST entry's snapshot, finds none, and falls back to 0018. Missing idx 10-13 and 19-39. MY FIRST HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG and the correction matters: I assumed the 141-statement drift was already-applied noise, which would have made 'install a current-schema snapshot at idx 39' the fix. It is not. Analysis of the drift shows 107 TABLES IN shared/* THAT HAVE NO MIGRATION AT ALL (71 blog_*, 4 truck_*, plus renewal_*, voice_*, booking_*, chatbot_*, email_autopilot_*, qbr_*, machine_*, meter_*, daily_*, service_*, and 9 singletons including customer_churn_scores and equipment_failure_predictions) — almost certainly created by db:push straight against the DB. Absorbing them into a snapshot would make the drift PERMANENT AND INVISIBLE and leave any migration-built environment missing 107 tables. That trap is documented explicitly so the next person does not fall into it. ALSO IMPORTANT: the non-contiguous file numbering is DELIBERATE — SUPA-002 renumbered 21 orphans to 0036-0056 so their `when` sorts after everything applied (drizzle only applies when lastDbMigration.created_at < folderMillis). Do NOT tidy it; I nearly did. COMMITTED: check-migration-journal.mjs gained check (e) — every journal entry must have a snapshot — as a RATCHET at the known gap of 25 rather than a hard gate, since failing outright would break CI on a pre-existing condition. NOT COMMITTED: any schema or migration change; the generated drift file was inspected and discarded and drizzle/ is byte-identical. REMAINING WORK needs a DB: introspect which of the 107 exist, apply the 21 pending journaled migrations, generate ONE reconciliation migration renamed to 0057+ with idempotent DDL, baseline it, then prove a no-op generate emits an EMPTY migration and drop SNAPSHOT_GAP_BASELINE to 0.] | RESOLVED 2026-08-26. Every AC met and verified against a scratch PostgreSQL 16 cluster, not statically. (1) Reproduced first: db:generate emitted 2,306 lines / 445 statements as 0040_repro_probe.sql, colliding with 0040_auto_orders.sql. (2) Root cause confirmed as the snapshot set — 15 snapshots (highest 0018) against 40 journal entries; journal itself untouched. (3) Fix is the sanctioned Step 3 of docs/COP-M00-migration-tooling.md, NOT the trap: the drift was captured as a real migration, drizzle/migrations/0057_cop_m00_schema_reconciliation.sql (118 CREATE TABLE, 299 CREATE INDEX, 20 unique, 15 ADD COLUMN, 9 FKs, 2 enum types, 1 enum value, 1 SET DEFAULT — zero DROPs, zero type narrowing), so the 107 unmigrated tables now HAVE a migration instead of being absorbed into a snapshot. Every statement made idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS, plus DO-block duplicate_object guards for FKs and enum types). Generated via db:generate, renumbered 0040->0057 with the journal tag updated; nothing hand-authored. (4) Numbering collision fixed for good: db:generate is now node scripts/db-generate.mjs, which renumbers whatever drizzle-kit writes to (highest on-disk prefix + 1). The deliberately non-contiguous SUPA-002 numbering is preserved. (5) Guard split: check-migration-journal.mjs now HARD-fails when the LAST journal entry has no snapshot (the only one generate reads) and keeps the 25 mid-chain gaps as a ratchet; proven by moving meta/0040_snapshot.json aside. PASS/FAIL TESTS: no-op db:generate -> 'No schema changes, nothing to migrate'; one nullable column -> exactly 'ALTER TABLE crm_notes ADD COLUMN cop_m00_probe varchar;' (probe reverted). 0057 applied to a DB built from the other 40 migrations: 0 errors; applied a second time: 0 errors. NOT DONE (needs DB access): 0057 has not been applied to any live environment — runbook in the doc (backup, db:migrate:status, db:migrate). It is a no-op where the tables already exist.

userStories.title: Extend the deals table with the copier-dealer fields the sales motion needs
userStories.description: As a copier sales rep, I need the deal to carry the facts that decide a copier deal, because `deals` today is a generic B2B deal — no motion type, no forecast category, no incumbent vendor, no lease buyout exposure, no trade-in, no current print volume, no target CPC.
acceptanceCriteria: Add to `deals`: dealMotion (new_logo | fleet_refresh | lease_rollover | expansion | renewal | competitive_takeaway | service_only), forecastCategory (pipeline | best_case | commit | closed), incumbentVendor, leaseBuyoutExposure (decimal), tradeInValue (decimal), currentMonthlyVolumeBw + currentMonthlyVolumeColor (integer), targetCpcBlack + targetCpcColor (decimal 10,4 to match contracts), and replacesContractId.
Migration generated with npm run db:generate (journal entry included — never hand-drop a .sql), reviewed, and committed with the schema change.
CPC decimal precision matches contracts.blackRate/colorRate (10,4) so quote and contract math do not disagree.
The fields surface on the deal record (COP-B02), are filterable/columnable in the deals index, and are available to the pipeline board card config.
dealMotion and forecastCategory replace free-text usage of the existing dealType/probability columns where they overlap; the old columns are back-filled or explicitly kept with a documented reason.
Every new field is optional at the API layer so existing deals remain valid; Zod schemas updated.
npm run check && npm run lint pass.
userStories.notes: [PHASE 1 / SCHEMA] Source: docs/crm-copier-overhaul.md (copier CRM overhaul audit, 2026-08-10), grounded in a direct read of the CRM client/server/schema trees rather than the docs. Foundation for COP-B04/B05/B06/B10 and COP-I06. Raw material already exists elsewhere and should be reused, not reinvented: business_records.competitorName/mainCompetitors, leases.buyoutAmount + buyout type enums, contracts.blackRate/colorRate. [BLOCKED 2026-08-11 on COP-M00 — `npm run db:generate` is broken in this repo, so the migration this story requires cannot be produced the sanctioned way. Attempted and reverted. The schema edit itself is done and correct; paste it back once COP-M00 lands. COLUMNS TO ADD to `deals` (all nullable, so existing rows stay valid): deal_motion varchar(40) [new_logo|fleet_refresh|lease_rollover|expansion|renewal|competitive_takeaway|service_only]; forecast_category varchar(20) [pipeline|best_case|commit|closed]; incumbent_vendor varchar; lease_buyout_exposure numeric(12,2); trade_in_value numeric(12,2); current_monthly_volume_bw integer; current_monthly_volume_color integer; target_cpc_black numeric(10,4); target_cpc_color numeric(10,4); replaces_contract_id varchar. CPC precision 10,4 deliberately MATCHES contracts.black_rate/color_rate so quote and contract math cannot disagree by rounding. varchar not pgEnum so new motions need no enum migration. NOTE: forecast_category and trade_in_value already exist on OTHER tables (opportunities, lease_dispositions) — they are genuinely new on `deals`. Also observed: `deals.custom_fields` (CRMX-003/004) is in the Drizzle schema but has NO migration, so it is part of the same drift.] | UNBLOCKED AND IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-26, now that COP-M00 landed. The schema edit is back in shared/schema.ts (deals, after custom_fields) exactly as this note specified: all ten columns, all nullable. The migration came out of the sanctioned npm run db:generate as drizzle/migrations/0058_cop_m04_deal_copier_fields.sql - ten ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN lines and NOTHING else, which is the first real proof that the COP-M00 fix works on live work rather than on a probe. AC3 verified in a database, not by reading: target_cpc_black/color land as numeric(10,4) and contracts.black_rate is numeric(10,4) in the same cluster, and 0.0085 round-trips at four decimals. AC6 verified by parsing: insertDealSchema (createInsertSchema, so the nullable columns are optional automatically) accepts a deal with none of the ten AND one with all ten, including currentMonthlyVolumeColor: 0. AC5 DECIDED, NOT DEFERRED: dealType and probability are KEPT and nothing is back-filled, with the reason in the schema comment - dealType is free text with rows behind it and stays the generic label; probability stays the rep's percentage; forecastCategory is a judgement call (commit vs best case) that no probability threshold can derive; and guessing a motion for a historical deal would poison the very forecast history COP-I06 exists to measure. API LAYER: the deals edge function is the only writer (server/routes-deals.ts was deleted under PROD-008b), and its POST builds an explicit whitelist, so all ten were added there or a create would have dropped them silently - the exact Drizzle/PostgREST failure CLAUDE.md warns about. Used ?? not || because 0 is a real monthly volume. Also added to BULK_FIELD_MAP (covers PATCH and bulk-update) and to toDealResponse as camelCase aliases. LIST LAYER: added to DEAL_LIST_SPEC.sortFields in BOTH twins (server/lib/crm-list-query.ts and supabase/functions/_shared/crm-list-query.ts); crm-list-spec-columns.test.ts passes 23/23, which is what proves every new sort field is a real column keyed the way Drizzle keys it. Only dealMotion and forecastCategory became filterKeys, because they are the closed vocabularies - an equality filter on a currency or a page volume would be a control that never matches, and those want a range filter the list layer does not have. Wired .eq() for both in the handler. UI: DEAL_MOTION_OPTIONS/FORECAST_CATEGORY_OPTIONS exported once from crm-object-registry.ts and shared by the column renderer and the quick filter so a value cannot be spelled two ways; nine new columns added to dealsConfig.fields, deliberately NOT to defaultColumns (a rep working new logos should not carry a lease-buyout column by default); two quick filters added, and the filter key IS the query param the handler reads, verified end to end - CrmIndexShell -> activeFilters -> CrmDataTable params.set -> parseCrmListQuery filterKeys. The board honours them too: EnhancedPipelineBoard forwards activeFilters to the same endpoint. DealDetail.tsx gained a read-only Copier profile card that renders only when the deal carries at least one of the fields, so a generic B2B deal does not grow a card of empty rows; CPC renders at FOUR decimals deliberately, because the default currency format rounds 0.0085 to 0.01, a 17% error on the number the deal turns on. VERIFIED: 0058 applied to a scratch PostgreSQL 16 database and a full copier deal INSERTed and read back with every column name the edge function writes; tsc holds at 521; eslint on the touched TS files is unchanged from before the change; check:migrations, check:phantom-cols, check:dup-tables, check:nav all pass. NOT DONE, and the reason AC4 is only partly met: (a) the deal RECORD surface is read-only - the editable version belongs to COP-B02's rebuild; (b) the pipeline board CARD field config is BoardOptionsMenu.tsx, which takes config.fields (so the new fields reach it by construction) but is imported by nothing - it is an orphan component, so there is no live card-config UI to appear in; (c) deno check could not run, no deno binary in this container. Side note: deals.custom_fields, which this story flagged as schema-present but migration-absent, is covered by COP-M00's 0057.

userStories.title: Associate deals with installed-base equipment (the serials a deal places or replaces)
userStories.description: As a copier sales rep, I need a deal to know which machines it replaces and which it places, because today `deals` has no link to `equipment` at all — so the system cannot tell what fleet a deal is actually about.
acceptanceCriteria: Deal↔equipment links use the existing crm_associations layer (CRMX-006) with an explicit role on each link — 'replaces' vs 'places' — rather than a new bespoke join table.
'equipment' is added to CRM_ASSOCIABLE_TYPES and the API-layer validation that guards those values.
API: attach/detach equipment to a deal, and list a deal's associated equipment with the fields a rep needs (serial, model, manufacturer, install date, lease expiry, meter type, location).
The deal record (COP-B02) shows an Equipment section listing associated machines with their current meters and contract rates, and lets a rep attach from the account's installed base in one step.
Attaching equipment that carries a lease or contract populates the COP-M04 fields (leaseBuyoutExposure, replacesContractId, current volumes) rather than making the rep retype them.
All queries tenant-scoped; associations survive the account lifecycle (lead→customer) without re-linking.
npm run check && npm run lint pass.
userStories.notes: [PHASE 1 / SCHEMA] Source: docs/crm-copier-overhaul.md (copier CRM overhaul audit, 2026-08-10), grounded in a direct read of the CRM client/server/schema trees rather than the docs. This is the join that makes the whole Phase 3 copier wedge possible — COP-B04/B05/B06 all depend on it. Depends on COP-M04. [GATED 2026-08-11 (loop triage): blocked on COP-M00. Not started — recorded so the backlog reflects the real dependency rather than looking merely untouched.] | UNBLOCKED AND BUILT 2026-08-26, after COP-M00 and COP-M04. AC1: links are crm_associations rows with an explicit relation, no new table - so they survive the lead->customer lifecycle like every other association and needed no migration. AC2: 'equipment' added to CRM_ASSOCIABLE_TYPES, and DEAL_EQUIPMENT_RELATIONS = ['replaces','places'] added alongside it; 'related' (the column default) is REJECTED on a deal-equipment pair, because a link that does not say which way it points is useless to COP-B04. Enforced via a superRefine on insertCrmAssociationSchema for Express. THE REAL FIND HERE: the crm edge function accepted ANY STRING as sourceType/targetType - it only checked the four fields were present - while Express validated against CRM_ASSOCIABLE_TYPES with Zod. Production runs the edge function, so the validation lived entirely on the host that does not serve users. Added supabase/functions/_shared/crm-associations.ts (the Deno twin - the Node file imports drizzle-zod and cannot load in Deno) with associationCreateError(), wired into the crm fn's POST, and locked by server/tests/unit/crm-associations-parity.test.ts, which also asserts the edge validator and the Zod schema return the same verdict on every case. AC3: GET/POST /deals/:id/equipment and DELETE /deals/:id/equipment/:equipmentId in the deals edge function (/api/deals is proxied, so Express is bypassed on both hosts and there is one implementation, not two). GET joins the rep fields server-side in THREE queries total regardless of machine count - associations, equipment, then one meter_readings and one contracts query grouped in memory - rather than fanning out per serial, which is the shape COP-I01 exists to prevent. POST verifies BOTH ends belong to the tenant before writing, so a rep cannot attach an arbitrary serial by id. AC4: DealEquipmentPanel replaces the placeholder that literally said this was blocked on the migration tooling; rows are grouped by role and carry serial, model, manufacturer, location, install date, lease end, meter type, CURRENT monthly volumes derived from the meter history, and the contract's black/color CPC at four decimals. Attach is a dialog over the account's installed base (scoped by the deal's customerId, with search as the way in when the deal has no account yet). AC5 IMPLEMENTED, and the semantics are the interesting part: attaching a machine as 'replaces' fills lease_buyout_exposure (summed over leases whose jsonb equipment_ids CONTAINS the machine), replaces_contract_id (matched on contract_number = equipment.service_contract_number, and ONLY when exactly one machine points at exactly one contract - an ambiguous answer is left for the rep), and the two current volumes (annualised from the newest meter pair). It fills BLANKS ONLY and never overwrites a value a rep typed, it returns what it wrote so the toast can say so rather than letting fields change unannounced, and it never throws - a derivation failure must not fail an attach that already succeeded. The arithmetic is pure and separately tested in supabase/functions/_shared/installed-base.ts: null rather than 0 when the meters cannot answer (fewer than two readings, same-date readings, or a counter that went DOWN, which means a reset meter or a replaced board), because a zero reads as 'this machine prints nothing' and would price the deal wrongly. AC6: every query is scoped by tenant_id on BOTH the association and the machine. ALSO FIXED IN PASSING: Express GET /api/equipment ignored ?customerId= while the equipment edge function has honoured it all along, so an account-scoped picker would have shown the whole tenant's fleet in dev and the right fleet in production. VERIFIED against a scratch PostgreSQL 16 database, not by reading: a deal-equipment association inserted and joined back with every column the handler selects; the lease jsonb containment (@>) returning the buyout; the meter pair coming back newest-first; and the contract resolving by number. tsc holds at 506; 151 test files / 3400 tests pass; check:edge-paths, check:phantom-cols, check:migrations, check:dup-tables, check:chained-where, check:nav and check:identical-fallback all pass. NOT DONE: no deno binary in this container, so deno check could not run; and the panel lives on the CURRENT deal record - COP-B02's rebuild will re-home it.

userStories.title: Sales Workspace — the rep's "My Day" home screen
userStories.description: As a sales rep, I need one screen that tells me what to do today, because there is no work surface at all — SalesCommandCenter is a forecast analytics dashboard, so reps have to go hunting across pages to assemble their own day.
acceptanceCriteria: A new /crm/my-day workspace is the default landing page for sales roles, composed of cards: Overdue tasks, Due today, Stalled deals (no activity in N days / past stage SLA), Meetings needing follow-up, Quotes awaiting signature, and Suggested tasks (COP-B03).
Cards are user-customizable — show/hide and reorder — with the layout persisted per user.
Every card is actionable in place: complete a task, log an activity, open the record, or snooze — without navigating away.
Every number is derived from real tenant data with an honest empty state; no mock fallbacks (see COP-I07).
The workspace loads in under 1s at realistic data volumes and degrades gracefully card-by-card if one query is slow or fails.
Role-aware: managers additionally see team roll-up cards; the card set respects RBAC scope (view_own vs view_team).
npm run check && npm run lint pass.

userStories.title: Suggested Tasks engine — ranked next actions from real signals, auto-expiring when stale
userStories.description: As a sales rep, I need the system to tell me which accounts need attention today, because nothing surfaces the signals the database already holds — stalled deals, breached stage SLAs, expiring quotes, lease windows, meter anomalies, ticket spikes.
acceptanceCriteria: Suggestions are generated on the existing workflow runtime (workflow-execution-service.ts + workflow-runtime.ts) via dispatchWorkflowEvent — no new parallel scheduler.

Signal set at minimum: no activity on an open deal in N days; deal past its pipelineStages SLA; quote expiring within N days; lease/contract inside the COP-B04 window; meter volume materially over contracted tier; service ticket spike on a customer machine.
Each suggestion carries the record, the reason in plain language, the suggested action, and a score used for ranking.
Suggestions AUTO-EXPIRE when the underlying condition clears (the rep logged the activity, the quote was signed) — a stale suggestion must never linger.
Admins can enable/disable each suggestion type per tenant and set its threshold; the whole engine respects the workflow kill switch.
Suggestions render on the COP-B01 workspace and are dismissible with the dismissal recorded.
Generation is idempotent — re-running a sweep does not duplicate suggestions (reuse the dedupeKey pattern).
npm run check && npm run lint pass.
userStories.notes: [PHASE 2 / AUTOMATION] Source: docs/crm-copier-overhaul.md (copier CRM overhaul audit, 2026-08-10), grounded in a direct read of the CRM client/server/schema trees rather than the docs. HubSpot renamed Guided Actions to Suggested Tasks in 2026 specifically to add auto-expiry — copy that behaviour, it is the part that makes the feature trustworthy. The durable runtime already exists; this is a signal library plus ranking on top of it. [BLOCKED 2026-08-11 (loop triage): needs PERSISTENCE, so it is gated on COP-M00. Three of its own acceptance criteria require durable state — suggestions must AUTO-EXPIRE when the underlying condition clears, dismissals must be RECORDED, and generation must be IDEMPOTENT via a dedupeKey. None of that survives a computed-on-read implementation, so it needs at least one new table, which cannot be migrated until db:generate is repaired. The signal library itself is otherwise ready to build: the durable workflow runtime exists (workflow-execution-service.ts + dispatchWorkflowEvent), and COP-B11's shared/deal-score.ts already computes several of the required signals (activity recency, stage SLA breach, next step overdue, close date passed) as a pure function that a generator could reuse directly rather than reimplement.]

userStories.title: Finish 1:1 sales email — real OAuth, inbox sync, send, and open/click tracking
userStories.description: As a sales rep, I need to send and track individual emails from inside a record, because Email Autopilot generates real drafts but its OAuth, inbox fetch, send, and provider-draft calls are all stubbed — so the rep's most-used tool produces nothing, and sequences are a runtime with no output.
acceptanceCriteria: Real Gmail and Outlook OAuth with tokens stored in the shared credential vault (replacing the base64 obfuscation the route file flags as TODO(vault)) — never returned to the client, only *_set booleans.
Real inbox sync replaces the stubbed message list; real send replaces createProviderDraft()'s fake external id.
Open and click tracking recorded per message and attributed to the contact and deal.
Every sent and received message is logged to the unified activity timeline via crm_associations, so it appears on the deal (COP-B02), contact, and account.
buildVoiceFingerprint() derives from the rep's real sent mail rather than injected samples, or is removed if that is out of scope.
Sequences (CRMX-009) send through this path — verify an enrolled contact actually receives a real message.
Send is gated by an explicit permission and respects unsubscribe/suppression state; scopes requested are the minimum needed.
npm run check && npm run lint pass.

Supporting DB indexes exist for the actual filter/sort combinations the saved views use (tenant-scoped composite indexes).
A regression guard exists so the benchmark is re-run rather than trusted — document how to run it.

userStories.title: Keyboard-first CRM — command palette actions and list navigation
userStories.description: As a power user, I need to drive the CRM from the keyboard, because the command palette exists but only navigates, so every create, edit, and log action still costs a mouse trip.
acceptanceCriteria: The command palette gains ACTIONS as well as destinations: create deal/lead/contact/company/task/note, log activity, send email, and search-and-open a record by name, serial, or quote number.
The palette opens on the standard shortcut from every CRM screen and is reachable on all supported platforms.
j/k (or arrow) navigation moves the selection through list rows and board cards; Enter opens; Escape clears.
Single-key shortcuts on a record for the frequent actions (note, task, email, log call), with a discoverable shortcuts dialog listing them all.
Every shortcut is keyboard-accessible with a visible focus state and does not trap focus or fire while typing in an input.
Shortcuts respect RBAC — a palette action the user lacks permission for is not offered.
npm run check && npm run lint pass.

userStories.title: Installed-Base Opportunity Radar — turn equipment, contracts, and meters into ranked pipeline
userStories.description: As a copier sales rep, I need the system to hand me today's best opportunities out of our own installed base, because every lease expiry, contract end, meter overage, and service-cost spike is already a dated, quantified sales trigger sitting in the database — and today it drives no pipeline at all.
acceptanceCriteria: A scheduled scan over equipment, contracts, leases, meter_readings, and service history produces ranked "plays", each with: the account, the machines, the trigger, the date it becomes live, and an estimated dollar value.

Play types at minimum: lease expiring within a configurable window; service contract ending; volume materially over the contracted tier; machine past a service-cost/margin threshold; color-capable device with negligible color usage; device off-network or not reporting meters.
Each play one-clicks into a deal pre-populated with the COP-M04 fields and the COP-M05 equipment associations — the rep never retypes what the system knows.
Plays are ranked by value and urgency, scoped to the rep's territory/ownership (COP-B09) and RBAC scope, and surfaced on the COP-B01 workspace.
Windows and thresholds are per-tenant configurable; the scan runs on the existing workflow runtime and honours the kill switch.
Dismissing or converting a play records the outcome so play-to-deal and play-to-won conversion can be reported later.
The scan is idempotent — re-running does not duplicate plays for the same trigger.
Every query tenant-scoped; the scan is chunked so a large installed base does not block.
npm run check && npm run lint pass.

A proposed fleet is modelled against the same volumes, producing a side-by-side current-vs-proposed comparison with the delta stated in dollars per month and over the term.

The assessment attaches to the deal, appears on its timeline, and feeds COP-B06 so the quote inherits the modelled fleet.
Output is presentable to a customer — an exportable/printable summary, not just an internal screen.
Machines with missing meters or unknown rates are shown as explicit gaps, never silently defaulted to zero or a guessed rate.

userStories.title: Enforce cookie consent: gate Sentry Session Replay and all non-essential telemetry
userStories.description: As a visitor, when I decline non-essential cookies I need that choice to actually take effect, because today the consent banner records a decision that nothing reads: hasConsent() in client/src/lib/cookie-consent.ts:128 is never called anywhere in the codebase, while Sentry Session Replay initializes unconditionally at boot in client/src/main.tsx:24 and records 10% of all sessions plus 100% of error sessions before any consent is given.
acceptanceCriteria: Sentry Session Replay is NOT initialized until hasConsent('analytics') returns true; error reporting without replay may remain if it is justified as strictly necessary and that justification is written into the Cookie Policy.
Sentry replay starts on consent grant (listen for CONSENT_CHANGE_EVENT) and stops/flushes on consent withdrawal, without requiring a page reload.
Every other non-essential script, pixel, or SDK added anywhere in client/ is routed through hasConsent(); a repo-wide grep confirms no ungated non-essential telemetry remains.
Global Privacy Control is honored at runtime, not just in the stored record: a GPC signal suppresses analytics and marketing categories before any script loads.
A CI guard (script + npm script, wired like scripts/check-edge-paths) fails when a known telemetry SDK is initialized outside a consent gate, so the pattern cannot be reintroduced.
A unit test asserts hasConsent() default-denies for analytics/preferences/marketing when no record exists and when the stored record version is stale.
Sentry is named in Privacy Policy section 2, in the Cookie Policy category table, and in Subprocessors.tsx (this overlaps LEGAL-007; whichever story lands first satisfies it).

The Cookie Policy claim 'Non-essential cookies are not set until you agree to them' is true as shipped, verified by loading the marketing site with a clean profile and confirming no Sentry replay request fires before consent.
npm run check && npm run lint && npm run build pass.
userStories.notes: [LEGAL / P0] Highest-exposure finding of the compliance audit. A consent banner that records a choice and ignores it is worse than no banner: it documents that the obligation was known. This is the fact pattern behind the CIPA session-replay litigation wave (Cal. Penal Code 631/632, $5,000 statutory per violation) and EU ePrivacy/GDPR Art. 6(1)(a) enforcement. Evidence: hasConsent defined at client/src/lib/cookie-consent.ts:128, zero call sites (grep -rn hasConsent client/src excluding the lib itself returns nothing). Sentry.init at client/src/main.tsx:24 with replayIntegration, replaysSessionSampleRate 0.1, replaysOnErrorSampleRate 1.0. Banner IS mounted (client/src/App.tsx:1272) and the consent model itself (GPC handling, versioning, default-deny) is well built; only the enforcement layer is missing. Note the module's own header comment already states the requirement it violates. POLICY-COPY RULE (all LEGAL stories, decided 2026-08-17): drafting legal/policy text alongside the code IS in scope, but every changed user-facing legal string must be called out in the commit body under a FOR COUNSEL REVIEW heading so it is reviewed before deploy. IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-18. client/src/lib/telemetry.ts is now the single owner of the Sentry lifecycle; main.tsx calls initTelemetry(). Error capture starts at boot (declared strictly necessary in the Cookie Policy); BrowserTracing, Replay AND BrowserSession release-health all wait for hasConsent(analytics) and are attached via Sentry.addIntegration on CONSENT_CHANGE_EVENT, stopped on withdrawal without a reload. BrowserSession had to be filtered out of Sentry defaults because it pinged once per page load pre-consent (caught by the browser probe, not by reading the code). GPC made authoritative in hasConsent(): a live signal overrides a stored accept-all for analytics+marketing. Removed replit-dev-banner.js, a cross-origin script client/index.html loaded on every production page view, which a client/src-only scan could never have seen. Guard scripts/check-telemetry-consent.mjs (npm run check:telemetry, wired into ci.yml) enforces three rules and was proven to fail on each. 7 unit tests in client/src/lib/cookie-consent.test.ts. End-to-end proof scripts/verify-telemetry-consent.mjs (npm run verify:telemetry) drives the real production bundle in Chromium: 8/8 PASS, including 0 Sentry requests before consent and tracesSampleRate returning to 0 on withdrawal. Typecheck holds at baseline 1058, build passes.

userStories.notes: [LEGAL / P0] FTC Rule on the Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials, 16 CFR Part 465, effective October 2024. Civil penalty up to $53,088 per violation. If no real customers exist yet, deletion is the only compliant option and the sections should be replaced with product-capability content. DECIDED 2026-08-17 by Dj Pearson: DELETE both sections. Remove the testimonials block from Homepage.tsx and the three named case studies from CaseStudies.tsx, replacing them with product-capability content. Do NOT invent substitute quotes, companies, or metrics. Unsubstantiated aggregate stats (30-40%, 15-25%, 4-7 month payback, 4.8/5, 90%+) go with them unless a written basis exists. userStories.title: Actually delete uploaded objects from storage when a file is deleted
userStories.description: As a customer, when I delete a file I need the bytes gone, because the file-storage edge function deletes the database row and leaves the storage object orphaned forever: the removal call at supabase/functions/file-storage/index.ts:288 is commented out with a note saying 'In production, also delete from Supabase Storage'.
acceptanceCriteria: supabase/functions/file-storage/index.ts DELETE handler removes the storage object before (or transactionally with) the row delete, matching the correct implementation already present at supabase/functions/files/index.ts:220.

Storage removal failure does not silently succeed: the endpoint returns an error, or records a durable retry/tombstone that a sweeper drains. A dangling object must never be reported to the caller as a completed deletion.

Both file endpoints are audited for parity of delete semantics, and the divergence is resolved (one shared helper, or one endpoint deprecated) so behavior does not depend on which URL the client happens to call.

Every other edge function that uploads to storage (branding-profiles, blog-assets, qbr, meeting-transcription recordings) is audited for a matching delete path; each one either removes its objects on delete or is listed in the story notes as a follow-up with a reason.
A backfill script identifies storage objects with no owning row and reports counts per bucket. It reports by default and only purges behind an explicit flag.
An integration or edge test asserts that after DELETE, a subsequent fetch of the storage path 404s.
npm run check && npm run lint pass; deno check passes on every edge function touched.
userStories.notes: [LEGAL / P0] Directly contradicts the deletion right stated in Privacy Policy section 6.1 ('Delete or deactivate your account', 'Signed-in users can export their data and delete...'). Promising deletion and retaining the data is a straightforward FTC Section 5 deceptive-practice theory and a GDPR Art. 17 failure. Evidence: supabase/functions/file-storage/index.ts:277-301, storage removal commented out at line 288; correct sibling at supabase/functions/files/index.ts:207-225. Both write to the 'files' bucket. Note the edge path normalization rule in CLAUDE.md when touching either function. POLICY-COPY RULE (all LEGAL stories, decided 2026-08-17): drafting legal/policy text alongside the code IS in scope, but every changed user-facing legal string must be called out in the commit body under a FOR COUNSEL REVIEW heading so it is reviewed before deploy. IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-18. New shared helper supabase/functions/_shared/storage-delete.ts (removeStorageObjects + removeStoragePrefix) is the single seam; three functions were wrong in three different ways. (1) file-storage: removal was commented out. (2) files: called remove() but DISCARDED the result - supabase-js returns errors in {data,error} rather than throwing, so every storage failure returned "File deleted" with the object still there, which is worse than not calling it. (3) branding-profiles: hard-deleted the profile row and never touched the logos, AND every logo re-upload abandoned its predecessor because keys are minted with a fresh uuid and only the public URL is stored - fixed by listing the prefix, which is the only way to find keys nobody wrote down. Ordering rule applied everywhere: remove bytes FIRST, and refuse to drop the row if that fails, because while the row exists the object still has a reference and the delete is retryable; dropping the row first and then failing loses the only pointer to it. AUDIT of the remaining buckets, per the AC: blog-assets soft-deletes by design and deliberately keeps its object (documented in its own header) - LEFT AS IS because removing bytes would break the restore the soft delete exists for, and the content is marketing images, but note a soft-deleted asset stays publicly fetchable since that bucket is public; qbr and meeting-recordings have NO delete path at all - nothing to fix, listed here as follow-ups. Orphan reporter scripts/report-orphaned-storage-objects.ts (npm run storage:orphans) reports by default, needs --bucket AND --purge to remove anything, and REFUSES to purge when a reference table is missing (files and file_uploads are drift tables in no schema/migration, so their absence would make every object look orphaned). VERIFIED: 14 unit tests on the helper + 4 integration tests that drive the REAL handlers against a stateful fake bucket and assert the object is absent afterwards; proven to catch the original bug by reverting file-storage to the commented-out version (2 of 4 fail, then pass again on restore). tsc holds at 1058, lint 11654 (-262 vs baseline, +15 no-console warnings in the CLI reporter, matching the existing scripts/*.ts convention), build passes, check:edge-paths green. GAP TO KNOW: deno check did NOT run - deno is not installed here and the install is blocked by the agent proxy (403) - and tsconfig.json includes only client/shared/server, so supabase/functions is NOT covered by npm run check either. The edge changes are evidenced by the integration test actually importing and executing both handlers, not by a type check. Run deno check in CI. UNRELATED PRE-EXISTING FAILURE seen while running the suite: server/tests/unit/universal-search.test.ts has 2 failures (expects 6 queries, gets 7); confirmed present with this story stashed, so not caused here and not fixed here.

userStories.title: Extend GDPR erasure to storage objects, not just database rows
userStories.description: As a data subject exercising the right to erasure, I need my uploaded content deleted too, because server/services/gdpr-erasure-service.ts anonymizes database columns and never touches Supabase Storage, so documents, logos, attachments, meeting recordings, and QBR artifacts survive a completed erasure request intact.
acceptanceCriteria: The erasure service enumerates and deletes (or irreversibly anonymizes) storage objects belonging to the subject across every bucket in use: files, branding-assets, meeting-recordings, qbr artifacts, blog-assets.

Objects that must be retained under an Art. 17(3) exemption are retained deliberately, with the exemption named in the erasure report notes, in the same style as the existing backup and audit-log notes at lines ~280-283.
The erasure result payload reports storage objects deleted per bucket alongside the existing per-table row counts, so the completion record is honest about scope.

A test covers a subject with at least one object in at least two buckets and asserts the objects are unreachable afterward.

userStories.notes: [LEGAL / P1] Evidence: server/services/gdpr-erasure-service.ts has no storage/bucket references at all (grep for storage|bucket|attachment|upload returns only profileImageUrl:null at line 147). It anonymizes users and businessRecords and documents its exemptions well, so the structure to extend is already there. Depends on LEGAL-003 landing a reliable object-delete helper; sequence 003 first. Bucket inventory from the audit: 'files' (files + file-storage fns), 'branding-assets' (branding-profiles/index.ts), 'meeting-recordings' (meeting-transcription/handlers/recordings.ts:15), qbr artifacts (QBR_STORAGE_BUCKET, default 'qbr-artifacts' in the edge fn and 'qbr' in server/routes-qbr.ts:373 -- note the two defaults disagree, which is its own bug), 'blog-assets'. POLICY-COPY RULE (all LEGAL stories, decided 2026-08-17): drafting legal/policy text alongside the code IS in scope, but every changed user-facing legal string must be called out in the commit body under a FOR COUNSEL REVIEW heading so it is reviewed before deploy. IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-18. New server/services/gdpr-storage-erasure.ts, called from executeErasure; ErasureResult gains a storage field with per-bucket outcomes reported alongside the row counts. Separate module because the objects are reached through the Supabase service client, not Drizzle: files, file_uploads, meeting_recordings and the QBR artifact table are DRIFT tables in no schema and no migration, so the code cannot be written against typed models. It probes candidate subject-link columns per table, tolerates a missing table or column, and reports what it could not reach instead of counting it as zero. Bucket scope: files (via files + file_uploads), meeting-recordings (user subjects) and the QBR bucket (customer/lead subjects) are erased; branding-assets and blog-assets are EXCLUDED with stated reasons - they are tenant assets, not personal data, and erasing one subject must not delete the company logo. TWO THINGS FOUND WHILE DOING IT: (1) a test caught a real bug in my own helper - isMissingTableError, mirrored from the edge-function version, falls back to a bare "does not exist" substring which ALSO matches "column x does not exist", so a missing column was misdiagnosed as a missing table and aborted the whole bucket instead of trying the next candidate column. Tightened here. THE SAME LATENT BUG IS STILL PRESENT in supabase/functions/customer-portal/handlers/_context.ts and the billing handlers, where it would make a genuine column error silently return [] instead of surfacing; flagged, NOT fixed here, because changing it touches billing behavior outside this story. (2) AC6 was not a formality: the "backups excluded" note was carried over unchanged and is FALSE for storage - pg_dump does not contain bucket contents, so there is no backup copy ageing out behind a failed object removal. Split into two accurate notes. Also hardened the caller: server/routes-gdpr.ts now leaves the request in_progress and returns 500 when any identified object failed to delete, matching that route existing principle that a failure must not falsely report completion, and the audit event records storageObjectsRemoved + per-bucket detail. VERIFIED: 11 unit tests (multi-bucket deletion asserted against stateful fake buckets, idempotency, failed-removal, missing table, unresolvable link column, tenant-bucket exclusion, subject-type scoping); tsc holds at 1058; lint 11656 (-260 vs baseline); build passes; full server suite 1951 passed with only the 2 pre-existing universal-search failures already confirmed unrelated. HONEST LIMIT: because the referencing tables are drift tables, the candidate link columns (uploaded_by, user_id, customer_id, business_record_id, contact_id) are informed guesses. If none matches the live schema the bucket is reported as unlinked and NOT silently skipped, but someone with live-DB access should confirm the real column names and tighten the specs.

userStories.title: Implement the 30-day post-termination data deletion the Privacy Policy promises
userStories.description: As the company, we need to do what the Privacy Policy says, because section 5.2 commits to deleting or anonymizing account and business data within 30 days of subscription termination and no job in the codebase implements that: the retention engine only covers eleven named tables, none of which are tenant account data or storage.
acceptanceCriteria: A scheduled job identifies tenants whose subscription terminated more than 30 days ago and deletes or anonymizes their account and business data, including storage objects.

The job is registered with the existing cron surface (server/services/cron-service.ts, alongside runScheduledRetention) rather than a new scheduler.
The job is dry-run by default with an explicit flag to execute, logs what it would delete, and writes an audit record per tenant processed.
