Privacy Policy section 5.2 is reviewed against what the job actually does, and either the code or the wording is corrected so they match exactly.
npm run check && npm run test pass.
userStories.notes: [LEGAL / P1] Evidence: Privacy Policy section 5.2 at client/src/pages/legal/PrivacyPolicy.tsx:262-272 promises 'for the life of your subscription and up to 30 days after termination, during which you may export your data, after which it is deleted or anonymized'. server/services/data-retention-service.ts IS wired to cron (server/services/cron-service.ts:81 imports runScheduledRetention) and works, but DEFAULT_RETENTION_PERIODS covers only audit_logs, data_access_logs, payment_audit_trail, security_sessions, gdpr_requests, incidents, change_requests, service_tickets, emails, notifications, temp_files. No tenant-termination trigger exists (grep for '30 days' in server/ returns only unrelated billing and briefing windows). Extend the existing service rather than building a parallel one. POLICY-COPY RULE (all LEGAL stories, decided 2026-08-17): drafting legal/policy text alongside the code IS in scope, but every changed user-facing legal string must be called out in the commit body under a FOR COUNSEL REVIEW heading so it is reviewed before deploy. IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-18. New server/services/tenant-purge-service.ts, wired into cron-service.ts beside the existing retention job and following its convention exactly: REPORT-ONLY unless TENANT_PURGE_ENABLED=true. KEY DESIGN CHOICE: the table list is DERIVED from the Drizzle schema at runtime (getTableConfig over every PgTable export, filtered to those with a tenant_id column) rather than written down. There are 501 tenant-scoped tables; a hand-maintained list would be stale within a release, and being stale here means either keeping data we promised to delete or deleting records we are required to keep. Retention is an ALLOWLIST mirroring the Privacy Policy exemptions - financial/tax 7y, security+audit 7y, support 3y, privacy-compliance evidence - so everything else is purged, which is what the promise actually says. FK ordering is solved by retrying failed tables until a pass makes no progress, rather than by a hand-maintained topological sort that would itself go stale. REVIEWING THE DERIVED OUTPUT WAS NOT OPTIONAL AND CAUGHT FOUR REAL ERRORS: (1) five financial tables were scheduled for deletion because the patterns missed them - customer_payments, lease_payments, vendor_bills, auto_invoice_generation and irs_mileage_logs, the last being a TAX record; (2) the security_.* pattern was open-ended and swept in seo_security_analysis, which is SEO tooling, so we would have retained data we promised to delete; (3) the tenant-parent rule read ^(tenants|companies)$ and companies is DEPRECATED CRM DATA (docs/crm-canonical-model.md), so retaining it would have preserved exactly the customer records the 30-day promise covers; (4) after fixing, only seo_audit_history remains in the financial-sounding purge list and it is correctly purged. Final split: 471 purged, 30 held. Lesson: patterns are a safety net for tables added later, never a substitute for reading the generated list - hence scripts/report-tenant-purge-plan.ts (npm run purge:plan), which prints the plan with reasons and highlights anything purge-bound whose NAME suggests a record worth keeping. It needs no DB credentials because classification is pure schema. ALSO: an audit record is written per tenant per run into audit_logs, which is itself a RETAINED table - the evidence that data was deleted has to outlive the data - and a failed audit write is surfaced as an error rather than swallowed, because an unrecorded purge is a deletion nobody can evidence. isWithinExportGracePeriod() derives export cutoff from the same PURGE_GRACE_DAYS constant so the two halves of the promise cannot drift apart. Privacy Policy 5.2 reworded to match what the job actually does (the window is the export opportunity; access ends when it closes). VERIFIED: 13 unit tests concentrated on classification, since that is where both failure directions originate; tsc holds at 1058; lint 11683; build passes; all five guards green; full server suite 1986 passed with only the 2 known pre-existing universal-search failures. NOT EXERCISED AGAINST A REAL DATABASE: no credentials here, so findTenantsDueForPurge and the delete passes are unrun. Review npm run purge:plan output and do a dry-run cycle in staging before setting TENANT_PURGE_ENABLED=true.

userStories.title: Audit storage bucket visibility and move QBR artifacts off public URLs
userStories.description: As a customer, my quarterly business review documents must not be readable by anyone holding the URL, because both QBR code paths call getPublicUrl() on artifacts that contain customer usage and spend data, and no migration in the repo establishes what the QBR bucket's visibility actually is.
acceptanceCriteria: The live visibility of every bucket is captured and recorded in docs/: files, branding-assets, meeting-recordings, blog-assets, and the QBR bucket. This is the first task in the story because the rest depends on it.
QBR artifacts are served via createSignedUrl with a short expiry instead of getPublicUrl, at both supabase/functions/qbr/index.ts:455 and server/routes-qbr.ts:384.
The QBR bucket is private. If it is currently public, existing artifact paths are treated as potentially disclosed and that is stated plainly in the story notes for a breach-assessment decision.
The QBR bucket name disagreement is fixed: the edge function defaults to 'qbr-artifacts' and the Express route defaults to 'qbr'. One canonical name, set in both.
The 'files' bucket is confirmed private, since it holds arbitrary customer uploads; if any code path returns a public URL for it, that path is converted to signed URLs.

blog-assets staying public is confirmed as deliberate (marketing images) and branding-assets staying public is confirmed as deliberate (tenant logos), each with a one-line rationale in the docs note. Neither should hold anything else.

A migration or documented setup step pins each bucket's public flag so the state is reproducible rather than whatever was clicked in a dashboard, following the pattern of drizzle/migrations/_backfill_blog_assets_bucket.sql.
npm run check passes; deno check passes on every edge function touched.
userStories.notes:
[LEGAL / P1] UNVERIFIED AT AUDIT TIME: getPublicUrl() returns a URL string regardless of bucket visibility, so the repo alone cannot prove the QBR bucket is public. Confirm against the live project before treating this as an incident. Evidence: supabase/functions/qbr/index.ts:450-456 and server/routes-qbr.ts:373-384 both getPublicUrl. Known public: blog-assets (drizzle/migrations/_backfill_blog_assets_bucket.sql:19 sets public=true, deliberate), branding-assets (supabase/functions/branding-profiles/index.ts:151 createBucket public:true, tenant logos). Handled correctly already: meeting recordings use server-side download() at supabase/functions/meeting-transcription/handlers/recordings.ts:217, not public URLs. POLICY-COPY RULE (all LEGAL stories, decided 2026-08-17): drafting legal/policy text alongside the code IS in scope, but every changed user-facing legal string must be called out in the commit body under a FOR COUNSEL REVIEW heading so it is reviewed before deploy. PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-18 - LEFT passes:false ON PURPOSE. Three ACs need live Supabase credentials this environment does not have (SUPABASE_URL/SERVICE_ROLE_KEY unset, no .env): AC1 capture live bucket visibility, AC3 confirm the QBR bucket is private and assess disclosure if it is not, AC5 confirm the files bucket is private. Those are the human-gated parts and they are the FIRST task in the story by its own wording, so the story is not done. DONE IN CODE: (AC2) both QBR paths moved off getPublicUrl. The fix is NOT a swap to createSignedUrl at the upload site - a signed URL expires, so persisting one just means a dead link later. Uploads now store the storage KEY and every read mints a 15-minute signed URL; new server/services/qbr-artifact-storage.ts for Express, and the edge fn signs inside toReport, which is the single mapper every read path already goes through. toArtifactKey accepts a bare key OR a legacy public URL so decks written before this keep working. (AC4) bucket-name disagreement resolved: Express defaulted to qbr, the edge fn to qbr-artifacts; both now use one setting defaulting to qbr-artifacts because the edge fn serves production. (AC6) branding-assets and blog-assets confirmed deliberately public with rationale in docs/storage-bucket-inventory.md. (AC7) drizzle/migrations/_pin_storage_bucket_visibility.sql pins all six buckets, following the _backfill_blog_assets_bucket.sql pattern, with a header telling the operator to run the audit FIRST because flipping a public bucket private is a disclosure event, not a migration side effect. NEW TOOL so the blocked ACs are one command: npm run storage:audit lists every bucket, diffs against intended state, and for each public bucket does an UNAUTHENTICATED GET on a real object - because getPublicUrl returns a URL either way, the only honest test is what an outsider actually receives. docs/storage-bucket-inventory.md has a marked placeholder for pasting its output. ALSO FIXED HERE: the LEGAL-004 erasure spec guessed a qbr artifact_url column that does not exist; the real columns are pdf_url and html_url (shared/qbr-schema.ts), now two specs. TWO PROCESS NOTES WORTH KEEPING: (1) esbuild caught a syntax error that a brace-balance check missed - a .replace() with a non-unique needle had wrapped the WRONG call site (qbr suppressions instead of qbr reports). Since supabase/functions is outside tsconfig include and deno is not installed, npx esbuild <file> --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null is the cheapest real syntax gate for edge functions. (2) check-types.mjs reported "errors DECREASED to 5 (-1053)" which was tsc ABORTING on a syntax error in routes-qbr.ts, not an improvement - my import block had been inserted into the middle of a multi-line import. Exactly the false-positive CLAUDE.md warns about; always eyeball an implausible ratchet win. After the repair the count holds at 1058. VERIFIED: 37 tests across the four storage/qbr suites; lint 11664 (-252); build passes; edge-path and migration-journal guards green; qbr edge fn syntax-clean under esbuild. REMAINING FOR A HUMAN: run npm run storage:audit with credentials, paste the table into docs/storage-bucket-inventory.md, apply _pin_storage_bucket_visibility.sql, and if the QBR bucket comes back public treat its objects as disclosed and escalate rather than just flipping the flag.
TRIAGED 2026-09-02 (not closed). Picked this up to work on and found the CODE HALF
ALREADY DONE, so this note exists to stop the next person re-investigating it.

Already in the tree:
  AC2  supabase/functions/qbr/index.ts stores the storage KEY and mints a 15-minute
       signed URL per read (:513 uploadArtifact, :577 createSignedUrl). No
       getPublicUrl remains anywhere under supabase/functions/qbr/.
  AC4  One canonical name: QBR_BUCKET / QBR_STORAGE_BUCKET defaulting to
       'qbr-artifacts' in both server/services/qbr-artifact-storage.ts and the edge
       function. The Express route the story names (server/routes-qbr.ts) no longer
       exists at all - /api/qbr is proxied - which is why
       server/services/qbr-artifact-storage.ts has no importer and sits in
       docs/server-orphans-baseline.json as "(test-only)". That is correct, not a
       loose end: it is the Node-side half of a helper whose Express caller was
       retired, and it is covered by server/tests/unit/qbr-artifact-storage.test.ts.
  AC6  docs/storage-bucket-inventory.md states the rationale for branding-assets
       and blog-assets staying public, and that nothing else belongs in either.
  AC7  drizzle/migrations/_pin_storage_bucket_visibility.sql pins all five buckets,
       idempotent and hand-runnable, in the _backfill_blog_assets_bucket.sql idiom.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT IS AC1, AC3 AND AC5, and none of them can be done from a
checkout. They need `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` against the live
project:

    SUPABASE_URL=... SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=... npm run storage:audit -- --markdown

then paste the output into the "Live state: NOT YET VERIFIED" section of
docs/storage-bucket-inventory.md. The doc already carries the breach-assessment
paragraph for the case where qbr-artifacts comes back public.

So this story is blocked on a credentialed human action, not on engineering. Leaving
it open is right; re-implementing the code half is not.

userStories.title: Complete the subprocessor list and disclose AI processors in the Privacy Policy
userStories.description: As a customer bound by our DPA, I need an accurate list of who processes our data, because Subprocessors.tsx names four vendors while the platform actually sends customer content to roughly a dozen, including OpenAI and Anthropic for document OCR, CSV refinement, meeting transcription, and proposal generation, neither of which is disclosed anywhere.
acceptanceCriteria: client/src/pages/legal/Subprocessors.tsx lists every third party that receives customer or personal data, each with purpose, data categories, and processing location. Verified against the codebase, not from memory.

At minimum the list adds: OpenAI, Anthropic, Sentry, Twilio, ZoomInfo, Apollo.io, DataForSEO, Microsoft (Graph), Intuit (QuickBooks), Google (Places, OAuth), Mailchimp. Each entry is confirmed against a real call site before it is listed.

The Privacy Policy states plainly which product features send customer content to AI processors, what content goes, and that it is not used to train third-party models (verified against the actual vendor terms in force, or the claim is not made).

Privacy Policy section 3.5 (Automated Decision-Making) is kept and extended rather than replaced; it is already accurate about lead scoring and predictive service being decision-support under Art. 22.
A CI guard cross-references outbound third-party API hosts and *_API_KEY environment variables against the subprocessor list and fails when a vendor appears in code but not in the list.
The subprocessor page carries a last-updated date and a stated change-notification mechanism, since enterprise DPAs typically require advance notice of new subprocessors.
npm run check && npm run build pass.
userStories.notes: [LEGAL / P1] For enterprise customers an undisclosed subprocessor is usually a breach of our own DPA, separate from the GDPR Art. 13/14 and international-transfer exposure. Evidence: client/src/pages/legal/Subprocessors.tsx lists only Supabase, Google Cloud Platform, Stripe, Twilio SendGrid. Actual outbound hosts found in server/ and supabase/functions/: api.openai.com, api.anthropic.com, api.twilio.com, api.zoominfo.com, api.apollo.io, api.dataforseo.com, graph.microsoft.com, login.microsoftonline.com, quickbooks.api.intuit.com, places.googleapis.com, accounts.google.com, us1.api.mailchimp.com, plus Sentry from the frontend bundle. Credentials in use: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN, SENDGRID_API_KEY, GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY, MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, APPLE_CLIENT_SECRET, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY. Good news already in place: ZoomInfo and Apollo.io ARE named in the Privacy Policy at lines 88-96; this story is about the subprocessor page and the AI gap. POLICY-COPY RULE (all LEGAL stories, decided 2026-08-17): drafting legal/policy text alongside the code IS in scope, but every changed user-facing legal string must be called out in the commit body under a FOR COUNSEL REVIEW heading so it is reviewed before deploy. IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-18. Subprocessors.tsx went from 4 providers to 19, split into two tables: 7 CORE (always in the data path: Supabase, GCP, Stripe, SendGrid, Sentry, OpenAI, Anthropic) and 12 CUSTOMER-ENABLED (Apollo, ZoomInfo, Twilio, Microsoft, Google, Apple, QuickBooks, Salesforce, Mailchimp, e-automate, PrintFleet, DataForSEO). The second table is not strictly required - those act under customer direction, not ours - but a customer working out where their data can go deserves more than the half we are obliged to publish. Added a data-categories column throughout. EVERY entry was confirmed against a real call site per the AC; four candidates were REJECTED as not data flows and recorded with reasons in the guard: HelloSign and AdobeSign (seed fixtures only - the signature send path is a stub that creates no envelope), Slack (a documentation URL in the integration catalog), Canon/HP/Xerox (seed fixture endpoints never called). MOST SIGNIFICANT DISCLOSURE: recorded service calls (routes-voice-ticket-close.ts) and meeting audio (meeting-transcription/_stt.ts) are sent to OpenAI for transcription - the audio of customer conversations leaves our systems - and imported file contents plus QBR fleet/usage/service data go to Anthropic. Neither was disclosed anywhere. Privacy Policy gains section 3.6 naming each feature and what content it sends. DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED: that data is not used to train third-party models. The AC allows the claim only if verified against the vendor terms in force, which cannot be done from here, so the policy points to the commercial terms and gives a contact instead of asserting it. Someone should confirm the account-level terms and then make the claim properly. GUARD: scripts/check-subprocessors.mjs (npm run check:subprocessors, wired into ci.yml) cross-references third-party hosts in server/ + supabase/functions/ AND *_API_KEY/_SECRET/_TOKEN env vars against the page, detecting 17 vendors. FIRST VERSION OF THE GUARD PASSED FOR THE WRONG REASON: it substring-searched the whole page, so deleting the OpenAI table row left the name in the surrounding prose and the check stayed green. Rewritten to parse only name: entries out of the subprocessor arrays, then re-tested by deleting the OpenAI row - now correctly fails with exit 1. Worth remembering as a guard-design trap: verify a guard by breaking the thing it guards, not by watching it pass. VERIFIED: tsc holds at 1058; lint 11664 (-252); build passes; browser render of /subprocessors, /privacy and /cookies confirms the new content is actually on the page (4345/12850/3097 chars, zero JS errors).

userStories.title: Article 14 notice for contacts sourced from data enrichment
userStories.description: As a person whose contact record was bought from ZoomInfo or Apollo rather than given by me, I have a right to be told you hold my data, and today nothing in the platform generates that notice or tracks which records came from enrichment rather than from the customer.
acceptanceCriteria: Enrichment-sourced contact records are marked with their provenance (source provider and acquisition date) at write time in the enrichment paths, so indirectly-collected records are distinguishable from customer-supplied ones.
A privacy notice is reachable for those data subjects covering the GDPR Art. 14 elements: identity of the controller, categories of data, source, purposes, legal basis, retention, and their rights.
Objection and erasure requests from an enriched contact are routable through the existing GDPR request flow without requiring an account.
Suppression is durable: an erased or objecting contact is not silently re-added by the next enrichment run.

The division of controller/processor responsibility between Printyx and its tenants for enrichment data is written down in docs/ and reflected in the DPA page, since the tenant is often the controller here.
npm run check && npm run test pass.
userStories.notes: [LEGAL / P2] The harder half of the data-provider question: disclosure to CUSTOMERS is already adequate (Privacy Policy lines 88-96 name ZoomInfo and Apollo.io), disclosure to the DATA SUBJECTS whose records were purchased is entirely absent. GDPR Art. 14 gives a one-month notice window from acquisition. Enrichment call sites: server/services/lead-intelligence-service.ts, server/routes-data-enrichment.ts, server/services/integrations-service.ts, server/routes-integrations-real.ts. Note the canonical CRM object model (docs/crm-canonical-model.md): contacts are companyContacts, companies are business_records. Scope the provenance columns to the canonical tables only. This one warrants counsel input on the controller/processor split before implementation. POLICY-COPY RULE (all LEGAL stories, decided 2026-08-17): drafting legal/policy text alongside the code IS in scope, but every changed user-facing legal string must be called out in the commit body under a FOR COUNSEL REVIEW heading so it is reviewed before deploy. MOSTLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-18 - LEFT passes:false, see the last AC. WHAT LANDS: new shared/data-provenance-schema.ts with TWO tables and drizzle/migrations/_contact_data_provenance.sql (hand-run, same reason as LEGAL-009: journalling without a snapshot widens the COP-M00 gap). (1) contact_data_provenance records source + acquisition date + which fields the provider supplied + Art.14 notice status, keyed by subject type+id rather than an FK because the same question applies to companyContacts AND business_records and the CRM is mid-migration between duplicate models - a join table survives that, two sets of added columns would have to move with it. (2) contact_suppressions is the durable half and is DELIBERATELY NOT tied to a contact row: the row is what gets deleted, the suppression is what has to survive it, otherwise the next enrichment run re-acquires the same person from the same provider and the erasure quietly undoes itself. Keyed by lower-cased email because that is what providers match on. WIRED, not just a library: lead-intelligence-service.enrichLeadFromApollo now calls isSuppressed() BEFORE applying any provider data and returns early, and recordProvenance() after applying it. isSuppressed FAILS CLOSED - a thrown query returns true, because a missing record costs a lead and a wrongly-acquired one costs a person who formally asked to be left alone. recordProvenance upserts and NEVER walks a sent/suppressed/exempt status back to pending. Caught myself using an 'as EnrichmentResult' cast to paper over the early return missing a required field and adding two it did not declare; fixed the interface properly instead (suppressed/reason are now declared, and suppressed:false is distinguishable from enriched:false - the caller needs to tell "found nothing" from "not allowed to look"). PUBLIC NOTICE: /data-sources, reachable WITHOUT an account because the people it is for do not have one and a notice behind a login is not a notice. Covers Art.14 elements: controller identity, source (Apollo/ZoomInfo named), categories, purposes, legal basis, retention, rights, and the supervisory-authority route. Verified rendering unauthenticated (2957 chars, no JS errors). NOT MET, hence passes:false: the AC requires the controller/processor division to be WRITTEN DOWN AND REFLECTED IN THE DPA PAGE. docs/enrichment-controller-processor.md drafts the position (customer=controller, Printyx=processor) and deliberately argues against itself in a section on where that is uncomfortable - notably that Printyx may hold the provider contracts and selects the providers, which looks more like joint control for the acquisition step, and that per-tenant suppression may not match what a data subject reasonably expects from one objection. I did NOT edit DataProcessingAgreement.tsx, because changing the DPA on my own reading of a contested question is exactly the kind of legal call this workstream has been routing to a human. Counsel needs to confirm the position and four specific facts listed in the doc, then the DPA edit is a small follow-up. VERIFIED: 10 unit tests focused on suppression durability and Art.14 triggering; tsc holds at 1058; lint 11683; build passes; migration-journal and deno-schema guards green.

userStories.title: Capture consent before recording meetings
userStories.description: As a participant in a recorded meeting, I need to be asked, because supabase/functions/meeting-transcription uploads and stores audio with no consent capture anywhere in the flow, and eleven US states require all-party consent to record a conversation.
acceptanceCriteria: Recording cannot start without an affirmative, recorded consent step; the consent record persists with timestamp, actor, and scope, using the existing consent surface (server/services/consent-management-service.ts, consentRecords) rather than a new one.
Participants are given notice before capture begins, not after.
The consent state is queryable and exportable per recording, so a later dispute can be answered with evidence.
Recordings that cannot be tied to a consent record are identified; the story notes state how many exist and what is being done about them.
Retention for recordings and derived transcripts is defined and enforced by the retention engine, matching whatever the Privacy Policy states.
Erasure of a participant removes or anonymizes their recordings and transcripts (coordinate with LEGAL-004 rather than duplicating the object-deletion logic).
npm run check && npm run test pass; deno check passes on the edge functions touched.
userStories.notes:
[LEGAL / P1] Not on the original question list; surfaced during the audit and carries real statutory damages. All-party-consent states include California (Penal Code 632, $5,000 statutory per violation under CIPA), Illinois, Florida, Pennsylvania, Washington, Massachusetts, Maryland, Michigan, Montana, Nevada, New Hampshire, Connecticut, Delaware, Oregon (varies by call type). Evidence: grep -i consent across supabase/functions/meeting-transcription, server/routes-meeting*, and client/src/pages/MeetingTranscription.tsx returns zero hits. Storage bucket 'meeting-recordings' at supabase/functions/meeting-transcription/handlers/recordings.ts:15. The consent infrastructure to build on already exists at server/services/consent-management-service.ts (recordConsent, withdrawal handling, audit). POLICY-COPY RULE (all LEGAL stories, decided 2026-08-17): drafting legal/policy text alongside the code IS in scope, but every changed user-facing legal string must be called out in the commit body under a FOR COUNSEL REVIEW heading so it is reviewed before deploy. MOSTLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-18 - LEFT passes:false. Enforcement is done and tested; two ACs are not fully satisfiable here. WHAT LANDS: POST /meeting-transcription/upload now REFUSES to record without consentConfirmed=true, a recognized consentMethod (verbal|written|checkbox|in_meeting_announcement), and at least one named participant. Checked BEFORE any row is written and before a single byte is stored. Consent goes into the EXISTING consent_records ledger per the AC, not a new table, so withdrawal/export/erasure keep working through paths that already exist; a recording is tied to its consent via proof_reference holding the recording id, because meeting_recordings is a drift table (no Drizzle schema, no migration) and bolting a column onto it would put the evidence where nothing else looks. FAILS CLOSED throughout: if the consent insert fails the metadata row is rolled back and the upload is refused, and if the audio upload later fails the consent record is deleted too (otherwise the coverage report would claim a nonexistent recording was covered). Needs one new consent_type enum value, added in drizzle/migrations/_recording_consent.sql. THAT MIGRATION IS HAND-RUN, not journalled: I first wrote it as 0057 and journalled it, and check:migrations correctly rejected it because a journal entry with no snapshot WIDENS the known snapshot gap (25->26, COP-M00). Generating a proper snapshot needs db:generate against a live DB. So it follows the established _backfill_*.sql / _pin_storage_bucket_visibility.sql convention instead. Until it is applied uploads fail closed, which is the safe direction. ALSO: GET /recordings/:id/consent answers what consent is on file (returns consented:false with a reason rather than 404, since "nothing on file" is a meaningful answer); meeting_recordings + meeting_transcriptions added to the retention engine at 730 days; Privacy Policy gains section 3.6 on recorded meetings (AI section renumbered 3.6->3.7); erasure of the audio itself was already covered by LEGAL-004, coordinated not duplicated. NOT FULLY MET: (1) "Participants are given notice before capture begins" - enforced as far as the API can: the uploader must state the method and record the exact notice text participants heard, which is stored on the consent record. But client/src/pages/MeetingTranscription.tsx is ENTIRELY MOCK DATA (useState with hardcoded recordings, no upload wiring anywhere in client/src), so there is no capture UI to put a visible notice in. When a real recording UI is built it must show the notice before capture starts. (2) "Recordings that cannot be tied to a consent record are identified; state how many exist" - scripts/report-recording-consent-coverage.ts (npm run recordings:consent-coverage) does exactly this and deliberately deletes nothing, but it needs SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY which this environment does not have, so THE COUNT IS UNKNOWN. Someone with credentials must run it; what to do with uncovered recordings is a legal call, not a script call. VERIFIED: 14 unit tests on the consent module (refusal cases, participant parsing, notice retention, ip/user-agent capture, source mapping, failure-not-throw); 58 tests green across all six suites this workstream has added; tsc holds at 1058; lint 11669; build passes; all three touched edge files syntax-clean under esbuild; migration-journal, subprocessor and edge-path guards green. | 2026-08-27 CROSS-REFERENCE: the AC1 blocker recorded above ("MeetingTranscription.tsx is ENTIRELY MOCK DATA, so there is no capture UI to put a visible notice in") is now filed as one of four confirmed instances on AUDIT-019, which covers the class. Nothing changes for this story — the enforcement side is done and the notice AC still needs a real capture UI — but the page is no longer an isolated oddity, and AUDIT-019 notes that wiring it is the option that unblocks this P1 rather than deleting a feature. The other blocker (the uncovered-recording count) still needs SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and remains unrunnable here.

[2026-08-29 AC2 BLOCKER CLEARED by AUDIT-019] The note above says "MeetingTranscription.tsx is ENTIRELY MOCK DATA, so there is no capture UI to put a visible notice in". That is no longer true. The page is wired to the edge function and its upload dialog now shows the consent notice text verbatim, requires a consent method and at least one named participant before the button enables, and posts consentConfirmed/consentMethod/consentParticipants/consentNoticeText as multipart. The client prefill and the server DEFAULT_RECORDING_NOTICE are locked by server/tests/unit/recording-consent-notice.test.ts, which also asserts the four methods the form offers are the four VALID_METHODS accepts; mutation-tested, a one-word change fails it. The fake Start Recording button - which flipped a boolean and captured nothing - is DELETED rather than rewired: there is still no in-app capture, and a button that looks like it is recording is worse on this feature than an obvious gap. So AC2 is met as far as the only capture path that exists (upload) allows; an in-app recorder, if one is ever built, still has to show the notice before capture starts.

ALSO FOUND AND FIXED: GET /recordings/:id/consent - the AC3 evidence endpoint this story built - WAS UNREACHABLE. handlers/recordings.ts implemented it, but the index.ts dispatcher switch on case recordings only forwarded transcription and process, so result stayed null and it 404d. It had never worked. The page now reads it for the selected recording. AC4 (count of recordings with no consent record) is UNCHANGED and still blocked: scripts/report-recording-consent-coverage.ts needs SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, which this environment does not have. That is the only remaining blocker, so passes stays false.

userStories.title: Verify or remove the SOC 2 Type II compliance claim
userStories.description: As the company, we cannot assert a certification we do not hold, because 'SOC 2 Type II compliance' appears as a security measure in the Privacy Policy itself and 'SOC 2 compliance' appears on a marketing page, and nothing in the repo evidences a current Type II report.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm whether a current SOC 2 Type II report exists, with the auditor and observation period recorded.

If it does not exist: remove the claim from client/src/pages/legal/PrivacyPolicy.tsx:257 and client/src/pages/marketing/ModernArchitecture.tsx:343, and replace it with the controls actually in place, which are real and worth stating (row-level security, encryption at rest and in transit, MFA, RBAC, audit logging).

Every other certification or framework claim in client/src is checked the same way (ISO 27001, PCI DSS, HIPAA, 'GDPR compliant'), and each is substantiated or removed.
A CI grep guard fails the build when an unapproved certification claim string is reintroduced.
npm run check && npm run build pass.
userStories.notes: [LEGAL / P1] A false certification claim is a clean FTC Section 5 deceptive-practice case and this one sits inside a legal document, which is the worst place for it. Evidence: client/src/pages/legal/PrivacyPolicy.tsx:257 ('SOC 2 Type II compliance and industry-standard security frameworks', listed among security measures in section 5.1) and client/src/pages/marketing/ModernArchitecture.tsx:343 ('Row-level security, encrypted data at rest and in transit, SOC 2 compliance...'). NEEDS A HUMAN ANSWER: does the report exist? Do not guess. If unanswered when this story is picked up, remove the claim, since removing a true claim is recoverable and keeping a false one is not. DECIDED 2026-08-17 by Dj Pearson: NO SOC 2 Type II report exists. Remove the claim from PrivacyPolicy.tsx:257 and ModernArchitecture.tsx:343 and replace with the controls actually in place and verifiable in the codebase: row-level security, encryption at rest and in transit, MFA, RBAC, audit logging. Do not substitute another certification claim. This resolves the human-decision blocker on this story. POLICY-COPY RULE (all LEGAL stories, decided 2026-08-17): drafting legal/policy text alongside the code IS in scope, but every changed user-facing legal string must be called out in the commit body under a FOR COUNSEL REVIEW heading so it is reviewed before deploy. Removed from: PrivacyPolicy.tsx (inside a legal document), ModernArchitecture.tsx (marketing), AND Login.tsx (the PUBLIC login screen, unauthenticated), plus two fabricated compliance DASHBOARDS - admin/SystemSecurity.tsx hardcoded green Compliant badges for SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, GDPR and CCPA next to invented audit scores (98/100, 95/100, 99/100, 87/100), and BusinessProcessOptimization.tsx hardcoded ISO 9001:2015 and SOC 2 Type II as Compliant with invented scores (96.7%, 94.2%), audit dates (Nov 2024, Sep 2024) and non-conformity counts (2, 1). None of it came from data - no useQuery, no API, pure literals. The dashboards are the more dangerous half: staff answer customer security questionnaires from what the product tells them, so a fabricated compliance screen becomes a written misrepresentation with a straight face. Both panels now state plainly that no report is held, that nothing tracks certification status, and list the controls that ARE real and verifiable in the platform (row-level security tenant isolation, encryption in transit and at rest, MFA, RBAC, audit logging) so a questionnaire can be answered from something true. Checked the whole client for the other frameworks per the AC: ISO 27001, ISO 9001, PCI DSS, FedRAMP, HIPAA-compliant, GDPR-compliant, CCPA-compliant - all now clean. GUARD: scripts/check-certification-claims.mjs (npm run check:certifications, wired into ci.yml) fails on any unapproved certification claim in client/src, with an APPROVED list that is deliberately EMPTY so obtaining a certification means adding it there with its report period and auditor in the same commit that publishes the claim. Disclaimer markers keep it from flagging its own fix. Proven to fire by restoring the exact Login.tsx wording: exits 1 naming the file and line. userStories.title: Send a cancellation confirmation and keep a durable cancellation record
userStories.description: As a subscriber who just cancelled, I need written confirmation, because several state auto-renewal statutes require an acknowledgement of cancellation and no cancellation email is sent today, even though the cancellation flow itself is well built.
acceptanceCriteria: Cancelling sends an immediate confirmation email stating what was cancelled, whether it takes effect immediately or at period end, the exact effective date, and what happens to the customer's data afterward.
The confirmation is also visible in-app, so it does not depend on email delivery succeeding.
A durable cancellation record is written (who, when, immediate vs period-end, effective date), retrievable later as evidence that cancellation was honored.

The data-handling sentence in the email matches the actual post-termination behavior implemented in LEGAL-005; if that story has not landed, the email states current behavior truthfully rather than the aspirational policy.
A test asserts both cancellation modes produce a record and enqueue a confirmation.
npm run check && npm run test pass.
userStories.notes: [LEGAL / P3] The cancellation flow itself PASSED the audit and needs no redesign: client/src/pages/SubscriptionSettings.tsx:205-235 offers cancel-immediately and cancel-at-period-end in one dialog, reachable self-serve, same medium as signup, with no retention gauntlet. That satisfies the click-to-cancel structure. The only gap is the acknowledgement: grep for cancel + email/notification in server/services/subscription-service.ts returns nothing. Cancel API at server/routes-subscriptions.ts:242. Notification helper to reuse: SubscriptionService.createNotification with channels ['in_app','email'], as used by the trial reminders at subscription-service.ts:780. POLICY-COPY RULE (all LEGAL stories, decided 2026-08-17): drafting legal/policy text alongside the code IS in scope, but every changed user-facing legal string must be called out in the commit body under a FOR COUNSEL REVIEW heading so it is reviewed before deploy. IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-18. CORRECTION TO MY OWN AUDIT: this story's note said 'no durable cancellation record' and 'no cancellation email'. Both were partly wrong and the real defect was narrower and more interesting. cancelSubscription ALREADY wrote a subscription_events row (durable record, real) AND a subscription_notifications row with channels ['in_app','email']. The in-app half worked. The email half did not: nothing anywhere reads subscription_notifications with status='pending' and sends it - the table is only INSERTed and then READ by the in-app list endpoint in routes-subscriptions.ts. So the channels array was a recorded intention with no mechanism behind it, exactly the same shape as the cookie banner in LEGAL-001. WHAT LANDS: new server/services/cancellation-confirmation.ts builds and sends a real confirmation through the existing email-service (the working path, same one the trial emails use), stating what was cancelled, whether it was immediate or end-of-period, the exact effective date, and that no further charge will be made. The event record now carries mode, effectiveDate, canceledAt, planId, AND whether the confirmation actually reached anyone (confirmationSent/confirmationRecipient/confirmationError) - a cancellation record has to answer, months later and to someone hostile, what happened and whether the customer was told. The in-app notification message gained the effective date and the no-further-charge sentence so it does not depend on email delivery. Sending never throws: a cancellation that succeeded must not report failure because the mail server was down, but the failure is logged and recorded on the event rather than swallowed. DELIBERATE WORDING CHOICE: dataHandlingSentence describes CURRENT behavior (export window open for 30 days, then deletion except stated categories) rather than the aspirational policy, because LEGAL-005's purge ships report-only until someone sets TENANT_PURGE_ENABLED=true. Promising completed deletion in an email would be the same class of untrue statement this workstream exists to remove, and there is a test asserting the sentence does not claim deletion has already happened. VERIFIED: 9 unit tests on the email content (effective date present in subject/text/html, immediate vs end-of-period distinguished, no-further-charge stated, org named, misuse contact given, plan name optional without leaving double spaces, export deadline arithmetic, retained categories named); tsc holds at 1058; lint 11683; build passes; full server suite 2005 passed with only the 2 known pre-existing universal-search failures.

userStories.title: Crisis-response guardrail before any AI surface is exposed outside authentication
userStories.description: As the company, we need a defined safety response before an AI conversational surface can reach anyone outside our authenticated B2B users, because no crisis handling exists anywhere in the codebase and the chatbot is one route change away from being public.
acceptanceCriteria: A documented policy states which AI surfaces may be exposed unauthenticated and what safety handling each requires before that can happen.

System prompts for any conversational surface include instructions to respond to self-harm, crisis, or emergency disclosures with appropriate resources and to not continue the sales or support script in that turn.
The response surfaces region-appropriate crisis resources (988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline in the US) rather than a generic deflection.
A CI or review guard flags removal of requireAuth from any chatbot or conversational AI route, so public exposure is a deliberate decision rather than a diff nobody noticed.
Tests cover a handful of crisis-phrasing inputs and assert the guardrail response, so a prompt edit cannot silently drop it.
npm run check && npm run test pass.
userStories.notes: [LEGAL / P3, deliberately low] Correctly scoped as low priority TODAY: the chatbot is authenticated internal B2B (every route in server/routes-chatbot.ts uses requireAuth + resolveTenant, e.g. line 831), there is no public widget, and the only unauthenticated surface is the marketing ROI calculator (supabase/functions/public-calculator), which is not conversational. grep for self-harm|suicide|crisis|988|hotline across server, supabase/functions, and client/src returns zero. This becomes urgent the day the chatbot is exposed to end customers or a public widget ships; the CI guard is the part worth having now, because it converts a silent risk into a visible decision. POLICY-COPY RULE (all LEGAL stories, decided 2026-08-17): drafting legal/policy text alongside the code IS in scope, but every changed user-facing legal string must be called out in the commit body under a FOR COUNSEL REVIEW heading so it is reviewed before deploy. IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-18. Confirmed the original low-priority assessment before building: /api/chatbot/query still has requireAuth, and an audit of ALL nine unauthenticated edge functions (client-metrics, csrf-token, hello, mobile-auth, oauth-proxy, public-booking, public-calculator, public-forms, signup) found none of them conversational. So there is no public surface today; the guardrail exists so it predates the exposure rather than being remembered after it. TWO LAYERS, deliberately. (1) DETERMINISTIC detector in server/lib/crisis-response.ts, called in routes-chatbot BEFORE any retrieval or model call. A system-prompt instruction is a request to a model that a prompt edit, model swap or long conversation can erode; the detector does not care. (2) CRISIS_SYSTEM_DIRECTIVE appended via withCrisisGuardrail() to the three conversational prompts (gpt5-service support, ai-employee-service support, deal-desk copilot), for what the detector misses. Data-processing prompts (CSV mapping, email parsing, OCR, dedup) were deliberately EXCLUDED - nobody is talking to them, and a directive there is noise that trains people to ignore it where it matters. The directive instructs the model to STOP the task and NOT to refuse, because a refusal is its own unsafe response: someone disclosing distress who gets 'I cannot discuss that' has been shut out at the worst moment. Resources are specific (988, 741741, 911), not a gesture at getting help. GUARD: scripts/check-ai-safety.mjs (npm run check:ai-safety, wired into ci.yml) enforces both that the chatbot route keeps requireAuth and that conversational prompts keep the guardrail. FIRST VERSION OF RULE 2 PASSED FOR THE WRONG REASON - it searched for the bare identifier 'withCrisisGuardrail', which survives in the import line after the call site is removed, so the simulated regression stayed green. Tightened to match the CALL. That is the SECOND time this session a guard passed on a surviving substring (LEGAL-007 was the first): verify a guard by breaking the thing it guards, every time. TESTS: 33, and the 10 false-positive cases matter as much as the 13 true positives - a detector that fires on 'this deadline is killing me' or 'the printer is dead again' trains people to ignore it, and an ignored safety response is worse than none because it looks like coverage. docs/ai-surface-exposure-policy.md lists six prerequisites before any public exposure, including that CRISIS_RESOURCES_US is US-only and showing a US number to someone abroad is worse than showing nothing. VERIFIED: tsc holds at 1058; lint 11683; build passes; all six guards green; full server suite 2038 passed with only the 2 known pre-existing universal-search failures.

userStories.title: A whole renewal-management feature, two data models, and no screen for either half of it
userStories.description: server/routes-renewal-management.ts (609 loc, 18 endpoints) and four edge functions - contract-renewals, renewal-activities, renewal-playbooks, expansion-opportunities (883 loc) - serve four real tables in shared/renewal-management-schema.ts that no client tree calls. Say why in docs/, the way docs/crm-canonical-model.md records the CRM decision

If the unwired model survives in part, name the specific capability it adds that the autopilot model cannot express - playbooks and expansion tracking are the two candidates - and build the screen for that, not for all 18 endpoints
If it does not survive, drop the four tables with a migration and delete the router plus the four edge functions together
Either way, the four edge functions leave docs/unreferenced-edge-fns-baseline.json - by gaining a caller or by ceasing to exist
server/routes-renewal-management.ts loses its AUDIT-026 header, because the question it records is answered
userStories.notes: FILED 2026-08-29 while triaging the CRM read-model cluster of AUDIT-024. Evidence for every claim above was gathered the same way as the other four instances: all four invocation paths checked per function (no client tree names the path across the seven trees, no crmProxies entry, no server.ts alias, no drizzle/cron/*.sql post), and the live pages' table set read off their edge functions rather than assumed. WHAT I DID NOT ASSESS: whether the 18 handlers and the four edge functions are CORRECT. The claim is only that nothing can reach them and that a second model owns the same domain. Two of the sibling opportunity read models triaged in the same pass turned out to be broken as well as unreachable, so do not assume this code runs until someone calls it.

userStories.title: Settings saved preferences into a table that does not exist, and dev proved nothing about it
userStories.description: Three defects on the /api/user surface, all fixed here, plus the reasoning that connects them. (1) PUT and GET /user/preferences read and wrote `user_preferences`, a relation in no Drizzle schema, no migration and no other file in the repository; the real table is user_settings, which is what GET /settings reads. The read swallowed the 42P01 and answered 200 with hardcoded defaults, so the Preferences tab looked like a user who had set nothing, and the write failed. (2) /api/user was not in crmProxies, so dev ran server/routes-settings.ts and production ran supabase/functions/user/ - and they disagreed about storage: Express put phone, jobTitle and department on user_settings and changed passwords by rehashing users.password_hash, while the edge function puts those three in users.metadata (they have no column) and changes passwords through GoTrue after verifying the current one with signInWithPassword. (3) /api/user/notification-preferences was served by neither backend, so the dialog behind the bell always rendered its own defaults and every save silently failed.
acceptanceCriteria: Both /user/preferences handlers read and write user_settings, and user_preferences appears in no .from() anywhere
/api/user is proxied so dev and prod run the same handler; server/routes-settings.ts is retired and the duplicate user-settings edge function is deleted
GET and PUT /user/notification-preferences are served, storing choices rather than the type catalogue
A test locks all of it, since none of it is visible to tsc
userStories.notes:
DONE 2026-08-29. server/tests/unit/user-settings-surface.test.ts, 10 assertions, mutation-tested in both directions.

WHAT THE FIXES ARE. Preferences now upsert named columns on user_settings (theme, language, timezone, date_format, time_format, currency) instead of spreading the request body into a phantom table, and the `notifications` jsonb is MERGED rather than replaced, because the preferences tab writes four channel toggles while the notification dialog keeps its per-type choices under a `detailed` key on the same column - a replacing write from either side erased the other. tenant_id is NOT NULL on that table and the JWT does not always carry a tenant claim, so resolveTenantId falls back to the users row rather than letting the upsert fail with a not-null violation that reads like a form bug. The notification dialog sends typeSettings only; labels and descriptions stay in the component, so a type added to the catalogue appears without a migration and nothing freezes copy into jsonb.

HOW I GOT HERE, AND THE MISTAKE IN THE MIDDLE, because it is the more useful half. I read the client's /api/user/* calls, grepped server.ts and edge-function-proxy.ts for an alias, found none, and concluded the whole Settings page was a production 404 - then wrote a server.ts override and a proxy entry pointing /api/user at the user-settings function, deleted the Express router, and started porting endpoints. All of it was wrong: supabase/functions/user/ has always existed, so production was always served, and the alias I added would have routed traffic AWAY from the complete implementation to a less complete duplicate. What caught it was check:routes reporting the domain as edge-only when I expected missing-edge. Reverted in full and redone.

THE RULE: check for the directory with the obvious name BEFORE checking for an alias. I have written 'grep the basename first' into CLAUDE.md twice this session and still checked the alias path first here, because the absence of an alias felt like the interesting finding. An absence is not evidence until you have looked for the presence.

WHAT THE INVERSION CHANGED. user-settings/ was the duplicate, not the live one, and is deleted (322 loc, no caller, in the unreferenced baseline). server/routes-settings.ts is still retired, but for the right reason: proxying /api/user makes its eight handlers dev-only, and the edge function covers seven of them - the eighth was POST /api/user/avatar, a multer upload no client tree calls.

STILL OPEN, and it is not this story's to decide: password changes go through GoTrue and leave users.password_hash stale, while server/auth-routes.ts still authenticates against that column through storage.authenticateUser. Two credential stores, one of which stops matching after a password change. Whichever is authoritative, the other needs to be written or removed.

userStories.title: MFA could be switched off with a stolen session, and no screen could switch it on
userStories.description: supabase/functions/mfa/ implements TOTP enrolment, backup codes, email and SMS OTP, admin reset and a compliance report across 700 lines, and no client tree named /api/mfa anywhere. The only MFA control that existed was a <Switch checked={userSettings?.twoFactorEnabled}> in Settings with no onCheckedChange - it rendered a state it could not change, and the state was permanently false because the only writer of that column was an Express router that never ran. Worse than the missing UI: POST /disable deleted every enrollment, and POST /backup-codes/regenerate issued a fresh set, on nothing but a valid session. Those are the two operations a second factor exists to protect, so a stolen token was enough to remove it. The Express implementation the edge function replaced DID verify a TOTP token first, which made production strictly weaker than dev on the control that matters.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /disable and POST /backup-codes/regenerate require a current TOTP or unused backup code, and audit the refusal
Settings can enrol, show backup codes, regenerate and disable, against the real endpoints
/api/mfa is proxied so dev exercises the same handler as production
The Express MFA router is retired or fixed - it gated on req.session.user, which nothing assigns
A test locks the gate, mutation-verified
userStories.notes:
DONE 2026-08-29. server/tests/unit/mfa-second-factor-gate.test.ts, 11 assertions; removing the gate fails three of them and dropping the code from the client's disable call fails a fourth.

THE GATE. requireSecondFactor accepts a TOTP code from a verified enrollment or an unused backup code, consuming the backup code exactly as login does. A user with NO verified enrollment passes deliberately - there is nothing to prove and nothing to protect, and refusing would leave a half-finished enrolment impossible to clear. It does not accept the account password, because this deployment has two credential stores that can disagree after a change (AUDIT-027), so 'the password' is not a single fact here while a TOTP code is.

THE EXPRESS ROUTER IS DELETED, and the reason is worth keeping. All 16 handlers gated on req.session.user; nothing in the codebase assigns it (server/types/express-session.d.ts had already recorded that finding), so every one answered 401 in dev as well as prod - it has never run. It also carried a SECOND storage model, the secret on user_settings.two_factor_secret, while the edge function uses mfa_enrollments. That is why the Settings flag was permanently false: the only code that could set it could not execute.

THE CARD. client/src/components/auth/TwoFactorCard.tsx reads /mfa/status rather than the stale column, enrols through /enroll/init and /enroll/verify, shows the ten backup codes once, and sends a code with both destructive calls. The QR image comes from a lazy `import('qrcode')` - that package is a server-side dependency here, so it is loaded only when the dialog opens (Vite splits it to a 24 kB chunk) and the dialog falls back to the base32 secret and the otpauth URI if it will not load. Every authenticator accepts those by hand.

STILL OPEN, and it decides whether any of this works in a given environment: mfa_enrollments and mfa_otp_tokens are created by drizzle/rls/auth-security-tables.sql, a hand-run file with no journal entry, so per SUPA-005 they may not exist in the live database at all. mfa_audit_logs and mfa_backup_codes ARE in migration 0000. Confirm all four before treating enrolment as available; the function will answer a 42P01 honestly, but a settings page that offers setup and then errors is worse than one that does not offer it.

Also open, and not this story's: nothing gates any route on MFA. requirePermissionWithMFA exists in enhanced-rbac-middleware.ts and is used nowhere, so enrolling changes what a user must type at login and nothing else.

userStories.title: Twelve registered Express routers authenticate against a field nothing assigns
userStories.description: 367 identity reads across 12 registered routers take the form `const user = req.session?.user` or `const tenantId = req.session.user?.tenantId`, with no other source - no req.user, no isAuthenticated, no getUserId/getTenantId. Nothing in this codebase ever assigns req.session.user: session login sets the flat req.session.userId / req.session.tenantId, the JWT path sets req.user, and a grep for an assignment finds only tests. Every handler in those files therefore answers 401, always, in dev as well as production. server/types/express-session.d.ts recorded this in a comment as a KNOWN LATENT BUG while declaring the type that makes it compile, and nothing measured it afterwards - which is the gap: the augmentation makes req.session.user.tenantId typecheck, so tsc reports a clean file, and no test mounts these routers.
acceptanceCriteria: A guard reports any server file whose only identity source is req.session.user, and fails on a new one
Every prefix among the 12 that a client actually calls either works or is proxied to an edge function that does
Each remaining file is either migrated to getUserId/getTenantId, retired in favour of its edge function, or annotated with which of those it needs
The baseline shrinks; it never grows
userStories.notes:
FILED AND PARTLY DONE 2026-08-29.

GUARD: scripts/check-session-user-auth.mjs, npm run check:session-auth, CI-wired. Baseline docs/session-user-auth-baseline.json at 12 files / 367 reads after this pass. Mutation-tested three ways: a new offender fails the gate, a baselined file that gains a real getTenantId call is reported resolved, and replacing the read with a comment mentioning it is NOT counted as a fix (comments are stripped on both sides, which this repo has needed four times now). A file with a fallback is deliberately not reported - apollo-routes.ts reads req.session.user three times for an activity write while gating every route on isAuthenticated, and it works; an early version of this analysis lumped it in with the dead ones and I nearly wrote it up as broken.

IT FAILS CLOSED, WHICH IS THE ONE PIECE OF GOOD NEWS. Every instance guards before using the value, so the result is a 401 rather than a query scoped to undefined - no tenant leak. But 12 routers answering 401 look, from the outside, exactly like a permissions problem, and this has been read as 'Express serves this in dev' in more than one place.

ONLY TWO OF THE TWELVE PREFIXES HAD LIVE CALLERS, and both are fixed. /api/lead-scoring: BANTAssessment.tsx could not load or save an assessment - 401 in dev from the dead router, and in production its raw fetch('/api/lead-scoring/bant/...') never reached the functions host at all (PROD-013), so the component was broken in both environments for two unrelated reasons. It uses apiRequest now and the prefix is proxied to supabase/functions/lead-scoring/, which covers all eleven of the router's resources; server/routes/lead-scoring-routes.ts is deleted. /api/email-campaigns: useEmailSequences got the same 401; proxied to supabase/functions/email-campaigns/. The other ten prefixes have no caller in any client tree, so nothing user-facing was broken by them.

email-marketing-routes.ts is RETAINED rather than deleted, with its eight now-shadowed handlers annotated in docs/shadowed-express-baseline.json. The whole file is dead the same way, but it also serves six prefixes that are not proxied (email-lists, email-list-members, email-sends, email-events, email-templates, email-unsubscribes) whose edge coverage is uneven, so retiring it is a per-prefix job rather than a file deletion.

WHAT IS LEFT, and it is a choice rather than a sweep. Twelve files remain. Each is one of three things: worth migrating to getUserId/getTenantId (if a caller ever appears), worth retiring in favour of an edge function that already covers it, or worth deleting outright. The third option is likely for most - advanced-billing-routes.ts is already annotated as PROD-008c, and gps-tracking, mileage, geofence-alerts, route-optimization, manufacturer-order, field-service and signature have no caller in any client tree. The fourth option, populating req.session.user in the login path, would revive all 367 reads at once and touches security-sensitive code; express-session.d.ts declared it out of scope and that judgement still looks right.
PROGRESS 2026-08-29 (part 2) - the ten remaining prefixes triaged, and the fail-closed claim now measured rather than sampled.

NO TENANT LEAK, CHECKED MECHANICALLY. 288 handlers across the eleven route files read req.session.user; every single one contains a 401 or 403 before it uses the value. So the failure is always a denial and never a query scoped to `undefined`. I had asserted this from reading four files; splitting each file on its route boundaries and checking every block is what makes it a fact.

ALL TEN REMAINING PREFIXES HAVE ZERO CALLERS in any of the seven client trees: /api/manufacturer-orders, /api/gps, /api/geofence-alerts, /api/mileage, /api/automated-billing, /api/route-optimization, and the root-mounted /api/signature-{requests,documents,signers} + /api/integration-credentials, /api/installations + /api/installation-checklists + /api/service-signatures, and /api/workflows + /api/executions + /api/triggers + /api/approvals. Only two have an edge function at all (manufacturer-orders, workflows), and both of those are themselves in docs/unreferenced-edge-fns-baseline.json. So none of these is a live broken feature; each is an unconnected one, and repairing the auth would not make any of them reachable.

ANNOTATED, NOT DELETED - 6,366 lines across nine files, 215 handlers. That follows PROD-008c's rule rather than PROD-008b's: a shadowed router whose edge function covers the same endpoints is safe to delete, and one with no replacement is unconnected work, which is a product call. Each header now names its own prefixes, its caller count, its edge coverage and the three options. advanced-billing-routes.ts gained a second paragraph (it could not run for two independent reasons, and only one was recorded), and middleware/mfa-enforcement.ts gained a header listing the three separate things that stop it being mounted.

THE ONE THAT DESERVES ATTENTION IS workflow-automation-routes.ts, and CLAUDE.md has been corrected for it. That line said "the registered router... the only workflow router in the tree", which is true and reads as "this is how you reach workflows". All 35 handlers 401 and nothing calls them. The runtime is a separate, genuinely live thing - dispatch comes from the edge seams and the boot-started sweeper, never through this router - so workflows execute and nobody can create, inspect or approve one. Registered is not reachable.


--- 2026-08-30 --- THE TEN REMAINING PREFIXES ARE CONFIRMED CALLER-FREE, and the
last file on the list turned into its own story.

Checked each of the eleven routers against all seven client trees rather than
client/src: /api/manufacturer-orders, /api/gps, /api/geofence-alerts,
/api/mileage, /api/automated-billing, /api/route-optimization and the six root
paths the signature and field-service routers mount (/api/signature-requests,
/api/signature-documents, /api/integration-credentials, /api/installations,
/api/installation-checklists, /api/service-signatures) all have ZERO callers.
/api/billing is the exception and is already covered - it is proxied, and its 39
shadowed handlers are PROD-008c's. So the story's "nothing user-facing is
broken" claim holds on a full re-check, not just the original one.

THE TWELFTH FILE, middleware/mfa-enforcement.ts, is not a router at all and is
now AUDIT-034. Following it up found that server/middleware/security-index.ts -
the only place enforceSessionTimeout, extendSessionOnActivity, enforceIpWhitelist,
requireMfaForAdmins and requireMfaVerification are ever applied - is imported by
nothing. Three security controls written and never mounted.

WORTH THE CORRECTION: a one-level grep says session-timeout.ts is used, because
routes-session-management.ts imports it. It takes the HELPERS and not the
enforcement middleware, so sessions still never time out. File-reachable is not
middleware-mounted, and that distinction is what the new server-orphan walk
makes visible - it correctly does NOT report session-timeout.ts, which is why
the annotation in security-index.ts has to carry the rest.
userStories.closure_note:
Closed 2026-09-01. All four acceptance criteria hold.

AC1 and AC2 were already done when this was filed as PARTLY DONE: the guard
exists, is CI-wired and mutation-tested three ways, and both prefixes with live
callers were fixed.

AC3 is what remained. Eleven of the twelve files carried a header explaining that
they cannot authenticate anyone; server/routes/email-marketing-routes.ts did not,
and it now does. Writing that header meant reading the file properly rather than
restating the story, and two things came out of it. Of its seven prefixes only
/email-campaigns has a caller anywhere - useEmailSequences, from the routed
/marketing/sequences page - and that prefix is PROXIED, registering at
routes-registry:297 against this router's :620, so the live page has never
touched these handlers. The other six have no caller in any of the seven client
trees, and only one of the six has an edge function at all. The
shadowed-express baseline describes retiring this file as a per-prefix job on
uneven edge coverage; that is true, and this narrows it to a question about
whether anyone wants the feature rather than how to port it.

AC4, the baseline shrinking: 12 files / 367 reads -> 11 / 365, and the honest
description is that the guard was over-reporting, not that a file was fixed.
server/middleware/mfa-enforcement.ts reads `(req as any).user || req.session?.user`
- req.user FIRST, which the JWT path does assign - so it was never a
session-only file. The fallback pattern matched a bare `req.user` and the cast
form put the words either side of `as any)`, which a word boundary does not
cross. The guard now recognises both, and exactly one file moved, so nothing
genuine was hidden by widening it.

That correction propagates. mfa-enforcement's own header opened "Three separate
things stop it" and named SEC-SESSION-001 as the second, on the reading that
mounting it would deny every request. It would not - a JWT request would
authenticate normally. The third blocker, QUALITY-002's Role-row-into-
parseRoleLevel bug, is already fixed at both call sites. So the header now says
two, and names the ones that are still true: nothing imports
enforceMfaForAdmins, and its two-factor state comes from
user_settings.two_factor_enabled while supabase/functions/mfa/ keeps enrolments
in mfa_enrollments - mounting it as written would treat every enrolled user as
un-enrolled and lock out exactly the privileged accounts it protects.

A file annotated with a reason that turns out to be wrong is worse than one with
no annotation, because the annotation stops the next reader checking. That is
the third correction of this shape this session.

server/tests/unit/session-user-auth-annotations.test.ts locks the headers on all
eleven, the cast-form fallback in the guard, and the corrected mfa-enforcement
reasoning.

Verified: 4,280 tests pass, check-types holds at 319, check:session-auth and
check:shadowed-express clean.

userStories.title: Thirty-three tables are read by a live feature and filled by nothing
userStories.description: The alert bell was the worked example: supabase/functions/performance/ read system_alerts correctly, the table is real, and the only insert against it anywhere is storage.createSystemAlert, which no caller names - so the bell was permanently empty in production and nothing reported an error, because an empty list is a perfectly good answer to 'what alerts are there'. A guard for that shape now reports 33 more: declared tables (not views) that an edge function reads and that nothing in supabase/functions, server, scripts or drizzle ever inserts into. Each is a surface that can only ever render empty. The read path is correct in every case, which is why none of them looks broken.
acceptanceCriteria: For each of the 33, answer the one question the guard asks: who fills this in? The answer is a UI that was never built, an importer never wired, an external feed that should be named in a comment, or a derivation that should replace the read
Where the answer is an external feed (this repo syncs from E-Automate), record it in a comment at the read site so the next reader does not re-derive it, and baseline the entry with that reason
Where the answer is a derivation, do what supabase/functions/performance/ now does for alerts: compute it from the tables that ARE filled, alongside the stored read rather than instead of it

Start with the live ones: contract_renewal_tracking (ContractRenewalDashboard, routed at /contract-renewal-autopilot, 11 client refs), kpi_values (reports, 64), customer_satisfaction_surveys and its two template tables (customer-portal, 48), enhanced_quote_pricing (pricing, 31), discount_analytics (deal-desk, 25)
docs/unwritten-tables-baseline.json shrinks; it never grows
npm run check && npm run test pass
userStories.notes:
FILED 2026-08-29 with the guard. scripts/check-unwritten-tables.mjs, npm run check:unwritten-tables, CI-wired, baseline 33 of 519 tables read. Mutation-tested three ways: a newly-read unwritten table fails the gate, a baselined table that gains an insert is reported as resolved, and an insert inside a COMMENT does not count as a writer.

WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT REPORT, so a pass is never read as proof: views (derived by definition), tables that do not exist at all (check:phantom-tables owns those, and the two lists are disjoint by construction), a writer whose table name is built at runtime, and - importantly - a writer that EXISTS but is unreachable. system_alerts itself would not appear here, because its insert exists; it is just that nobody calls it. Unreachable-writer is a harder question and this check does not attempt it, which means the true number is larger than 33.

EXTERNAL FEEDS ARE THE MAIN FALSE-POSITIVE RISK. This repo syncs from E-Automate, and those rows arrive outside the codebase. A table with external_* columns is a candidate for that explanation - but it is an explanation to VERIFY and write down, not to assume: the point of the baseline entry is to record which of the four answers applies.

THE ONE I CHECKED PROPERLY: contract_renewal_tracking. ContractRenewalDashboard is routed at /contract-renewal-autopilot and EDGE-002g built its endpoints against that table specifically. server/services/contract-renewal-service.ts only ever reads it (three findFirst calls), routes-contract-renewal.ts drives that service, and there is no insert anywhere in the tree. So the renewal autopilot can analyse nothing, because nothing ever creates a contract to track. The likely producer is a derivation from service_contracts approaching their end date - which is exactly what this pass ported into the alert bell for contract expiration - but 'tracking' implies mutable state (renewal risk, churn score, an owner) that a derived read cannot hold, so it wants a real producer rather than a view.

OTHERS WORTH KNOWING WITHOUT HAVING VERIFIED THEM: renewal_analytics sits behind the same dashboard; integration_metrics is what PROD-014a's ERP aggregation reads; the three customer_satisfaction_* tables back the customer portal's survey surface; supply_monitoring, supply_usage_history and supply_replenishment_analytics are all of auto-supply-replenishment's inputs, which makes that whole feature suspect rather than one endpoint.
PROGRESS 2026-08-29 - auto-supply-replenishment triaged, and one honest fix shipped from it.

THE FEATURE IS INERT, not partially working. AutoSupplyReplenishmentDashboard is routed at /auto-supply-replenishment and calls four endpoints, all of which the edge function serves. But the function's inputs are: supply_monitoring (declared, NEVER WRITTEN), supply_usage_history (same), supply_replenishment_analytics (same), plus `inventory` and `tenant_settings`, which are on the phantom-tables baseline and do not exist at all. So POST /analyze-all - the AI loop that scores depletion risk and creates orders - iterates zero rows every time, and the dashboard counts zeros off an empty table. Nothing is broken in the sense of erroring; there is simply no producer for any of it.

THE ONE FABRICATION IN IT IS FIXED. `averageLeadTime: toNumber(analytics?.average_lead_time) || 3.0` ported an Express default, and since supply_replenishment_analytics is never written, that `|| 3.0` was not a fallback - it was the answer, every time. The routed page reported a 3.0-day average lead time it had never measured. The page then did the same to the other two, rendering null as `$0.00` saved and `0 emergencies prevented`. All three return null now with an `unbacked` line naming the missing producer, and the page renders a dash. "We saved $0.00" is a claim; "not measured" is the fact. server/tests/unit/supply-replenishment-unbacked.test.ts locks both ends, mutation-tested.

WHAT THE PRODUCER WOULD BE, for whoever takes this on: a supply_monitoring row is an installed device's consumable level, so it should come from the remote-monitoring path - equipment plus meter or device readings. That path has the same problem one layer up: client_collected_metrics and client_discovered_devices (monitoring-clients) are both on this story's list, and device_readings and printer_metrics are on the phantom-tables list. So the whole telemetry chain from device to reorder has no first link, and fixing supply_monitoring alone would not fill it.

PROGRESS 2026-08-29 (part 3) - a sibling class worth naming, found while triaging the fleet cluster: a table that does not exist at all, read by a LIVE page. check:phantom-tables already reports those, but only as a table-plus-file pair; nothing connects the pair to whether a user can reach it.

/api/devices is called by two ROUTED pages - ManufacturerIntegrationDevices and FleetMonitoringDashboard (/fleet-monitoring) - and supabase/functions/devices/ reads `.from('devices')`. There is no `devices` table: not in any Drizzle schema, not in any migration. Six edge functions read it. So both pages get a 42P01 on every list request.

Repointing it is NOT a rename, which is why this is a story rather than a fix. The real fleet table is device_registrations, and its column set differs: it has customer_id and status, but NO manufacturer (the handler filters on it) and no created_at (it is registered_at, which the handler orders by). The `customer:customer_id (id, company_name)` embed also needs a declared FK from device_registrations.customer_id, and that column is a bare varchar with no constraint - PostgREST embeds across declared foreign keys and nothing else.

FOUR OF THE SIX READERS ARE DELETED, because they had no caller on any of the four invocation paths and read the nonexistent table on top of it: fleet-dashboard, fleet-devices, customer-devices and customer-metrics. Unreferenced-edge-fn baseline 88 -> 84, phantom-table references 113 -> 109. The two that remain are devices/ and order-toner/, both live, and both belong to whoever takes the repoint - order-toner is reached from the same pages through /api/devices/:id/order-toner.


--- 2026-08-29 (AUDIT-032) --- SIX OF THE 33 HAVE THEIR ANSWER, AND IT IS NOT
"nobody built the writer".

client_collected_metrics, contract_renewal_tracking, renewal_analytics,
supply_monitoring, supply_replenishment_analytics and supply_usage_history all
declared tenant_id as an INTEGER while tenants.id is a varchar uuid, so no write
naming a real tenant could ever have succeeded (42804) and no read could have
matched one (22P02). Under PostgREST the read error leaves .data null and the
callers write `?? []`, which is precisely the empty-table signal this baseline
keys on - so the guard was reporting the symptom of a type defect as a missing
feature. AUDIT-032 converted all 21 such columns (migration 0062, proven against
a real Postgres) and added check:tenant-id-types.

These six stay in the baseline: they are still unwritten. But the question for
each has changed from "who was supposed to fill this in" to "wire up the writer
that now can". Check the tenant_id type before writing up any remaining entry
the same way.

userStories.title: Three routed pages read /api/device-monitoring, which production does not serve
userStories.description: DeviceMonitoring (/device-monitoring), SupplyRunway (/supply-runway) and SupplyOrders (/supply-orders) are all routed and between them call nine endpoints under /api/device-monitoring. There is no supabase/functions/device-monitoring/, the prefix is not proxied, and no server.ts alias maps onto it - so in production every one of those calls goes to functions.printyx.net/device-monitoring and 404s. The backend behind them is real and good: server/routes-device-monitoring.ts, 735 lines over device_metrics, device_registrations, device_alerts and device_supply_orders, with a header recording a previous drift fix. It has simply never had a production host.
acceptanceCriteria: supabase/functions/device-monitoring/ serves the nine endpoints the three pages call: GET /latest-metrics, /active-alerts, /supply-forecast, /supply-orders, /device/:serialNumber/history, /device/:serialNumber/alerts, and POST /alerts/:id/{acknowledge,snooze,resolve} and /supply-orders/:id/{approve,cancel}

It imports the projection and the forecast from supabase/functions/_shared/device-monitoring-shape.ts rather than reimplementing them - that module exists for this port and is already what Express uses
/api/device-monitoring is added to crmProxies so dev exercises the same handler, and the Express router is then retired or annotated

The two queries that use raw SQL are the porting hazards and need explicit handling: loadLatestPerDevice uses DISTINCT ON (use latestPerDevice() over a (device_id, collection_timestamp desc) ordering) and the alert and order reads LEFT JOIN device_registrations (PostgREST embeds only across a declared FK; check whether one exists before assuming .select('*, device_registrations(...)') works)
npm run check && npm run test pass, and the guard sweep by exit code is clean
userStories.notes:
FILED 2026-08-29, with the groundwork done so the port is a data-fetch wrapper rather than a rewrite.

WHY IT IS PRIORITY 2. This is not an unconnected feature like PROD-008c or AUDIT-026 - three pages are routed, reachable from the nav, and every request they make dies in production. It is the largest live prod-404 found so far.

WHAT THIS PASS DID. supabase/functions/_shared/device-monitoring-shape.ts now holds shapeMetricForUi, decorateAlert, latestPerDevice and forecastSupplies, and server/routes-device-monitoring.ts imports them - so the shaping has ONE definition before a second host exists, rather than after. That matters more than it sounds: the three pages read flat keys that no table stores under those names (tonerBlack, serialNumber, currentLevel), so the projection IS the contract, and this repo's other duplicated projections have all drifted. Ten server runtime files already import from supabase/functions/_shared, so the cross-boundary import is an established pattern rather than a new risk.
