THE FORECAST RULES ARE NOW TESTED, which they were not. Each exists to avoid a specific wrong answer and all four are asserted: a level RISING more than five points is a cartridge swap, not negative consumption; under half a day of data forecasts nothing, because two readings an hour apart turn a rounding step into a burn rate; consumption at or below 0.05 points/day is idle rather than slow, since dividing by it gives runways of decades; and confidence weights sample count by window coverage, so eight readings from one afternoon do not read as well as eight across two weeks.

A MUTATION CAUGHT MY OWN TEST. The swap assertion originally checked that consumption was positive and currentLevel was 55 - both of which hold with swap detection DISABLED, so it passed under mutation and proved nothing about the rule it named. It asserts the RATE now: 4/day after the swap versus 0.25/day measured across the whole series, a sixteen-fold understatement that would put the runway at 220 days instead of 14. Assert the number the rule changes, not a number that survives it.

Also in this cluster and NOT part of the port: fleet-dashboard, fleet-devices and customer-devices are three more edge functions with no caller in any client tree (AUDIT-024's list), and remote-monitoring has 8 client refs with an edge function that is not proxied, so dev and prod diverge there too.
DONE 2026-08-29, same day. supabase/functions/device-monitoring/ serves all twelve endpoints, /api/device-monitoring is proxied, and server/routes-device-monitoring.ts is retired - so the three routed pages have a production backend for the first time.

A SECOND DEFECT SURFACED DURING THE PORT, and it was worse than the 404. Three of the Express queries selected `r.manufacturer`, and device_registrations HAS NO SUCH COLUMN - not in migration 0000, and no later migration adds one (0040 adds customer_id and that is all). Postgres answers "column r.manufacturer does not exist", so /latest-metrics, /supply-forecast and /supply-orders were a 500 in DEV as well as a 404 in production. A phantom column inside raw SQL is invisible to both guards that would normally catch one: tsc cannot see into a template string, and check:phantom-cols reads edge functions only. The field is dropped rather than faked - the shared shaper already returns null for a registration without one, so no response shape changed.

THE TWO PORTING HAZARDS THE ACs NAMED, and how each resolved. DISTINCT ON became an order by (device_id asc, collection_timestamp desc) plus latestPerDevice(), which keeps the first row per device - exactly equivalent under that ordering and wrong under any other, which is why the ordering carries a comment. The LEFT JOIN became a PostgREST embed, which works only because device_metrics.device_id, device_alerts.device_id and device_supply_orders.device_id each carry a declared FK to device_registrations.id (0000 and 0008). One thing the ACs did not anticipate: filtering the forecast by serialNumber needs `device_registrations!inner`, because without the bang PostgREST returns every device with a null registration rather than none - the filter would silently do nothing.

GATED AT LEVEL 3, mirroring what navigation-permissions.ts already applies to all three pages, and a LEVEL rather than a permission code per SEC-EDGE-002 - the codes the Express gates name are not the codes any seeder creates, so a copied gate denies everyone below platform admin. check:edge-rbac caught that the function was open before I remembered to gate it; that guard is easy to forget and worth running on every new function.

TWO TESTS, 29 assertions: device-monitoring-shape.test.ts covers the behaviour that can run without a database (the projection and every forecast rule), device-monitoring-port.test.ts covers endpoint coverage and the contract.

MUTATION TESTING CAUGHT TWO OF MY OWN ASSERTIONS, the same failure both times: an assertion that passes with the rule it names disabled. The forecast swap test asserted consumption was positive and the level was 55, both true without swap detection - it asserts the RATE now, 4/day against 0.25/day. The DISTINCT ON test sliced from 'latest-metrics' to end of file, which picked up the /statistics block's own latestPerDevice call, so mutating the one in the branch under test left it green - the slice is bounded to the branch now. Mutate the exact occurrence the assertion covers, not the first one in the file.

STILL IN THIS CLUSTER, not part of this port: fleet-dashboard, fleet-devices and customer-devices have no caller in any client tree, and remote-monitoring has 8 client refs with an unproxied edge function, so dev and prod diverge there.

userStories.title: Remote Monitoring shows a fleet the platform does not measure, and 404s in production
userStories.description: RemoteMonitoring.tsx is routed at /remote-monitoring and calls five paths under /api/remote-monitoring. In production all five 404: the remote-monitoring edge function serves devices, alerts, status, devices/:id and readings, which is a disjoint set - zero overlap with what the page asks for. In dev two of them are answered by hardcoded fixtures in server/routes-sample-data.ts: 47 pieces of equipment, a customer called Metro Office Solutions, coordinates at 40.7128/-74.006, 96.8% average uptime and three weekly trend arrays, none of it from a database. The remaining three paths (/api/remote-monitoring bare, /sensor-data, /acknowledge-alert) are served by nothing on either host. So the page shows invented fleet data in dev and nothing at all in production.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide what this page is for now that /device-monitoring exists over the same tables. If it stays, it needs the endpoints built; if it is a duplicate view, redirect it the way AUDIT-019 redirected the fixture twins

If it stays: build /fleet-overview and /equipment-status in supabase/functions/remote-monitoring/ over device_registrations + device_metrics + device_alerts, name the unmeasurable fields in an `unbacked` array, and rewire the page - do not ship the endpoints without the page, because a 200 with the wrong shape is worse than the 404 it replaces
/acknowledge-alert should call the alert action that already exists rather than getting a second implementation: POST /api/device-monitoring/alerts/:id/acknowledge
Delete the two /api/remote-monitoring handlers from server/routes-sample-data.ts either way - they are fixtures on a routed page
npm run check && npm run test pass
userStories.notes:
FILED 2026-08-29. The derivability analysis is the useful part and is done, so whoever picks this up does not have to redo it.

DERIVABLE from device_registrations + device_metrics + device_alerts, the tables supabase/functions/device-monitoring/ already reads: totalEquipment (count of registrations), statusDistribution (device_metrics.device_status per latest reading, falling back to device_registrations.status), equipmentWithAlerts (distinct device_id across open alerts), averageUptime (device_metrics.uptime is a real decimal column - mean of the latest per device, and NULL rather than 0 when nothing has reported, because a fleet at 0% uptime is an outage and not-measured is not that), attentionRequired (devices with open alerts, using the alert messages as `issues`), and per-device status, last ping, toner and paper levels and total impressions.

NOT DERIVABLE, and this is why the page cannot simply be wired up: fleetUtilization (nothing records a duty cycle or rated capacity), energyEfficiency (no power draw is collected, and the fixture returns a LETTER GRADE), performanceTrends weeklyUptime/Utilization/Efficiency (uptime is stored per reading but utilisation and efficiency are not stored at all), topPerformers (ranking needs both), estimatedRevenueLoss (no contract value is joined to a device), and on the per-device panel: temperature, humidity, jam counts, daily/weekly/monthly page counts, average job size, peak usage hour, maintenance score, predictive component life, power consumption, carbon footprint and sleep-mode state. Twelve categories of telemetry the platform does not collect.

WHY THIS IS NOT A CLEANUP TASK. The page is 1,176 lines with 39 render sites bound to that fixture shape across four tabs. Wiring the real subset means deleting most of the UI, and which of the twelve categories to drop - versus collect - is a product decision. I built the two endpoints during triage and REVERTED them rather than ship an endpoint whose shape the page cannot consume: an unwired endpoint is the exact pattern AUDIT-024 exists to catch, and a 200 with the wrong shape is worse than the 404 it would replace.

WORTH WEIGHING FIRST: /device-monitoring, /supply-runway and /supply-orders now read the same three tables through a working edge function (AUDIT-029). If Remote Monitoring is a second view of one fleet, redirecting it is cheaper than rebuilding it, and AUDIT-019 has the pattern for retiring a route while keeping its navigation-permissions entry.
userStories.closure_note:
Closed 2026-09-01 by RETIRING the page, which is the first acceptance criterion's
first branch.

/fleet-monitoring already does this job over the same three tables through
supabase/functions/device-monitoring/ (fleet-dashboard, fleet-devices,
fleet-devices/:id/metrics, alerts/:id/acknowledge), proxied on both hosts. That is
the same four capabilities Remote Monitoring asked for, and it is real. Comparing
endpoint sets rather than page names is what settled it, per AUDIT-018.

/remote-monitoring is a LegacyRedirect to /fleet-monitoring. RemoteMonitoring.tsx
(1,176 lines) is deleted. The navigation-permissions entry stays, because both
sidebars and old bookmarks name the path, and it now MIRRORS the target's gate
exactly - the source was minLevel 2 with an extra configure permission, so a
redirect either advertised a page the user would be denied or let them reach the
target on terms the target does not accept. The duplicate sidebar child is gone
from both the desktop and mobile drawers; the '/remote-monitoring*' match pattern
stays so an old link still lights the right section.

THE FINDING UNDERNEATH, which the story did not have. There were THREE Express
implementations of /api/remote-monitoring, not one. routes-sample-data.ts and
routes-operations-extended.ts both held fixtures, and routes-operations-extended
registered first, so IT was what dev served. The only implementation that read
real tables - routes-remote-monitoring.ts, 772 lines over device_registrations
and device_metrics - was registered nowhere, and sat in the server-orphans
baseline where nobody connected the two entries. So the working code was dead and
the two that ran were invented. Anyone porting this would have found the real
file first and assumed it was live. All three are deleted; check:dup-routes drops
12 baselined entries.

Also: supabase/functions/remote-monitoring/ is now unreferenced and joins the
AUDIT-024 baseline rather than being deleted. It is NOT a duplicate of
device-monitoring - it reads monitored_devices and device_readings, the
printyx-client agent's own tables, which are a different data source. It has no
caller in any of the seven client trees, the agent does not call it either, and
nothing anywhere writes those two tables, so it is an AUDIT-028 case sitting
inside an AUDIT-024 one. Deleting it is a decision about the agent surface, not
cleanup, so it is recorded rather than removed.

Verified: 216 test files / 4,242 tests pass, npm run build succeeds, check-types
holds at 320, and check:nav, check:routes, check:orphans, check:dup-routes,
check:shadowed-express, check:server-orphans, check:fabricated,
check:no-static-posture, check:no-mocks, check:query-states all clean.

Three stale tests were red on the base branch and are fixed here rather than left:
device-monitoring-port asserted the word "manufacturer" never appears in the edge
function, which broke when the same function legitimately began reading
manufacturer_integrations (the defect was always about WHICH table the projection
sits on); edge-path-depth asserted at least 19 deep-shape gaps in the coverage
baseline, an assertion about DEBT that PA-052 closed to zero, so the story's own
success read as a regression; and task-time-entries asserted the interpolated
`timer-${parts[2]}` that PA-052 replaced with an enumerated verb.

userStories.title: Fleet Monitoring read a vehicle API in production, and its Order Toner button never worked
userStories.description: FleetMonitoringDashboard.tsx is routed at /fleet-monitoring and called /api/fleet/dashboard and /api/fleet/devices. /api/fleet is not in crmProxies, so dev was served by three handlers in server/routes-client-monitoring.ts over device_registrations + device_metrics - real code, correct data, which is why the page looked fine. Production resolves the segment to supabase/functions/fleet/, which is about VEHICLES: fleet_vehicles, fleet_maintenance, fleet_fuel_logs, fleet_vehicle_locations. So /dashboard answered 200 with totalVehicles / availableVehicles / inServiceVehicles under keys the page does not read, and every card rendered its `|| 0` fallback; /devices 404'd, because the vehicle function has no such branch. Two domains colliding on one prefix word is worse than a missing route: nothing errors, nothing logs, and the screen is quietly all zeroes. Third defect, independent of the collision: Order Toner posted to /api/devices/:id/order-toner, whose handler inserted device_id / order_type / items / requested_by into supply_orders. supply_orders has none of those columns - it is machine_id / color / part_number / quantity / created_by_user_id, with machine_id NOT NULL - so the insert was always a PGRST204 the handler reported as 'Failed to create toner order'. Ordering toner from this screen has never worked on either host. The page also sent `colors` while the handler read `items`, so even against the right table it would have written an empty order.
acceptanceCriteria: All four endpoints move to /api/device-monitoring, which is proxied - so dev and production run one implementation of them (this is the AUDIT-029 host, and it already owns device_registrations, device_metrics, device_alerts and device_supply_orders)
The dashboard roll-up is pure and tested: registrations are the denominator, alerts come from device_alerts rather than being re-thresholded, and metrics for a deregistered device are not counted
Order Toner writes device_supply_orders on its real columns, one row per colour, triggered_by='manual', and refuses an empty colour list rather than writing a blank order
The three Express /api/fleet/* handlers are deleted; nothing serves a printer endpoint under /api/fleet
npm run check && npm run test && npm run build pass
userStories.notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-29.

WHAT SHIPPED. Four branches added to supabase/functions/device-monitoring/: GET /fleet-dashboard, GET /fleet-devices, GET /fleet-devices/:id/metrics, POST /fleet-devices/:id/order-toner. The arithmetic is buildFleetDashboard + enrichDeviceWithMetrics in _shared/device-monitoring-shape.ts, next to the shapers the other three pages already share; 22 tests in server/tests/unit/fleet-monitoring-port.test.ts, each mutation-tested. The three Express handlers are gone and the file carries a note saying not to re-add a printer endpoint under /api/fleet.

FIELDS DELETED RATHER THAN PORTED. The old handler also returned devicesWithAlerts, averageUptime, statusDistribution and topDevicesNeedingAttention. The page has never rendered any of them, and averageUptime was onlineDevices/totalDevices under a name that promises uptime. AUDIT-019's rule applies: delete a claim with no backing measurement instead of relabelling it. fleetUtilization was the same problem in a card the page DOES render - it counted devices with a reading in the last 24 hours and printed the quotient under 'Fleet Utilization', a measurement of print volume that nothing here takes. It is now reportingRate, the card says 'Devices Reporting', and the response carries reportingDevices / totalDevices / reportingWindowHours so the caption can state the denominator.

SEARCH WAS NEVER SERVER-SIDE. The page's query key was ['/api/fleet/devices', searchQuery] and the default queryFn joins key elements with '/', so a typed term arrived as a path SEGMENT - /api/fleet/devices/abc - which the Express route never matched either. The page has always filtered client-side. The term is out of the key now and the handler takes no search or status parameter, because accepting one nothing sends is how a filter comes to look supported.

WHAT THIS EXPOSED. supabase/functions/fleet/ now has NO caller in any client tree - the printer page's mistaken /api/fleet reference was the only thing that made it look reachable, so check:unreferenced-edge-fns had a phantom pass on it. Baselined (84 -> 85). It is a complete vehicle-fleet back end - vehicles, maintenance, fuel log, GPS locations - with no UI anywhere, which is AUDIT-024's shape. Its four tables are also in no Drizzle schema and no migration, which is AUDIT-028's. Whoever picks up either should start here: it is the cleanest instance of both.

userStories.title: Twenty-one tables declared tenant_id as an integer, so no tenant could read or write them
userStories.description: tenants.id is `varchar PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()`. Twenty-one tables across four schema files declared `tenant_id integer NOT NULL`, and an integer column cannot hold a uuid, so both halves of multi-tenancy failed on every one of them. Reproduced against Postgres 16: a read filtered on a real tenant id gives 22P02 'invalid input syntax for type integer', and an insert gives 42804 'column is of type integer but expression is of type character varying'. Nothing caught it. tsc cannot: the Drizzle column type and the tenantId variable agree within each file, and the Express layer types tenantId as any, so `eq(t.tenantId, tenantId)` typechecks. check:phantom-cols reads edge functions and checks column NAMES, not types. And PostgREST leaves .data null on error while this codebase writes `?? []` around it, so the symptom was an empty dashboard, indistinguishable from a table nobody has filled in yet. Six of these tables sit in docs/unwritten-tables-baseline.json for exactly that reason - client_collected_metrics, contract_renewal_tracking, renewal_analytics, supply_monitoring, supply_replenishment_analytics and supply_usage_history were recorded as tables nothing writes to, when the truth is that nothing could. The affected features are auto-supply replenishment (5 tables), contract renewal including the routed /contract-renewal-autopilot dashboard (5), document automation (6, PROD-008d) and the printyx-client monitoring agent (5).
acceptanceCriteria: All 21 tenant_id columns are varchar in both the Drizzle schema and a journaled migration
The migration is proven to apply, not just written: run it against a real Postgres, twice, including against a database that already ran the hand-run inbound_webhook_events file
The parseInt(tenantId) workaround the wrong type forced is removed - a uuid parseInts to its leading digits or NaN, so it filtered on a tenant that does not exist
A guard prevents a new one, on both the schema side and the migration side, since either alone can be wrong
npm run check && npm run test && npm run build pass
userStories.notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-29. Found while investigating SUPA-024's document-management convergence: DocumentManagement.tsx's only possible backing tables are the document-automation ones, and they turned out to be untenantable.

PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED. Both failure modes were reproduced on Postgres 16 in this container (COP-M07's scratch instance), and migration 0062 was applied to a database built in the pre-migration shape: it converts all 21, exits 0 on a second run, exits 0 when the hand-run inbound_webhook_events file was applied first, and the insert+read that previously errored now works. Verifying a migration by reading it is how COP-M00 happened.

THE GUARD READS BOTH SIDES. scripts/check-tenant-id-types.mjs flags a Drizzle declaration whose column helper is not textual, AND replays the migration chain in journal order (CREATE TABLE establishes the type, a later ALTER COLUMN changes it) so a hand-written .sql cannot reintroduce one. Reading either side alone gives the wrong answer here, because 0000 creates these as integer and 0062 converts them. Hard gate at zero, CI-wired, mutation-tested four ways.

WHAT THE TYPE CHANGE SURFACED. 37 new tsc errors, all of them call sites that had declared `tenantId: number` to match the wrong column - 22 signatures across four services (auto-supply-replenishment, contract-renewal, document-generation, document-ocr-ai). Widening them cleared all 37 and 4 pre-existing errors on top; the ratchet went 334 -> 329. The one substantive fix among them is predictive-service-dispatch-service.ts:180, which did `eq(clientCollectedMetrics.tenantId, parseInt(tenantId))` - somebody hit the mismatch and coerced the uuid to make tsc happy, which at runtime filtered on 550 for a tenant whose id starts '550e8400'.

STILL OPEN. The migration is committed and UNAPPLIED, like 0057. Nothing in this story wires up the features these tables belong to - auto-supply replenishment, contract renewal and document automation each still need their writers reached (AUDIT-028, PROD-008d). What changed is that they can now work at all.

userStories.title: Four mobile pages, three back ends, and none of them agree about what /api/mobile is
userStories.description: CR-017 removed sixteen handlers from routes-workflow-mobile.ts that queried eight tables existing nowhere. What is left is a routing tangle nobody has decided about. FOUR ROUTED WEB PAGES call /api/mobile*: MobileServiceApp (/dashboard, /jobs, /route-optimization, /service-report), MobileFieldService (/photos, /sessions), MobileOptimization (/devices, /metrics) and MobileFieldOperations (four /api/mobile-field paths). TWO EDGE FUNCTIONS serve those prefixes - supabase/functions/mobile/ has photos, sessions and sync; supabase/functions/mobile-field/ has my-tickets, today, check-in, check-out, log-time, parts-inventory, request-parts, add-note and update-status - and NEITHER prefix is proxied, so dev and production run disjoint implementations. The result, path by path: /photos and /sessions work in production and 404 in dev; /dashboard and /route-optimization work in dev and 404 in production; /jobs, /service-report, /devices and /metrics exist on NO host at all; and all four /api/mobile-field paths are now 404 on both after CR-017 deleted the phantom-table handlers behind them. Two of the surviving dev handlers are pure fixtures: /api/mobile/dashboard returns 1247 completed jobs, a 4.8 technician rating, $2,340.50 of revenue today and a van stock inventory, at a hardcoded 40.7128/-74.006; /route-optimization is the same shape. /api/mobile/dashboard has EIGHT callers including the native app at mobile/app/(app)/(dashboard)/index.tsx, so a technician opening it sees invented numbers in dev and nothing in production. MobileFieldOperations.tsx is 1507 lines of CRUD over field_technicians, field_work_orders and voice_notes and has therefore never loaded on either host.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide what each of the four pages is for before writing any endpoint - MobileFieldOperations duplicates /technician-management (which works, over the real technicians table) for technicians and service_tickets for work orders, and its voice-notes third has no backing anywhere
Whatever survives is served by ONE host: proxy /api/mobile and /api/mobile-field and extend the edge functions, rather than adding Express handlers a proxied prefix would shadow
Delete the /api/mobile/dashboard and /route-optimization fixtures either way - they are mocks on a live page with a native-app caller (AUDIT-019's rule)
Do not ship an endpoint whose shape a page cannot consume: AUDIT-030 records why a 200 of the wrong shape is worse than the 404 it replaces
npm run check && npm run test pass
userStories.notes:
FILED 2026-08-30 out of CR-017, which fixed the half that was mechanical (sixteen handlers over eight tables that do not exist) and stopped at the half that is a product decision.

WHAT IS ALREADY ESTABLISHED, so nobody has to redo it:

THE REAL TABLES that could back these pages are technicians, service_tickets, time_tracking_entries, mobile_service_sessions, ticket_notes, parts_requests and inventory - the set supabase/functions/mobile-field/ already reads. That function is a TECHNICIAN'S OWN view (my tickets, my day, check in, log time). MobileFieldOperations is a DISPATCHER'S view of the whole fleet. Same prefix, different audience, which is most of why this drifted.

CALLER COUNTS, all seven client trees: /api/mobile/dashboard 8, /photos 5, /sessions 4, /devices 3, /mobile-field/work-orders 3, /mobile-field/voice-notes 3, /mobile-field/technicians 3, /time-tracking 2, /metrics 2, /device-tokens 2 (iOS only), /mobile-field/metrics 1. The native apps (mobile/, ios/) and the web app call overlapping but different subsets, so retiring a path needs checking against all seven, not client/src.

WORTH KNOWING BEFORE TOUCHING /api/mobile/dashboard: its fixture is the one the native dashboard screen renders. Deleting it without a replacement takes that screen from wrong-in-dev to empty-in-dev, which is the right direction but is a visible change to the app.

NOT IN SCOPE HERE and already handled: the eight phantom tables, the fabricated GPS write in POST /api/mobile/sync, and the `SELECT 95.5 as gps_accuracy` in /mobile-field/metrics are all gone (CR-017), and scripts/check-sql-string-tables.mjs now hard-gates their reintroduction.

WF-V-02 (2026-09-02): the interim technician surface is now client/src/pages/MobileFieldService.tsx, routed at /mobile-field-service/:ticketId with the bare path serving the caller's own assigned queue from /api/mobile/sync. It no longer hard-codes ticket-123/tech-456, and the mobile function takes the technician from the JWT. Point any technician-surface work here rather than at a new page.

userStories.title: Three security controls are written, exported, and applied by nothing
userStories.description: server/middleware/security-index.ts exposes applySecurityMiddleware, which is the ONLY place enforceSessionTimeout, extendSessionOnActivity, enforceIpWhitelist, requireMfaForAdmins and requireMfaVerification are ever applied - and nothing imports that file. Established by walking the import graph from server/index.ts rather than by grep, which matters here: session-timeout.ts HAS an importer (routes-session-management.ts) and so is not an orphan, but that importer takes only the helper functions (getActiveSessions, terminateSession, logoutOtherSessions, getSessionConfig) and never the enforcement middleware. File-reachable is not middleware-mounted. So today: sessions never time out on inactivity, no IP whitelist is enforced, no privileged user is ever required to hold MFA, and requireMfaVerification gates nothing. The implementations are real, not stubs - session-timeout reads per-tenant compliance_settings and tracks security_sessions; mfa-enforcement reads per-tenant MFA settings, resolves the user's role level and checks both role and path. apiVersioning and legacyRouteSupport from the same module are the exception: server/routes.ts mounts them directly, so API versioning does work. Note SEC-MFA-001 fixed the MANAGEMENT side - disabling MFA or regenerating backup codes now needs a second factor - which is a different thing from requiring an admin to have MFA at all.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide per control whether it is wanted: session idle timeout, IP whitelist, MFA-required-for-admins. Each is a behaviour change with a lockout mode, not cleanup
Whatever is enabled is verified against a real database before it ships - requireMfaForAdmins 403s an admin whose MFA is not enrolled, and enforceSessionTimeout writes to security_sessions
Enabling one means updating the annotation in security-index.ts and the assertion in server/tests/unit/server-orphans.test.ts that currently locks the not-mounted state
Whatever is not wanted is deleted rather than left exported, so the next reader does not have to re-derive that it never ran
npm run check && npm run test pass
userStories.notes:
FILED 2026-08-30, out of SEC-SESSION-001's remaining files. mfa-enforcement.ts was one of the twelve session-user-auth offenders, which is how this surfaced.

THE DURABLE HALF SHIPPED: scripts/check-server-orphans.mjs, npm run check:server-orphans, CI-wired, baseline 151. It is the server-side counterpart to check:orphan-files, walking from server/index.ts through every static and dynamic import - including routes-registry's table-driven `await import(variable)` mounts, which a scan for import(' would miss entirely. The client ratchet's own header records that four separate stories hand-rolled the same walk and threw it away; the server side had done it three times in one week (ten reporting services, team-alert-service, this). Mutation-tested four ways, including that reachability is TRANSITIVE - warehouse-reporting-service has an importer, and that importer has none.

WHAT THE BASELINE HOLDS beyond this story: 151 files, of which 13 are middleware, 39 services and 17 routers. It is a TODO list. Several entries are probably deletable and a few are probably features nobody wired, which is the PROD-008c question; the guard does not distinguish them and should not.

WHY NOTHING WAS MOUNTED IN THIS PASS. requireMfaForAdmins answers 403 to any user at or above MFA_REQUIRED_LEVEL (4, manager and up) who has not enrolled, subject to per-tenant settings this container cannot read. Turning it on blind is how an admin team locks itself out. The same goes for enforceIpWhitelist. These want a real database and a rollout order, not a commit.

userStories.title: Close the 23 sub-resource paths a page calls that its edge function never dispatches
userStories.description: As a user, a tab or button that reads a sub-resource of a record must return that sub-resource, not the record itself.
acceptanceCriteria: For each path below: implement the branch in the edge function, or delete the caller if the feature is not backed by a table.

Confirm the current behaviour per path before fixing it - a handler that reads parts[0] as the id and ignores parts[1] answers 200 WITH THE PARENT OBJECT, which a component maps over and renders as empty; that is different from a 404 and different again from a handler that dispatches on a variable the guard cannot see.
Every query filters by tenant_id AND by the parent record id - PA-021 found two handlers that filtered by tenant only and showed every customer the whole tenant fleet.
Remove each closed path from docs/edge-path-coverage-baseline.json; npm run check:edge-coverage stays green.
userStories.notes:
[ROUTING/MEDIUM] Opened 2026-08-30 by PA-025, which extended check:edge-coverage to look PAST an id. Until then the guard captured one segment and rejected anything holding a `$` or `{`, so a call shaped `/api/equipment/${id}/meter-readings` was dropped entirely - the placeholder failed the literal test and the segment behind it was never examined.

These 23 are that blind spot emptied out. They are FINDINGS, not accepted debt: each is a live page calling a sub-path whose literal segment appears nowhere in the domain edge function.

  /api/address-books/:id/export
  /api/address-books/:id/import
  /api/address-books/exports/:id/download
  /api/demos/:id/status
  /api/equipment/:id/meter-readings
  /api/equipment-lifecycle/:id/available-transitions
  /api/equipment-lifecycle/:id/can-transition/:id
  /api/import/jobs/:id/duplicates/:id/resolve
  /api/integrations/:id/disconnect
  /api/integrations/:id/test
  /api/integrations/calendar/:id/connect
  /api/integrations/calendar/:id/events
  /api/integrations/calendar/:id/events/:id
  /api/manufacturer-integrations/:id/discover
  /api/onboarding/checklists/:id/generate-pdf
  /api/platform-crm/assignment-rules/:id/test
  /api/platform-crm/assignment-rules/:id/toggle
  /api/platform-crm/business-records/:id/convert-to-tenant
  /api/platform-deals/:id/bant
  /api/social-media/cron-jobs/:id/execute
  /api/social-media/posts/:id/broadcast
  /api/tasks/:id/timer/start
  /api/tasks/:id/timer/stop

SPOT-CHECKED BY HAND, so the list is not taken on the tool word: equipment/:id/meter-readings is called by CustomerEquipment.tsx and the equipment function has exactly one GET-with-id branch, which returns the equipment row - the silent-200 shape. integrations/:id/test is called by SystemIntegrations.tsx, platform-deals/:id/bant by PlatformDealDetail.tsx, and social-media/posts/:id/broadcast by SocialMediaGenerator.tsx (which also uses a raw fetch, a separate class). None of the four segments appears in its function.

A guard match is not proof either way - the header says so - so confirm each before changing it. Three of the first four paths checked under a quoted-literal-only rule were FALSE positives, because a handler can name a segment without quoting it on its own (`path === '/summary'`, or a regex `/^\/public\/([^/]+)\/respond$/`). The matcher was tightened for that and 16 such entries left the baseline; the 23 here survived it.

PROGRESS 2026-09-01 (commits 651aab7, beaba51, f944348, f6882ec, 6ff4061):

  [x] /api/equipment/:id/meter-readings
  [x] /api/platform-deals/:id/bant
  [x] /api/integrations/:id/disconnect
  [x] /api/integrations/:id/test

The two shapes the story predicted both turned up, one each. equipment reads
parts[0] as the id and never looks at parts[1], so the sub-path landed in the
single-equipment GET and answered 200 WITH THE EQUIPMENT ROW - the silent-200.
platform-deals already gates every branch on `!subResource`, so its unmatched
sub-path fell to the trailing 404 instead. Confirm which one you have before
writing the branch; they need different regression tests.

A third defect rode along on the first path and is worth expecting elsewhere:
CustomerEquipment.tsx's MeterReading interface (currentMeterCount /
previousMeterCount / printVolume / readingType) matches no table. A caller that
has never received real data has no pressure to name real columns, so a
silent-200 path is a likely place to find a phantom shape - budget for the
re-bind, not just the branch.

BOTH HOSTS: /api/equipment is NOT in crmProxies, so dev is Express and prod is
the edge fn; the branch needed a mirror in routes-mobile-api.ts. /api/platform-
deals IS proxied, so routes-platform-deals.ts is shadowed and the edge fn was
the only place to change. Check crmProxies per path before assuming one or two
edits.

platform_bant_qualification has NO tenant_id (platform-level; the root-admin
gate is the control) and is keyed on business_record_id UNIQUE with an optional
deal_id, so the lookup tries deal_id then falls back through the deal's
business_record_id. No row answers assessed:false with a null status - the page
was rendering `|| 0` scores whether or not an assessment existed, so returning
zeros would have kept the bug.

server/tests/unit/edge-path-depth.test.ts used equipment/:id/meter-readings as
its worked example and asserted it was IN the baseline; that assertion is now
inverted. Expect to touch it again as more entries close.

4 of 23 closed, 19 left. A THIRD outcome shape turned up beyond the two the
story predicted: neither of these paths was REACHABLE in production, because
GET /api/integrations answers a bare array on Express and { data, total, page,
limit } on the edge fn, and the page did `(integrations || []).filter(...)` - so
prod threw before any button rendered. Check that a page renders at all before
concluding a sub-path is the only thing wrong with it; extractRecords is the
settled answer to that split (PA-021).

The honest-answer question bit here too. Neither backend can contact an
arbitrary provider from a /test endpoint, so the edge branch checks credential
completeness against INTEGRATION_CONFIGS and returns connectivityVerified:false,
and the page renders the returned message. The old toast said "The integration
is working correctly" on any 2xx, which was a claim about a provider the call
never reached. If a /test path in the remaining 19 has no provider client behind
it, do the same rather than answering a bare 200.

Filed PA-053 from this path: /api/integrations is one prefix over TWO TABLES
(system_integrations in dev, platform_integrations in prod) and the page's field
shape matches neither, so its list is still empty on both hosts. That is a
data-contract rewrite, deliberately not folded in here.

  [x] /api/demos/:id/status
  [-] /api/tasks/:id/timer/start   FALSE POSITIVE
  [-] /api/tasks/:id/timer/stop    FALSE POSITIVE

7 of 23 accounted for (5 fixed, 2 false positives), 16 left. Commit f944348.

A FOURTH outcome, and the worst so far: the path is missing because the whole
FEATURE is unbuilt, and both hosts fake it. /demo-scheduling's create button
answered 201 with a hand-built object and no insert, in an edge function whose
every branch was a TODO saying the demos table did not exist - while
demo_schedules has been in migration 0000 all along. Before implementing a
sub-path, check that its siblings write anything; here /:id/status was the least
of it. Grep the table name in drizzle/migrations before believing a TODO that
says a table is missing.

Two traps that came with it. server/routes-demo-scheduling.ts read as the real
router (seven handlers, real schema imports, validation) and was registered by
nothing, and its own POST also said "return success response until schema is
updated" - so wiring the orphan up would have shipped the same fiction. And
GET /demos/customers selected `status` from `companies`, a column that table does
not have, so it 42703'd: the picker was empty and no demo could be created even
to be lost. check:phantom-cols does not see it because `companies` is one of the
14 tables declared twice.

THE TIMER PAIR WAS A FALSE POSITIVE, of a kind the guard's own header predicted
and the story's second AC asks you to look for. Both verbs are fully implemented;
the dispatcher just composed the op name as `timer-${parts[2]}`, so neither
'start' nor 'stop' appeared as a token anywhere. Fixed on the SOURCE side rather
than by loosening appearsIn - the dispatcher now enumerates the two verbs, which
is what a reader needs anyway, and closes the "any third segment is forwarded and
fails deeper in" behaviour. Do not widen the matcher to accept a segment after a
hyphen; 'e-automate' would then satisfy a gap named 'automate'.

  [x] /api/manufacturer-integrations/:id/discover  (501, honestly - see PA-054)

8 of 23 accounted for, 15 left.

TWO BASELINES HELD THE TWO HALVES OF THIS ONE, and neither entry pointed at the
other - PA-020's lesson, again. docs/raw-api-fetch-baseline.json recorded all
three of ManufacturerIntegration.tsx's fetch() calls; this baseline recorded the
missing /discover branch. A raw fetch carries no Authorization header, so those
buttons would have 401'd in production even once the branch existed. When a
finding here names a page, grep the OTHER baselines for that page before
starting.

THE PATH WAS MISSING FOR A THIRD REASON BESIDES THE BRANCH: the edge function
looked every per-integration path up with .eq('manufacturer', parts[0]), and
`manufacturer` is a pgEnum while the only caller passes integration.id. A uuid in
an enum filter is 22P02 - a 500, not a miss - so /test was broken in prod too,
and Express keys the same paths by id, so the page worked in dev. parts[0] is now
resolved as id-or-name (uuid shape decides, and a uuid never reaches the enum
column). Worth checking in the remaining 15: a branch can exist and still never
match, if the two hosts address the resource differently.

/discover answers 501 rather than a number it did not achieve, because discovery
runs the four vendor adapters in server/manufacturer-integration-service.ts and
the browser cannot reach Express in production at all. Filed as PA-054. Both
hosts' /test were also fabricating - Express returned Math.random() > 0.3 as a
connection RESULT (check:no-random-metrics misses it: the value is a const, not a
property assigned on one line), the edge function returned an unconditional
"Connection to X is working" under a comment saying a real test would go here.
Both now report what is stored, with connectivityVerified false.

  [x] /api/social-media/posts/:id/broadcast
  [x] /api/social-media/cron-jobs/:id/execute

10 of 23 accounted for, 13 left. Commit 6ff4061.

THE TWO BASELINED PATHS WERE TWO OF SIX DEFECTS ON THAT ONE FUNCTION, which is
the pattern to expect from here on: a domain missing a sub-path is usually a
domain nobody has diffed against its Express counterpart. The others were
cron-jobs POST/PUT/DELETE (only the list existed), a /generate that returned
hand-written marketing copy with generated:true on it, and TWO branches missing
a `!postId` guard - the list branch swallowed GET /posts/:id, and the create-post
branch swallowed POST /posts/generate, so the page's Generate button wrote a post
out of the generate FORM instead of generating one. When you add a branch behind
an id, check the branches ABOVE it for the same missing guard; that is a
two-character bug with a large blast radius.

A PORT CAN CARRY A SECURITY CONTROL WITH IT. broadcast posts to a
tenant-supplied webhook URL from a function holding the service-role key, and
Express has guarded that with safeFetch since CR-005, so the port needed
supabase/functions/_shared/{ssrf,safe-fetch}.ts first - same ranges, same
hostnames, same redirect re-validation - locked by
server/tests/unit/ssrf-parity.test.ts. Deno.resolveDns replaces dns.resolve4/6
and a PermissionDenied is treated as a REFUSAL, not as "no records": failing open
in that branch would disable the whole control silently. Any remaining path that
sends to a user-supplied URL should import that helper rather than fetch().

  [x] /api/address-books/:id/export          501 + PA-055
  [x] /api/address-books/:id/import          501 + PA-055
  [x] /api/address-books/import              501 + PA-055
  [x] /api/address-books/exports             501 + PA-055
  [x] /api/address-books/exports/:id/download 501 + PA-055

15 of 23 accounted for, 8 left.

A CLOSED STORY CAN BE THE FINDING. ABK-014 is titled "Edge function: address book
import + export endpoints", every one of its nine acceptance criteria names an
edge endpoint, and it is marked passes:true - while the edge function serves
books and entries CRUD only. Its own closure note says what happened: the work
shipped as Express routes and "bringing the Supabase edge function to
import/export parity for prod remains a follow-up". That follow-up was never
filed, so passes:true has been asserting the opposite for two months. Filed as
PA-055 and ABK-014's note corrected in place (CRMX-011a's rule). Before treating
a passing story as evidence that an endpoint exists, read its closure note - the
one here was honest and nobody had connected it to anything.

Three of the eight remaining are the equipment-lifecycle pair and the
import/jobs duplicate-resolve path; expect the same question there, since these
five could not be ported in a tick: ~1,350 lines of vendor parsers, multipart
upload, and an export cache that is an IN-PROCESS Map with a 15-minute TTL. That
last one is not just unportable - it is already wrong behind a second Node
instance, so an export generated on one and downloaded from another 404s today.
When a path cannot move, check whether the thing blocking it is also broken where
it currently lives.

The download's 404 was the misleading kind: /exports/:id/download made bookId the
literal string "exports", so getBook answered "Address book not found" - a
message about the wrong noun entirely. All five now answer 501 naming the host,
which is what a production log needs.

  [x] /api/platform-crm/assignment-rules
  [x] /api/platform-crm/assignment-rules/:id/test
  [x] /api/platform-crm/assignment-rules/:id/toggle

18 of 23 accounted for, 5 left - all in platform-crm: territories, managers,
scoring-models, scoring-rules, business-records/:id/convert-to-tenant.

A THIRD `!resourceId` GUARD WAS MISSING, this time on a proxied prefix so it was
broken on BOTH hosts: GET /platform-crm/business-records matched
/business-records/:id and /:id/contacts as well and returned the paginated LIST,
making the single-record and contacts branches below it unreachable since they
were written. Three instances now (two in social-media, one here). Grep for
`endpoint === '<x>'` without a `!resourceId` before adding anything behind an id.

THE ENDPOINTS EXISTED NOWHERE - not this function, not Express - while
platform_lead_assignment_rules had been in the schema all along. Four routed
pages call this family and three of them are still unserved. Expect the same for
the remaining five, and check the table before assuming it needs building.

The page was a phantom shape on top of that, so the two halves had to land
together: it posted `name` where the column is `rule_name`, offered two
assignment types the column's vocabulary does not contain, and collected six
filter fields (lead grades, lead tiers, record statuses, regions, company size,
annual revenue) that no column stores - conditions that would have vanished on
save. Deleted rather than defaulted, per AUDIT-016. Its two stat cards summed
fields nothing records; platform_lead_assignment_history could back the
assignment count with a server-side aggregate, which is worth doing when
/territories lands.

/test reports `unevaluated` beside the count, because company_size and geography
are jsonb here with no matching column on platform_business_records, and deal
size lives on platform_deals. A match count with two of five criteria silently
skipped is a different claim from the one the toast was making.

  [x] /api/platform-crm/territories
  [x] /api/platform-crm/managers

20 of 23 accounted for, 3 left: scoring-models, scoring-rules and
business-records/:id/convert-to-tenant. Commit dc3067d.

/managers being unserved is why the assignment-rule work in 9fe62ef could not
name a target: the picker was empty on every platform CRM page. When two pages
share a lookup endpoint, fixing one page's CRUD does not make it usable - check
what its selects are populated from.

A FOREIGN KEY IS PART OF THE ENDPOINT. platform_lead_assignment_rules.
assign_to_territory_id references platform_sales_territories, so DELETE had to
check it and name the rules still pointing at the territory; a blind delete is a
23503 the caller reads as "something went wrong". Same shape as `code` being
UNIQUE - answered 409 rather than letting a duplicate surface as a 500. Worth
doing on every delete branch in the remaining work.

owner_id is NOT NULL and the form never collected it, so a create defaults it to
the caller rather than failing. That is the demo_schedules contact_person
decision again (f944348): when a NOT NULL column holds something the form
legitimately does not ask for, derive it from context instead of blocking the
write or inventing a value.

  [x] /api/platform-crm/scoring-rules
  [x] /api/platform-crm/scoring-models   NO TABLE - caller removed

22 of 23 accounted for. One left: business-records/:id/convert-to-tenant.
Commit 25b384a.

AN UNSERVED ENDPOINT CAN GATE THE REST OF ITS PAGE. PlatformLeadScoring fetched
scoring-models, which nothing served, and then gated its rule list on the
result - `enabled: !!selectedModelId`. No model could load, so the rules query
never ran, so the page was inert end to end. Fixing scoring-rules alone would
have changed nothing visible. When a page has two queries and one feeds a
selector, check whether the second is enabled on the first.

A BROKEN QUERY KEY CAN HIDE BEHIND A DEAD ENDPOINT. The rules key was
['/api/platform-crm/scoring-rules', selectedModelId] and getQueryFn joins with
'/', so a selected model would have requested /scoring-rules/<modelId>. Nobody
ever saw it because the query never ran. Third instance of the query-key defect
in this repo, first one masked by a second bug.

scoring-models had no table and no endpoint, so the caller went, per this
story's second option. Grades and tiers are pgEnums on
platform_business_records and nothing stores a threshold mapping a score onto
one, so the model's grade A/B/C/D and tier hot/warm/cold settings would have
changed no grade. Deleted rather than mocked.

TWO VOCABULARIES WERE INVENTED, and both are validated server-side now: category
offered 'technographic' (the column's list is demographic | firmographic |
behavioral | engagement | bant) and the operators were camelCase
greaterThan/lessThan plus a 'between' the table cannot express. A rule saved
under either would never be read by any scorer - the same class as COP-E02's two
stage vocabularies. Check the column COMMENT for a vocabulary before trusting the
select options a page offers.

  [x] /api/platform-crm/business-records/:id/convert-to-tenant

COUNT CORRECTED. The running totals in the notes above ("15 of 23", "18 of 23",
"22 of 23") were WRONG: they counted BASELINE ENTRIES removed, and several of
those are not on this story's list of 23 - platform-crm/territories, /managers,
/scoring-models, /scoring-rules and the two depth-1 address-books entries were
all closed alongside the listed paths but were never part of the 23. Against the
story's own list the true figure is 16 of 23 done, 7 left:

  [ ] /api/equipment-lifecycle/:id/available-transitions
  [ ] /api/equipment-lifecycle/:id/can-transition/:id
  [ ] /api/import/jobs/:id/duplicates/:id/resolve
  [ ] /api/integrations/calendar/:id/connect
  [ ] /api/integrations/calendar/:id/events
  [ ] /api/integrations/calendar/:id/events/:id
  [ ] /api/onboarding/checklists/:id/generate-pdf

The check that settles it, rather than a tally kept by hand: intersect the
story's 23 against the flattened baseline. Do that instead of counting commits.

The last one was also the cleanest instance of the whole story's shape. Every
column the conversion needs was already on platform_business_records -
record_type, tenant_id, converted_from_prospect_at, converted_by,
conversion_source - and the caller had been posting a placeholder
{ tenantId: 'new-tenant-id' } under a comment saying it "would be generated". The
work was never blocked on schema or on a decision; the endpoint simply did not
exist and no one had looked.

Three write-path rules worth carrying into the remaining seven: a second
conversion would orphan the first tenant, so answer 409 naming what the record
already points at; a UNIQUE slug gets suffixed on collision rather than failing
the whole operation; and when step two fails after step one succeeded, return
what WAS created, because a bare 500 reads as "nothing happened" and the retry
makes a duplicate.

  [x] /api/equipment-lifecycle/:id/available-transitions
  [x] /api/equipment-lifecycle/:id/can-transition/:id

18 of 23 done, 5 left. Commit 9880b02.

  [ ] /api/import/jobs/:id/duplicates/:id/resolve
  [ ] /api/integrations/calendar/:id/connect
  [ ] /api/integrations/calendar/:id/events
  [ ] /api/integrations/calendar/:id/events/:id
  [ ] /api/onboarding/checklists/:id/generate-pdf

PORTING A PATH IS HOW YOU FIND OUT WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES. These two were a
straightforward port of a pure state machine until the validator turned out to
be a stub: runValidations() says "Mock: assume all pass for now" and returned
passed:true with "<requirement> verified" for every requirement, which the dialog
drew as a green tick per row plus a progress bar that always read 100%. Moving a
machine to Disposed showed "Data Wiped Confirmed - verified" and "Certificate Of
Destruction - verified" over nothing. Both hosts now report the requirements as
outstanding with requirementsChecked:false. Read the function a branch depends on
before porting the branch; a mock two calls deep is invisible from the route.

isValid stays TRUE rather than flipping to false. Neither answer can be
established, and refusing every transition that has requirements at all would be
a different false claim - the honest move was to say what is unknown and leave
the decision with the operator. Worth reusing wherever a "validation" turns out
to be unimplemented.

THE ABSENCE-ASSERTION TRAP FIRED AGAIN, third time in this repo's history: the
parity test asserts the dialog no longer reads validation.passed.length, and the
JSX comment explaining why the progress bar was removed names that expression, so
the first run reported its own explanation as the defect. Strip comments on both
sides of any absence check.

ON THE REMAINING FIVE: onboarding/checklists/:id/generate-pdf is a real port, not
a blocked decision - Express uses puppeteer, but supabase/functions/proposals/
already renders PDFs with pdf-lib via esm.sh plus a section renderer
(_html-to-pdf.ts), and several edge functions already upload to Supabase Storage.
The work is rewriting the 251-line checklist HTML as sections that renderer
handles, since it degrades unknown divs to text and the template is built from
flex field-groups. Do not port the CSS.

  [x] /api/integrations/calendar/:id/connect
  [x] /api/integrations/calendar/:id/events
  [x] /api/integrations/calendar/:id/events/:id

21 of 23 done, 2 left: import/jobs/:id/duplicates/:id/resolve and
onboarding/checklists/:id/generate-pdf.

THE PATH WAS NOT MISSING, IT WAS THE WRONG ADDRESS. CalendarProvider called
/api/integrations/calendar/{type}/connect|events|events/:id, which nothing has
ever served, while supabase/functions/meetings/ serves the same capability at
/api/meetings/calendar/* over calendar_connections and calendar_events - with the
real Google and Microsoft clients in _shared/google.ts and _shared/microsoft.ts,
and push propagation to the provider on create, update and delete. The fix was
pointing the caller at the surface that works, not building a fourth calendar
implementation. Before implementing any remaining path, grep _shared/ for the
capability: two of this story's paths turned out to be duplicates of live code.

THE COMPONENT WAS INERT IN A WAY THAT HID THE OTHER TWO PATHS. `providers` was
two hardcoded entries with isConnected:false and nothing ever set it true, so
createEvent, updateEvent and deleteEvent all threw "Calendar provider not
connected" before reaching any endpoint. Both /events paths therefore had NO
reachable caller - which is why nobody had reported them. disconnectProvider only
mutated local state, so it always toasted success and the provider reappeared on
the next render.

A SCOPED PROXY ENTRY, NOT A WHOLE-PREFIX ONE. Express owns the rest of
/api/meetings through meeting-scheduling-routes and meeting-transcription-routes,
both mounted at the /api root, and serves nothing under /calendar - so
'/api/meetings/calendar' is proxied with a pathPrefix and the scheduling and
transcription handlers keep working in dev.

Filed PA-056: connecting still cannot work, because no authorize flow for
CALENDAR scopes exists that production can reach. oauth-proxy requests sign-in
scopes; the real consent flow is Express-only AND writes to system_integrations,
while the events code reads calendar_connections. Two stores, one capability.

  [x] /api/import/jobs/:id/duplicates/:id/resolve

22 of 23 done. One left: onboarding/checklists/:id/generate-pdf.

THE MISSING BRANCH WAS THE SMALLEST PART. The per-row resolve buttons 404'd, but
the whole review step around them was decorative: validation set
duplicates_detected:0 and recorded nothing, GET /duplicates returned [] always,
and resolve-all answered "Duplicates resolved" without touching a row - WHILE the
execute path matched every row against existing companies (name + city + state,
falling back to name + phone) and merged into whatever it found. The user was
shown nothing to review, told duplicates were resolved, and their rows were
merged into records they never saw. csv_import_duplicates, with row_number,
match_score, matching_fields and a resolution enum, had existed all along.

A RULE THAT EXISTS TWICE IS A RULE THAT DISAGREES WITH ITSELF. Detection and
execute now share _shared/import-duplicate-match.ts; if they drift, the user
reviews one set of duplicates and the import merges a different one, which is
worse than not asking. The case the test pins hardest: a NAME ALONE is not a
duplicate - two customers can share a name in different states, and merging them
on that basis is the damage the review exists to prevent.

HONOURING A DECISION IS PART OF OFFERING IT. Execute skips rows resolved `skip`.
`create_new` is recorded and still merges, because forcing a second company row
means bypassing the match; rather than do that silently the response carries an
`unhonoured` line, so the count cannot read as a clean import. Same shape as the
`unbacked`/`unevaluated` arrays elsewhere in this story.

Two traps in the detection pass worth reusing: re-running it must DELETE the
previous rows or a second validation stacks duplicates; and a failed candidate
lookup must not be treated as "no duplicate", because skipping the row there
sends it straight to execute, which merges without asking.

A python replace() without an assert silently did nothing when its anchor was
absent (this file has no normalizePath import), and only the parity test caught
it. Assert every anchor.

  [x] /api/onboarding/checklists/:id/generate-pdf

ALL 23 DONE. Verified by intersecting the story's list against the flattened
baseline, not by counting commits: 0 remain.

  16 implemented against real tables
   4 answered honestly where the work is a port or a decision, each with a story
     (address-books x3 -> PA-055, manufacturer discover -> PA-054)
   2 false positives (the task timer pair), fixed on the SOURCE side so the
     accepted verbs are visible to a reader and to the guard
   1 repointed at the surface that already served it (the calendar trio counts
     as three of the 16 above)

I FILED A HIGH-SEVERITY BUG AGAINST A DEAD FILE. Reading
supabase/functions/onboarding-checklists/, I found it querying `onboarding_checklists`
(the user lifecycle progress record) while filtering on customer_id and status,
which are not columns on it, and embedding `sections:onboarding_sections`, a
relation in no schema - and wrote it up as the whole onboarding surface being
dead in production. It is not: segment 0 resolves to supabase/functions/onboarding/,
which uses equipment_onboarding_checklists and onboarding_dynamic_sections
correctly. The file I read is a second directory nothing reaches, already in
docs/unreferenced-edge-fns-baseline.json. PA-057 is now a cleanup story for
deleting it.

What made it convincing was COP-M01's annotation on that dead function: a careful,
specific 501 arguing the CALLER's model was wrong. Every field it named maps onto
the table the LIVE function uses. A well-reasoned note on a dead file is
indistinguishable from one on a live file. Check which directory the router
resolves - ls the function dir against the URL's first segment - before believing
a finding, and check the unreferenced baseline before writing one up.

THE PDF WAS A PORT, NOT A BLOCKER, and the same is true of PA-055's. puppeteer
does not run in an edge function, but supabase/functions/proposals/ already
renders PDFs with pdf-lib through a section renderer, and several functions
already upload to Supabase Storage. What does NOT port is the CSS: that renderer
degrades unknown tags to bare text, so a template built from display:flex
label/value divs comes out as a wall. Re-emit the content as headings and tables
and it renders cleanly. Before concluding a rendering path cannot move, grep
_shared/ and the other functions for the capability - twice in this story the
answer was already in the tree.

CORRECTED 2026-09-02 by WF-L-01. The two equipment-lifecycle paths above are marked
[x], and the branches were written correctly - but NOTHING COULD REACH THEM. The same
commit that added them left index.ts importing canTransition, getAvailableTransitions
and getValidationRequirements from _shared/equipment-lifecycle-transitions.ts while
also re-declaring all three locally, which is a JavaScript SyntaxError. server.ts loads
each function inside a try/catch and omits the ones that throw, so /api/equipment-
lifecycle/* answered 404 "Function not found" in production for the life of the file.
The prefix is not proxied, so dev was served by Express and never exercised it.

So this story's own closing rule - verify against the artifact, not against the commit -
has a second half: a branch that exists is not a branch that runs. check:edge-coverage
reads the file as text and cannot tell the difference. The standing guard is WF-G-01
(npm run check:edge-boot); it is what would have caught this the day the port landed.

userStories.title: Converge /api/integrations onto one table and re-bind SystemIntegrations to real columns
userStories.description: As an admin, the System Integrations page must list the integrations I actually have, from the same table in dev and production.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide which table backs /system-integrations - system_integrations (OAuth connections) or platform_integrations (connector catalogue) - and record the decision in the page header and in CLAUDE.md.

Converge the other host onto it with PER-PATH proxy entries. A bare /api/integrations entry is rejected: Express owns oauth/init and :provider/callback, which the edge function does not serve, and the proxy forwards the whole prefix.
Re-bind every field SystemIntegrations.tsx reads to a real column; delete the ones with no backing column rather than defaulting them (description has none).

Replace the hardcoded Device Management / Accounting / CRM category list with the categories the chosen table actually holds; an integration in no listed category must still be reachable, not silently dropped.
Resolve the three status vocabularies in ONE shared map, not by widening the union in the page.
The list renders the tenant real rows in dev AND against the edge function; an empty tenant shows an empty state, not three empty category cards.
userStories.notes:
[ROUTING/MEDIUM] Opened 2026-09-01 by PA-052, which added the /:id/disconnect and
/:id/test branches this page calls and could not verify them against a rendering
page.

/system-integrations is routed and its integration list is EMPTY on both hosts,
for two independent reasons stacked on each other.

ONE PREFIX, TWO TABLES. /api/integrations is not in crmProxies, so dev is
server/integrations/routes.ts over `system_integrations` (the OAuth connection
store: name/provider/type/status/configuration/credentials/last_sync) and prod is
supabase/functions/integrations/ over `platform_integrations` (the connector
catalogue: integration_key/integration_name/category/sync_frequency/
last_synced_at/last_sync_status). Different row sets behind one prefix - AUDIT-031's
shape, without even the 404 that usually exposes it.

A BARE PROXY ENTRY IS NOT THE FIX, and this is the part to get right before
starting. Express owns POST /api/integrations/oauth/init and
GET /api/integrations/:provider/callback - the real Google/Microsoft OAuth flow,
over `system_integrations` - and the edge function has neither. crmProxies
forwards the WHOLE prefix and falls through only on a network error, so proxying
would take OAuth from working-in-dev to 404-in-dev.

THE PAGE'S OWN SHAPE MATCHES NEITHER. SystemIntegrations.tsx's `Integration`
interface is name/category/description/status/provider/lastSync/config, and:
  - `description` is a column on neither table.
  - `category` is hardcoded in the render to 'Device Management' | 'Accounting' |
    'CRM'. platform_integrations.category holds erp/crm/ai/data-enrichment, and
    the Express response carries no category at all. So the three category cards
    filter to nothing whatever the backend answers - this is why the list is
    empty even after PA-052 fixed the crash.
  - `status` is read as connected|disconnected|error|pending.
    platform_integrations documents configured|active|error|paused (and the edge
    fn's own isActive helper already tolerates three spellings);
    system_integrations documents active|inactive|error|pending while DEFAULTING
    to 'disconnected'. Three vocabularies.

The work: decide which table backs this page, converge the other host onto it
(per-path proxy entries, since the prefix cannot be taken whole), then re-bind
every field the page reads to real columns and drop the ones with no column -
EnhancedProductAccessories/Vendors recipe. Do not resolve the status vocabulary
by widening the union in the page; put it in one shared map.

Already done by PA-052, do not redo: extractRecords on the list (the prod
`.filter is not a function` crash), the /:id/disconnect and /:id/test branches on
both hosts, and the deletion of the typed-in 99.2% Success Rate card.

DONE 2026-09-01, commit c4f449e.

THE DECISION, for the record: platform_integrations backs /system-integrations.
Three reasons, in order of weight - it is the only candidate with a `category`
column and the page groups by category; production has always served
/api/integrations from it; and the integration hub dashboard already reads it.
system_integrations remains the OAuth CONNECTION store behind /oauth/init and
/:provider/callback (PA-056).

AC 2 WAS NOT ACHIEVABLE AS WRITTEN and the reason is worth keeping: the proxy
registers with app.use(prefix), which is PREFIX matching, so there is no way to
express "/api/integrations/:id/test" as an entry, and a bare '/api/integrations'
would swallow the OAuth pair the edge function does not serve. Converging the
TABLE delivers what the AC wanted - one store behind one URL on both hosts -
without moving the OAuth flow. When an AC names a mechanism rather than an
outcome, check the mechanism exists before planning around it.

Two defects found in passing, both worse than the divergence the story was filed
for. The Connect dialog posted a hardcoded
`config: { apiKey: 'test', endpoint: 'test' }` and ignored all three of its
inputs, so it stored the literal string 'test' as an API key. And the edge
function's update branch mapped `isEnabled` onto `is_enabled`, not a column on
platform_integrations, so any caller sending it got a PGRST204.

The empty list had TWO causes stacked, and PA-052 only cleared the first. The
`.filter is not a function` crash was one; the other was the category cards being
hardcoded to Device Management / Accounting / CRM while the column holds
erp/crm/ai/data-enrichment, so every group filtered to nothing whatever the
backend answered. Fixing a crash does not mean a page renders.

userStories.title: Port the manufacturer device adapters to the edge so discovery and metric collection run in production
userStories.description: As a dealer admin, Discover Devices and metric collection must work in production, not only against the dev Express server.
acceptanceCriteria: Move the four manufacturer adapters (discoverDevices, registerDevice, collectMetrics) into supabase/functions/_shared/ and call them from the manufacturer-integrations discover branch, which currently answers 501.
Do the same for POST /api/devices/:deviceId/collect, which has the same Node-only shape.
Devices land in device_registrations filtered by tenant_id AND integration_id, and a discovery run that registers nothing says so rather than reporting a count it did not achieve.
A vendor API that errors surfaces the failure; it must not be swallowed into an empty device list that reads as a successful discovery of zero devices.
Check drizzle/cron/ for a scheduled caller before deleting the Node copy.
Do not add a bare /api/manufacturer-integrations proxy entry as part of this - it would break discovery in dev until the port lands.
userStories.notes:
[ROUTING/MEDIUM] Opened 2026-09-01 by PA-052, which added the /:id/discover
branch the page calls and could only answer 501 from it.

MFP device discovery cannot run in production. The per-manufacturer adapters
live in server/manufacturer-integration-service.ts - four classes, each a
discoverDevices() that fetches the vendor API and a registerDevice() whose result
is inserted into device_registrations - and the browser cannot reach Express in
production, because getApiUrl rewrites /api/* straight to the functions host. So
the Discover button worked in dev, 404'd in prod, and now answers 501 saying why.

The same applies to POST /api/devices/:deviceId/collect (metric collection),
which is the other half of that service and has the identical shape.

The logic is portable - plain fetch plus an insert, no Node-only APIs - so the
work is mechanical rather than architectural: move the four adapters to
supabase/functions/_shared/, have the edge branch call them, and keep the Node
copy only if the scheduled collector still needs it (check whether anything in
drizzle/cron/ posts to it before deciding). Credentials come out of the
integration row, which is already encrypted at rest per PA-013's scope.

Do NOT settle this by proxying /api/manufacturer-integrations to the edge
function as it stands: the edge copy has no discovery, so that would take
discovery from working-in-dev to 501-in-dev as well.

Already done by PA-052, do not redo: the id-vs-manufacturer-name lookup (the
edge function keyed every per-integration path on the `manufacturer` pgEnum
while the only caller passes a uuid, which is 22P02 rather than a miss), the
three raw fetch() calls on the page, and the fabricated /test results on both
hosts - Express returned Math.random() > 0.3 as a connection result, the edge
function returned an unconditional "Connection to X is working".

DONE 2026-09-01, commit 02878d2.

AC 5 checked and answered: nothing in drizzle/cron/ calls discovery or
collection, so no scheduled caller keeps the Node copy alive. It stays regardless
because Express still serves dev - which is what
server/tests/unit/manufacturer-adapters-parity.test.ts exists for. No
/api/manufacturer-integrations proxy entry was added (AC 6).

A VENDOR FAILURE IS NOT AN EMPTY FLEET, and this one had been reported as one
since the feature was written: every adapter's discoverDevices catches its own
fetch error and returns [], so "could not reach the vendor" and "this customer
has no devices" were the same answer. The branch answers 502 when the adapter
throws, and when it genuinely returns nothing it says which of the two that might
be. Worth looking for wherever an adapter or client swallows its own error and
returns a collection.

NO UPSERT WAS AVAILABLE. device_registrations indexes (tenant_id, device_id) and
integration_id, neither unique, and PostgREST's onConflict needs a unique
constraint - so an upsert would have failed outright, and a plain insert would
duplicate the whole fleet on every re-run. Existing ids are read first and
updated in place. Check for the CONSTRAINT, not just an index, before writing an
onConflict.

SCOPE GREW BY ONE PAGE, correctly: /api/devices is proxied by neither host, so
the list and per-device metrics on ManufacturerIntegrationDevices.tsx 404'd in
production too. Serving all three from device-monitoring - which already owns
device_registrations and device_metrics per AUDIT-031 - was cheaper than leaving
a page where one button works and the list behind it does not.

userStories.title: Bring address book import/export to the edge function (the follow-up ABK-014 named and never filed)
userStories.description: As a service admin, importing and exporting an MFP address book must work in production, not only against the dev Express server.
acceptanceCriteria: Port the four vendor parser/serializer pairs, _shared csv/encoding/options, canon/crypto.ts and the conversion engine into supabase/functions/_shared/address-book/, and lock them against the Node copies with a parity test.
Serve POST /import, POST /:id/import (both with ?preview=true), POST /:id/export and GET /exports/:id/download from the edge function; the 501 stubs PA-052 added come out.
Multipart follows the importCsvDegraded pattern in supabase/functions/service-products/index.ts, capped at 25 MB.

Decide where generated export bytes live - Supabase Storage, a column on address_book_exports, or regeneration on download - and apply the same answer on the Express side, replacing the in-process exportCache Map that cannot survive a second Node instance.
Source passwords are never persisted to disk, DB or logs, and the grep-based test asserting it covers the edge copy too.
Correct ABK-014 rather than leaving it asserting an edge implementation that does not exist.
userStories.notes:
[ROUTING/MEDIUM] Opened 2026-09-01 by PA-052. This is the follow-up ABK-014's own
closure note says is outstanding - "bringing the Supabase edge function to
import/export parity for prod remains a follow-up (constrained multipart)" -
which was never filed, on a story whose title is "Edge function: address book
import + export endpoints" and whose every acceptance criterion names an edge
endpoint that does not exist. The Express implementation is real and complete;
the edge one was never started.

Five paths the address-book UI calls, all Express-only:

  POST /api/address-books/import              (+ ?preview=true)
  POST /api/address-books/:id/import          (+ ?preview=true)
  POST /api/address-books/:id/export
  GET  /api/address-books/exports/:id/download

In production each fell to the function's generic 404, and the download fell into
getBook() looking up an address book whose id is the literal "exports", answering
"Address book not found" - a message about the wrong thing entirely. PA-052 made
all five answer 501 with the reason; that is a signpost, not the fix.

THREE THINGS HAVE TO MOVE, and the third is a design decision, not a port:

1. ~1,350 lines of vendor parsers and serializers under
   server/services/address-book/vendors (canon, konica, ricoh, xerox, plus
   _shared csv/encoding/options and canon/crypto.ts) and the 123-line
   conversion-engine. These are pure and unit-tested, so they move cleanly, but
   the credential vault has a Deno counterpart already
   (supabase/functions/_shared/credential-vault.ts) and the two must not diverge
   - lock them the way ssrf-parity.test.ts locks the SSRF lists.

2. Multipart upload. Express uses multer; the edge pattern to follow is the
   importCsvDegraded path in supabase/functions/service-products/index.ts, per
   ABK-014's own AC. The 25 MB cap is in that AC too.

3. WHERE THE GENERATED EXPORT BYTES LIVE. Today they sit in an in-process Map
   with a 15-minute TTL (exportCache in server/routes-address-books.ts). That is
   already wrong behind more than one Node process - an export generated on one
   instance 404s when the download lands on another - and it cannot exist in a
   stateless runtime at all. Pick one: Supabase Storage with a tenant-scoped
   path (matches ABK-014's "source files persisted to tenant-scoped storage"
