userStories.notes:
Source: docs/WORKFLOW-AUDIT-2026-09-02.md (workflow deep dive, 2026-09-02). Evidence: server/services/equipment-lifecycle-state-machine.ts:577,693 (log only), :582-618 and :628-676 (real warranty and email); supabase/functions/equipment-lifecycle/index.ts transition handler updates current_stage and inserts the transition only. dependsOn: WF-L-01, WF-C-09. FILED 2026-09-02.

WF-L-08 done, on both hosts.

THE DEFECT, and it is worth reading the shape of it. `installed -> active` is the moment a machine becomes a serviced, billable asset, and neither host did any of it. The Express state machine's handler opened with:

  try { log.info('Equipment monitoring activated'); } catch (error) { log.error('Failed to activate monitoring', error); }

A log line inside a try/catch with nothing in it that could throw. The warranty stamp and the welcome email immediately below it ARE real - which is exactly why the block read as implemented and why US-050 closed claiming "activate monitoring" was done. And it was dev-only anyway: the production edge transition handler set current_stage, inserted a transition row and returned, so none of the six stages' side effects ran in production at all. The result was that no device was ever registered for monitoring, no contract term ever started, and no baseline meter was ever captured - so the first billing cycle counted from zero on a machine that had already printed, and the contract WF-C-09 deliberately leaves un-dated at proposal acceptance stayed un-dated forever.

AC1. supabase/functions/_shared/lifecycle-activation.ts holds the decisions; each host does its own IO (PostgREST inline in the edge handler, drizzle in server/services/lifecycle-activation-effects.ts, which IMPORTS the shared module rather than copying it - it is plain TypeScript with no imports of its own, so both runtimes load it and there is no twin to drift). Registration, contract start date, lease first payment date and baseline reading, with every write checked independently: "registered for monitoring but no baseline captured" is a real state and a different one from "nothing ran".

FOUR RULES, each a decision rather than an implementation detail.

NO INTEGRATION, NO REGISTRATION. device_registrations.integration_id is NOT NULL with a foreign key to manufacturer_integrations, which itself needs a manufacturer, an auth method and credentials. Manufacturing a placeholder integration to satisfy the constraint would put a fake vendor connection in the tenant's integrations list, so a tenant with no active integration for that manufacturer gets a NAMED skip instead. Free-text `equipment.manufacturer` is matched onto the enum ("Konica Minolta" -> konica_minolta, "HP Inc." -> hp), because failing to see that would skip a registration the tenant can actually make. The device is registered with status `unknown`, not `online`: nothing has heard from it yet.

A BASELINE METER IS NEVER ZERO BY DEFAULT. A machine arrives having printed its own test pages - tens, sometimes hundreds - and a baseline of 0 bills the customer for every one of them on the first cycle. So the reading comes from the acceptance form or there is no baseline row and the caller is told which. A genuine zero on one meter is kept when another is present.

A CONTRACT IS STARTED ONLY WHEN THERE IS EXACTLY ONE CANDIDATE. WF-C-09 leaves start_date null at proposal acceptance precisely so nobody invents a term; this is the event that sets it. Two un-started contracts for the same customer is ambiguous and picking one would start the wrong one, so it is reported and left for a human - unless `equipment.service_contract_number` names one, which resolves it.

NOTHING IS OVERWRITTEN. A contract already dated, a lease with a first payment date and a device already registered are left alone: re-accepting a unit must not move a term that is already running.

AC2. active -> retired marks the registration `offline` rather than deleting it - device_metrics references it ON DELETE CASCADE, and the meter history of a retired machine is what the final invoice is built from. Idempotent, and it says so when there was nothing registered.

AC3. server/tests/unit/lifecycle-activation.test.ts, 22 tests. The last block RUNS AGAINST A REAL DATABASE: it plans from live manufacturer_integrations and contracts rows, applies the writes, and asserts the registration, the contract start date and the baseline reading exist. Executed against PostgreSQL 16 for this story - CNX-11001 registered with status `unknown` against the Canon integration and customer acct-1, CT-2026-0001 started, and one meter_readings row at 412 bw / 37 color with previous meters 0 and the baseline note. It skips when WF_L08_TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset so CI stays green without a database, and it is the only test in the suite that is skipped by default.

AC4. US-050's note is corrected in place. It claimed all six stages' side effects were implemented; the monitoring half of two of them was a log line, and the whole set was dev-only. The correction also says plainly that the other five entries were not re-audited and may carry the same shape.

Verified: 4909 unit tests pass (2 skipped, one of them AC3's when no scratch database is offered), tsc holds at 308, and 20 guards are clean. Note for anyone touching the new shared module: it lives under supabase/functions/_shared and is therefore outside eslint's scope by ignore pattern, so lint says nothing about it - the tests are what hold it.

userStories.title: Onboarded devices become equipment rows
userStories.description: As service, a device configured during onboarding must be the same row meter reads, tickets and toner replenishment query. onboarding_equipment.equipment_id is nullable, unconstrained and set only when a caller already passes an id; the onboarding function never creates the equipment row, so a device can carry real IP, hostname and serial data and never exist in equipment.

userStories.notes:
Source: docs/WORKFLOW-AUDIT-2026-09-02.md (workflow deep dive, 2026-09-02). Evidence: shared/schema.ts:3750 (onboarding_equipment.equipment_id comment); supabase/functions/onboarding/index.ts:450-524. dependsOn: none. FILED 2026-09-02.

WF-L-09 done, on both hosts.

The defect. `onboarding_equipment.equipment_id` was nullable, unconstrained, and set only when a caller already had an id to pass - and no caller did. Neither the edge function nor the Express router ever created an equipment row. So a device could carry a real serial, IP, MAC, hostname and install location through an entire onboarding checklist, be marked installed, and never exist in `equipment` - the table meter reads, service tickets, contracts and toner replenishment all query. The install completed and the machine was invisible to every downstream system.

AC1. POST /onboarding/:id/equipment now links, matches or creates. The decision lives in one module - supabase/functions/_shared/onboarding-equipment-link.ts with the Node twin at server/lib/onboarding-equipment-link.ts - and takes its three IO calls as arguments, so both hosts share one behaviour and it is testable without a database. An explicit equipmentId is VERIFIED rather than trusted (unverified it is a foreign-key violation the installer reads as "failed to add equipment"). Otherwise a serial match wins over a create. The customer comes from the checklist, because equipment.customer_id is NOT NULL and inventing one attaches the machine to the wrong account; with no customer the link is skipped and says so. A failed link never loses the device the installer just recorded - the onboarding row is written either way, with the outcome reported as `equipmentLink` on the response.

SERIAL UNIQUENESS IS GLOBAL, NOT PER TENANT. equipment.serial_number is `.unique()` on the whole table, so a serial already registered to another tenant can neither be linked (it is not their row) nor inserted (23505). That case is skipped with a reason rather than surfacing as a 500. Reproduced on Postgres 16.

Migration 0075_onboarding_equipment_fk.sql adds the foreign key, ON DELETE SET NULL - deleting a machine must not delete the record of the install that put it there - plus an index. Orphaned ids are cleared first: an id resolving to no row is already meaningless, and failing the migration on one would leave the column unconstrained on exactly the databases that need it most. PROVEN against a real PostgreSQL 16: applies twice, clears the orphan while keeping the valid link, rejects a non-row on insert, and leaves all three install records standing after the equipment row is deleted.

Three fields onboarding collects have no column on `equipment` - hostname, macAddress, networkAssignment. They are named in the response's `unpersisted` array rather than smuggled into `notes`, where nothing would read them.

AC2. The equipment detail dialog in CustomerEquipment.tsx has a "Start onboarding checklist" action: it creates the checklist for that customer, adds the device with equipmentId already set, and opens the checklist. So the record and the machine are the same thing from the first click rather than two rows somebody reconciles later. Worth knowing for whoever picks up the next story on that component: four of the five existing row-menu items (Meter Readings, Schedule Service, Update Status, Edit Equipment) have no onClick and do nothing.

AC3. server/tests/unit/onboarding-equipment-link.test.ts, 19 tests. The link branches - created, matched, explicit, unverified explicit, cross-tenant serial, missing customer, no serial - run for real against injected fakes. The two read paths could not be executed (both are Deno edge functions importing supabase-js from esm.sh), so what is asserted instead is the thing that decides whether the device shows up: the row this code writes is checked column-by-column against the REAL Drizzle table via getTableColumns - no phantom column, every NOT NULL column without a default filled - and then against each endpoint's own filter, GET /api/equipment on tenant_id plus the customer scope and GET /api/customers/:id/equipment on tenant_id AND customer_id. Verified the tests bite by mutating the module: dropping customer_id and removing the cross-tenant guard fails six of them.

AC4. check:phantom-cols and check:spread-insert-keys both clean, along with migrations, edge-boot, edge-paths, edge-rbac, routes, shadowed-express, server-orphans, orphans, nav, a11y-names, sql-string-tables, unwritten-tables and phantom-tables. 4842 unit tests pass and tsc holds at 308. eslint on CustomerEquipment.tsx goes 8 pre-existing errors to 7.

userStories.title: Production ticket lists show equipment model and technician name
userStories.description: As a dispatcher, the queue must show what machine and who. supabase/functions/service-tickets/index.ts never joins equipment or technicians, so equipmentModel and assignedTechnician are blank in production; the dev Express route joins them (AUDIT-013 fixed dev only).
acceptanceCriteria: The list and single-ticket handlers enrich each row with equipment model and serial and the technician name, under the keys ServiceHub.tsx reads.
A unit test asserts both fields for a ticket with equipment_id and assigned_technician_id set.
/api/service-tickets is proxied and the covered Express handler is deleted.
userStories.notes:
Source: docs/WORKFLOW-AUDIT-2026-09-02.md (workflow deep dive, 2026-09-02). Evidence: supabase/functions/service-tickets/index.ts:106-144 vs server/routes-mobile-api.ts:62-104. dependsOn: none. FILED 2026-09-02.
CLOSED 2026-09-02.

supabase/functions/service-tickets/_enrich.ts adds customerName, equipmentModel,
equipmentSerial and assignedTechnician to the list AND the single-ticket handler,
so a ticket does not gain or lose fields depending on which screen opened it.

A THIRD FIELD WAS BLANK AND THE STORY DID NOT NAME IT. ServiceHub.tsx reads
customerName, and its normalizer maps ticket columns but not that one - because the
Express handler already emitted it in camelCase. The edge function emitted
customer_name. So the customer name was blank in production too, alongside the
machine and the technician. The snake key and the nested customer object are kept
for the callers that read them.

THREE BATCHED in() LOOKUPS, NOT AN EMBED. PostgREST cannot join these without a
foreign key, so it is one round trip per related table over the distinct ids on the
page - 3 for any page size, not N. Every lookup is tenant-scoped, and there is a
test for that specifically: the Drizzle version scoped both sides of each join, and
an id that leaked in from another tenant must resolve to null rather than to that
tenant's row.

AC3 IS DONE BUT IT COST MORE THAN THE STORY EXPECTED, and the guard is what found
it. /api/service-tickets is proxied and the two covered Express handlers (the list
and /stats) are deleted. check:shadowed-express then reported SEVEN handlers under
the prefix, five of which I had not seen:

  /:id/analysis (GET+POST, routes-service-analysis.ts) - LIVE. ServiceTicketAnalysis.tsx
    POSTs it and it is the only implementation on either host. Kept by MOUNT ORDER:
    registerServiceAnalysisRoutes now runs BEFORE registerEdgeFunctionProxy, the same
    fix as the inbound-webhook ordering, because the proxy forwards the whole prefix
    and falls through only on a NETWORK error, never a 404.
  /:id/{check-in,session,request-parts,parts-requests,complete} (routes-enhanced-service.ts)
    - an unbuilt mobile field-service workflow with NO CALLER in any of the client
    trees. Nothing regressed, because nothing called them.

routes-enhanced-service.ts mounts at the /api ROOT, so moving it ahead of the proxy
the way routes-service-analysis.ts was moved would put every route it owns ahead of
every proxied prefix. Too broad, so those five are annotated in the retained baseline
instead. The lesson: before proxying a prefix, run check:shadowed-express against the
change rather than grepping for the router you already know about - I found two of the
seven by hand and the guard found the rest.

TWO /stats IMPLEMENTATIONS DISAGREED ABOUT THE STATUS VOCABULARY, which proxying
would have silently resolved in favour of whichever one survived. Express counted
status='in-progress' (the spelling in the schema comment); the edge function counted
'in_progress' (the spelling server/seeds/demo-data.ts writes); and 'completed'
counted as resolved only in Express. The edge version now counts BOTH spellings and
all three resolved-ish values, because a superset cannot under-count and
under-counting is the failure that looks like real data. WHICH SPELLING IS CANONICAL
IS STILL OPEN - service_tickets.status is a bare varchar with a comment, not an enum,
and both spellings are in the tree. That is COP-E02's shape and wants its own story.

/api/service-tickets/:id/attachments is called by the iOS app
(APIEndpoint.swift:420) and served by NOTHING on either host - no Express route, no
edge branch. Found while mapping the prefix; not this story's to fix.

userStories.title: Mobile Field Service works a real ticket instead of ticket-123
userStories.description: As a field technician, I check in, take photos, log parts and time, and close my ticket from my phone. client/src/pages/MobileFieldService.tsx hard-codes serviceTicketId ticket-123 and technicianId tech-456 (comment: mock for demo); the mobile edge function behind it is real and moves service_tickets.status through in_progress and completed, so the only web page with a working check-in backend cannot be used.

userStories.notes:
Source: docs/WORKFLOW-AUDIT-2026-09-02.md (workflow deep dive, 2026-09-02). Evidence: client/src/pages/MobileFieldService.tsx:80-82. dependsOn: WF-R-07. FILED 2026-09-02.

DONE 2026-09-02 (WF-V-02). The check-in console works a real ticket, and the
technician is the person holding the token.

WHAT WAS THERE. `const serviceTicketId = 'ticket-123'` and
`const technicianId = 'tech-456'`, under the comment "Mock service ticket ID for
demo". The backend is real - the mobile function moves service_tickets.status
through in_progress and completed - so the only web surface with a working check-in
could not be pointed at anything. The ticket now comes from
/mobile-field-service/:ticketId and the technician from the JWT.

THE SECOND HALF IS A HOLE, NOT A GAP, and it is the part worth reading.
`?technicianId=` was taken from the caller and used UNCHECKED on both
GET /mobile/sessions and GET /mobile/sync, so any authenticated member of the
tenant could read another technician's sessions, their assigned tickets - which
carry the customer's address, contact name, email and phone - and their photos.
POST /mobile/sessions took `body.technicianId`, so one technician could open a
check-in against another's name. The id is now honoured only when the named
technician is inside the caller's WF-R-07 scope: a supervisor may look at their
crew, a technician may only be themselves, and the session insert takes the caller
outright. Out of scope answers 403 rather than quietly substituting the caller -
returning different data than was asked for is how a UI comes to show the wrong
person's work while looking like it worked.

`includeUnowned: false` on that check, unlike everywhere else: "this row belongs to
nobody" is not a reason to let someone act as a named other person.

A BUG IN MY OWN NEW CODE, caught by the test I wrote for it. The picker read
`data.tickets`; the sync response is
`{ syncedAt, technician, data: { serviceTickets, activeSessions, photos }, counts }`.
It would have rendered an empty queue forever and said nothing - the PA-040 shape,
a page reading key names its endpoint does not send. The test now pins the response
shape as well as the page's read of it.

THE PICKER, since AC1 offers a route id OR a picker and this does both: the bare
/mobile-field-service is the caller's own assigned queue, from /api/mobile/sync,
which is the endpoint that already answered "what is assigned to me". That is what
makes the console reachable without knowing an id, and it is where ServiceHub's new
"My service calls" button lands. An empty queue says a dispatcher assigns service
calls rather than showing a blank page - WF-V-03 is the dispatch board that fills
it.

VERIFIED: server/tests/unit/mobile-field-service.test.ts, 14 tests. Eight drive the
real mobile handler - the default-to-caller, the 403 for another technician, a
supervisor reaching their crew but not another, the same rule on sync, and the
session insert ignoring a body-supplied id. Six read the page. check:edge-rbac now
lists `mobile` as gated.

userStories.notes:
Source: docs/WORKFLOW-AUDIT-2026-09-02.md (workflow deep dive, 2026-09-02). Evidence: client/src/pages/ServiceHub.tsx:230-253, :988-1022. dependsOn: WF-V-01. FILED 2026-09-02.

WF-V-03 done. There has never been a working assign step in this product. No page anywhere wrote service_tickets.assigned_technician_id except the mobile check-in's side effect; /service-dispatch was an AUDIT-015 ComingSoon over ~1,070 deleted lines of fixtures; and ServiceHub's "Smart Routing" modal recommended "John Smith, 95% match, ETA 30 min" and "Sarah Johnson, 87%" - two hardcoded objects, ids tech-1 and tech-2 belonging to no row - beside an Assign button with no onClick.

AC1. client/src/pages/ServiceDispatchOptimization.tsx is now the dispatch board: the open queue sorted by priority then scheduled date, filters for status and priority, and a technician select per row that PATCHes /api/service-tickets/:id with assignedTechnicianId plus status 'assigned' (or 'open' when cleared). Load comes from a new GET /service-tickets/dispatch-load, computed SERVER-side over the whole tenant rather than from the board's own list, because that list is scoped to the caller and counting from it would under-report anyone whose other work the dispatcher cannot see - a number that looks precise and is quietly wrong. The assignment inserts a user_notifications row (action_url /mobile-field-service/:id, priority high for an urgent call), inside try/catch: a failed notification must never roll back a real dispatch, and that table can be absent on an older database. No notification on an unassign or on a dispatcher taking a ticket themselves.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, because the page's old title promised it: route optimization, live technician GPS and drive-time estimates. There is no routing endpoint and no technician location feed, so all three are missing rather than approximated, and the file header says so.

AC2. The Smart Routing modal, getIntelligentRoutingSuggestions and the showIntelligentRouting state are deleted from ServiceHub.tsx; the button now opens the board that actually assigns. A SECOND fabrication in the same page went with it: the "Filter by technician" select listed tech-1/tech-2/tech-3 as John Smith, Sarah Johnson and Mike Wilson, so picking any of them filtered the board to nothing. Options are now derived from the technicians who actually hold tickets in the list.

AC3. Assignment goes through WF-R-07's denyIfTicketOutOfScope, which the PATCH branch already called; the board is gated at minLevel 3 in navigation-permissions.ts.

AC4. server/tests/unit/service-dispatch.test.ts, 19 tests. It found a real defect in the transition the story names last. The PATCH handler read `body[camelKey] || body[snakeKey]`, so the board's `assignedTechnicianId: null` became undefined - and supabase-js JSON.stringifies the update payload, which drops an undefined key before PostgREST sees it. UNASSIGNING WAS A NO-OP: 200 back, ticket still assigned, no error anywhere. The same `||` swallowed laborHours: 0 and any cleared text field. Fixed to take whichever key the caller actually sent, null included. The two regression tests fail on the pre-fix expression and pass on the fix (verified by reintroducing it).

Testability: the field mapping, load arithmetic and notification row moved to supabase/functions/service-tickets/_dispatch.ts, because index.ts pulls supabase-js from esm.sh and vitest cannot import it.

GUARD FIX, and it is the reach-back trap check:phantom-cols' own header warns about. `const { updateData, changes } = applyTicketFields(...)` is a destructuring pattern, which its declaration regex did not match, so `.from('service_tickets').update(updateData)` resolved fifty lines back to the unrelated `const updateData = { … }` in the POST /updates branch and reported six columns of service_ticket_updates as phantom columns of service_tickets. Correct code accused, which the script's own comments call worse than a missed finding. Destructured names are now bound with no keys, the same way parameters are, so resolution stops there. Baseline unchanged at 204 and nothing retired.

Verified: 4823 unit tests pass, tsc holds at 308, and edge-boot / edge-paths / edge-rbac / phantom-cols / routes / edge-coverage / unwritten-tables / nav / orphans / a11y-names / fabricated / no-mocks / no-static-posture / no-random-metrics all pass. eslint on ServiceDispatchOptimization.tsx is clean; ServiceHub.tsx goes 26 pre-existing errors to 25.

Source: docs/WORKFLOW-AUDIT-2026-09-02.md (workflow deep dive, 2026-09-02). live half. server/routes-preventive-maintenance.ts held four handlers whose own
comments said "Sample maintenance schedules until schema is updated" - and NOTHING
IMPORTED IT, so it was dead in dev too (it was already in
docs/server-orphans-baseline.json). server/routes-sample-data.ts held the SAME four
endpoints under a header reading "Preventive Maintenance Automation Routes (Mock)",
and that file IS registered, so it is what dev actually hit. Both are gone: the
orphan deleted outright, the live four cut out of routes-sample-data.ts with a note
in their place. Before assuming which fixture a page was reading, check which of
them is registered - the dead one is easier to find and is not the answer.

AC1 - shared/maintenance-schema.ts declares maintenance_schedules and
maintenance_records, and migration 0071 captures them. The columns are exactly the
ones supabase/functions/maintenance/ already reads and writes, recovered from its
queries rather than designed fresh: redesigning the shape would have meant
rewriting a working handler to match a table nobody had written down. IF NOT EXISTS
throughout, because this environment has no credentials for the live project and
therefore cannot tell whether db:push already created them there - which is exactly
the case that form is for. Applied TWICE to a real PostgreSQL 16 to prove it: both
runs clean, both tables created, an insert works. The migration will NOT correct a
live table that exists with a different shape, and the header says so.

AC2 - /api/maintenance is proxied, so the two hosts run one implementation.

AC3 - /auto-generate is real. It used to submit five hard-coded ids ('eq-001'..
'eq-005') to an endpoint that persisted nothing and returned an invented annual
saving while reporting success. The page now generates for the tenant's equipment
that has no active schedule yet - the only set the button can sensibly mean - and
says so when there is none. The handler filters to equipment THIS TENANT OWNS,

AUDIT-019 call. Predictive maintenance is real elsewhere: /service/predictions runs

and satisfaction over months asserts a measured series, and neither is recorded

userStories.title: Boot-load guard: every edge function must import cleanly
userStories.description: As the team, a function that fails to parse must fail CI, not 404 forever. The dispatcher loads each function with await import inside try/catch and omits failures; equipment-lifecycle shipped unparseable and stayed invisible for the life of the file.
acceptanceCriteria: A script under scripts/ dynamically imports every supabase/functions/*/index.ts (Deno or a tsc parse pass with the same module settings) and fails on any import-time error; wired into CI beside check:edge-coverage.
A runtime check compares the dispatcher’s available list against the on-disk directory list and fails on a missing function; runnable against the live host.
Running it before WF-L-01 reports equipment-lifecycle; after, zero.
userStories.notes:
Source: docs/WORKFLOW-AUDIT-2026-09-02.md (workflow deep dive, 2026-09-02). Evidence: supabase/functions/server.ts:82-99. dependsOn: none. FILED 2026-09-02.
CLOSED 2026-09-02. scripts/check-edge-boot-load.mjs, wired as npm run check:edge-boot
and into .github/workflows/ci.yml beside check:edge-coverage.

NO DENO IN CI OR IN THE DEV CONTAINER, and tsc cannot do this either: tsconfig.json's
include is client/shared/server only, the edge tree imports npm: and https: specifiers
tsc cannot resolve, and a semantic pass over 268 functions that use `any` everywhere
would bury one real finding under thousands. So the guard reproduces the three things
that actually stop a module LOADING, using the TypeScript parser only, walking the
transitive relative-import graph from each index.ts (540 files) because `await import`
is transitive - a broken file under _shared/ takes down every function that imports it:

  PARSE    grammar errors in any reachable file.
  RESOLVE  a RELATIVE specifier naming no file on disk. Bare, npm:, jsr:, node: and
           https: are skipped - this cannot see the deploy's import map and guessing
           would be noise.
  BIND     a top-level name given more than one VALUE binding where at least one is
           lexical (import / const / let / class). That is exactly the set V8 throws
           on. Type-only declarations are erased before the module runs so they are
           not conflicts, and repeated `function`/`var` declarations are legal and are
           not reported - modelling the JS rule rather than the TS diagnostic is what
           keeps this at zero false positives on a tree this size.

AC3 verified by restoring the pre-fix equipment-lifecycle/index.ts: the guard names it
with all three identifiers and exits 1; after WF-L-01 it reports zero across all 268.

AC2 is --host <url>: fetch <host>/health (which server.ts:119-131 already answers with
the list it actually loaded) and diff against the on-disk directories. A function on
disk and absent from /health failed to import; the boot log has the matching
"Failed to load <fn>" line.

IT FOUND A SECOND DEFECT ON ITS FIRST RUN, which is the argument for the resolve pass
existing at all: _shared/address-book/conversion-engine.ts imported SerializeOptions
from './vendors/_shared/options', a directory that does not exist - every sibling
serializer uses './options.ts'. Fixed. But it is an `import type`, so it is ERASED
before the module runs and cannot break a boot, and reporting it would have been a
false positive on the one thing this script claims to measure. The resolve pass now
skips type-only imports and exports and says why. A guard that reports real bugs
outside its own stated invariant is how the next real finding gets ignored.

BLIND SPOT, in the script header too: this does not execute module top-level code, so
a throw at import time - an env var read at module scope, a failing top-level await -
is invisible to the static pass. --host is the answer to that half.

userStories.title: Hard guard: every table an edge function names must be declared or explicitly allow-listed
userStories.description: As the team, an undeclared relation is a runtime 42P01. check:phantom-tables gates only undeclared tables behind a silent catch and fabricated fallbacks; sales_handoffs, work_orders, appointments, lead_routing_rules, maintenance_schedules and purchase_order_line_items all passed it.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/check-phantom-tables.mjs (or a sibling) resolves every .from(literal) in supabase/functions against pgTable declarations plus CREATE TABLE across the migration chain, and fails on any miss not in an explicit drift allow-list with a reason per entry.
The six tables above are the seed findings; each is fixed or allow-listed with its owning story id.
The guard strips comments before matching and is CI-wired.
userStories.notes:
Source: docs/WORKFLOW-AUDIT-2026-09-02.md (workflow deep dive, 2026-09-02). dependsOn: none. FILED 2026-09-02.
CLOSED 2026-09-02. scripts/check-phantom-tables.mjs hardened in place rather than
given a sibling: two guards over the same corpus with two baselines is how they drift.
Already CI-wired (ci.yml:99) and already comment-stripping (PA-031), so AC3 was met
before this - the work was AC1 and AC2.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG WITH IT. The resolver was fine: it already checked every
.from(literal) in supabase/functions against pgTable/pgView in shared/ plus CREATE
TABLE/VIEW across drizzle/{migrations,functions,rls}. What failed was the CONTRACT.
`allowed` was a flat array of "table (file)" strings under one blanket note, and
--update-baseline swept every finding into it, so all six seed findings sat there
green. A question nobody is required to answer stops being a question.

`allowed` is now an OBJECT keyed by table and an entry is REJECTED unless it carries a
non-empty `reason` and the `story` that owns it, with `files` pinned so an allow-listed
table cannot silently spread to a second function. --update-baseline PRUNES ONLY - it
never adds - so a new undeclared relation cannot enter without somebody writing down
why. The failure message prints the JSON to paste. Four gates verified by hand: a novel
finding fails with paste-ready JSON, a reason blanked to '' fails, --update-baseline
refuses to add the novel finding while still pruning a reference that went away, and
the clean tree passes.

I DID NOT WRITE 73 REASONS. The 93 pre-existing entries (73 distinct tables) moved to
`unreviewed`, verbatim, shrink-only, labelled in the file as a triage queue that is
NOT justified and NOT accepted. Inventing plausible justifications for 73 tables in one
pass is the same fabrication this guard exists to catch. The six with an identified
owner were promoted; the rest need a story each.

THE SIX, EACH WITH ITS OWNER (AC2) - all confirmed absent from shared/ and from every
migration, not taken on the audit's word:

  sales_handoffs            WF-C-06   Two handoff models, neither wired. The one that
                                      exists is shared/sales-handoff-schema.ts (four
                                      tables) behind server/routes-sales-handoff.ts,
                                      which has no caller; this edge fn is unreferenced.
                                      Creating sales_handoffs would entrench the wrong
                                      one.
  work_orders               WF-V-07   work-orders/ and service-contracts/ are
                                      unreferenced, but technician-management is LIVE.
  appointments              WF-L-06   scheduling/ is unreferenced, but today-dashboard
                                      is LIVE (ios/Printyx/Core/Network/APIEndpoint.swift:305).
  lead_routing_rules        WF-S-02   The one already handled honestly - 503
                                      ROUTING_RULES_UNAVAILABLE since EDGE-002g.
  maintenance_schedules     WF-V-04   maintenance_records is in the same state; Express
                                      serves dev from fixtures, so the hosts disagree.
  purchase_order_line_items WF-P-01   The only one whose correct relation is already
                                      known: purchase_order_items, declared twice.

A NEW SIGNAL, BECAUSE A REASON NEEDS EVIDENCE. Each finding now carries
`discardsError`: the file destructures a PostgREST result as `const { data } = ...`
with no `error`. PostgREST leaves .data null on failure and this codebase writes `|| []`
around it, so that combination renders an empty list at 200 and reports nothing - the
notification-bell shape. technician-management's GET /:id/schedule is the worked
example: `const { data: schedule } = await query` over work_orders, then `schedule ||
[]`, so a technician's schedule is permanently empty rather than an error. Same in
today-dashboard for appointments (7 such destructurings). --list prints the count per
file, which is what makes triaging the remaining 73 cheap. The `data: { user }` form is
excluded by rule: every handler's auth destructuring takes `error: userError` alongside
it and is correct.

AND A BLIND SPOT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT CLOSE, recorded in the script header. The
42P01/PGRST205 swallow gate keys on that literal appearing in the file, and EDGE-002g
moved the predicate into _shared/postgrest-errors.ts (isMissingTableError), so every
function using the shared helper is invisible to it. Widening it to count the import
would have fired on the CORRECT code and not on the broken code: the helper is used to
answer 503, which is an honest report that the relation is missing, while the silent
failure is the destructuring above. discardsError is the signal that separates them.
Closing the gate by making it wrong in the other direction is worse than naming it.
